title: Egyptian man who fire-bombed pro-Israel rally in Colorado pleads guilty to federal hate crimes
body: The man who lobbed gasoline bombs at a pro-Israel rally in Colorado last year, injuring several people, including a woman who later died, pleaded guilty on Thursday to federal hate-crime charges, the US Department of Justice said.Mohamed Sabry Soliman, 47, an Egyptian national, is already serving a life sentence for his guilty plea in May to more than 100 state charges, including first-degree murder. Soliman pleaded guilty to nine counts of hate-crime offenses and three explosives charges in federal court in Denver, according to the DOJ. The charges are punishable by life in prison after federal prosecutors declined to seek the death penalty.The plea deal asks that Soliman be sentenced to life in prison plus 50 years. Soliman will be sentenced on January 7."The defendant admitted that he committed the attack because of the actual or perceived Jewish religion and Israeli national origin of the group he targeted," the DOJ said in a statement.David Kraut, a federal public defender listed as Soliman's lawyer, did not immediately respond to a request for comment.Soliman admits to tossing Molotov cocktailsSoliman has admitted tossing two Molotov cocktails at people taking part in a rally in downtown Boulder on June 1, 2025, held in solidarity with hostages seized by Hamas terrorists who stormed Israeli villages from the Palestinian enclave of Gaza on October 7, 2023.Prosecutors said Soliman yelled "Free Palestine" as the gasoline bombs he lobbed at the crowd burst into flames outside a municipal courthouse in the heart of Boulder's popular Pearl Street shopping district.Admitting his guilt in state court nearly six months ago, Soliman denounced his own crimes as contrary to "the teachings of Islam" and insisted he bore no ill will toward Jewish people. He went on to lament the "thousands of families who have lost their families in Palestine and Gaza," and said the "enemy is Zionism."Authorities in Colorado identified 29 victims from the attack, including 14 who were burned or injured while fleeing and 15 who were close enough to be considered targets of attempted murder. One victim, 82-year-old Karen Diamond, died of her injuries later that month. Her husband suffered severe burns and survived.The firebombing came amid heightened tensions over the 2023 Hamas raid and Israel's military assault in Gaza, which sparked a surge in anti-Jewish and anti-Muslim hate crimes across the US and a wave of pro-Palestinian protests that many Israel supporters branded as antisemitic. Pro-Palestinian protesters reject accusations that their support of Gazans amounts to antisemitism.Family's immigration detentionAccording to affidavits filed in court by prosecutors, Soliman told investigators after his arrest that he had planned his attack for a year, but delayed going through with it until after his daughter had graduated from high school.Soliman, who had lived with his wife and five children in Colorado Springs, also has asserted that his family members were unaware of his intentions beforehand.The family was taken into immigration custody in June 2025 after his arrest and transported to a detention facility in Texas. They were held until a court-ordered release on April 23, 2026, more than 10 months later.The children and their mother, who subsequently divorced Soliman, were rearrested on April 25 of this year just after returning to Colorado. They were freed again when attorneys intervened a day later, according to court documents.Court records entered at about the time that Soliman reached a plea deal with federal prosecutors earlier this month showed that he had withdrawn motions seeking to preclude any further attempts at removing his family.

title: Gasoline prices to fall 42 agorot Sunday, defying forecasts of a jump to near-record levels
body: Gasoline prices will fall by 42 agorot per liter at midnight between Saturday and Sunday, the Energy and Infrastructure Ministry's Fuel and Gas Administration announced on Thursday, defying earlier forecasts of a sharp increase to near-record levels.The price reduction comes after an approximately 13% decline in gasoline prices in the Mediterranean basin, partially offset by an approximately 2% rise in the dollar exchange rate.The maximum price of a liter of self-service, unleaded 95-octane gasoline, including VAT, will fall to NIS 7.35, compared with the current NIS 7.77. The additional charge for full-service fueling will remain unchanged at 26 agorot per liter.The announcement came as a surprise to Israeli drivers. Earlier on Thursday, sources in the energy market estimated that prices at gas stations would rise by approximately 30 agorot, reaching around NIS 8.30 per liter.Those forecasts were based on a combination of rising global oil prices amid expectations of a regional escalation involving Iran and the strengthening of the US dollar following the election results.However, the Fuel and Gas Administration's calculations produced a positive turnaround, delivering a significant price reduction that will provide immediate financial relief to millions of vehicle owners across Israel.Despite the welcome news at gas stations, drivers will need to closely monitor developments at the Finance Ministry in the coming days.Consumers currently benefit from a reduction in the excise tax on gasoline amounting to NIS 1 per liter. The measure, introduced by Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich for a limited period, carries a budgetary cost of approximately NIS 326 million per month.The current temporary order is set to expire on November 3.The Energy and Infrastructure Ministry has already issued a warning: "If the excise tax order is not updated, the temporary provision concerning the excise tax order will expire overnight between November 4 and 5, meaning that from November 5, the maximum price will stand at NIS 8.35 per liter."To prevent the dramatic NIS 1-per-liter increase on November 5, the finance minister must sign an extension of the tax benefit for another month.Such a move would bring the total budgetary cost of the excise tax subsidy over the past three months to approximately NIS 800 million.

title: Yemen's Houthis say they attacked Saudi Ras Tanura refinery; no Saudi confirmation
body:
Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis said on Thursday they had attacked Saudi Arabia's Ras Tanura oil refinery, the largest in the kingdom, the Rabigh refinery, and an Aramco facility in Abqaiq, as well as King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh and King Fahd International Airport in Dammam.
There was no immediate confirmation from Saudi authorities of the Houthi claims.

title: Protesters rally outside Eisenkot's home with calls to include Arab parties in coalition
body: Protesters gathered outside Yashar chairman Gadi Eisenkot's home in Herzliya on Thursday, urging the opposition leader to form a government with Arab parties following the release of Israel's election results, which left neither political bloc with a Knesset majority.The demonstrators chanted, "There is no change without partnership," calling on Eisenkot to cooperate with Arab parties to prevent Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu from forming another government.Among those attending the demonstration was Amir Badran, deputy mayor of Tel Aviv-Jaffa, who expressed support for a political partnership between the opposition and Arab parties.The completed vote count left Netanyahu's bloc with 53 seats, compared with 48 for the four main opposition parties, 13 short of the 61 seats required for a parliamentary majority. Eisenkot's Yashar emerged as the largest opposition party with 21 seats, behind Netanyahu's Likud, which secured 27.Arab parties may hold key to potential opposition governmentThe results have put the Arab parties at the center of potential coalition negotiations, with their combined 19 seats potentially offering a path to an alternative government.The Joint List secured 11 seats, while Mansour Abbas's Ra'am won eight, bringing the Arab parties to a combined record 19 seats.For Eisenkot and his opposition allies to fulfill their campaign pledge not to join a Netanyahu-led government, cooperation with at least some of the Arab parties would likely be necessary, whether through a formal coalition or outside parliamentary support for a minority government.Ra'am, which previously participated in the Bennett-Lapid coalition, is considered a potential partner in such an arrangement.However, substantial political obstacles remain, particularly opposition from Yisrael Beytenu chairman Avigdor Liberman, whose party secured seven seats.Liberman has reportedly distanced himself from his opposition allies and has rejected both joining a coalition with Arab parties and forming a minority government dependent on their support.His position could complicate efforts to assemble the parliamentary majority needed to replace Netanyahu, even if the other opposition parties reach agreements with Arab factions.Opposition leaders begin coalition talksWith the vote count complete, political leaders have begun meeting to explore possible coalition arrangements.Eisenkot met with B'Yachad chairman Naftali Bennett on Thursday, as well as Democrats chairman Yair Golan, as negotiations over the formation of the next government began taking shape.Golan, who has publicly supported cooperation with Arab parties as part of efforts to form a government without Netanyahu, also met with Ra'am chairman Mansour Abbas on Thursday to discuss building a political partnership and exploring possible arrangements for establishing an alternative government.

title: CENTCOM chief briefs Trump on Iran military options in meeting with Hegseth, Caine - report
body: US Central Command (CENTCOM) chief Adm. Brad Cooper, the top US commander in the Middle East, briefed US President Donald Trump on military options for Iran, a source with knowledge of the briefing told The Jerusalem Post on Thursday.The Wall Street Journal first reported the briefing earlier on Thursday, citing US officials and others with direct knowledge of the meeting. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, Joint Chiefs Chairman Gen. Dan Caine, and other cabinet members were also present, according to the report.  This comes a day after the military leaders met with Vice President JD Vance, one of the people told the WSJ. Vance has reportedly reached out to Iran to revive peace negotiations, although Trump dismissed the reports, saying Vance had communicated with the Iranians only to discuss shortages of medical equipment. US warns Gulf states to be prepared for campaignThe US had told multiple Gulf Arab countries to be prepared for a short, intense military campaign after the US midterm elections, WSJ previously reported, and the US appears to be readying for another attack, sending an additional Patriot system to Israel and moving troops off bases where they were more vulnerable to escalation.Additional air defenses, munitions, and supplies have also been sent to the region, according to the report.  Iran has warned both publicly and privately that it will attack a wide variety of US and Gulf state targets if the US strikes.

title: Legendary X-Men, Star Trek actor Patrick Stewart dies at 86
body: Patrick Stewart, who rose from poverty in England to become an accomplished Shakespearean stage actor and then achieved global stardom as the erudite Captain Jean-Luc Picard in TV's "Star Trek: The Next Generation" and the telepathic Professor Charles Xavier in the "X-Men" movies, has died at the age of 86.Stewart, knighted in 2010 by Queen Elizabeth II for his contributions to drama, died at his home in Los Angeles, according to a statement on his X account."We announce with great sorrow the passing of Sir Patrick Stewart yesterday at his home in Los Angeles, in the loving care of his beloved wife Sunny following a brief and poignant journey with Alzheimer's Disease and Lewy Body Dementia," it said.Stewart became an actor at age 18 and gained acclaim on the stage as a member of the Royal Shakespeare Company beginning in the 1960s. But it was not until after he was hired at age 47 for "Star Trek: The Next Generation" - a TV series that ran from 1987 to 1994 as a sequel to the original 1960s "Star Trek" - that he gained mainstream fame, acting into his 80s."Make it so," his character Picard often said, instructing a subordinate to carry out a command, or sometimes deploying the similar catch phrase, "Engage."Patrick Stewart's rise to fame as Captain Jean-Luc PicardIt was a role he had debated even taking after his longtime friend and fellow Shakespearen Ian McKellen advised him to spurn "Star Trek" and remain in theater. Stewart did take the role and became both a fan favorite and an indispensable part of a lucrative sci-fi franchise, playing Picard not only in 176 episodes over seven seasons of that series but also in several "Star Trek" films and in the later streaming series "Star Trek: Picard" that began airing in 2020 when he was 79."As the seven seasons of TNG ("The Next Generation") went by, the distinction between Jean-Luc Picard and Patrick Stewart became thinner and thinner, until it was impossible for me to know where he left off and I began. So much of what I believed and felt went into that show," Stewart told the Guardian newspaper in 2022.Stewart also initially balked at being cast as the wheelchair-using mutant Professor X in the "X-Men" movies, based on the popular Marvel comic book character."I said, 'Look, I know this isn't science fiction, but it's fantasy, and I've done that.' But they persuaded me that it wouldn't be like 'Star Trek,' so I did it. And yet again I was proved wrong," Stewart told the Guardian.He became a critical part of another big-money franchise starting with the first entry "X-Men" in 2000 and followed by several more.Patrick Stewart's childhood marked by poverty and domestic abuseStewart was born on July 13, 1940, in the English town of Mirfield in Yorkshire. He was raised in poverty, with a father who he said returned from World War Two an alcoholic who suffered from post-traumatic stress syndrome and physically abused Stewart's mother. Stewart recalled putting his body between his father and mother to try to protect her.As a child, Stewart said, acting became a "safe space" after a schoolteacher introduced him to Shakespeare - specifically "The Merchant of Venice" - during a class when he was 12. He started losing his hair at age 17 and was bald by 19. He was embarrassed at the time, but eventually embraced it."Star Trek," created by Gene Roddenberry, presented a hopeful vision of the future, with humankind venturing into the cosmos in spaceships exceeding the speed of light and encountering alien races. The original series' enduring popularity and the success of spinoff films prompted Roddenberry to create the sequel series, "The Next Generation."Jean-Luc Picard's cerebral leadership contrasted with Captain KirkThe Picard character was the opposite of the swashbuckling and sometimes unintentionally buffoonish Captain James T. Kirk, played by William Shatner, of the original series - envisioned as more cerebral and disciplined, though sometimes coming across as stuffy, humorless, or self-important.Stewart recalled being a little too serious with his castmates early on."I tell the story of calling a meeting of my principal fellow cast members and telling them that I thought we were not disciplined enough, that we should not be fooling about on the set as much as we were but taking everything seriously," Stewart told the New Yorker in 2023."And one of the cast members said, 'Oh, come on, Patrick, we've got to have some fun.' And I thumped the chair and said, 'We are not here to have fun' - which they have never let me forget. They taught me so much about loosening up and being freer," Stewart added.Stewart also felt the series improved over time, faulting his own portrayal of Picard in the first two seasons."I found it lacking intimacy. It was very authoritative, but there were few other qualities in him," Stewart said, adding that his work got better in subsequent seasons.In fact, the finest work for the entire cast may have been the two-part, time-bending series finale.He became Sir Patrick Stewart when he was knighted by the Queen at Buckingham Palace in 2010. He told reporters that his heroes were British actors Laurence Olivier, John Gielgud, and Alec Guinness, who were also knighted, adding that being "in that company is the grandest thing that has professionally happened to me."Stewart was married three times and had two children. He married American musician Sunny Ozell in 2013.

title: Broken promises or new elections? Netanyahu, Eisenkot face coalition dilemma
body: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and his opponent Gadi Eisenkot will have to break their promises to their constituents if they want to form and lead Israel's next government.Their potential political allies will have to do the same.Netanyahu's Likud and Eisenkot's Yashar party both garnered more votes than any of the other nine parties that met the threshold to join the next parliament.Netanyahu and the bloc of parties that ideologically align with him, however, secured only 53 of the 61 seats needed for a governing majority in the 120-seat Knesset. The Eisenkot bloc won 48. For Eisenkot, three divisive issues are likely to dominate the debate and force some politicians to renege on campaign pledges: aligning with Arab parties, mandatory military service for Haredi men and a unity government with Netanyahu.Support from the Arab partiesEisenkot's bloc includes four Jewish Israeli parties, referred to as Zionist parties: his own party Yashar, B'Yachad led by former prime ministers Naftali Bennett and Yair Lapid, Israel Beytenu led by Avigdor Liberman, and the Democrats led by Yair Golan.Eisenkot could easily become prime minister with a 67-seat coalition if he added the Arab parties, Ra'am with 8 seats and the Joint List with 11. But that is far from straightforward. Three of the bloc's four parties — Yashar, B'Yachad and Israel Beytenu — explicitly pledged not to form a government with the Arab parties. And relying on their support would face an additional legitimacy hurdle given Netanyahu's advantage among Jewish voters.Eisenkot himself has repeatedly and unequivocally said he does not intend to form a government with the Arab parties. During the campaign, he set four conditions for joining his government, including a commitment to Israel as a Jewish and democratic state and to the values of the Declaration of Independence, mandatory military or national service, and recognition of Hamas as a terrorist organization. In an interview with Channel 12 News in late September, Eisenkot, a former IDF chief of staff, said the Arab parties did not meet his conditions and therefore would not be part of the government.On election night and since then, he has continued to speak of a coalition with Jewish Zionist parties.Naftali Bennett, the former prime minister who relied on the support of the Ra'am party in 2021, when he and Lapid formed their coalition, also ruled out sitting in a government with the Arab parties. Liberman, whose party won seven seats, said he would form a coalition made up of “Zionist parties only.” Only Golan spoke prior to the election of sitting with Arab parties and has since the election called on the other three parties in his bloc to do so. One attempt to circumvent the issue would be for Eisenkot to form a minority government that would depend on votes from Ra'am and the Joint List from outside the coalition. A more solid version of that game plan would be a coalition that included Ra'am but relied on the Joint List from outside the government. However, this option is also likely to face significant political and public opposition. The Joint List stated in an official declaration following the election that it was willing to engage in “political cooperation to bring down Netanyahu's government,” but it did not publicly clarify whether, and under what conditions, it would support a government led by Gadi Eisenkot. Ra'am leader Mansour Abbas said in an interview with Channel 12 News on the eve of the election: “I will know how to bring a government to the Knesset.”The draft issueWithout the Arab parties' support, the change bloc could theoretically turn to the 13 seats held by the ultra-Orthodox parties, Shas and United Torah Judaism, to form a government. All four parties in the bloc made ending the ultra-Orthodox exemption from military service a central campaign issue. Cooperation with those parties would amount to breaking an explicit campaign promise.Shas and UTJ have similarly promised their Haredi constituents that they would not allow for forced conscription.A unity government with Netanyahu With the path to a government that excludes Netanyahu looking tenuous at best, the change bloc's alternative would be to join Netanyahu in a national unity government. But that, too, would represent a flagrant breach of its campaign pledges. The one clear binding principle of these four parties is their goal of unseating Netanyahu, Israel's longest-serving prime minister, whom they have said poses an existential threat to the country. In a late-October radio interview, Eisenkot said, “I unequivocally commit that I will not sit under Netanyahu, not even in a rotation,” in which he and Netanyahu would share the prime ministership. Bennett said in a radio interview, “I am not going to sit under him because he is the person destroying the State of Israel.” Liberman wrote on X two weeks ago, “With Netanyahu — even if the world turns upside down, we will not sit with him under any circumstances.” Yair Golan, leader of the Democrats party, said, “We will not sit with Netanyahu and his partners. Period.”The challenge for NetanyahuOn the other side, Netanyahu also has no clear path to forming a government. The parties in his coalition defied expectations by winning 53 seats, but securing the eight additional seats needed for a majority appears out of reach. Netanyahu deployed the prospect of the Arab parties in the coalition as a cudgel to bash the opposition during the campaign. In a speech on the eve of the election, Netanyahu called cooperation with those parties “a disgrace.”That may not stop him from trying to form a government with one of the Arab parties, particularly Ra'am, whose leader Mansour Abbas told Channel 12 on election night that he was speaking with politicians from both blocs. Netanyahu during the 2022 election held talks with Abbas about forming a government.Even if Netanyahu were to do the unthinkable and cooperate with the Arab parties, however, he would be unlikely to secure a majority. His ultra-nationalist partners, Itamar Ben-Gvir and Bezalel Smotrich, made clear during the campaign that such cooperation was out of the question for them.With all apparent paths to a government blocked, forming a coalition in Israel may require a fundamental breach of campaign promises that would shake up the entire political system. The alternative is another election, which would be held if no side succeeds in forming a government.

title: Majority of opposition voters back Eisenkot-led government with Arab party Ra'am - poll
body: A majority of voters for Israel's four main change-bloc parties support a government led by Gadi Eisenkot that includes the Arab Ra'am party, according to a survey conducted by the Hebrew University's Accord Center on Tuesday evening, as polls were closing in the Knesset election.The survey found that 61% of voters for Eisnekot's Yashar, Naftali Bennett's B'Yachad, Yair Golan's Democrats, and Avigdor Liberman's Yisrael Beytenu favored forming a government with Mansour Abbas' Ra'am, making it the most popular option among supporters of the parties seeking to replace Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.Another 20% preferred holding new elections, while 12% supported a rotation government with Netanyahu. Just 7% favored forming a coalition with the ultra-Orthodox parties.The poll was conducted on October 27, between 9:15 p.m. and 10:27 p.m., among 467 respondents who had already voted for one of the four parties. The results were weighted according to party size.The findings come amid uncertainty over the formation of Israel's next government, after Tuesday's election left neither Netanyahu's bloc nor the change bloc with the 61 Knesset seats required for a parliamentary majority without support from Arab parties.The possibility of cooperation with Ra'am, led by Mansour Abbas, has become a central issue in coalition discussions. While the survey indicates substantial support for such an arrangement among change-bloc voters, the bloc's leaders have expressed differing positions on cooperation with Arab parties.*רוב מצביעי גוש השינוי, כולל מצביעי ליברמן, בעד ממשלה עם רע"מ ובהימנעות של הרשימה המשותפת* מרכז אקורד מהאוניברסיטה העברית ערך היום (29.10) סקר בזק שבדק את עמדות מצביעי גוש השינוי לממשלה הנשענת מבחוץ על תמיכת רע"מ ובהימנעות הרשימה המשותפת. הממצאים חד-משמעיים: *59% ממצביעי גוש השינוי מעדיפים שאיזנקוט ירכיב ממשלה עם רע"מ ובהימנעות המשותפת על פני כל אופציה אחרת.* רק 26% מעדיפים ממשלת רוטציה עם נתניהו, 10% מעדיפים בחירות נוספות ו-5% מעדיפים ממשלה בשיתוף המפלגות החרדיות. הממצא עקבי עם הסקר שנערך בסיומו של יום הבחירות, שבו 61% ממצביעי האופוזיציה תמכו בממשלה בתמיכת רע"מ. תוצאות האמת ותרחיש הכולל את הרשימה המשותפת לא שינו את רמת התמיכה. מפילוח התשובות עפ"י מפלגות עולה שממשלה עם רע"מ ובהימנעות המשותפת היא האופציה המועדפת על מצביעי כל אחת מארבע מפלגות הגוש. תומכים בה 93% ממצביעי הדמוקרטים, 59% ממצביעי ישר!, 47% ממצביעי ביחד וכן 42% ממצביעי ישראל ביתנו. (הסקר נערך ב-29 באוקטובר 2026 בקרב 935 משיבים שהצביעו לישר!, ביחד, הדמוקרטים וישראל ביתנו. התוצאות משוקללות לגודל המפלגות בתוצאות הבחירות).— Eran Halperin (@eranh75_eran) October 29, 2026Golan pushes for majority coalition with Arab partiesGolan has argued that the opposition could secure a majority with Arab parties, while Eisenkot, Naftali Bennett, and Avigdor Liberman have opposed bringing Arab parties into a governing coalition.The four opposition parties had agreed to coordinate their election efforts ahead of the vote, although questions remained over the composition of a future government and the selection of its leader.An earlier Israel Democracy Institute survey, published before the election, found that Eisenkot was the most broadly acceptable candidate for prime minister among both Jewish and Arab respondents. That survey also examined public preferences for new elections and alternative government arrangements in the event of a political deadlock.

title: Shin Bet probes foreign election interference, warns against blaming Arab voters
body: The Shin Bet (Israel Security Agency) said Thursday its investigation into suspected foreign interference in Israel's election was based on intelligence it collected itself and not information supplied by a political party.The inquiry should not be a reason to cast suspicion on all Arab voters, it added.Its statement followed a day of competing allegations over Tuesday's election, after Central Elections Committee chairman Justice Noam Sohlberg's instruction to investigate suspected foreign funding and election bribery became public.Money from abroad, perhaps from Qatar and Turkey, allegedly was used to influence voting in Arab communities, Israeli media outlets reported.Likud cited the allegations to argue that Arab parties had “stolen” the election, and other parties must not rely on their votes to form a government or replace the Knesset speaker.Arab party leaders denied wrongdoing, while opposition figures accused Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu of using an unfinished investigation to undermine the legitimacy of the results.The dispute has extended beyond suspected offenses to the role of Arab parties in the next Knesset. The Shin Bet's statement did not announce findings establishing foreign interference, and overturning election results would require a separate court proceeding.The Shin Bet said its investigation remained unfinished, and statements about the substance or nature of the suspicions did not represent its position. The inquiry was focused and limited, it said, adding that it should not be used to discredit a community that voted democratically and lawfully.The Central Elections Committee also rejected claims of systematic election misconduct. In a response issued with Sohlberg's approval, acting Director-General Dean Livne said the election had been conducted lawfully, and as far as the committee knew, allegations of systematic harm to election integrity were unfounded.The inquiry would not delay publication of the final results or prevent President Isaac Herzog from selecting a party leader to begin the coalition-building process, a committee source told The Jerusalem Post.Asked whether the investigation could lead to another election, the source said it was “far too early for such a question.”“First, we need to examine whether there was any impact and whether it affects the distribution of Knesset seats at all,” he said.In a letter dated Wednesday and made public on Thursday, Sohlberg instructed Shin Bet Director David Zini to investigate suspected foreign funding and election bribery.He described serious suspicions but expressly said he could not assess their merits. He directed Zini to obtain evidence to substantiate or refute them and requested any available findings during the coming week, citing the timetable for election appeals.The sequence is important: The Shin Bet was in possession of intelligence before Tuesday's vote; Sohlberg's written directive and Zini's meeting with Netanyahu followed on Wednesday; and the inquiry became public on Thursday. The precise date the investigation began, and when Sohlberg first received the information, remain unclear.Neither Sohlberg's letter nor the Shin Bet's subsequent statement identified countries, political parties, or funding routes. Encouraging voter participation is not, by itself, evidence of election bribery.The Shin Bet said no one outside the agency, apart from Sohlberg, had been exposed to the intelligence before the election ended. On Election Day, Zini publicly described voting as secure and properly supervised.The Shin Bet said Zini had personally briefed Netanyahu, Yashar chairman Gadi Eisenkot, and opposition leader Yair Lapid during the preceding 24 hours at Sohlberg's request and with his approval. Zini initiated the Wednesday evening meeting with Netanyahu.Meanwhile, four more suspects had been arrested on suspicion of election bribery and were being questioned by Lahav 433 – The National Crime Unit, the Israel Police said Thursday.Three residents of the South were arrested Tuesday morning, and the case was later transferred to Lahav 433.The police reported finding cash and Ra'am voting slips during searches. That case remains separate from the election-fraud investigation.Police dismiss Likud claimsThere had been relatively few election-integrity incidents of Election Day, and there was no investigative or intelligence support for Likud's broader allegations of a stolen election, the police said Thursday.On Wednesday, Likud said Arab parties had stolen the election through bribery, intimidation, fraud, and other offenses, adding that it was submitting hundreds of testimonies and pieces of evidence to the authorities. The party intends to seek the invalidation of results at polling stations where it suspects irregularities, a Likud lawyer told the Post.Ra'am chairman Mansour Abbas welcomed Sohlberg's instruction to investigate, denied that Ra'am had any connection to the affair or other cases, and pledged full cooperation with law enforcement. He accused Netanyahu of inciting against Arab citizens and seeking to delegitimize them.Qatari Foreign Ministry spokesperson Majed Al Ansari said Qatar had not interfered in the election or funded activities intended to influence its outcome. He accused Israeli politicians and their media contacts of drawing Qatar into domestic political disputes through disinformation.Turkey also denied interfering in the election, and the presidency's Center for Combating Disinformation said the allegations were baseless.The Joint List accused Netanyahu of trying to steal the election and described the allegations as a campaign to undermine the legitimacy of Arab votes. It urged opposition leaders to reject the accusations and act on the election results.Eisenkot, speaking after meeting Zini and Sohlberg, said it was too early to understand what had happened, “or whether anything happened at all,” and called for an investigation free of political interference.He accused Netanyahu and Likud of an organized campaign to delegitimize the results and vowed to oppose any departure from the scheduled Knesset swearing-in.Eisenkot said his teams were preparing bills on conscription and service, a state commission of inquiry into the October 7 massacre, and budget allocations, which he intended to bring to a vote when the Knesset convenes.The Democrats chairman Yair Golan called for genuine suspicions to be investigated. He accused Netanyahu of trying to delegitimize the electorate's decision, particularly Arab voters.The Democrats MK Naama Lazimi compared Likud's campaign to the January 6 storming of the US Capitol.Section 86Knesset Elections Law Section 86 provides a court procedure for challenging election results. No automatic cancellation is triggered by suspicions or unlawful funding. Challenges may concern elections conducted unlawfully, incorrect allocation of votes or seats, or votes obtained illegally. A central requirement is that the alleged irregularity could have affected the results.Eligible challengers include participating candidate lists and their candidates, MKs, factions of the newly elected Knesset, Central and Regional Election Committee members, and the attorney-general.An appeal must be filed with the Jerusalem District Court, sitting as an administrative court, within 14 days of publication of the results. A three-judge panel hears the case, and the deadline may be extended in special circumstances.The court can order a new election nationwide or at a particular polling station, correct the allocation of votes, or determine that one candidate was elected instead of another.A further appeal on a legal question generally requires permission from the Supreme Court president. If the election is annulled nationwide, those eligible to challenge the results can appeal before five Supreme Court judges or a larger odd-numbered panel.An election appeal does not suspend the Knesset's work or invalidate decisions it has already taken.Amichai Stein and Yonah Jeremy Bob contributed to this report.

title: Lagos govt threatens to seal illegal boreholes, prosecute operators
body:
The Lagos State Government has warned borehole operators to obtain the necessary permits or risk having their facilities sealed and facing prosecution.
The Lagos State Water Regulatory Commission ( LASWARCO ) said drilling boreholes and extracting groundwater without authorisation could contaminate underground water, cause land subsidence and threaten the state’s water resources.
The warning comes amid concerns over groundwater pollution in Lekki.
In August 2025, the Permanent Secretary, Office of Drainage Services and Water Resources, Mahmood Adegbite, warned that residents in the area could be consuming contaminated water because of inadequate wastewater treatment.
Mr Adegbite, who spoke at a stakeholders’ meeting, called for proper wastewater treatment to prevent further contamination and reduce the risk of waterborne diseases, according to Radio Nigeria Lagos.
Lagos began regulating borehole drilling and groundwater extraction in 2022 to curb pollution and manage its underground water resources.
The then Executive Secretary of LASWARCO, Funke Adepoju, stated that the regulation covered groundwater abstraction, consumption, supply and distribution.
In its latest statement posted on Facebook on Thursday, LASWARCO noted that the Lagos State Environmental Management and Protection Law, 2017, empowered it to regulate borehole drilling, groundwater extraction and water supply services.
The commission’s Executive Secretary, Oluwabukola Adeyemo, said anyone intending to drill a borehole or extract groundwater must first obtain the required permits.
“Drilling or abstracting groundwater without LASWARCO authorisation is illegal and punishable under the Law,” Ms Adeyemo said.
She stated that the commission would seal facilities operating without the required authorisation and prosecute offenders.
Ms Adeyemo urged residents and community leaders to report illegal borehole drilling and unauthorised groundwater extraction.
Complaints can be made through LASWARCO’s hotline on 0816 878 2223 or at Block 19, third floor, Lagos State Secretariat, Alausa, Ikeja.

title: There is no other Stella for Ebola, By Azu Ishiekwene
body:
The most expensive thing in Nigeria is not petrol, not food or medicines, not even cement. It is memory loss – an epidemic that has obviously been escalated by screen addiction from its initial default mode of poor record-keeping and absence of institutional diligence.
Nigeria has met Ebola again. Not with the terror of 2014 – which has all but been forgotten – when a Liberian-American named Patrick Sawyer walked into Lagos carrying a virus and a stubborn disregard for other people’s lives.
This time, it’s with a quieter, more bureaucratic alarm – an imported case in Abuja, not from the West but from the east coast of Africa. A 42-year-old woman reportedly arrived from Uganda, developed symptoms four days later, sought care at a private hospital, and tested positive for the Bundibugyo (Ugandan) strain on 20 October.
The good news is that the patient has been evacuated, is in isolation and is receiving care. The bad news is that Nigerians have a special talent for treating preparedness like aso-ebi : impressive on D-day and impossible to find at the next occasion.
Twelve years ago, Ebola taught Nigeria a lesson written in the blood of health workers. It also gave us Dr. Ameyo Stella Adadevoh, the physician whose refusal to let a highly infectious patient leave helped stop an epidemic before it became a national catastrophe. She paid with her life. Nigeria does not need another such invoice.
The current case reads like a travel itinerary. According to the Nigeria Centre for Disease Control (NCDC), the patient returned to Abuja from Uganda through Addis Ababa on 3 October. She developed symptoms on 7 October, was admitted to a private health facility on 11 October, and the NCDC was notified on 19 October. Laboratory confirmation came on 20 October.
That timeline deserves attention. There were 17 days between the index case arriving in Abuja and confirmation, and 12 days between symptom onset and notification. In infectious-disease terms, that is not a gap. It is a corridor.
Ebola is not malaria. It does not announce itself with a neon sign. Early symptoms such as fever, fatigue, muscle pain, headache, and sore throat can masquerade as ordinary ailments that Nigerians treat with paracetamol, prayer, pepper soup, and the national motto: “It is well.”
By 25 October, the NCDC said 53 contacts had been identified and were being monitored. On 26 October, the patient and her husband were medically evacuated to Switzerland, where she is receiving specialised care.
On 20 July, 2014, Sawyer, a Liberian government official, flew from Monrovia to Lagos via Lomé. He was infected with the Zaire strain of Ebola, the deadliest of the species. He collapsed at the airport and was taken to First Consultants Medical Centre in Obalende, where Dr Adadevoh and some of her colleagues took the bullet that could have turned Lagos into an Ebola graveyard.
Sawyer, by several accounts, wanted to leave the hospital. He reportedly resisted isolation. In a country where “the customer is always right” has been elevated to a theology, Adadevoh did something – she disagreed with the customer.
She and her team kept him in the hospital, alerted the authorities, and began the difficult work of containment. Sawyer died on 24 July, 2014. Adadevoh tested positive for the virus on 4 August, while caring for him and died on 19 August, 2014, aged 57.
Nigeria eventually recorded 20 Ebola cases and eight deaths in that outbreak. It was declared Ebola-free on 20 October, 2014, barely three months after Sawyer’s arrival. The world called it a success. Nigerians called it a miracle. Both descriptions were true, but neither should obscure the cost: eight people died, including heroic health workers, because one man’s illness met one doctor’s courage.
There is a temptation to reduce Adadevoh’s story to inspiration. Nigerians love inspiration; it is cheaper than infrastructure.
But inspiration is not a substitute for systems. Adadevoh’s heroism was effective because it was eventually supported by contact tracing, laboratory capacity, isolation, communication, and coordination.
The Ebola Emergency Operations Centre, established during that response, became a model praised internationally. It showed that Nigeria could organise when it chose to. Nigeria showed that capacity again with COVID-19 when even first-world countries were confounded.
That is where forgetfulness meets tragedy. Nigeria does not lack competence. It lacks consistency. We can mobilise brilliantly for a crisis, then dismantle the machinery once the cameras leave. We build emergency operations centres with the urgency of a man whose house is on fire, only to let them gather dust until the next fire.
The 2026 case is a test of institutional memory. Do we still have the laboratories, the trained personnel, the isolation capacity, the surveillance network, the community trust and the political will that carried us through 2014 and COVID-19?
The fact that the NCDC was notified on 19 October, eight days after admission, suggests the system eventually worked. Every day of delay expands the contact list, deepens anxiety and increases the burden on already stretched health workers.
In 2014, Nigerians received text messages recommending bathing with salt water at dawn. Grown men and women, including some who could operate complex businesses and quote economic statistics, obediently scrubbed themselves with salt. It did not kill Ebola. It did, however, reportedly cause injuries and deaths from excessive salt consumption.
The lesson was simple: panic is also a public-health hazard. Fear makes people hide symptoms, avoid hospitals, blame outsiders and embrace dangerous remedies.
If Dr Adadevoh could speak today, she would probably not ask for statues. She would ask practical questions: Where are the isolation beds, gloves, gowns, face shields? Are oxygen supplies available, not “available on request,” which in Nigerian English means unavailable? Are health workers trained and insured? Is there a functioning referral system from private clinics to public isolation centres? Are contact tracers properly equipped? Is there a single, credible source of information rather than twelve competing WhatsApp broadcasts?
Nigeria’s political class loves emergencies. An emergency provides photo-ops, special committees, presidential directives and the dizzying grammar of “stakeholders.” One more thing: emergencies are also pipelines for big money, and cash out. Prevention, by contrast, is boring. It involves maintenance, training, data, procurement and accountability.
Perhaps it is instructive that Ebola has visited Nigeria in campaign season, when politicians remember that power resides with voters and move from town to city to village telling deadly lies like the Ebola virus. It will be easier to trace political lies in this season, when politicians are at their mobile best, than to trace a virus.
But the truest memorial to Adadevoh is not a plaque. It is a health system in which no doctor has to choose between personal safety and public duty. It is a country where a suspected case is reported within hours, not days. It is an isolation centre that works before the emergency, not one hastily converted from a conference hall after the first alarm.
Adadevoh stepped on a virus on our behalf. Twelve years later, Ebola has returned with a different strain, a different city and a different patient. The virus has changed its address. The question is whether Nigeria has changed its habits.
Azu Ishiekwene is Editor-In-Chief of LEADERSHIP and author of the book, Writing for Media and Monetising It .

title: GoDaddy expects to hit high end of full-year revenue guidance
body:

title: Umrah: Tinubu Arrives In Saudi Arabia
body: President Bola Tinubu has arrived in the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia. The President landed at the King Abdulaziz International Airport, Jeddah, on Thursday night. He was received by the Nigerian ambassador to the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, Yakubu Gambo, and Saudi’s head of Royal Protocol, Ahmad bin Thafir. Tinubu is in the country to perform Umrah, an Islamic spiritual exercise involving a pilgrimage to the Holy City. He departed Abuja for Makkah on Thursday afternoon. The event is an opportunity for spiritual reflection, devotion, and prayers for the nation’s peace, unity, stability, and continued progress, Tinubu’s media aide, Bayo Onanuga, said in a statement on Wednesday. According to the statement, the President will perform the religious rites associated with Umrah, seeking Allah’s guidance and blessings for Nigeria and its people. He is expected back in the country next week. The post Umrah: Tinubu Arrives In Saudi Arabia appeared first on Channels Television .

title: Putin outlines root causes of Ukraine conflict to Stubb, Store — presidential aide
body:
MOSCOW, October 29. /TASS/. Russian President Vladimir Putin outlined the root causes of the Ukraine conflict during Tuesday’s phone call with Finnish President Alexander Stubb and Norwegian Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Store, Russian Presidential Aide Yury Ushakov said in comments to Channel One.
"Our president outlined the root causes of the conflict at the request of those on the other end of the phone. That is how the conversation began," Ushakov said.
"Absolutely," the presidential aide replied when asked whether the root causes dated back to 2014.
Ushakov also refuted a report by the Financial Times (FT), claiming that Putin had allegedly devoted a significant part of the conversation to medieval Slavic history.
"Of course not. Were British representatives there, or what? How would they know? That’s complete nonsense," the Russian presidential aide said.

title: Uncrewed AEW capability flight-tested on MQ-9B
body:
EL MIRAGE, California. Saab and General Atomics Aeronautical Systems (GA-ASI) completed a flight test integrating Saab’s LoyalEye airborne early warning (AEW) radar with the MQ-9B remotely piloted aircraft, the companies announced in a statement.
Conducted at GA-ASI’s Desert Horizon Flight Operations Facility in Southern California, the test evaluated the integrated system’s ability to detect, track, and classify airborne targets from an uncrewed platform. The companies say stakeholders observed the capability in real time during a representative operational scenario.
The test is part of an evaluation program that began with the system’s first flight in May 2026. Saab says LoyalEye on MQ-9B is intended to operate either independently or alongside crewed airborne early warning and control platforms, providing persistent surveillance where endurance, geographic reach, and reduced aircrew exposure are priorities.

title: Putin Says Nordic Leaders Were Right to Call Him, Despite EU Criticism
body:
Russian President Vladimir Putin defended Finnish President Alexander Stubb and Norwegian Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Støre over their Oct. 27 telephone call with him, saying they were right to reach out despite criticism from other European leaders.
Speaking at a press conference after the Russia-Africa summit on Thursday, Oct. 29, Putin confirmed that the conversation took place at the initiative of the Nordic leaders and covered a wide range of issues.
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official .
“I know that criticism was later directed at them, but it is not for us to judge whether this [the call] is right or wrong. I believe it is right,” Putin said, according to Interfax-Ru .
“After all, there are people in Europe who do not want to inflict a strategic defeat on Russia, as some do, but want to establish some kind of constructive dialogue,” he added.
The remarks came on the same day that the Kremlin ruled out European participation in the next month’s Abu Dhabi negotiations with Ukraine and the US.
Moscow, according to the Russian president, backs any effort to rebuild relations with Europe, whether with the EU as a bloc or individual countries.
Russia has always supported steps toward restoring “full-format and full-fledged relations” with European states, he added.
However, during the same remarks, Putin warned that a war between Russia and Europe would have “no winners,” claiming that the West had failed in its goal of inflicting a strategic defeat on Russia and was unlikely to achieve it by 2030, Russian-state owned media TASS reported.
The warning comes as European governments step up preparations for a possible confrontation.
Germany’s elite KSK special forces began training for a role in conventional warfare with Russia, shifting away from its traditional focus on hostage rescue and counterterrorism, Brig. Gen. Andreas Kuhne told Germany’s BILD earlier this week.
European countries are also facing a rise in hybrid warfare threats, including sabotage, espionage, cyberattacks and frequent drone incursions into their airspace.
While some European leaders have described the situation as already amounting to a war, as the line between hybrid tactics and direct conflict continues to blur, others have been more cautious, refraining from such labels to avoid escalating tensions with Moscow.
The abrupt discussion drew a mixed response from Ukraine’s European allies, particularly from other Nordic countries, who said the call was not coordinated with them in advance.
Danish Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen said she was “very sceptical about this independent initiative by Norway and Finland,” Euronews reported, adding that Russia’s ongoing escalation against Ukraine remains evidence that “Moscow is not serious about diplomacy.”
“We have previously emphasised, with clear backing from the rest of Europe, that when others have gone solo and, for example, travelled to Moscow, it is crucial that we, Europeans, stand together,” she continued, in a reference to former Hungary Prime Minister Viktor Orbán who flew to Russia to meet with Putin at the time of his tenure.
Swedish Prime Minister Ulf Kristersson reiterated that she also has “pretty low expectations for this kind of [direct] talk.”
Støre defended the call by saying Europe needs to speak with Russia, instead of only relying on messages mediated by the US administration, which has a different take on the war.
The content of the call had also become a point of dispute.
On Wednesday, Oct. 28, the Financial Times reported that Putin spent much of their 90-minute conversation discussing medieval history , while an immediate ceasefire was barely raised.
Støre rejected the FT’s report, asking the newspaper to correct it. “That he gave a lecture on Slavic history is simply not correct,” he said, adding that the time was distributed relatively evenly between the participants. The newspaper has refused to issue a correction.
The call came after a week of diplomacy involving the two Nordic leaders.
On Oct. 20, they hosted a meeting between President Volodymyr Zelensky and senior US envoy Steve Witkoff for talks in Oslo , with US President Donald Trump’s son-in-law, Jared Kushner, joining remotely.
Witkoff then traveled to St. Petersburg for a direct meeting with Putin on Oct. 21, where he urged Putin to consider resuming trilateral talks with Ukraine and the US, bringing documents outlining approaches to ending the war.
The Kremlin reiterated that a just and lasting peace in Ukraine was possible only if Russia’s interests were taken into account.

title: Responsible mining must be the standard, not the exception – Dr Zanetor Rawlings
body: The Minister for Environment, Science and Technology, Dr Zanetor Agyeman-Rawlings, has called for responsible mining practices to become the standard in Ghana, stressing that mineral extraction must not come at the expense of the environment. She made the call after visiting Zijin Mining’s operations at New Abirem in the Eastern Region as part of a field tour to assess the environmental impact of mining activities. Dr Agyeman-Rawlings said the visit presented a contrast to the environmental destruction she witnessed at illegal mining sites in Osino, demonstrating that mining could be conducted responsibly with deliberate measures to minimise damage and restore degraded areas. During the visit, she said, officials of the mining company took her through their environmental management practices, including land reclamation, the rehabilitation of mined-out areas and tree planting initiatives aimed at protecting and restoring the environment. The Minister acknowledged the importance of Ghana’s mineral resources to economic development but cautioned against extraction practices that threaten water bodies, farmlands and ecosystems. She stressed that protecting the environment was essential to safeguarding the wellbeing of future generations. “Our mineral resources are important to Ghana’s economic development, but their extraction must never come at the expense of our water bodies, farmlands, ecosystems and the wellbeing of future generations,” she said. Dr Agyeman-Rawlings insisted that responsible mining should not be treated as an exception but adopted as the standard across the sector. “Responsible mining must not be the exception. It must be the standard,” she added.

title: Troops neutralise two high-profile ISWAP leaders, others in Borno
body: By Ndahi Marama, Maiduguri The troops of Joint Task Force (North East), Operation HADIN KAI (OPHK), have killed 15 Boko Haram terrorists, including two (2) prominent ISWAP Qayids, Abu Musanna and Hassan Abu Huraira in Kerenoa, Marte Local Government Area of Borno State. This is as the Theatre Commander of OPHK, Major General Ibikunle Ajose on Thursday commissioned the newly constructed three blocks of 12-family Corporals and Below Quarters (CBQ) at Maimalari Cantonment, Maiduguri. The commissioning forms part of activities to commemorate the Chief of Army Staff (COAS), Lieutenant General Waidi Shaibu’s one year in office, which also reflects his commitment to improving troops’ living conditions, strengthening morale and enhancing operational effectiveness. In a press statement signed by the Media Information Officer, Headquarters Joint Task Force North East Operation HADIN KAI, Captain Mohammed Goni on Thursday said: “Troops of OPHK continued to record operational successes through sustained intelligence-led offensive operations aimed at degrading terrorist capabilities and dismantling their networks across the theatre. “In a further operation, OPHK air assets, at about 9:20 pm on 28 October 2026, conducted an armed reconnaissance and air interdiction mission in the Kerenoa Marte Local Government Area of Borno State, resulting in the neutralisation of 15 terrorists and the destruction of an IED hideout. “The mission followed intelligence reports on terrorist activities in the area. During the operation, the air assets tracked two terrorists on a motorcycle to a makeshift structure beneath a tree. Further surveillance revealed additional movements around the location, indicating the presence of other terrorists. Consequently, the location was engaged with precision strikes. “Following the strikes, Battle Damage Assessment (BDA) indicated that 15 terrorists were neutralised, while structures at the location were destroyed. Additionally, a secondary fire observed after the engagement suggested that the targeted structure may have been used for the storage of terrorist IED logistics hub. “It has been confirmed that 2 prominent ISWAP Qayids, Abu Musanna and Hassan Abu Huraira were amongst those neutralised while several other fighters were severely wounded, including the Wali (ISWAP Governor) of the area who is reported to be critically injured. “The operation forms part of OPHK’s sustained intelligence-led air offensive aimed at degrading terrorist capabilities, disrupting their hideouts and dismantling logistics networks across the theatre. The Joint Task Force continues to conduct coordinated operations against terrorist elements in the North East to achieve its Operational mandate of restoring total and long-lasting peace in the region,” Goni stated. Meanwhile, the Nigerian Army has reaffirmed its commitment to personnel welfare with the commissioning of three blocks of 12-family Corporals and Below Quarters (CBQ) at Maimalari Cantonment, Maiduguri. The commissioning reflects the commitment of the Chief of Army Staff (COAS), Lieutenant General Waidi Shaibu NAM, to improving troops’ living conditions, strengthening morale and enhancing operational effectiveness. The commissioning forms part of activities to commemorate the COAS one year in office. The COAS was represented at the ceremony by the Theatre Commander, Joint Task Force (North East) Operation HADIN KAI (OPHK), Major General Ibikunle Ajose, on Thursday, 29 October 2026, at Maimalari Cantonment, Maiduguri. Delivering the COAS’ remarks, Major General Ajose stated that decent accommodation and a conducive living environment were essential to sustaining troops’ morale, discipline and effectiveness. He emphasised that operational excellence on the battlefield must be supported by adequate welfare provisions and a strong administrative foundation at home. He described investments in accommodation as investments in human capital and a practical demonstration of the Nigerian Army’s appreciation of personnel’s sacrifices and contributions to national security. The COAS expressed profound appreciation to the President and Commander-in-Chief of the Armed Forces of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, His Excellency Bola Ahmed Tinubu, GCFR, for his continued support to the Nigerian Army, particularly in force development and personnel welfare. He also acknowledged the contributions of relevant departments and directorates, contractors, project supervisors and other stakeholders whose efforts supported the execution of the projects, noting that sustained institutional support remains vital to the Army’s transformation and operational effectiveness. The COAS charged beneficiary personnel and their commanders to maintain a strong culture of discipline, accountability and proper maintenance to preserve the facilities for long-term use. The commissioning reinforces the Nigerian Army’s Soldiers First Concept, which places the welfare, wellbeing and professional development of personnel at the centre of its institutional priorities and recognises their importance to sustained morale, operational readiness and effective service to the nation. Beyond the quarters commissioned, several other projects are ongoing at Maimalari Cantonment to improve living and working conditions. These include additional Corporals and Below Quarters, the drilling of two boreholes, construction of a 50-bed ward for 7 Division Medical Services and Hospital, a new Headquarters 7 Division complex, Senior Officers’ Quarters and the renovation of existing family accommodation. These interventions reflect broader efforts to strengthen military infrastructure and provide personnel and their families with improved housing, healthcare and essential facilities. In his welcome address, the Acting General Officer Commanding 7 Division and Commander Sector 1 OPHK, Brigadier General Solomon Diwa, described the commissioning as another significant milestone in the Army’s welfare initiatives. He noted that Corporals and Below constitute a vital component of the Army’s fighting strength and perform indispensable roles at the tactical level. He stressed that providing them with decent accommodation demonstrates the Army’s recognition of their service and sacrifices while reinforcing the connection between personnel welfare, high morale and combat readiness. Similarly, the Acting GOC urged occupants to uphold high standards of cleanliness, take ownership of the quarters and ensure their responsible use. In his project description, the Commander, 47 Engineer Brigade, Brigadier General Abubakar Saleh, disclosed that the renovation was awarded to Messrs Ammah Contractors Limited by the Office of the Chief of Army Staff, Directorate of Procurement. He explained that following a site assessment, six blocks of six-family Corporals and Below Quarters, comprising 36 two-bedroom flats, were selected for renovation as suitable alternatives to the originally designated structures. He noted that the buildings were previously in a severely dilapidated condition, with leaking roofs, structural cracks and damaged floors. The renovation involved extensive structural rehabilitation, including the introduction of columns and beams, repairs to damaged floor slabs and masonry, replacement of roofing sheets, doors and windows, and complete electrical and plumbing installations. He added that 47 Engineer Brigade supervised the project under the guidance of Headquarters 7 Division to ensure compliance with approved specifications and quality standards. While delivering the vote of thanks on behalf of the beneficiaries, Warrant Officer Ogunmodede Sunday expressed his sincere appreciation to the Chief of Army Staff, Lieutenant General Waidi Shaibu, NAM, for prioritising personnel welfare through the Soldiers First Concept. He also thanked the Theatre Commander for his leadership and for representing the COAS at the occasion. He noted that the renovated quarters and other ongoing infrastructure projects demonstrate the Nigerian Army’s commitment to improving personnel welfare and living conditions. He pledged that the beneficiaries would maintain the facilities responsibly and reciprocate the gesture through discipline, professionalism and dedication to duty. He concluded by appreciating the project supervisors, contractors and everyone who contributed to the success of the project, while praying for God’s continued protection of troops, blessings upon their families and lasting peace and security for Nigeria.
