title: Patrick Stewart, a perceptive patriarch in 'Star Trek' and 'X-Men,' dies at 86
body:
Patrick Stewart was trained as a Shakespearean actor, and he brought that gravitas to all his roles, along with a playful sense of purpose. He was knighted in 2010. Jack Taylor/Getty Images hide caption
Patrick Stewart was trained as a Shakespearean actor, and he brought that gravitas to all his roles, along with a playful sense of purpose. He was knighted in 2010.
Sir Patrick Stewart's most famous characters tackled concepts such as honor, morality and courage. He played Professor X in the X-Men franchise and Jean-Luc Picard, captain of the starship USS Enterprise, on the show St ar Trek: The Next Generation and its later spinoff, Picard .
Stewart died Wednesday at 86. A post on his Facebook and Instagram pages said he died at home in Los Angeles after a "brief and poignant journey with Alzheimer's Disease and Lewy Body Dementia."
Although he was beloved for playing compassionate father figures who united families of misfits, Stewart's own upbringing in Yorkshire, England, was harsh. He remembered his father as alcoholic and abusive. He found solace in school and, eventually, in Shakespeare. He joined the Royal Shakespeare Company in 1966 and debuted on Broadway in 1970 in A Midsummer Night's Dream .
"To stand in the middle of an empty stage in an empty theater and feel that I was at home was everything," he told NPR in 2023 . "But it took a while for me to get there."
Patrick Stewart in 1970, during rehearsals for the Royal Shakespeare Company's production of The Two Gentlemen of Verona . Evening Standard/Hulton Archive/Getty Images hide caption
Stewart played alongside some of the best Shakespeareans of his time, including Judi Dench and Ian McKellen. He was lecturing on Shakespeare at UCLA when his name came up for the lead in a new series of Star Trek .
"Don't do this, Patrick," he remembered McKellen advising him. "You're a very good stage actor. That's where you ought to be. Don't do it."
But Stewart's agent had reassured him that the show was unlikely to make it past the first season. As the actor recalled to NPR, he was encouraged to take what he believed to be a quick and easy job. "'Do six months' work. Make some money for the first time in your life and get well known. Get a suntan, and go home.' And I thought, 'Yeah, that doesn't sound too bad. I could live with that.'"
But Star Trek: The Next Generation was a tremendous hit. It aired for seven seasons, from 1987 to 1994. Stewart was embraced by fans, who adored the character's penchant for Earl Grey tea and cool-headed leadership, with such signature phrases as "Engage!" and "Make it so!"
But success on the starship Enterprise came at a cost. Throughout his career, Stewart portrayed only a handful of Shakespeare's leading men. He put some of that character energy into an award-winning, one-man version of Charles Dickens' A Christmas Carol , in which Stewart played more than 40 roles.
By the beginning of the 21st century, Stewart had reestablished himself on stage while also lending his voice to numerous big-budget animated films. He went on to dominate another blockbuster franchise, the X-Men, beginning in 2000. He'll appear for the last time in his role as Professor Charles Xavier in the upcoming movie Avengers: Doomsday .
As for his signature role, Stewart thought he was done playing Picard. But a team of producers — including writer Michael Chabon — had different ideas. They pitched him a new show, Star Trek: Picard , that began streaming on the CBS service now called Paramount+ in 2020.
"I would've been happy just shaking Patrick Stewart's hand and telling him how much I loved him on Star Trek ," Chabon told NPR . "But to be able to actually write words that he will speak and act is — it's incredible."
In the show, Picard is struggling with the psychological damage that led to leaving Starfleet. The performance is vintage Stewart. His character is keen-eyed, haunted, weary, yet joyful. While this Picard was trapped in the past, Patrick Stewart spent his career charting the future.
This story has been updated to remove a photo of Patrick Stewart in character as Jean-Luc Picard that had been reversed by the agency that provided it.
NPR does not offer or accept money for coverage or interviews. Anyone who makes such an offer or request is not an NPR employee and does not represent NPR.

title: Patrick Stewart, ‘Star Trek: The Next Generation’ actor, dead at 86
body:
Sir Patrick Stewart , known for his role of Captain Jean-Luc Picard in Star Trek: The Next Generation , died at his home in Los Angeles on Wednesday, according to a statement shared on his social media .
“We announce with great sorrow the passing of Sir Patrick Stewart yesterday at his home in Los Angeles, in the loving care of his beloved wife Sunny, following a brief and poignant journey with Alzheimer’s Disease and Lewy Body Dementia,” a statement posted to Stewart’s social media said.
“He has been held in the warm embrace of family and friends, surrounded by live music, prayer, tears, laughter, and the kind of profound emotion that only he could inspire after a lifetime of devotion to us all,” the statement added.
“We will forever cherish the peaceful ease and reflection on his face, an enduring reminder of his invincible grace,” the statement continued. “A son of Mirfield in the West Riding of Yorkshire, he travelled from the Royal Shakespeare Company to an equally acclaimed career spanning six decades on Broadway, the silver screen and television.”
The statement said that Stewart “explored the human condition in all its poetic complexity and brought hope not only to the far reaches of the Marvel Cinematic Universe, but into science fiction’s most iconic final frontier aboard the Starship Enterprise.”
“He will be remembered for the dignity, compassion and humanity he brought to every role — in his art and life,” the statement concluded.
The post also included a quote from Stewart’s 2023 book, Making It So: A Memoir .
“Like me, Jean-Luc has lived an unusual life that has taken him far beyond the bounds of normal human experience. But he is also someone who has remained true to his earthbound roots, for they are what gave him his identity. In the end, he feels the call of home, as do I,” Stewart said.
In lieu of flowers, Stewart’s family has asked for contributions to be may to the Johns Hopkins Alzheimer’s Disease Research Center Fund and Alzheimer’s Foundation of America Caregiver Resources.
In lieu of flowers, memorial contributions may be made to: Johns Hopkins Alzheimer’s Disease Research Center Fund https://t.co/luC5CdcWDy
Alzheimer’s Foundation of America Caregiver Resources https://t.co/zvNptfyuNd
Photo Credit: Tommy Garcia pic.twitter.com/km8zhYu5fs
— Patrick Stewart (@SirPatStew) October 29, 2026
While best known as Professor Charles Xavier and Captain Jean-Luc Picard from the X-Men and Star Trek: The Next Generation series and films, Stewart spent more of his career onstage than in the X-Mansion or on the USS Enterprise.
Besides playing everyone from Claudius to Macbeth, he often performed a one-man rendition of A Christmas Carol and did West End and Broadway runs of Harold Pinter’s No Man’s Land and Samuel Beckett’s Waiting for Godot in repertoire with Ian McKellen.
Stewart was first introduced as the character Xavier in the original X-Men trilogy, and appeared in several films including X-Men , X-Men 2 , X-Men: The Last Stand , X-Men Origins: Wolverine , The Wolverine and X-Men: Days of Future Past before Professor X’s death in 2017’s Logan . He reappeared in Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness in 2022.
Stewart first stepped onto the USS Enterprise in 1987 for Star Trek: The Next Generation , playing Picard throughout 1987-1994. After the series, he went on to appear in the films Star Trek: Generations with William Shatner, Star Trek: First Contact , Star Trek: Insurrection and Star Trek: Nemesis .
He also showed off his comedic chops aboard Seth MacFarlane’s Starz show Blunt Talk for two series and voiced Poop in The Emoji Movie . He made appearances on Robot Chicken , Futurama and The Simpsons.
Alzheimer’s disease is a chronic neurodegenerative disease that destroys brain cells, causing thinking ability and memory to decline over time, according to the Alzheimer Society of Canada .
Alzheimer’s disease is the most common type of dementia, accounting for 60 to 80 per cent of all cases of dementia, and it is irreversible.
According to the Alzheimer Society of Canada, by the year 2050 more than 1.7 million Canadians are expected to be living with dementia, with an average of 685 individuals being diagnosed each day.
Dementia with Lewy bodies (DLB) is a type of progressive dementia that leads to a decline in thinking, reasoning and independent function, according to the Alzheimer’s Association .
Symptoms may include spontaneous changes in attention and alertness, recurrent visual hallucinations, REM sleep behaviour disorder, and slow movement, tremors or rigidity, the organization notes.
Stewart is survived by his wife Sunny Ozell, and his two children, Sophia and Daniel.

title: Canada faces ‘critical gaps’ on military combat ammunition: AG warns
body:
It will take several years to bring the Canadian military’s stockpile of ammunition up to where it should be, according to a new report from the auditor general.
With the current gaps, the financial watchdog said Canada is far behind on its commitments made to its NATO allies for collective defence.
In the report, released Thursday, Canada’s Auditor General Karen Hogan said a flawed inventory management system, dysfunctional data analysis and contracts plagued with inefficiencies has resulted in the Department of National Defence (DND) not knowing how much ammunition it has or needs, or how to get more.
“These findings are like the importance of sound planning and acting on known problems before an emergency occurs,” she told reporters Thursday. “Responding to immediate needs is important, but so is being prepared for future challenges.”
“It’s time for National Defence to get all these administrative matters ironed out so that they can make the best use of the funding that they have.”
The auditor general’s office first started sounding the alarm on the inefficiencies two decades ago. In 2024, the government dedicated $9.2 billion over 13 years to support strategic stockpile replenishment.
But Hogan said the current pace at which contracts are being awarded is not sufficient to meet demands.
Public Services and Procurement Canada had four strategic source agreements with Canadian companies to produce ammunition through the Munitions Supply Program, according to the audit. But two of those four agreements had expired over three years ago, Hogan said.
The report found there is a major discrepancy in the supply of munitions for training exercises and munitions to be used in combat.
Five Canadian Armed Forces (CAF) groups accounted for 87 per cent of the total regular-use ammunition assigned by quantity in the 2023-24 to 2025-26 fiscal years, the report said.
Within those groups, only 56 per cent of their assigned regular‑use ammunition was used in the same period.
Hogan said some of the excess inventory can be used in an emergency, but not all training ammunition is lethal.
The auditor general looked at 100 different types of stockpile admission and found it was lacking required types and quantities required to meet targeted operational requirements.
“For national security reasons, I can’t talk to you about the specifics of where there are critical gaps, but there are critical gaps in some of the ammunition,” Hogan said.
In response to the report, Defence Minister David McGuinty said he agrees with the auditor general’s six recommendations and is already acting upon them.
“We’re going to have to make sure we marry that production capacity with the storage, transportation and use of information,” he said. “There’s progress to be made and we intend to fully implement these recommendations.”

title: Alyoshki resident says drones constantly buzzing over town during summer
body:
SIMFEROPOL, October 29. /TASS/. There was a constant buzz of drones over the town of Alyoshki in the Kherson Region in the summertime, local resident Alexander Zakharov told TASS.
"Five minutes pass, and another one is flying. That constant buzzing - I now feel an automatic urge to hide when I hear a buzzing sound," he said, when asked about drone activity during the summer.
The Russian Armed Forces introduced a ceasefire in the Kherson direction at 4:00 a.m. Moscow time (1:00 a.m. GMT) on October 27 to prepare for a humanitarian operation in the town of Alyoshki. Earlier, Russia and Ukraine agreed to a ceasefire in Alyoshki, brokered by US First Lady Melania Trump, to facilitate humanitarian aid deliveries and the evacuation of civilians via a special safe corridor. On September 21, Russian Presidential Spokesman Dmitry Peskov described the situation in Alyoshki as critical, saying that food and medicine could not be delivered there amid ongoing Ukrainian shelling and drone attacks. Slightly over 1,000 residents currently remain in Alyoshki, down from a population of 20,000.

title: Zelensky: Russian strikes killed 19 people in Dnipro, Chernihiv, Kremenchuk
body:
The Ukrainian leader said this in his nightly video address , Ukrinform reports.
"Today, the Russians carried out extremely brutal strikes on Dnipro, Chernihiv, Kremenchuk. Against civilians – ordinary people. In these three cities alone, 19 people were killed in daytime attacks. My condolences to their families and loved ones. Dozens of people were injured. In Dnipro, a Russian 'Shahed' struck the train station. People were waiting for a train – the regular Dnipro-Zaporizhzhia route," he said.
Zelensky said Russian forces had struck the very center of Chernihiv, killing two 15-year-old girls, Yana and Mariia.
"In Kremenchuk, in the Poltava region, the Russians struck an area of the city right among ordinary residential buildings. In this strike alone, six children and 26 adults were injured. Three people were killed. By evening, there were more strikes on Dnipro," the president said.
He stressed that Russian strikes continued throughout the day in the Donetsk, Kharkiv, Chernihiv and Sumy regions.
"A blatant display of Russian brutality. They are doing this deliberately – when everyone is counting on steps toward de-escalation. Russia is showing its true attitude toward all of this," Zelensky said.
He recalled that on Thursday, the leaders of several countries and many public figures had expressed their condolences to Ukraine and the Ukrainian people.
"We are grateful to them. It is important that this not be limited to condolences. There must be fair treatment toward Ukraine and toward Russia. Ukraine needs support, and Russia must face pressure," he said.
Zelensky also recalled that the United Kingdom would provide Ukraine with an additional GBP 10 billion over the next three years.
"Yesterday, we had a strong decision from the United Kingdom – I would like to thank Prime Minister Burnham. Ukraine will receive an additional GBP 10 billion over the next three years. A very strong decision. We also discussed with the Prime Minister the need for new sanctions against Russia. There is also a decision by the Netherlands to support Ukraine – we agreed on this yesterday with Prime Minister Jetten. Thank you, Rob! It was a substantive meeting, and we count on further steps regarding air defense for Ukraine as well," Zelensky concluded.

title: Raptors defence clicking early in the season
body:
TORONTO – RJ Barrett knows that the Toronto Raptors have been the toughest team to score on early in the NBA season, but he’s a little scared to talk about it.
“Don’t jinx us, man,” Barrett said, shaking his head courtside at OVO Athletic Centre, when asked about Toronto’s defence.
The Raptors have limited their opponents to a league-low average of 102.5 points over the first four games of the season, including a 117-94 loss to the Minnesota Timberwolves last Sunday that skewed the number.
“We’ve been a good defence the past couple years, so just trying to build off of that,” said Barrett, alluding to Toronto having the fifth-best defensive rating by the end of the 2025-26 regular season. “Everybody that’s coming into the game is focused, focused on the game plans, and I think we’re doing well, but we can take it to another level.”
The Raptors (3-1) lead the league in steals, generating 14.3 per game, well ahead of the Los Angeles Clippers (12.5) and New Orleans Pelicans (12.3).
Head coach Darko Rajakovic said that generating turnovers is a result of good positioning and discipline.
“When we do our schemes the way we’re supposed to do, when you’re disciplined, it puts us in position to be effective with our hands and to create steals and to make the other team turn the ball over a lot,” Rajakovic said courtside at Toronto’s training facility.
“Any time when we are one step behind or not in the right spots, that leads us to gambling. Gambling is never good for us on the defensive end of the floor. The more discipline we have, the more we’re doing what we’re supposed to do.”
Barrett said that he likes the Raptors’ aggressive way of playing defence and getting turnovers for one simple reason.
“Easy buckets, man. Free buckets,” said Barrett. “The object of the game is to score more points than the other team, so if we could get some turnovers and get out in transition, get some easy buckets, that opens up the whole game for us.”
Toronto has set this high defensive standard despite missing two-time NBA Defensive Player of the Year Kawhi Leonard for half of their games. Leonard is out as he rehabilitates swelling in his left knee.
Media reports on Thursday said that Leonard will miss three to four weeks of the season, but Rajakovic said that the Raptors don’t have an exact timeline.
“Seven days from now, we’re going to review where he’s at and have a clearer plan,” said Rajakovic. “Right now, he’s going through the treatments.
“He’s reacting well to those treatments, and in seven days’ time, we’re gonna have a much better feel.”
The Raptors host the Orlando Magic (1-3) for the second game in a row on Friday. Toronto beat Orlando 129-99 on Wednesday, but Friday’s game will have higher stakes as it’s the first NBA Cup game for both teams.
Leonard, Nate Bittle (avulsion fracture in his right foot) and Malachi Smith (two-way contract) were all unavailable to play on Friday. The seven-foot Bittle was active during Raptors practice on Thursday, however.
“I think it’s seven to 10 days that he’s been out of the boot already,” said Rajakovic. “So (Bittle) is slowly ramping up. He’s reacting really well to those workouts.
“He’s pain-free, and now we are in the process of reconditioning him and getting him ready.”
This report by The Canadian Press was first published Oct. 29, 2026.

title: Just In: Tinubu lands in Saudi Arabia for Umrah
body: President Bola Tinubu on Thursday evening arrived in Saudi Arabia, landing at the King Abdulaziz International Airport in Jeddah. He was received by Nigeria’s ambassador to Saudi Arabia, Yakubu Gambo, and the Saudi head of royal protocol Ahmad bin Thafir. The President is scheduled to perform Umrah, also known as the lesser hajj, and is expected to return to Nigeria next week after completing the religious exercise. Thursday’s trip marks the second time Tinubu has travelled to Makkah to perform Umrah since assuming office on May 29, 2023. President Tinubu visited the holy city in November 2023, shortly after attending the Saudi-African Summit in Riyadh, where he also prayed for divine guidance in leading Nigeria. The latest trip is part of a series of foreign engagements undertaken by Tinubu since becoming president. He has visited more than 30 countries in over 50 unique and recurring trips. The post Just In: Tinubu lands in Saudi Arabia for Umrah appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: Britain sets out £298 billion defence spending plan as government forecasts nearly 60,000 new jobs and industrial growth
body: The employment estimate, published in the UK Defence Footprint 2026 report, covers spending announced in the Defence Investment Plan and measures growth by 2029–30 against 2023–24 levels. The £298 billion represents total planned defence expenditure over four years. The report links procurement for the armed forces with efforts to expand Britain’s industrial capacity and increase exports. It identifies Dreadnought submarines, the Future Combat Air System and directed energy weapons as programmes offering opportunities for overseas sales, commercial applications and dual-use technology. Domestic orders alone will not sustain industry The ministry acknowledges that British military demand cannot support the full industrial base the country needs. Export orders and international partnerships are therefore central to its plans for maintaining production capacity and skilled employment. “UK demand alone will not sustain the size and scale of defence industrial base we need for our national security,” the report states. It describes exports as supporting both Britain’s security relationships and the companies supplying its armed forces. MOD spending with UK-based industry reached £34.1 billion in 2025–26, up 3% from the previous year. Separate employment estimates show that its expenditure supported 274,000 industry jobs in 2024–25, an increase of 10%. The ministry placed more than 2,000 new contracts in 2025–26, including over 500 directly with small and medium-sized businesses. Direct expenditure with those companies totalled £1.3 billion during the year. Funding for factories, testing and training The government has allocated £250 million over five years to Defence Growth Deals in Scotland, Wales, Northern Ireland, South Yorkshire and Plymouth. The agreements support research, supply chains and training, alongside measures to make defence work more accessible to smaller businesses. Plymouth’s £50 million deal will expand support for surface and underwater drone development through waterfront laboratories and testing facilities. Investment in Wales will widen access to MOD test ranges and provide infrastructure allowing smaller suppliers to undertake classified work directly. A separate £182 million skills package over five years will support engineering and advanced manufacturing training. It includes five Defence Technical Excellence Colleges in England, one in Wales and up to two in Scotland. Under an agreement between government and industry, 40,000 young people a year are to be offered opportunities and employment in skilled defence careers by 2030, rising to 50,000 by 2035. The commitment covers employment, apprenticeships and training as the sector recruits the workforce needed to deliver Britain’s defence programmes.

title: US journalist on ground in Alyoshki in touch with Melania Trump about situation there
body:
SIMFEROPOL, October 29. /TASS/. American journalist John Chay, a member of the humanitarian mission to Alyoshki in the Kherson Region, said he is in contact with US First Lady Melania Trump regarding the situation in the town.
"We are also in contact with Melania Trump [regarding the humanitarian mission in Alyoshki]. We are communicating with her," the Newsmax representative told reporters upon arriving in Simferopol, Crimea, near the Kherson Region.
A humanitarian mission to support civilians is currently underway in the frontline town of Alyoshki in the Kherson Region. A temporary ceasefire on the Kherson front is in effect from 4:00 a.m. local time on October 27 (1:00 a.m. GMT) until 10:59 p.m. local time on November 1 (8:59 p.m. GMT). The main delivery of aid is scheduled for October 29-30. Voluntary evacuation will be arranged for anyone wishing to leave. Those who decide to stay will receive food, medicine and essential supplies.
Preparations for the mission began in May 2026 with the assistance of Russian Ombudswoman Yana Lantratova, Ukrainian Ombudsman Dmitry Lubinets and the mediation of US First Lady Melania Trump. Representatives of international media arrived in the town as part of the delegation.

title: ‘No retiree will be forgotten’ — Tinubu promises pension reforms
body:
President Bola Tinubu has pledged to implement a long-delayed minimum pension guarantee and expand healthcare support for retirees, saying his administration is determined to ensure that Nigerians who served the country are not abandoned after retirement.
Mr Tinubu made the commitment on Thursday at the National Pension Conference and Awards, held at Transcorp Hilton, Abuja, as part of the maiden National Pension Week 2026.
Represented by the Secretary to the Government of the Federation, George Akume, the president said pension security was a national obligation and that his administration was determined to improve the welfare of retirees.
“A pension is not a favour granted by Government. It is a wage earned, deferred and held in trust. It is a promise. And this Administration has resolved that the promise will be kept,” he said.
He said his administration was working to address outstanding pension obligations and improve retirees’ welfare through measures intended to strengthen the Contributory Pension Scheme.
The measures include implementing the Minimum Pension Guarantee under the Pension Reform Act 2014 and expanding PenCare, a healthcare support programme for eligible retirees.
“Since enactment, that promise has never been honoured. Under President Tinubu, it will be,” Mr Akume said, conveying the president’s commitment to implementing the minimum guarantee.
The president also reiterated his administration’s commitment to the N758 billion Federal Government Pension Bond, which was approved to settle outstanding accrued pension rights and strengthen the Pension Protection Fund.
“That was not an accounting exercise. It was an act of restitution to Nigerians who served their country and were made to wait for what they had earned,” Mr Akume said on behalf of the president.
The president said pension security should be treated as a government responsibility rather than a discretionary benefit for retired workers.
“Above all, no Nigerian who has served this nation will be forgotten in retirement. Nigeria will keep faith with those who kept faith with Nigeria.”
The proposed Minimum Pension Guarantee is intended to provide a safety net for eligible retirees under the Contributory Pension Scheme whose retirement income is inadequate.
Although the Pension Reform Act 2014 provides for the guarantee, the minimum amount payable and the detailed implementation arrangements will depend on the relevant guidelines from the National Pension Commission ( PenCom ).
The president also highlighted PenCare, a healthcare support programme intended to improve access to essential medical services for low-income retirees.
The initiative is designed to extend retirement support beyond pension payments by helping eligible beneficiaries access healthcare services.
PenCom has begun rolling out PenCare, with an initial phase targeting 30,000 retirees. The programme is funded jointly by the commission and participating pension fund operators.
According to the president, the initiative reflected a broader approach to retirement welfare, judging the pension system not only by the savings contributors accumulate but also by the security and dignity those savings provide in retirement.
He urged relevant institutions to ensure that the measures produced tangible improvements in pensioners’ lives.
The Director-General of PenCom, Omolola Oloworaran, said Nigeria’s pension assets rose from N20.79 trillion in July 2024 to N31.8 trillion in August 2026.
The N11.01 trillion increase represents about a 53 per cent growth over the period.
However, she said the expansion of pension assets had not translated into adequate retirement income for many contributors, particularly private-sector workers.
“Almost 70 per cent of private sector employees earn below the national minimum wage in retirement. More than 55 per cent of all retirees whose pensions fall below the minimum wage come from the private sector,” she said.
Ms Oloworaran attributed the problem partly to employers calculating pension contributions on limited portions of workers’ earnings rather than their full remuneration.
She said the statutory combined pension contribution of 18 per cent comprises 10 per cent from employers and eight per cent from employees, warning that inadequate pensionable earnings could weaken retirement benefits.
“Our private sector workers are retiring into poverty. This must change,” she said.
The PenCom chief urged private employers to contribute to the Pension Protection Fund alongside the Federal Government and pension industry operators.
She also challenged pension fund administrators to generate returns that exceed inflation, which continues to erode the purchasing power of retirement savings.
“Beating inflation is not an aspiration. It is your job,” she said.
Ms Oloworaran disclosed that the commission had secured commitments from pension industry operators to establish three million additional funded, active Retirement Savings Accounts within the next year. The target is intended to extend coverage to workers currently excluded from formal pension arrangements.
She also announced that President Tinubu would launch the Pension Security Initiative on 10 November, incorporating PenCare and the minimum pension guarantee.
The commission further directed pension fund administrators and custodians to complete their recapitalisation by 30 June 2027.
“Every pension fund administrator and custodian must complete recapitalisation by 30th June 2027. We are not changing our minds,” she said.
Highlighting recent improvements, Ms Oloworaran said some federal retirees had received pension increases ranging from 67 to 120 per cent, while certain Nigeria Social Insurance Trust Fund pensioners recorded increases exceeding 1,000 per cent.
She added that retired professors could now receive pensions equivalent to their final salaries, while some retirement benefits were being processed within 48 hours.
The commission also announced an exit benefit scheme for retirees from treasury-funded federal ministries, departments and agencies, with symbolic cheques presented at the event.
President Tinubu warned pension fund administrators and custodians against exposing workers’ retirement savings to reckless investments, insisting that the pursuit of higher returns or national development must not compromise contributors’ financial security.
He said pension assets must be managed with transparency, accountability and strict risk-management standards.
Although pension savings could support infrastructure development and economic growth, he said investment decisions must prioritise the interests of the workers whose contributions make up the funds.
“National development must never come at the expense of pensioners. Every investment must stand on its own merits, pass rigorous tests of risk and return, and serve the best interests of contributors,” he said.
The president warned that inflation was weakening the purchasing power of retirement savings, making it necessary for pension operators to deliver sustainable returns without compromising capital preservation.
“Preservation without growth is a slow erosion. Retirement savings that fail to keep pace with inflation quietly betray the very people who saved them,” he said.
He urged pension fund administrators and custodians to strengthen their investment expertise, diversify portfolios responsibly, reduce operating costs and improve accountability.
According to him, the pension industry’s performance should be measured by the financial security it delivers to retirees rather than the volume of assets under management.
The president also called on PenCom to enforce pension regulations firmly and fairly, while urging public and private-sector employers to remit pension contributions fully and promptly.
He described the deduction of workers’ pension contributions without transferring the money to their Retirement Savings Accounts as a breach of trust.
The president further called on state governments, organised labour and other stakeholders to expand pension coverage, including among traders, artisans, farmers, transport operators and other self-employed Nigerians.
He said the government would promote the Personal Pension Plan and new distribution channels to make retirement savings more accessible to people outside conventional salaried employment.
“Pensions for All must mean exactly that: all,” he said.
He urged stakeholders to ensure the summit produced measurable commitments, including increased enrolment, faster benefit payments, improved investment performance and clearer disclosure of pension fund activities.
Meanwhile, the Chairman of the House of Representatives Committee on Pensions, Jallo Mohammed, said the National Assembly was reviewing the Pension Reform Act 2014 and other pension-related legislation.
He said proposed amendments, including legislation concerning intelligence and military pensions, were progressing through legislative consideration ahead of public hearings.
Mr Mohammed also disclosed ongoing engagement with NNPC Pension Fund Limited over compliance with PenCom directives following years of regulatory concerns.
He pledged continued legislative oversight to improve pension administration, strengthen regulatory compliance and protect contributors’ retirement savings.
“Our shared objective must be to build a pension industry that not only protects the savings of today’s workers, but also guarantees greater financial security and dignity for future generations of retirees,” he said.
Nigeria’s Contributory Pension Scheme was established under the Pension Reform Act 2004 and subsequently governed by the Pension Reform Act 2014. The framework requires employers and employees in covered employment to contribute towards retirement savings, with pension fund operators managing the accumulated funds under regulatory oversight.
The scheme was introduced to address weaknesses associated with previous pension arrangements, including delays in benefit payments and the accumulation of unfunded liabilities.
However, some retirees have continued to face inadequate pension payments, delays in receiving accrued rights and difficulties meeting healthcare costs after leaving employment.
In October, PenCom announced that the Federal Government’s pension intervention had been used to clear inherited accrued pension liabilities dating back to 2007, with the commission reporting that 957,045 beneficiaries had been covered.
The commission has also identified the Minimum Pension Guarantee and PenCare as measures intended to improve the financial security and welfare of retirees.
President Tinubu said the success of the reforms should ultimately be measured by their effect on pensioners’ lives.
“The true measure of our success will not be how much money the system holds. It will be how much security, and how much dignity, it delivers,” he said.

title: MTN’s profit before tax for Q3 hits GH¢ 11.3 billion
body: Telecoms giant MTN has seen its profit before tax for the first nine months of this year hit GH¢ 11.3 billion. The figure represents a 51.8% jump over the GH¢ 7.7 billion it recorded during the same period in 2025. The figures were captured in MTN Ghana’s performance report for the nine-month period ended September 2026, released to the investing public on 29 October 2026. The report puts MTN’s total revenue as of September 30 at GH¢ 23.2 billion, representing a 35.7% increase over the figure recorded during the same period last year. In terms of expenditure, MTN invested some GH¢ 3.2 billion in capital expenditure during the first nine months of this year. Service revenue increased by 33.5% YoY to GH¢ 23.2 billion in the first nine months of 2026, reflecting what MTN describes as continued execution across both our Connectivity and Fintech businesses. Sustained demand for data services, increasing adoption of digital financial services, and continued customer engagement across our digital platforms supported growth. Mobile Money Business MTN’s Mobile Money Business grew by 26.5% to reach GH¢ 5.3 billion, according to the company. The growth was supported by continued expansion across both core wallet services and advanced financial services, alongside a 6.9% YoY increase in active Mobile Money users to 18.9 million. Basic services revenue increased by 22.2% YoY to GH¢ 3.5 billion, supported by growth in person-to-person transfers, while advanced services revenue increased by 28.7% YoY to GH¢ 1.9 billion, driven by higher adoption of digital payments, lending, and other value-added services. Transaction volumes and values continued to grow during the period, reflecting broader ecosystem participation and increasing digital payment adoption. Mobile Money contributed 23.2% of service revenue, compared with 24.9% in the corresponding period of 2025. MTN puts the number of active Mobile Money users at 18.9 million, representing a 6.9% increase. CEO on Third Quarter Earnings According to MTN Ghana Chief Executive Officer Stephen Blewett, growth remained well diversified across the company’s key revenue streams. He also stated that data revenue increased by 39.9% YoY in Q3, supported by sustained demand for data and digital services. The Chief Executive Officer said the third-quarter performance further strengthened the company’s nine-month results, demonstrating the resilience and diversification of its growth engines. He added that “this performance also reinforced our capacity to generate earnings and cash flow while continuing to invest in the long-term growth of the business and deliver returns to shareholders.” Mr. Blewett added that, while the global environment remains challenging, Ghana’s operating environment remains relatively stable. This is due to the fact that “inflation remains on a moderating trajectory, external reserves have strengthened, and economic activity continues to demonstrate resilience.” Dividend Payment Based on its financial performance for the third quarter, the MTN Board is proposing a gross interim dividend of GH¢ 0.03 per share for the third quarter ending 30 September 2026. The company stated that all dividends are subject to the deduction of applicable taxes. The number of ordinary shares in issue as of the date of the declaration is 13,236,175,050. Scancom PLC’s tax reference number is C0003632776. MTN said the declaration is in line with the requirements of Ghana Stock Exchange rules, including the relevant dates relating to the payment of the dividend. Consequently, an investor purchasing MTN GH shares before the relevant date will be entitled to the Q3 interim dividend. However, an investor buying MTN GH shares on or after Thursday, 26 November 2026, will not be entitled to the Q3 interim dividend. On Thursday, 10 December 2026, the net dividend will be transferred electronically to the bank accounts or mobile money wallets of shareholders who use these facilities.

title: Russia’s anti-LGBT crackdown is punishing homophobes, too. Mediazona documents five cases of people penalized for posts that weren’t meant to promote LGBTQ rights.
body: A rainbow flag on the U.S. Embassy building in Russia, June 2020 Nearly three years ago, Russia’s Supreme Court banned the nonexistent “international LGBT movement” as extremist. Since then, “LGBT extremism” has become grounds for at least 14 criminal investigations and hundreds of citations for administrative offenses. Because the system often doesn’t look into the context in which a rainbow flag appears on social media, even homophobes end up being targeted. Mediazona has compiled cases in which opponents of same-sex relationships have been punished for “promoting” them. In 2013, Russia passed a law banning the promotion of “nontraditional sexual relationships” to minors. In December 2022, the authorities extended the ban on “gay propaganda” to people of all ages. They also amended the Code of Administrative Offenses to prohibit “promotion of pedophilia” and the distribution of information “capable of making minors want to change their sex.” In November 2023, the Supreme Court outlawed the “international LGBT public movement” by declaring it an “extremist organization.” Vera Makeyeva, a retiree from Kurgan who welcomed Russia’s ban on the “LGBT movement,” was fined under that ban six months later — 1,500 rubles for old reposts of homophobic content featuring a rainbow flag. “It’s my own fault. I hadn’t cleaned up my photo albums in 13 years. Some people were interested enough to go through them,” Makeyeva told Mediazona. Pyatigorsk resident Pyotr Voronin was jailed for one day for an image showing the presidents of Ukraine and France alongside a swastika and a rainbow flag (both are considered extremist symbols in Russia). Voronin had intended to mock Ukraine and France — and was outraged that “the FSB’s AI decided I was spreading propaganda.” “I asked [in court], ‘So maybe I should officially apologize to Zelensky?’ Basically, the AI that reads our messages online is a complete idiot, and we mean nothing to it,” Voronin concluded. Vladimir Sugakov, a retiree from the Kemerovo region, was fined 100,000 rubles for “LGBT propaganda” in homophobic posts. Among the posts that caught law enforcement’s attention was a slideshow of photographs from Pride events set to Sergei Trofimov’s song “Petushki” (“Little Roosters,” Russian prison slang for gay men). Sugakov said the video criticized the LGBTQ community, but the police and the court didn’t bother to look into it. He decided against appealing the fine, saying he wasn’t an “idiot” who would “take on the system.” In Moscow, a video titled “Nazi Initiation” led to a 100,000-ruble fine. In it, a young man shaves his head, puts on clothes popular with neo-Nazi skinheads, and has sex with two similar-looking men. The video ends with an image of a swastika and the message “Join our ranks!!!” The Moscow resident who posted the video said he had done so “as a joke.” The court saw “LGBT propaganda” rather than humor. Father Grigory (Grzegorz Zwoliński), a Polish Catholic priest who lived in Kirov, had long criticized Archbishop Paolo Pezzi, who heads the Catholic Archdiocese of Moscow, for supporting the LGBTQ community. Father Grigory added a rainbow flag to one of his posts about Pezzi “to draw attention.” He was fined 1,000 rubles for it. The fine, in turn, led to the revocation of his Russian residence permit and a ban on re-entry. After 24 years in Russia, the priest returned to Poland, where he now writes that the “rainbow church” took revenge on him. title: Russia to continue supplying grain to Africa, Putin says
body:
MOSCOW, October 29. /TASS/. Russia will continue to supply grain to Africa both on a commercial basis and free of charge, President Vladimir Putin said at a press conference following the Russia-Africa Summit.
"Russia will continue to act as a responsible supplier of grain to Africa; as before, we will continue to do that both on a commercial basis and free of charge," he said.
Putin pointed out that discussions at the summit had confirmed that many African leaders viewed agriculture as the key area for cooperation with Russia. "They expect our country to continue to make a feasible contribution to strengthening food security on the African continent and supplying consumer markets with essential food products. We are certainly ready and open to that," the Russian president added.

title: 2027: Tinubu Can Be Sure Of Victory In Imo With My Name On Ballot — Okorocha
body: Former Imo State Governor Rochas Okorocha has expressed confidence that President Bola Tinubu will win Imo State in the 2027 presidential election if he is on the ballot as the All Progressives Congress (APC) candidate for Imo West Senatorial District. Okorocha is locked in a battle with his successor, Governor Hope Uzodimma, over the APC ticket for Imo West, with both laying claim to victory in the party’s primary election. The APC, however, submitted Uzodimma’s name to the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) as its candidate, prompting Okorocha to challenge the decision in court. On Thursday, the Federal Capital Territory High Court ruled that Okorocha secured the majority of votes cast in the primary and should be declared the winner. Speaking on Channels Television’s Politics Today hours after the judgment, Okorocha said his presence on the ballot would guarantee Tinubu’s victory in the state. “What is important to me now is how will Asiwaju be elected in Imo State. With this my name coming on the ballot paper now, Asiwaju can be sure that his victory is given in Imo State,” he said. The former governor celebrated the ruling, insisting that the judiciary was not for sale. He also said Uzodimma had “met his waterloo”, alleging that the court had pronounced his documents “were forged”. Okorocha urged people in the South-East to approach the 2027 presidential election strategically, advising the Igbo to put political calculations ahead of emotions. According to him, supporting Tinubu would amount to a strategic alliance that could benefit the South-East politically in the future. “As Southeasterners we are not going to politics now with emotions, we have to go to politics with strategy. So, supporting Tinubu for Ndigbo is a strategic alliance. “We cannot afford to gamble for four years. Any time Nigerians think it is the time for Ndigbo to be president, we should be proper presidents.” Okorocha added that he would work more effectively with other South-East governors to secure Tinubu’s victory in the region if he were placed in charge of the president’s campaign in Imo State. However, the Imo State Commissioner for Information, Declan Emelumba, rejected the judgment, describing it as “a complete travesty of justice”. He said the state government would approach the Court of Appeal to seek its reversal. The Imo APC has also maintained that Uzodimma remains its candidate for the Imo West Senatorial District in the 2027 general elections. The post 2027: Tinubu Can Be Sure Of Victory In Imo With My Name On Ballot — Okorocha appeared first on Channels Television .

title: Care for Alyoshki residents what matters most — US journalist
body:
SIMFEROPOL, October 29. /TASS/. Newsmax representative Luke Kjeldsen, who arrived in Russia as part of a humanitarian mission to Alyoshki in the Kherson Region, stressed the importance of ensuring that residents receive care and everything they need.
"Well, I think we're going to find a lot of that out tomorrow. <...> But we're looking to monitor that, document it, and report the story that we see," Kjeldsen told TASS.
"Well, we're here to talk about Alyoshki, and I realize Alyoshki is part of the Kherson [Region]. But I think what everybody wants is some peace for these civilians who are living in that area right now, in Alyoshki," he said, emphasizing the importance of ensuring that "these people can be taken care of."
A humanitarian mission to support civilians is underway in the frontline town of Alyoshki. A temporary ceasefire in the Kherson sector runs from 4 a.m. Moscow time (1 a.m. GMT) on October 27 to 10:59 p.m. (7:59 p.m. GMT) on November 1, 2026. The main aid deliveries are scheduled for October 29-30.
Voluntary evacuation will be available to anyone wishing to leave. Those who remain will receive food, medicine and other essentials.
Preparations for the mission began in May 2026 with assistance from Russian Human Rights Commissioner Yana Lantratova and Ukrainian Ombudsman Dmitry Lubinets, and mediation by US First Lady Melania Trump. Representatives of international media outlets arrived in the town as part of a delegation.

title: More Than 100 Lawmakers Push to Include SHIPS for America Act in Defense Bill
body:
Essential news coupled with the finest maritime content sourced from across the globe.
Rep. John Garamendi speaks outside the U.S. Capitol during a press conference with lawmakers, labor leaders and maritime industry representatives urging passage of the SHIPS for America Act, legislation aimed at revitalizing U.S. shipbuilding and the maritime industrial base.
A bipartisan group of 119 lawmakers is urging congressional leaders to preserve and expand provisions of the SHIPS for America Act in the final fiscal year 2027 National Defense Authorization Act (NDAA), warning that rebuilding the U.S. maritime industry is essential to national and economic security.
In an October 29 letter to House and Senate leadership, the lawmakers called for retaining shipbuilding provisions already approved by the House while considering additional measures from the broader legislation that were left out.
The letter was led by Representatives Trent Kelly (R-MS) and John Garamendi (D-CA), along with Senators Todd Young (R-IN) and Mark Kelly (D-AZ), the bipartisan sponsors of the SHIPS for America Act.
“As negotiations proceed on the National Defense Authorization Act (NDAA) for Fiscal Year 2027, we write to share our strong support for the inclusion of the bipartisan, bicameral Shipbuilding and Harbor Infrastructure for Prosperity and Security Act of 2025,” the lawmakers wrote.
The push comes as Congress works to finalize the annual defense policy bill, which has emerged as a potential vehicle for advancing long-sought reforms to the U.S. commercial maritime industry.
What’s in the SHIPS for America Act? Key Provisions to Restore U.S. Maritime Power
The House-passed NDAA, H.R. 8800, includes elements of the SHIPS for America Act under Title XXXVI. According to the letter, those provisions were agreed to unanimously in the House.
But the lawmakers argue that the measures represent only a starting point.
“The inclusion of these provisions is a necessary start for revitalizing the U.S. maritime industry,” they wrote, adding that Congress should give further consideration to provisions omitted from the House-passed bill.
The SHIPS for America Act is a sweeping proposal aimed at reversing decades of decline in American commercial shipbuilding and shipping. It seeks to establish long-term federal maritime policy and oversight, improve the competitiveness of U.S.-flagged vessels in international commerce, rebuild domestic shipyards, and expand recruitment, training, and retention of American mariners and shipyard workers.
The lawmakers pointed to the enormous gap between U.S. shipbuilding capacity and that of its Asian competitors.
China, South Korea, and Japan collectively account for more than 90% of global shipbuilding by tonnage, while the United States builds less than 1%, according to figures cited in the letter.
The lawmakers also noted that fewer than 100 U.S.-flagged vessels participate in international commerce, compared with an estimated Chinese fleet of more than 5,500 ships.
That imbalance, they argued, poses risks that extend well beyond commercial competition.
“Especially should the United States enter a prolonged conflict, a robust Merchant Marine, outfitted with U.S. shipping vessels manned by American mariners, would be critical for addressing any potential logistical challenges associated with the transportation of supplies,” the letter states.
The legislation has attracted support from maritime unions, commercial carriers, shipbuilding interests, and industry associations. The lawmakers also pointed to the Trump administration’s stated commitment to restoring U.S. maritime dominance.
The latest letter demonstrates the breadth of congressional support for the initiative, with signatories spanning both parties and both chambers. Among those signing were Senators Susan Collins, Elizabeth Warren, Richard Blumenthal, Amy Klobuchar, Katie Britt, and John Fetterman, along with Representatives Joe Courtney, Rob Wittman, Salud Carbajal, and John Moolenaar, chairman of the House Select Committee on China.
The letter was addressed to House Speaker Mike Johnson, Senate Majority Leader John Thune, House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries, and Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer.
While the House has already approved several SHIPS for America Act provisions, the final scope of maritime reforms included in the NDAA remains unresolved.
The lawmakers are now pressing congressional leadership to preserve those provisions and go further before the defense bill reaches the president’s desk.
“Now, we ask that these provisions be retained and strengthened in the final National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2027,” the letter concludes.

Patrick Stewart, best known for his roles in Star Trek and X-Men , has died at age 86. A message posted to Stewart’s Instagram account says the actor died in his Los Angeles home on Wednesday “following a brief and poignant journey with Alzheimer’s Disease and Lewy Body Dementia.”
Born in 1940 in Mirfield, Yorkshire, England, Stewart began his acting career in theater . He eventually landed the role of Captain Jean-Luc Picard in Star Trek: The Next Generation , which ran from 1987 to 1994. Stewart returned as the Star Trek captain in subsequent films , including Star Trek: Generations (1994), Star Trek: First Contact (1996), Star Trek: Insurrection (1998), and Star Trek: Nemesis (2002). Stewart also starred as Professor Charles Xavier in several X-Men movies. He was knighted by Queen Elizabeth II in 2010 .
“His sonorous voice and singular talent will forever be synonymous with indelible performances in every genre,” the message on Instagram says. “He explored the human condition in all its poetic complexity and brought hope not only to the far reaches of the Marvel Cinematic Universe, but into science fiction’s most iconic final frontier aboard the Starship Enterprise.”

title: 8-year-old severely injured in wolf attack inside German zoo enclosure
body:
An eight-year-old child was severely injured after being attacked by a wolf inside an enclosure at a German zoo.
The incident occurred on Wednesday morning before the regular opening of the Johannismühle Wildlife Park south of Berlin, during a zookeeper day for children, the zoo said in a news release .
The wolves were being given water at the time of the incident, it said, adding that the quick response of staff prevented two other children from being attacked. Emergency services arrived quickly on scene and provided treatment to the injured child.
The child was transported to a hospital by rescue helicopter. Four people, including three children, are being cared for by the emergency chaplaincy, the statement added.
The zoo said it was “deeply saddened” by the incident that potentially involved “several wolves.”
“When a child is injured in this way, it deeply affects us,” the statement continued.
“The incident must be extremely distressing, especially for the family and those who witnessed it. Our thoughts are with them.”
“We sincerely hope the child recovers soon and wish all those affected strength to cope with what they have experienced,” it concluded.
The wildlife park will also provide psychological support for those affected by the incident. A debriefing session with the relevant authorities and security organizations, including the post-incident support team, has been planned, the zoo said without providing a date.
The wildlife park was closed after the incident and will remain shut until further notice.
“Besides supporting those directly affected, the focus is now on a factual investigation of the incident,” the zoo said.
The Lower Nature Conservation Authority and the Veterinary and Food Inspection Office will receive a report from the police, which will be used to determine a course of action.
The Veterinary and Food Inspection Office will visit the wildlife park soon to conduct an on-site inspection to ensure compliance with animal welfare regulations, the zoo confirmed.
The health and behaviour of the wolf or wolves involved in the incident will also be assessed. The park is legally permitted to exhibit animals in a zoological facility, including polar wolves and wolves.
During its last inspection in July 2025, no safety-related defects were found in the fences or enclosures, which are checked every morning, nor were any animal welfare violations identified, the zoo said. A planned inspection will re-evaluate those findings, the news release added.
This is not the first wolf attack to occur in Germany this year.
In March, a wolf bit a woman in a shopping area in Hamburg, authorities said, in what is believed to be the first such attack since wolves returned to the country in 1998.
Wolf attacks on livestock in Europe have been a growing concern to farmers for years, however. Last year, the European Parliament voted to change wolves’ status from “strictly protected” to “protected.”
Since 2002, there have been two recorded fatal wolf attacks in North America, one in Saskatchewan in 2005 and one in Alaska in 2010, according to the International Wolf Center .

Reddit is announcing a huge shift: It’s going to start requiring users to log in.
Right now, you can browse Reddit without having an account, and the site is generally a great resource for crowdsourced information on a whole range of topics. I know I’m not the only person who appends “reddit” to a lot of Google searches to find answers to things written by actual humans instead of robots . But that openness has made it a target for scraping and automated traffic, leading Reddit to file lawsuits over alleged unauthorized access of its data and make product changes like limiting access to “Old Reddit.”
There’s no definitive timeline on when this change will roll out to all users, or how the site will work if you’re logged out. (If I send my friend a link to a thread and they aren’t logged in, what will they see?) To start, Reddit will test the logged-in requirement in “select markets outside the US” in the “coming months,” according to CEO Steve Huffman . “We’ll look at the impact on the user experience, on our business, and on the whole Reddit ecosystem, figure out where the right boundaries are, and go from there.” Reddit has also rebuilt and is rereleasing the Reddit app’s incognito mode.
Huffman claims the login requirement is better for Reddit’s user experience and its ads business and is “more protective of Reddit data.” The “vast majority” of unauthorized Reddit access happens “through our logged-out experiences,” though the company will still strike licensing deals of its data with companies, like the deals it made with OpenAI and Google in 2024. Huffman notes that Reddit does not need to know a logged-in user’s identity — “Honestly, we don’t want to know” — just that the user is logged in at all. And he says that more logged-in users lets the company deliver “more relevant ads.”
“This is a big change for Reddit, where we’ve allowed logged-out access to basically all of Reddit for the last two decades,” Huffman says. “And I don’t know about you, but as someone whose life has been defined by the open internet, it’s a big change for me. But I’ve come to the conclusion that this is the right decision for our platform and the right decision for our business.”
Reddit is making this announcement alongside its Q3 2026 earnings, which were released today . Search traffic was “down meaningfully” in Q3, Huffman says in the company’s shareholder letter , with logged-out traffic and web traffic being the most heavily impacted. “During October, we have seen that search traffic has dropped by more than 1 million referrals on average per week,” Huffman says.
However, Huffman notes that app and logged-in daily active unique users make up “over 80% of the monetization on Reddit,” which he says “speaks to the strength of Reddit as a destination and the impact of our ongoing product work.”

title: What killed 500-plus penguins? How scientists solved the mystery
body:
A small group of Adélie penguins return to their colony. A mega-colony of these penguins was hit by a big die-off in early 2024. Ralph Vanstreels hide caption
Sailing toward the Danger Islands, Dr. Ralph Vanstreels had a good idea of what he might find: A lot of dead Adélie penguins.
It was March 2024 and a virus had been sweeping through the area, leaving deceased birds in its wake.
Vanstreels got the crime right but the culprit wrong. There were dead penguins but a virus was not to blame.
As his vessel pulled up to a landing ramp on one of the islands — located just off the Antarctic Peninsula — Vanstreels and his fellow researchers immediately noticed bumps in the snow.
"Was each bump a rock or was it a carcass? We had to do quite a bit of intensive searching [through the snow]," says Vanstreels, who is based in Argentina and is a wildlife veterinarian with the University of California, Davis.
The team ultimately found more than 537 penguin carcasses on just the ramp, which he estimates was about the size of an airport runway.
There were many more carcasses elsewhere on the Danger Islands, which are home to two mega colonies for penguins. The researchers estimate there were thousands of dead Adélie penguins and other species of birds. But they had to work quickly and couldn't do a complete count, Vanstreels says.
A view of the Adélie penguin colony at Beagle Island, one of the Danger Islands. A few penguin carcasses are scattered on the rocks. Ralph Vanstreels hide caption
"You cannot stay there very long because you might be locked down with an iceberg blocking your way out," he says.
As the team has pieced together this tragic penguin mystery, Vanstreels says, the case holds broader lessons for tracking the spread of diseases globally.
Now let's time jump to Australia a few months ago for another bird disease conundrum.
In June, H5N1 — high pathogenicity avian influenza also known as bird flu — arrived in mainland Australia. Up until that point, Australia had been the only continent to dodge the virus which has traversed the globe, leaving a trail of carcasses in its path.
Since late 2021, the virus has led to the death of nearly 300 million poultry birds. Either the virus killed them or they were culled as a preventive measure to stop the spread of the disease, according to the World Animal Health Information System. Further, bird flu is estimated to have killed millions of wild animals and marine mammals, although it's hard to get an exact figure.
Researchers were amazed that Australia could stay bird-flu-free for six years. And the virus didn't take the path that scientists expected.
"We have a lot of migration of birds between Australia and Southeast Asia, so for the first few years, we're like: That's where the virus is coming from," says Dr. Amandine Gamble , an assistant professor at Cornell University in the Department of Public and Ecosystem Health.
The way bird flu eventually got there was from the other direction. It came from Antarctica likely via migrating birds.
"This is a virus that's not assisted by airplanes," Michelle Wille , senior research fellow at the Center for Pathogen Genomics at the University of Melbourne, told NPR in 2025. "This is a virus that's traveling by mass mortality after mass mortality after mass mortality after mass mortality."
So when Vanstreels set sail to check on the penguins, he assumed bird flu would be the culprit.
Bird flu arrived in Antarctica in late 2023 and early 2024. Vanstreels and his colleagues rapidly arranged for a trip to try to figure out exactly what was happening.
"The expedition was initially fully set up to look for bird flu because that was the panic," he explains, adding that ongoing fear of a continuing global panzootic — or pandemic among animals — is justified.
In several layers of warm clothes covered by protective gear — double gloves, coveralls, glasses and masks — Vanstreels and the team started taking samples of the penguin corpses they found.
"We looked a little bit stiff when walking — like a penguin walking almost — because of all the gear," he says. "We had very strict biosafety standards."
They brought samples from the deceased penguins back to a mini-lab on their boat. By evening, they had early results. But not the results they expected.
"There is bird flu here, but the virus loads are low," he recalls. "That was a little bit puzzling."
A scientist conducts the necropsy of an Adélie penguin chick collected at Heroina Island, one of the Danger Islands where disease struck. Ralph Vanstreels hide caption
The carcasses were not very old, so Vanstreels would have expected to find far more bird flu virus if that had killed the birds. Perhaps something else was the main driver? "We were unsure what was happening," he recalls.
So what killed the 500-plus penguins on the landing ramp and the many others on the island?
Back on land several months after the voyage, in the Netherlands, Vanstreels' colleagues did more investigation. "Under the microscope, you can see that there's bacteria in the tissues," he says — not virus.
They discovered a different disease, a bacterial disease that causes avian cholera (which is distinct from human cholera).
Vanstreels and his team's findings were published in October in the journal the Proceedings of the Royal Society B .
So how worried are they about avian cholera?
The disease is not considered a major threat to humans since the strain that is specialized to birds is distinct from the strain specialized to mammals. "The risk for human infection is not really that high when you see an outbreak on birds," Vanstreels says. But, it does kill birds worldwide — especially in cold environments where the bacteria thrives.
While there's not enough research to know exactly how common avian cholera is, the disease has been on the radar of scientists for decades. However, it's not exactly top of mind. The last time researchers looked for it in the Antarctic Peninsula was 25 years ago.
"One could be misled to think that: Well, that was a unique thing that happened back in 2001, and nothing's happened ever since," says Vanstreels. Instead, it is possible that avian cholera die-offs could be occurring regularly, only scientists haven't been checking.
One of his big takeaways from this bird-flu-that-turned-out-to-be-avian-cholera event?
"Yes, there is a big thing with bird flu. But we still want to keep checking for the other diseases because they might be mixing up in the middle," Vanstreels says.
Like any good mystery, the case of the cholera-stricken penguins has got scientists wondering: Whodunit?
There's a theory that avian cholera might have been introduced to Antarctica decades ago from researchers who brought poultry from the U.S., Vanstreels says.
The Adelie penguin mega-colony at Heroina Island at the peak of the breeding season. The photo was taken in January 2025, a year after the outbreak. Ralph Vanstreels hide caption
Gamble, of Cornell University, adds that the strain of avian cholera found in penguins in Antarctica is "very close" to the strain found 5,000 miles away on Île Amsterdam in the Southern Indian Ocean.
"Antarctica is way more connected to the rest of the world than we think it is," she says.
It's hard to track diseases in Antarctica but, she says, it's turning out to be an important piece in the global pathogen puzzle.
The work of keeping tabs on what's happening has fallen to a number of different countries since Antarctica is not governed by any one government. It was designated as a continent of peace and science by the mid 20th-century Antarctic Treaty , which now has 58 parties — among them are the U.S., France, Japan and Russia. Many nations have research stations and team up on scientific undertakings, including tracking pathogens — be it bird flu or avian cholera — that travel great distances and don't respect borders.
"So this Avian cholera outbreak is just showing this is not a unique event," says Gamble. "We really need international collaboration."

title: 'Star Trek,' 'X-Men' star Patrick Stewart dies at 86
body:
Patrick Stewart, the legendary actor known for his roles in " Star Trek : The Next Generation" and the "X-Men" film franchise, has died at the age of 86, his representative announced Thursday.
Stewart died "in the loving care of his beloved wife Sunny" after a "brief and poignant journey" with Alzheimer's disease and Lewy body dementia, according to a statement shared on his social media by his longtime spokesperson, Kelly Bush Novak.
"He has been held in the warm embrace of family and friends, surrounded by live music, prayer, tears, laughter, and the kind of profound emotion that only he could inspire after a lifetime of devotion to us all," the statement continued. "We will forever cherish the peaceful ease and reflection on his face, an enduring reminder of his invincible grace."
Alzheimer's disease is the most common form of dementia, the loss of memory, problem-solving and thinking abilities. It is a progressive disease that begins with mild memory loss and ultimately has no cure, according to the U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention.
Lewy body dementia is a type of dementia that can cause complications with movement, behavior, thinking and mood, according to the CDC.
It is unclear when Stewart was diagnosed with Alzheimer's and Lewy body dementia.
Known for his commanding presence and voice, Stewart's career spanned six decades across Broadway, film and television.
Born on July 13, 1940, in Mirfield, a town in England, Stewart's love for the theater began at an early age, thanks to one of his English teachers, who he said "put a copy of Shakespeare in my hand [and] said, 'Now get up on your feet and perform,'" according to the BBC .
Stewart went on to study drama at Mirfield Secondary Modern School but dropped out at 15 to pursue local theater, according to a biography published on the official Hollywood Walk of Fame website.
In 1966, Stewart became a member of the Royal Shakespeare Company and stayed with them until 1982.
He made his television debut in 1967, appearing on "Coronation Street," a British soap opera, which followed the everyday lives of working-class people in the fictional England town of Weatherfield.
He went on to land more television roles, appearing in the TV movie adaptation of Shakespeare's "Antony and Cleopatra" in 1974 and the 1975 TV mini series "North & South."
In 1987, Stewart was cast as Capt. Jean-Luc Picard in "Star Trek: The Next Generation," which is widely considered his most famous and iconic role.
Stewart played the starship captain for seven seasons, spanning 1987 to 1994, and also played the character in multiple feature films. He later reprised the role for the series "Star Trek: Picard."
Speaking with NPR in 2022, Stewart opened up on his initial apprehension about taking the role.
"I was unprepared for what being cast in an American TV series meant because I'd never done that before," Stewart said. "I'd done, you know, a mini-series in the U.K. and so forth."
He continued, "It was terrifying to me because what it meant was that I was going to have to shut down my career, which actually -- and I don't know whether there is any connection here -- but actually had started to take off in a way that I was very pleased with."
"I'd been playing leading Shakespearean roles for a number of years, and now I was getting leading roles on television, and I was being offered transfers into the West End and transfers to Broadway. And the idea that I would have to shut that down for six years was horrifying," he added.
In his 2023 book, "Making It So: A Memoir," Stewart further reflected on playing Capt. Picard, writing, "Like me, Jean-Luc has lived an unusual life that has taken him far beyond the bounds of normal human experience. But he is also someone who has remained true to his earthbound roots, for they are what gave him his identity. In the end, he feels the call of home, as do I."
His success on "Star Trek: The Next Generation" led to more blockbuster and voice-acting roles, including the 1998 television adaptation of "Moby Dick," in which he voiced Capt. Ahab, and more.
In 2000, he was cast as Professor Charles Xavier -- Professor X -- in the "X-Men" film franchise, ultimately portraying the character in eight films over more than two decades.
Leading up to his death, Stewart returned as Professor X in "Avengers: Doomsday," which will be released in theaters Dec. 18, 2026.
Stewart was honored with a star on the Hollywood Walk of Fame in 1996. He was also immortalized outside the TCL Chinese Theater in Hollywood in January 2020, just days ahead of the premiere of "Star Trek: Picard."
Outside of acting, Stewart was also a philanthropist and activist for survivors of domestic violence, LGBTQ+ equality, human rights, global refugees, veterans' mental health and animal welfare.
Stewart is survived by his wife Sunny Ozell and his two children, Daniel Stewart and Sophie Alexandra Stewart, whom he shared with his first wife, Sheila Falcolner.
Disney is the parent company of Marvel, ABC News, and "Good Morning America."

title: IN BRIEF: FSB reports new cases of Kiev recruiting Russian teenagers for terrorism
body:
MOSCOW, October 29. /TASS/. Russia’s FSB has released new details about Ukraine luring Russian teenagers into committing terrorist acts through the popular youth dating chatbot Divinchik.
- The FSB has reported new cases of teenagers being recruited by the special services of Ukraine to commit terrorist attacks through the popular youth dating chatbot Divinchik / Leo - Dating, Communication, New Friends.
- It said that in August-September 2026 alone, eight minors aged 14 to 17 and two adult Russian citizens (19 and 24 years old) were detained in Moscow, St. Petersburg and the Leningrad Region, Nizhny Novgorod, Omsk, Ryazan and Sverdlovsk regions.
- According to the FSB, the detainees planned or had already committed arson attacks on law enforcement vehicles, gas stations, energy and transport infrastructure facilities on the instructions of the Ukrainian special services.
- They also served as couriers for transferring funds received from defrauded citizens to crypto exchange offices.
- It said that since July 2025, 56 Russians aged 12 to 24, users of the Divinchik Telegram service, who committed crimes under the psychological influence of the special services of Ukraine, have been detained in various regions.
- The FSB showed a video recording of the detention of several teenagers involved in terrorist attacks through the popular youth dating chatbot Divinchik.
- In the footage, the young people said that they had met with young women in the chat, after which they were contacted by unknown people and forced to commit illegal acts through deception, blackmail and threats.
- As a result, several detainees set fire to gas stations, another photographed a relay cabinet, after which he was ordered to set it on fire to allegedly close his criminal case.
- The special services of Ukraine have involved two underage St. Petersburg schoolgirls in committing terrorist attacks through Telegram chatbot Divinchik /Leo, Svetlana Petrenko, an official representative of the Investigative Committee of Russia, told TASS.
- As a result, one of the schoolgirls set fire to a gas station in September 2026.
- Also in September, the second schoolgirl, while at a police station, poured flammable liquid over official cars, after which she set them on fire.
- After that, she went to another police department but was detained.
- In addition, a teenager has been brought to criminal responsibility in the Leningrad Region.
- A young man purchased flammable liquids and set fire to a gas station in St. Petersburg and the Leningrad Region, recording his actions on video.
- He acted on the instructions of a person who contacted him after meeting a young woman in the chatbot Divinchik and threatened negative consequences for him and his family members.
- They were all placed under house arrest.
- You should not divulge your personal data or the data of your loved ones when texting on a dating site, the FSB warned.
- It also said you should never give them your bank details, click on directed links, provide coordinates (geolocation) or photo and video images of buildings, structures, terrain, cars, equipment or people.
- People claiming to be from the Russian special services can later use this information for blackmail purposes, coercing the dupe into committing crimes under the threat of criminal prosecution.
- The Investigative Committee of Russia has urged parents to monitor their children's online activity so that they do not become involved in terrorist attacks and other illegal activities under the influence of the special services of Ukraine.
- Petrenko also reminded that no one should offer up their personal data when communicating on the Internet.
- The best thing to do if you receive a suspicious offer during online communication is immediately report it to the law enforcement agencies.
- In accordance with Article 31 of the Criminal Code, a person is not subject to criminal liability for a crime if he voluntarily and definitively refused to bring this crime to an end.

title: Rivian’s R2 is officially its best-selling vehicle
body:

The mass-market R2 has quickly become the company’s top seller by volume, but high-margin software deals and the Volkswagen partnership are the real forces keeping the automaker in good financial health.
