Rivian reported its third quarter earnings of 2026, providing us a closer look at the company’s financial health as it ramps up production of its all-important R2 electric vehicle — which is now, for the first time, outselling all of Rivian’s other EVs.
Rivian said it brought in $2.155 billion in revenue, a 38 percent increase compared to the $1.558 billion in Q3 2025. Of that amount, $1.55 billion came from automotive revenue, which is up 36 percent year over year. Comparatively, the company reported $605 million from software and subscription services, a 45 percent increase year over year. As EV sales slow down, the company is seeking to make more money from its digital products, including the Autonomy Plus package .
Automotive gross profits were on an upward trajectory, a sign that the company’s finances were improving as it delivered more vehicles. Rivian made $176 million in gross profit this quarter, a $152 million improvement compared to the same time last year. The company still lost $80 million in Q3 automotive gross profits, which is much better than the $130 million loss a year ago.
In other words, Rivian is losing less than it did a year ago because they sold more cars and made more money per vehicle. (Also, the company continued to sell pollution credits to other carmakers, and also received a tariff refund from the government — all of which was recorded as revenue.)
Rivian is losing less than it did a year ago because they sold more cars and made more money per vehicle.
Rivian brought in $256 million in profit in software and services, up $102 million from last year, with a strong 42 percent profit margin. Most of this cash came from licensing their tech to Volkswagen , alongside customer subscriptions for Rivian’s Autonomy Plus driving features. In many ways, Rivian’s tech partnership with Volkswagen and software sales are currently paying the bills, keeping the company profitable overall while it absorbs a lot of heavy upfront costs from launching the R2.
Earlier this month , Rivian reported a record sales quarter, with 19,751 vehicles produced and 19,248 delivered. That represents an 85 percent year-over-year increase in production and a 45 percent jump in deliveries. (For a direct-to-consumer automaker like Rivian, deliveries serve as a proxy for sales.)
Rivian doesn’t break down sales by model, so we don’t exactly how many R2s have reached customers so far. But the company said that the R2 is now the “best-selling Rivian vehicle by volume,” outselling the R1T and R1S, as well as the Electric Delivery Van (EDV).
“We had great results with R2 becoming our best selling vehicle by volume in the third quarter,” Rivian CEO RJ Scaringe said in a statement, ahead of the company’s earnings call this afternoon. “Customer and media feedback on R2 has been exceptional.”
The R2 was designed from the ground up to be Rivian’s higher-volume, mass-market offering — and by overtaking the company’s more expensive, lower-volume legacy vehicles, it seems to be doing just that. Still, the R2 isn’t bringing in the bulk of the revenue yet, as indicated by Rivian’s use of the phrase “by volume.” Most of the money is still coming from the VW partnership and its software division.
But that could change once Rivian starts shipping the more affordable versions of the R2 , like the $55,485 Premium trim (coming in late 2026), the $49,985 Standard Long-Range (early 2027), and the $46,495 Standard (late 2027).

title: GYMFEST: Organisers hail increased participation, target international breakthrough
body:
The third edition of GYMFEST Championship will hold in Lagos on 7 November, with 278 young gymnasts expected to showcase their skills as organisers intensify efforts to develop grassroots talent and improve Nigeria’s prospects in international gymnastics.
The event, organised by Tee Tumblers Gymnastics Club (TTGC) in collaboration with the Society of the Performing Arts in Nigeria (SPAN), will take place at The Dome, 1 Freedom Way, Lekki Phase 1, from 8 a.m. to 6 p.m.
Yoyin Akpose, co-convener of the championship and founder of Tee Tumblers Gymnastics Club, said participation had increased from fewer than 100 children at the inaugural edition to 278 registered participants this year.
“At some point, we have to tell some schools, please wait until next year. We don’t have the capacity for any more this year, but it’s encouraging to see that parents are interested now and the community keeps growing,” she said at a press conference in Lagos.
Mrs Akpose said the competition was established to provide children with opportunities to showcase their abilities, develop their skills and gain experience in competitive gymnastics.
She expressed confidence that sustained grassroots development could help Nigeria produce gymnasts capable of competing internationally.
“I know, we do have the talent, so that’s why I have the drive and the motivation to keep pushing because I feel like I know we will get there,” she said.
Mrs Akpose said her determination to promote gymnastics was reinforced by watching an international competition last week, where she was disappointed by the limited representation from Nigeria and West Africa.
She said the experience strengthened her resolve to create opportunities for young Nigerians to develop their abilities and compete at the highest level.
Gymnastics remains a developing sport in Nigeria, and GYMFEST seeks to encourage more schools and clubs to participate while increasing awareness of its competitive and developmental benefits.
Oluremi Jemitola, chief operating officer of SPAN, said the championship was established through the vision of the organisation’s founder and chairperson, Sarah Boulos, to promote healthier, more confident communities through movement, creativity and the performing arts.
She said the partnership between SPAN and Tee Tumblers, which began three years ago, had strengthened the competition’s technical capacity and contributed to its growth.
“Today, we are proud to say that, together, we have built and continue to grow what we aspire to be Nigeria’s biggest gymnastics competition,” Mrs Jemitola said.
She added that the organisers hoped to establish GYMFEST as Africa’s leading gymnastics festival and competition, with global recognition as a long-term ambition.
According to her, the championship goes beyond sporting performances by helping children develop confidence, discipline, teamwork and perseverance. It also provides an opportunity for parents to celebrate their children’s progress and coaches to receive recognition for their contributions.
Oluyomi Olusanmi, director of school sports at the Lagos State Sports Commission, commended the organisers for providing opportunities for children to participate in organised sporting activities.
Representing the commission at the press conference, Ms Olusanmi said the initiative aligned with Lagos State’s development agenda, particularly its focus on youth engagement and children’s overall development.
She explained that sports helped develop children’s cognitive, affective and psychomotor skills, contributing to their intellectual, social and physical growth.
Ms Olusanmi added that participation in sports could provide career opportunities and help address social challenges, including truancy, juvenile delinquency and negative peer pressure.
She said the championship supported the commission’s vision of making Lagos a leading sports destination in Africa.
The organisers said their partnership with the commission would help expand gymnastics participation beyond Lagos and contribute to the sport’s development across Nigeria.
The organisers acknowledged the support of ProvidusUnity Bank, the diamond partner, alongside Banksome Group, Leadway Assurance, YD Company, Studio24, Indomie and Gratia Chin Chin.
They said the partners had contributed financially and supported efforts to ensure the event’s success.
The festival will also feature the GYMFEST Souk, where vendors will sell food, pastries, clothing, gymnastics attire and other products. A children’s play area catering to different age groups will provide additional activities for families.
The organisers said the championship would allow participants to demonstrate skills developed through months of training while encouraging more children to embrace gymnastics.
Tunde Eludini is a graduate of the Obafemi Awolowo University Ile-Ife, Nigeria where he studied International Relations. He is a Senior Correspondent coordinating the sports section for PREMIUM TIMES. Twitter : @tundeyeludini

title: Fredericton’s emergency shelter space shrinks ahead of winter
body:
As colder weather approaches, those who operate homeless shelters in Fredericton are preparing to work with less this year.
Fredericton Homeless Shelters Inc. has run an emergency out-of-the-cold shelter in a building at the exhibition grounds for two winters now. The site allowed for around 33 beds.
However, the building is set to be demolished as part of a redevelopment project.
This week, Fredericton City Council approved another emergency shelter to operate this winter — but it’s at the Small Craft Aquatic Centre on the city’s south side, which is a smaller space.
“The Aquatic Center has been the appointed place right now and it will provide 10 emergency beds for overnight use during the winter months,” said Vanessa Foss, Fredericton Homeless Shelters Inc.’s director of business development.
Foss says the organization also has a men’s shelter with a 27-bed capacity and a women’s shelter with 10 beds “plus emergency couch.”
According to the latest numbers from the Human Development Council, as of September there were 353 people experiencing homelessness in Fredericton .
The data also showed 179 people were chronically homeless, which refers to people who have at least six months of homelessness over the past year or recurrent experiences of homelessness over the past three years.
“The numbers (of unhoused people) have increased quite a bit, so there’s a substantial need for individuals for housing and emergency shelters,” said Foss. “Between housing and shelter, there’s a significant need.”
Foss says work is ongoing to build a permanent shelter, but short-term measures are coming soon.
“We have started up our supported housing, so we have two houses now and then we’ll be opening a third in January. So that is increasing some supported housing elements, but that bigger project will be to come,” Foss said.
Council also approved a new courtyard lot for 12 Neighbours, a tiny home community, which will add 15 new units. The units offer a bridge between emergency out-of-the-cold services and permanent supportive housing.
“One of the things it does is helps us, of course, to deploy solutions more quickly but also house individuals that have some additional complexities that make it difficult for them to succeed even in a supportive, permanent housing context,” said Marcel LeBrun, president of 12 Neighbours, who spoke to council on Monday.
The Aquatic Centre emergency shelter will open in mid-December and is approved to stay open until the end of April.

title: Zelensky: Intelligence reports Russia preparing new ballistic missile strikes
body:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said this in his nightly video address , Ukrinform reports.
"We now have intel about the Russians preparing new ballistic missile attacks. We need the capabilities to shoot down all this Russian evil," he said.
Zelensky also said he had held a meeting of the Supreme Commander-in-Chief's Staff earlier today, with countering Russian ballistic missiles as the key issue.
"Sanctions pressure is insufficient – and we need the packages from partners that we have discussed with them. When it comes to key jurisdictions, sanctions can indeed have a significant restrictive effect, but not immediately – only over time. Sometimes this requires months of work. The longer sanctions packages targeting ballistic missiles are delayed, the longer Russia can maintain its supply schemes for the components needed for this production," he said.
He instructed the Ukrainian Foreign Ministry to accelerate this work with partners.
"We also set additional tasks for our long-range sanctions, which work much faster. For now, no public details on this, but everyone could see in recent weeks that Ukraine’s long-range capabilities are delivering results," he said.
Zelensky recalled that Ukraine had carried out two missile strikes that destroyed two Russian Su-34 fighter-bombers and also hit an Iskander missile launcher.
"Thank you, guys, for the result! Glory to Ukraine!" the president said.

title: Lost your spark? The "silent sister" of depression, and a quiz to spot her
body:
Some people with clinical depression can't get out of bed. But what about those who exhibit other signs of depression who never stop moving, and may double down on their work?
Psychiatrist Dr. Judith Joseph says the second group often goes unnoticed, even by the people living it. She calls it "high-functioning depression": people who keep meeting their obligations at work and at home while quietly losing the ability to feel pleasure.
"When you are joyful, you have better physical health, you have better relationships, you have better productivity at work," Joseph said in an interview for the Your Turn podcast . "So why don't we prioritize it?"
At the center of Joseph's work is anhedonia: a reduced ability to feel joy, pleasure or interest in things that once brought those feelings. Joseph describes it as "the silent sister" of depression.
"One sister is depressed, and crying, and not getting out of bed, and getting all the attention," she says. "The other one is quiet and numb." Anhedonia may not seem like a crisis in the classic sense, Joseph says. "But it is an existential crisis, and it's not something to ignore."
In a peer-reviewed study published in the journal Cureus, Joseph and colleagues interviewed adults using a set of questionnaires designed to assess high-functioning depression, trauma and anhedonia.
The results supported the researchers' hypothesis that people with high-functioning depression have increased levels of anhedonia and trauma. Participants with higher anhedonia scores also had higher high-functioning depression scores.
Parents and caregivers had the highest anhedonia and high-functioning depression scores in the study.
The authors note that high-functioning depression is not an official diagnosis in the DSM-5, the manual clinicians use to diagnose mental health conditions. They say that is part of the problem: people who keep functioning may not recognize their symptoms or seek treatment until they reach burnout.
Joseph says she often sees the pattern in women who are the steady presence for everyone around them. They are so focused on their responsibilities at work and at home that they don't realize they are burned out, or close to it.
"But eventually something's gonna give," she said. "Either they do break down and they have a clinical depression and they lose their functioning, they go into distress or crisis, or they physically break down."
She said she has seen patients end up in the emergency room without understanding why, only to learn they had been carrying unresolved emotional pain.
Joseph said the pattern is common in professions that discourage vulnerability, including her own. In medicine, she said, crying after a patient died was seen as weakness.
"In medicine, we focus on the crisis," Joseph said. "You're [taught] to look for the mania, for the psychosis." She believes there should be more focus on anhedonia, the loss of sense of joy.
Joseph developed an anhedonia quiz based on the Snaith-Hamilton Pleasure Scale, a measure of the capacity to feel pleasure that was published in the British Journal of Psychiatry.
The questionnaire asks about everyday experiences, such as whether you have trouble enjoying praise, whether you savor your meals or other small pleasures, and whether you struggle to enjoy your work or accomplishments because they never feel good enough.
The quiz is not a diagnostic tool. It's an invitation to take stock of what might be standing in the way of a fuller, more joyful life. If you'd like to take the quiz, you'll be asked to share your email to see the results.
In her book, "High Functioning: Overcome Your Hidden Depression and Reclaim Your Joy," Joseph also outlines a framework she calls the Five V's:
Joseph says anhedonia appears across many conditions, in many people in midlife and other times, too. "It's something that we need to learn how to detect," she said, because it can be a silent problem.

title: First M-346 For Frecce Tricolori Takes Flight
body: Days after its rollout, the first M-346 trainer jet destined to the Frecce Tricolori aerobatic team took off for its maiden flight. The first M-346 trainer jet destined to the Italian Air Force’s Frecce Tricolori aerobatic team has now conducted its maiden flight, days after being rolled out of factory at Leonardo’s facilities in Venegono. The aircraft conducted a short functional test flight on Oct. 29, 2026, before landing again at Venegono’s airfield. The photos you can see in this article were captured by local aviation photographer Jacopo Castelli , who kindly shared them with us. This M-346 is the first of 15 that will be delivered to the Frecce Tricolori , of which ten aircraft will be assigned to the main formation, one to the commander and four will be spares. According to unconfirmed sources, additional M-346s of the team are in final assembly. The first M-346 trainer jet destined to the Frecce Tricolori aerobatic team enters Venegono’s runway. | Source: Jacopo Castelli/@spotter_jaki A new livery As we reported on occasion of the rollout, the aircraft has been painted in the new livery announced in 2024, although it is still missing the number and the Frecce Tricolori markings on the tail. The new livery is designed by Pininfarina , the renowned Italian design and engineering firm famous for its work in the automotive industry, particularly in the design of luxury and high-performance vehicles. However, the new livery has been met by criticism by many aviation enthusiasts before of the many differences when compared with the current livery. In fact, this livery is characterized by a matte dark blue, instead of the glossy blue associated with the Frecce’s MB-339s . Additionally, a large white patch covers the dorsal area of the M-346, while a white line can be seen on the underside. This line will accompanied by the green and the red on separate sides to make up for the Italian flag’s colors, replacing the symmetric design used on the MB-339 . The underside of the first M-346 trainer jet destined to the Frecce Tricolori aerobatic team. | Source: Jacopo Castelli/@spotter_jaki When the livery was unveiled in 2024, statements mentioned it has been designed to highlight the Frecce Tricolori’s flight through a three-dimensional design, ensuring that there is always a recognizable graphic element capable of conveying a sense of speed and dynamism to the audience during the maneuvers. However, in addition to these aesthetic reasons, there are also functional reasons. Starting from the main color, the most criticized aspect, the darker, matte blue and the large use of white increase the M-346 ’s visual contrast against the clear sky and in overcast sky, respectively. Additionally, the asymmetry obtained on the underside with the green on the right side, the white in the middle and the red on the left allows the pilots to immediately identify the orientation and positioning of the aircraft during formation flight and maneuvers. A new ride for the Frecce Tricolori The M-346 Advanced Jet Trainer (T-346A in accordance with the Italian MOD Mission Design Series) was chosen as the successor of the team’s MB-339s in 2024. The decision was announced during an event celebrating the team’s return from their North America Tour 2024 . Visualizza questo post su Instagram Un post condiviso da Aplace2land – Capenti Fabrizio & Tiziano aviation photos (@aplace2land) On the same occasion, the service also presented the new livery designed by Pininfarina , which was applied to an aircraft towed in front of the guests attending the ceremony. A week later, the annual multiyear defense planning document (Documento Programmatico Pluriennale della Difesa), which reviews the military funding for 2024-2026, mentioned the acquisition of 20 additional M-346s by the Italian Air Force. The Frecce Tricolori would get 15 of those aircraft, while the remaining 5 will join the other 18 currently used for training by the 61st Wing and the International Flight Training School (IFTS). The team will thus receive ten aircraft for the main formation, plus the one of the commander and four spares. These aircraft will be in the same general configuration of the ones already in service, instead of the newer Block 20 aircraft . However, they will also have other customized features specific to their role in the aerobatic team. The first M-346 trainer jet destined to the Frecce Tricolori aerobatic team lines up for departure. | Source: Jacopo Castelli/@spotter_jaki Among these features are specific recording equipment and the smoke generators. The team uses a liquid composed of vaseline oil to which non-polluting pigments are added, sprayed near the engine’s exhaust to produce the colored smoke. The M-346s will replace the team’s aging MB-339s , which were adopted in 1982. The initial plan was to equip the Frecce Tricolori with the M-345 High Efficiency Trainer , chosen to replace the ItAF fleet of MB-339s, but the decision has been reverted. Thanks again to Jacopo Castelli for the photos he sent us, you can find more of his work on Instagram at @spotter_jaki .

title: ADL-Boundless study finds simple messaging aids American in identifying online antisemitism
body: The Anti-Defamation League (ADL) Center for Antisemitism Research (CAR) and educational organization Boundless released a new research study on Thursday, revealing that a brief message reminding young Americans that hatred of Jews is broadly rejected can significantly improve their ability to recognize and report online antisemitism.Jonathan Greenblatt, ADL's CEO and national director, explained that “young people are encountering antisemitism online every day, and too often they don't recognize it for what it is.”He added that “this research shows that something as simple as reminding people that hatred of Jews is not accepted by most Americans can move them to recognize it and speak up. That is a practical, scalable tool for educators, platforms, and community leaders.”The study, titled “Bridging the Gap: What Young Americans Miss About Online Antisemitism,” was conducted to examine how young adults interact with hateful online content and to test which educational approaches effectively influence recognition and reporting behavior.The study surveyed 7,499 Americans aged 18 to 44 nationwide between July 9 and July 17, using the opinion research firm Cint.The sample comprised 3,043 Gen Z participants (aged 18-29) and 4,456 Millennials (30-44), alongside 3,229 Democrats, 2,319 independents, and 1,951 Republicans.Participants were randomly assigned to read one of six short educational messages addressing antisemitism, ranging from neutral factual definitions and personal narratives, such as a story about a mother named Maya encountering a swastika near a school, to historical explanations of scapegoating, social norming, and broader prejudice – or to receive no message at all – before evaluating real examples of social media posts.Many young adults struggle to identify antisemitic content, study findsThe evaluated social media post examples included classical antisemitic tropes, such as religious slurs referencing the “synagogues of Satan,” right-wing posts targeting officials with accusations of “treason” over alleged allegiance to Israel, and contemporary rhetoric concerning Israel and Zionism from both the political Left and Right. The study also included non-ideological material and a racist control post featuring memes about Black achievements, to measure false positives.The findings showed that many young adults struggle to identify antisemitic content even when it is overt. Among the untreated control group, 22-29% disagreed that classical antisemitic posts were antisemitic. That difficulty increased when encountering contemporary antisemitism expressed through hostile language about Israel and Zionism, where disagreement rose to 32-37%.The study also measured participants' willingness to take action by reporting harmful material to social media platforms, finding that baseline readiness to report offensive posts was generally lower than overall recognition rates.To explore and test whether brief educational prompts could bridge the gap between spotting hate and taking action, the study evaluated six different interventions.Most messages produced little measurable change. However, the social norming message, which emphasized via survey data that 82% of Americans want online antisemitic hate speech removed and 77% want government action, yielded statistically significant improvements in both the ability to spot offensive material and the willingness to report it to platforms.Compared with individuals who saw no messages, those who read the social norming intervention were 6.1% more likely to recognize a contemporary nonpartisan antisemitic post and 5.6% more likely to report it. The intervention also led to a 6.9% increase in understanding offensive right-wing contemporary posts and a 5.9% increase in reporting classical left-wing antisemitism.“The impact of a short message that most Americans reject antisemitism was moderate, but when you consider how quick and easily scalable such a message is, this result is groundbreaking,” Matt Williams, vice president of the ADL's CAR said.Study identifies generational differences“Moving the needle 6% on recognizing and reporting antisemitic content doesn't seem like much for a room full of people but think of what a 6% reduction across millions could bring about.”The study also highlighted generational differences in how young adults respond to online hate. While Millennials were somewhat better than Gen Z at spotting antisemitic posts, Gen Z respondents who successfully identified antisemitism were more likely to report it – at 77% compared to 68% for Millennials.Williams told The Jerusalem Post that nevertheless, determining whether younger users view reporting toxic content as an expected baseline duty while older users see offensive posts through the lens of free expression remains a question for further study.The report identified distinct patterns among political independents. When presented with a disinformation awareness message explaining how antisemitism uses scapegoating and conspiracy theories to manipulate public anger, independents showed an 11% increase in recognizing classical right-wing antisemitism and about a 10% improvement in understanding contemporary antisemitism from both political sides. Furthermore, the research found that Democrats and Republicans were equally likely to recognize antisemitism regardless of whether it originated from their own political side.Based on these results, the report outlines several key actionable recommendations for educators, platform developers, and community leaders.The authors stressed that initiative leaders must prioritize recognition above all else, cautioning that young adults cannot respond to or report online antisemitism if they fail to recognize it in the first place.Interventions must also specifically focus on training individuals to identify contemporary forms of antisemitism, particularly when expressed through language surrounding Israel and Zionism.In parallel, organizations should avoid relying solely on generic educational content or emotional appeals, as brief exposures to standard informational text or perspective-taking narratives failed to yield significant shifts in behavior.Furthermore, funding and strategic outreach should actively invest in scalable social norming campaigns and expand testing around disinformation awareness. Reinforcing that antisemitism is broadly rejected by the public proved to be the single most effective tool for driving action, while teaching media manipulation techniques showed unique promise among political independents.Interventions must be tailored to target audiences to account for distinct demographic gaps, addressing Gen Z's primary challenge with content recognition alongside Millennials' action gap when deciding whether to report toxic posts.Aviva Klompas, co-founder and CEO of Boundless, told The Jerusalem Post that future efforts must look beyond simply documenting abuse. “We want to move beyond pointing out that antisemitism is a problem and figure out what actually works to address it,” she said.“When people see antisemitism online, particularly in posts with thousands of likes or shares, they may assume that those views are widely accepted. One of the most important findings is that reminding people that social media doesn't necessarily reflect public opinion and that most Americans reject antisemitism can make a real difference.”Klompas further spoke of the need for adaptive strategies, telling the Post, “We also want to keep exploring how to build resilience to manipulation and disinformation.“Our findings among political independents suggest that helping people recognize the techniques used to spread antisemitic conspiracy theories may be particularly effective. Perhaps the broader lesson is that we need to question our own assumptions about what works.“Just because a message resonates within the Jewish community doesn't mean it will persuade the audiences we're trying to reach. We need to test our approaches, learn from the evidence, and be prepared to adapt,” she said.Addressing practical applications for technology platforms, Williams told the Post that the ADL “continuously talks with and shares our research with social platforms,” while exploring ways to operationalize findings independently.

title: Germany’s Zverev becomes tennis world No. 1
body: Alexander Zverev accelerated his ascension to number one in the world rankings for the first time in his career on Thursday as he beat Tallon Griekspoor 6-4, 7-5 to reach the quarter-finals of the Vienna Open. The 29-year-old German was already assured of finishing the season top of the ATP rankings but, in the absence of current incumbent Jannik Sinner, two-time Grand Slam champion Zverev will now take that crown in next week’s updated standings after winning his opening two matches in the Austrian capital. Long seen as tennis’ nearly-man, Zverev has enjoyed a stellar 2026, breaking his major duck by picking up the titles at the French and US Opens. Now he has broken further ground by becoming only the 30th man to claim top spot since the rankings were first published in 1973. He will be aged 29 years and 196 days when Monday’s new rankings are published, making him the second-oldest first-time number one after Australian John Newcombe. Due to a knee injury Italy’s Sinner decided to end his season at the start of October, opening the way for Zverev to dethrone him. And the big-serving Hamburg native ensured he did just that ahead of the season-ending ATP Finals next month by seeing off Martin Landaluce and Griekspoor in his opening two matches in Vienna. Zverev needed to save four match points against Spain’s Landaluce in his first-round match on Tuesday, but was much more comfortable as he defeated Griekspoor in straight sets to write his name into the history books. He raced out of the blocks on Thursday, breaking the 30-year-old Dutchman in the very first game and then confidently serving his way into a one-set lead. The second frame went to 5-5 before Zverev pounced on Griekspoor’s serve to get his nose in front. The match met an unexpected stoppage as Zverev brought up match point when a smash off the German’s racquet caused part of the electronic board behind Griekspoor to malfunction. But once the umpire covered the problematic panel up with a towel, Zverev then sealed his new ranking with an unreturnable serve. title: Public companies double share of blockchain revenue since 2022: Report
body:
A new 1kx report finds that public companies are capturing a larger share of blockchain revenue, driven by institutional adoption and real-world applications.
Publicly traded companies accounted for 16% of blockchain industry revenue in 2026, more than double their 7% share in 2022, according to a new report from crypto investment firm 1kx.
The increase comes as overall blockchain revenue is projected to decline 28% year over year to roughly $100 billion in 2026. The report analyzed data from more than 2,600 protocols and earnings reports from 104 publicly traded companies through the third quarter.
The researchers attributed the growing share of public companies partly to new stock market listings, including stablecoin issuer Circle, which went public in 2025, and revenue growth among existing companies. The 10 largest publicly traded companies in the study doubled their blockchain-related revenue over the past three years.
Coinbase and Circle generated approximately $3.3 billion in combined blockchain-related revenue in the first half of 2026, according to 1kx, while publicly traded Bitcoin miners earned roughly $2 billion. Traditional financial firms, including JPMorgan, BlackRock, CME Group, Visa and Robinhood, accounted for another $1.1 billion collectively.
Revenue remains concentrated among a relatively small number of businesses. The six largest publicly traded companies accounted for roughly 50% to 60% of the group’s revenue, according to the report.
Related: BlackRock files for third Bitcoin ETF, still no Solana or XRP
The report also found that revenue from broader economic activity surpassed blockchain infrastructure revenue for the first time in the third quarter, reaching approximately $5.3 billion compared with $5.1 billion, according to 1kx.
The category, which includes tokenized assets, payments and prediction markets, grew 58% year over year in the first half of 2026. Together with institutional adoption, it accounted for 33% of total blockchain revenue in the third quarter, with the report projecting a 30% share for the full year.
Institutional and broader economic activity to reach 30% of blockchain revenue in 2026. Source: 1kx report
RWA.xyz data shows the value of distributed tokenized real-world assets rose roughly 51% over the past year, from $26.16 billion in October 2025 to $39.54 billion as of Thursday. Tokenized equities grew even faster, surging 471% over the same period to $3.77 billion.

title: Alberta referendum saw 70.4% turnout — highest voter participation in decades
body:
The historic Alberta referendum on separation saw voters trek to the polls in the highest numbers in decades.
That’s according to official results from Elections Alberta , which peg voter turnout on the separation question at 70.4 per cent.
The turnout is the highest for a provincewide vote since at least 1975, but it fell short of breaking the record of 81.8 per cent turnout seen in the 1935 general election.
Last week’s vote was on 10 questions, with three-quarters of voters saying they want to stay in Canada rather than hold a second, binding referendum on separation.
The other nine questions saw voters approve the province pursuing changes to immigration policies while rejecting questions urging them to approve the province taking more action to wrest power from the federal government.
The government has said the earliest Albertans could expect to see legislation on immigration is next spring.

title: 5th Edition of Ghana Corporate Brands Conference and Honours launched
body: Maven Communications is set to bring together C-suite executives, brand and marketing leaders, communications practitioners, customer experience professionals, academics and policymakers for the fifth edition of the Ghana Corporate Brands Conference and Honours, a platform focused on the future of branding in Ghana’s evolving business environment. Under the theme, “Shaping the Future of Corporate Branding in Ghana: Building Brands with Strategic Intent, Inspiring Excellence, and Earning Lasting Trust”, the event is expected to convene key voices from business, academia and industry to discuss emerging branding trends, reputation management, customer expectations and the growing role of technology in shaping public perception. The conference comes at a time when organisations face increasing pressure to strengthen stakeholder trust, differentiate themselves in competitive markets and remain relevant in an era defined by digital influence and instant access to information. Responding to a changing branding landscape Ghanaian consumers are widely perceived to have a preference for foreign goods and services, a perception rooted in the country’s early exposure to international trade, when merchant vessels arriving on the shores of the then Gold Coast introduced local consumers to foreign products. Today, however, the marketplace has become significantly more complex. Consumers are better informed, more connected and more influential than ever before. Through digital platforms and social media, they can compare brands, evaluate customer experiences and make purchasing decisions based on information from virtually anywhere in the world. For organisations operating in Ghana, this presents both a challenge and an opportunity. While competition extends far beyond national borders, businesses also have greater opportunities to build brands that inspire confidence, foster loyalty and create lasting value. Against this backdrop, the Ghana Corporate Brands Conference and Honours seeks to stimulate meaningful conversations around brand leadership, reputation management and sustainable business growth. Brand building beyond products and services Speaking on behalf of Maven Communications, Managing Director and Event Director Seth (Jojo) Danso Asante said successful brands are now defined by far more than the products and services they offer. “The business landscape is evolving rapidly. Brands are no longer defined solely by their products or services. Brand perception, customer expectations, digital influence, reputation and commercial performance are increasingly interconnected,” he said. “Changing consumer behaviour, rapid technological advancement, social media, artificial intelligence, digital journalism and greater access to information have fundamentally changed how organisations build brands.” According to him, organisations must adopt a more deliberate and integrated approach to brand management to remain competitive and credible in today’s marketplace. From reputation management to reputation leadership As stakeholder expectations continue to evolve, reputation is increasingly becoming a leadership issue rather than a function handled exclusively by communications or public relations teams. Every customer interaction, employee experience, leadership decision, digital engagement and public statement contributes to how an organisation is perceived. Industry leaders increasingly recognise that brands are ultimately judged by the experiences they create, the promises they fulfil, the trust they earn and the value they deliver. The conference will therefore examine the intersection of brand strategy, marketing, communications, customer experience, reputation management and business performance, offering practical insights into building brands that are resilient, distinctive and commercially sustainable. Honouring excellence in corporate and product branding Running alongside the conference is the Ghana Corporate Brands Honours, an initiative established to recognise organisations and individuals that have demonstrated a sustained commitment to building, managing and strengthening corporate and product brands. The honours will celebrate excellence in areas such as corporate identity, product positioning, market visibility, brand consistency, consumer engagement and strategic brand development. Recognition through the honours provides a benchmark of achievement and highlights institutions whose branding efforts continue to contribute to the growth and advancement of Ghana’s corporate landscape.

title: Specialist shortage persists as Manitoba gains ground on doctor recruitment
body:
A new report from the organization that represents doctors in Manitoba suggests the province continues to close the gap on physician recruitment.
But Doctors Manitoba said more work is needed to attract specialists and find physicians in rural areas.
Annual data from the group released on Thursday show the province now has 235 physicians for every 100,000 residents.
The organization said that’s a 4.5 per cent increase compared with the previous year and comes close to the national average.
The shortage is nearly half the size it was three years ago, when it reached its peak.
“This is a huge amount of progress in a relatively short period of time over that three-year time gap and it deserves recognition … but the progress is uneven,” Dr. Alon Altman, president of Doctors Manitoba, told reporters.
The report was compiled using information from the Canadian Institute for Health Information, the College of Physicians and Surgeons of Manitoba and an annual Doctors Manitoba physician survey.
It determined Manitoba is short 217 specialists. Some of the areas impacted include emergency and cardiology medicine; surgical specialties such as urology; and nuclear medicine and radiology.
Altman said these shortages contribute to longer waits for consultations, tests and surgeries.
“These aren’t just numbers; this affects the entire system,” he said.
The shortage has prompted some patients to travel out of province and in some situations pay out of pocket to receive faster care, said Altman.
Most of the physician growth seen elsewhere is fueled by international recruits, including some doctors the province hired from overseas, the organization said.
The province has said that focused recruitment efforts in the United Kingdom over the last two years have resulted in 52 hires. Another 42 physicians have moved from elsewhere in Canada.
While recruitment efforts have improved, retention strategies are needed. The report found 40 per cent of physicians are considering retiring, leaving the province or reducing their clinical hours in the next three years.
Kathleen Cook, health critic for the Opposition Progressive Conservatives, said the NDP government needs to address working conditions, including burnout, isolation and low morale, to keep Manitoba a competitive market.
“Bringing more doctors into the system is a good thing only insofar as we’re actually keeping them. If we’re losing them further down the line, then it’s going to be a major problem for Manitoba,” she said.
Health Minister Uzoma Asagwara acknowledged more work is needed to tackle wait times for emergency rooms and surgeries.
“Reports like this one from Doctors Manitoba help chart a path forward, and we’re going to keep working,” said Asagwara.
Doctors Manitoba is urging the government invest in equipment and technology, reduce administrative red tape and include physicians in decision-making that affects medical care.

title: NAIMOS targets suppliers of equipment used in illegal mining in Aowin and Enchi
body: The National Anti-Illegal Mining Operations Secretariat (NAIMOS) has announced plans to target individuals and businesses manufacturing or selling equipment used in illegal mining as part of efforts to curb galamsey in Aowin and Enchi in the Western North Region. Director of Operations at NAIMOS, Colonel S. K. Appiah, said the taskforce would focus on the supply chain supporting illegal mining activities in addition to enforcement against operators. Speaking during a tour of the taskforce’s operations in the area, he said the objective was to enforce the law and halt the destruction of the environment without unnecessarily undermining legitimate livelihoods. “We are not here to destroy livelihoods, but to enforce the law,” he said. “A lot of people have gone out of their way, destroying water, destroying forest reserves.” Aowin and Enchi are endowed with gold deposits, forest reserves and major water bodies, including the Tano and Bia rivers. However, illegal mining activities have raised concerns about damage to water bodies, agricultural lands and forest ecosystems. Colonel Appiah warned that continued environmental degradation could have serious consequences for future generations, urging residents to support efforts to stop illegal mining. “I always tell them that if their predecessors had done it this way, we’d not have been alive to meet it as it is. And we count on your support to ensure that we are able to curb illegal mining within this district,” he said. He expressed confidence that sustained enforcement and community cooperation could help restore areas damaged by illegal mining. “So that going into the future we’ll be able to recover the lands, recover the water, and then we’ll see marked improvement in the levels,” he added. The planned crackdown extends the focus beyond miners to businesses and individuals who manufacture, distribute or sell equipment used in illegal operations. NAIMOS is expected to continue its activities in the Western North Region, targeting those involved in illegal mining and the supply networks that support it. Illegal mining, commonly known as galamsey, remains a major environmental concern in Ghana because of its effects on forests, rivers and farmland. Although successive governments have pledged to tackle the practice, enforcement and accountability remain central to efforts to address the problem. The effectiveness of the latest operation will depend on the extent to which authorities can enforce the law consistently and disrupt the networks sustaining illegal mining.

title: Palisades nuclear plant will restart before end of year, Chris Wright says during visit to 'zombie reactor'
body: Despite a string of safety incidents, the shuttered Palisades nuclear plant in Michigan might be restarted before the end of this year, according to US Energy Secretary Chris Wright . Mr Wright visited the reactor owned by Holtec International that was shut down in 2022 but is now in the process of restarting. The plant has become a symbol for the nuclear energy sector in the US, which is experiencing something of a renaissance due in part to the heavy electricity needs of data centres. On Thursday, the US Energy Secretary said that Palisades "would be back running before the end of this year" while speaking with reporters during a tour of the reactor. "It will be 800MW of additional, reliable and secure energy," he added, concluding the news conference by taking shots at the Democratic Party. "This is a reversal of the stuff Democrats did for years, doing everything they can to stand in the way of energy production and the contrast could not be more stark." Thanks to President Trump, Michigan’s Palisades Nuclear Plant is set to restart later this year. It will lower costs for millions of Michiganders, create jobs and prevent blackouts. We are all in on energy addition! pic.twitter.com/kCBekgjzgb — Secretary Chris Wright (@SecretaryWright) October 29, 2026 But the restart has its critics. Kevin Kamps , executive director for environmental advocacy group Don't Waste Michigan, hit back shortly after Mr Wright's visit to Palisades. "Once they restart this zombie reactor , all bets are off," Mr Kamps said, calling the reactor by a name used by critics of restarting decommissioned nuclear plants. "They are playing radioactive Russian roulette on the Lake Michigan shore, wasting billions of dollars of state and federal taxpayer money to do so, and they are risking a Chornobyl- or Fukushima-scale catastrophe, putting in peril the Great Lakes, the Great Lakes State, and beyond." Michael Keegan , another director of Don’t Waste Michigan, said the "public relations slathering of icing on this rancid cake is a whitewash. Mr Wright's visit follows an incident that cemented the concerns of those who have voiced opposition to the plant's restart. In September, a nuclear fuel assembly was tipped during a refuelling process at the plant. The US Nuclear Regulatory Commission said no radiation had been released. Shortly after workers successfully retrieved the tipped nuclear fuel assembly, Holtec described the recovery as a "remarkable demonstration of technical ingenuity and precision manufacturing". Still, it was yet another blemish on the plant's record. In 2012, an NRC report warned about the work culture at the plant, where it said safety concerns were routinely dismissed. In 2016, when the plant was owned by Entergy, security staff were placed on leave for failing to properly follow fire prevention protocol. And in October 2025, a worker at Palisades fell off a refuelling bridge into a pool of water, though was not seriously injured. The NRC sent a letter to Holtec this month following an inspection that determined that although Palisades maintained a safety-conscious work environment overall, “a chilled work environment” existed in the supply chain and quality assurance departments. “Employees in these two work departments are hesitant to raise safety concerns using all available avenues without fear of retaliation,” the NRC said. Patrick O’Brien, Holtec's director of government affairs and communications, previously told The National that Holtec was “taking actions to address these issues and will continue our work to maintain and strengthen a healthy safety-conscious work environment”. He also said that safety was of the utmost priority, adding that the reactor would "return to service when all required work is complete and all federal requirements and industry standards are met".

title: Awujale succession: DSS invites Fusengbuwa ruling house leaders
body: By James Ogunnaike, Abeokuta The Department of State Services (DSS) in Ogun State has reportedly invited three leaders of the Fusengbuwa ruling house over the alleged sale of expression-of-interest forms to princes seeking to become the next Awujale of Ijebuland. Those reportedly invited are the Chairman of the ruling house, Otunba Abdulateef Owoyemi; the deputy chairman, Otunba Dokun Ajidagba; and the vice chairman, Prof. Fassy Yusuf. The invitation comes amid an ongoing dispute over the selection of a new Awujale following the death of the previous monarch, Oba Sikiru Adetona, in July 2025, at the age of 91, after 65 years on the throne. A letter circulating online, purportedly signed by one Yemi Oloto, directed the three ruling house leaders to appear before the State Director of Security at the DSS office in Oke-Mosan, Abeokuta, on Thursday, October 29, 2026, at 4 p.m. The letter, which indicated that the meeting was connected with an investigation into the sale of expression-of-interest forms to princes interested in the vacant stool, read in part: “I am directed to invite you for a meeting with the State Director of Security (SDS), Department of State Services (DSS), Ogun State, Oke-Mosan, Abeokuta, today, 29th October, 2026, 1600 hours (4 p.m.). “The meeting is in furtherance of investigating activities in respect of the sale of expression-of-interest forms to interested princes for the vacant stool of Awujale of Ijebuland.” The letter further stated that an officer had been designated at the main gate to facilitate the invitees’ entry into the premises, before concluding with the director’s best wishes. When contacted, Prof. Yusuf confirmed receiving the invitation but said he was in Abuja attending to a matter before the Supreme Court and would therefore be unable to honour it. The professor of Mass Communication and lawyer said: “I just received the letter from the DSS not long ago, but I am in Abuja attending to a matter at the Supreme Court. I have discountenanced their letter.” Similarly, Ajidagba confirmed receiving the invitation on Thursday afternoon, saying it was delivered at about 2:30 p.m. with instructions to report at the DSS office by 4:30 p.m. He, however, questioned the timing of the invitation, arguing that matters relating to the succession process were already before the courts. “I received the DSS invitation on Thursday at about 2:30 p.m., and I was told to report at their office by 4:30 p.m. There was, however, no way I could honour such an invitation when all of these matters are already in court. The status quo must be allowed to remain; that is the position of the law,” he said. There was no immediate confirmation from the DSS on the reported invitations or the allegations prompting them. The latest development comes against the backdrop of previous engagements between security agencies and stakeholders in the Awujale succession process. Security agencies, including the Ogun State Police Command, had reportedly summoned nine kingmakers in Ijebu-Ode and the three Fusengbuwa ruling house leaders on two occasions to appear at the police headquarters in Eleweran, Abeokuta. The invitations were said to be connected with allegations of bribery and financial inducement in the selection of a new Awujale and paramount ruler of Ijebuland. Owoyemi has repeatedly denied wrongdoing in connection with the succession process. The three ruling house leaders have also instituted legal proceedings against the Ogun State government over the suspension of the selection process, which has remained stalled since January 2026. In August, the Fusengbuwa ruling house leaders approached the Ogun State High Court sitting in Ijebu-Ode, seeking orders compelling the completion of the process for selecting the next Awujale and paramount ruler of Ijebuland. The suit, numbered HCJ/149/2026 and dated August 21, 2026, was instituted by Owoyemi, Ajidagba and Yusuf. The defendants include Ogun State Governor, Dapo Abiodun; the Attorney-General and Commissioner for Justice, Mr Oluwasina Ogungbade (SAN); the Ogun State Executive Council; the Commissioner for Local Government and Chieftaincy Affairs, Ganiyu Hamzat; and the Secretary of Ijebu-Ode Local Government. Also joined as defendants are members of the Awujale Afobaje/Kingmakers Council, including Olorogun Sonny Kuku, Chief Rasheed Adesanya, Chief Oluwaranti Lekan Osifeso, Chief Jimi Lawal, Chief Abimbola Okenla, Chief Kunle Ogunade, Chief Agboola Alausa, Chief Adebisi Adaran and Chief Ayotunde Ola Odulaja. Among other reliefs, the claimants are asking the court to determine whether the state government had the legal authority to order or facilitate the alleged entry into and locking of the Awujale palace on January 20, 2026. According to the claimants, the action was intended to physically prevent the kingmakers from convening and concluding the statutory process for selecting a successor to the late monarch. The dispute has further complicated efforts to fill the vacant traditional stool, with the government maintaining that the process must be conducted peacefully and in accordance with the applicable procedures. Meanwhile, Governor Abiodun has assured the people of Ijebuland that a new Awujale will emerge before May 29, 2027. The governor gave the assurance on Tuesday at the Ogun East Senatorial District stakeholders’ meeting in Ijebu-Ode, where he engaged representatives of various interest groups on traditional affairs, governance and the economic prospects of the district. According to a statement issued on Wednesday, Abiodun reaffirmed his administration’s commitment to ensuring a smooth and acceptable succession process. “On the succession process for the revered Awujale stool, Abiodun assured the people that his administration was committed to facilitating a smooth, peaceful and widely acceptable process leading to the emergence of a new monarch,” the statement said. The governor acknowledged the significance of the Awujale institution to the cultural heritage, identity and unity of Ijebuland, urging residents to remain calm and patient while the necessary procedures were being concluded. He added that his administration was giving the matter the attention it deserved to ensure that the process was completed peacefully and that the eventual emergence of a new monarch enjoyed the acceptance and support of the people. The Awujale stool became vacant in July 2025 following the death of Oba Adetona, who ruled for 65 years and was widely regarded as one of Nigeria’s longest-reigning traditional rulers. The Ogun State Government halted the succession process in January 2026, citing petitions from security agencies and other stakeholders. The suspension followed an earlier halt in December 2025 over procedural concerns. A total of 95 aspirants—94 princes and one princess—reportedly emerged from the Fusengbuwa ruling house nomination exercise held in Ijebu-Ode in December 2025 before the government suspended further proceedings. The post Awujale succession: DSS invites Fusengbuwa ruling house leaders appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: Italian Army CH-47F crashes in Bosnia, killing at least four
body:
An Italian Army CH-47F Chinook crashed in Bosnia and Herzegovina on Thursday, October 29, killing at least four people and injuring 11 others during an operation in support of the European Union Force (EUFOR) Althea mission.
The helicopter went down in the Gorice area, near Brčko in northeastern Bosnia and Herzegovina. All 15 people aboard were Italian, according to local authorities. Initial reports indicated three fatalities, but a fourth person later died from injuries sustained in the crash.
Footage circulating online shows the Chinook rotating while descending rapidly before disappearing behind trees. The cause of the accident remains unknown.
The Italian Ministry of Defense confirmed that one of its helicopters had crashed while operating as part of EUFOR Althea and said the circumstances were being investigated. EUFOR also confirmed fatalities and serious injuries but had not released a detailed casualty count.
No civilians were injured and no civilian property or infrastructure was damaged, according to EUFOR.
The helicopter was an ICH-47F operated by the Italian Army Aviation, although its military serial has not been identified.
Italy has maintained an Army Aviation detachment with EUFOR in Bosnia and Herzegovina since January 2026. The contingent is provided by the 4th Army Aviation Regiment "Altair" and operates CH-47F Chinooks and AB-205 helicopters.
The aviation detachment supports EUFOR operations with missions including troop and cargo transport, reconnaissance, support for ground forces and training activities.
The ICH-47F is the Italian Army version of Boeing's tandem-rotor CH-47F. The aircraft involved in Thursday's accident was destroyed, according to the Aviation Safety Network, which has not listed its registration or manufacturer serial number.
EUFOR said a full investigation into the accident would be conducted.

title: Brawl in Armenia’s parliament: Pashinyan says he “supports” his party colleagues
body: Pashinyan on the brawl in Armenia’s parliament Armenian Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan said at his weekly briefing that he condemned violence but supported MPs from his own party. He added that being in the opposition “does not give you the right to get cheeky”. Pashinyan was commenting on a brawl in the National Assembly between MPs from the ruling Civil Contract party and the opposition Strong Armenia faction. As usual, the parliamentary session was broadcast live, showing MPs punching and kicking each other. Deputy Speaker Vaagn Aleksanyan even threw a chair towards opposition MPs. «Я приветствую и поддерживаю действия депутатов фракции “Гражданский договор”. [Швыряли] cтул или что-то еще — это была адекватная и правильная реакция», — подчеркнул премьер-министр Пашинян. Он заявил, что тем, кто попытается применить насилие, власти «обломают руки». По его мнению, обязанность властей — не допустить в стране вседозволенности. Защитница прав человека не согласилась с позицией Пашиняна. Анаит Манасян отметила, что подобные инциденты лишь укрепляют в обществе настроения, оправдывающие насилие. «Парламент должен быть площадкой для демократических дискуссий, а не “полем боя”», — заявила она. ‘Another attempt is being prepared to deprive Armenia of its independence’ — Pashinyan ‘Transparent and competitive, but also cause for concern’: PACE report on Armenia’s elections Armenian citizenship to become harder and five times more expensive under Interior Ministry draft Details: What happened in parliament Tensions in the chamber began during a speech by Taron Chakhoyan, an MP from the ruling Civil Contract party. He raised the issue of corruption and mentioned former Armenian president and opposition Armenia bloc leader Robert Kocharyan and his associates. Chakhoyan then addressed Narek Karapetyan, head of the Strong Armenia faction, and included his relatives on the list of people he accused of corruption. Karapetyan’s uncle, prominent businessman Samvel Karapetyan, faces accusations of large-scale money laundering involving the abuse of official powers. “People mired in corruption are now lecturing us about corruption and fake news, claiming that their relatives have supposedly become targets of [government pressure]. Mr Karapetyan, it’s not my fault that your entire family is involved in politics, including your uncle, father and cousin,” Chakhoyan said. He continued listing his accusations and reminded MPs that Narek Karapetyan’s cousin had once proposed setting up a government ministry to “satisfy all women”. “You still haven’t apologised for that,” Chakhoyan said. In February this year, Sargis Karapetyan, Samvel Karapetyan’s son, made a controversial statement : “In a strong Armenia [that is, after the Strong Armenia party, led by his father, comes to power], there will be no dissatisfied women.” He made the remark during a podcast discussion about ways to address demographic problems. Asked about the possible creation of a “ministry of sex”, Karapetyan said: “As far as I know, you can’t solve demographic problems without sex.” Many in Armenia considered his comments an offensive remark directed at women. After Chakhoyan’s remarks, Strong Armenia faction leader Narek Karapetyan shouted something from his seat, addressing Chakhoyan with the familiar and dismissive term “ara”. Chakhoyan retorted: “You’re ‘ara’ from head to toe!” The verbal exchange escalated into a fight. Parliament Speaker Ruben Rubinyan urged those present to calm down. However, he did not suspend the session or stop its live broadcast. “I’m not going to suspend the session. I want everyone to see all of this,” he said. Tensions continued to rise. Deputy Speaker Vaagn Aleksanyan threw a chair towards opposition MPs, prompting Rubinyan to finally call a recess. The altercation continued for some time outside the chamber. Armenia’s anti-corruption campaign: law on confiscating illicit assets takes effect Expert analysis of the law’s provisions, the need to prevent political selectivity in its application, and whether confiscated property is genuinely being returned to the people. After the recess, Taron Chakhoyan apologised to everyone who had witnessed the scenes in the chamber for the opposition’s behaviour. He described the opposition MPs’ actions as “hooliganism” and suggested that they had planned the incident in advance. “If you think you can attack an MP and go unpunished, provoke a fight and escape the consequences, that won’t happen. You have just seen that for yourselves. You can’t provoke a fight and then run out of the chamber without getting hit back,” the MP said. The ruling party blamed the opposition for the incident. According to the parliament speaker, Narek Karapetyan tried to hit Taron Chakhoyan, but another opposition MP, Garnik Davtyan, struck the first blow. The opposition offered the opposite account, holding the ruling faction responsible. “Ruben Rubinyan bears full responsibility for what happened. He encouraged provocations by the instigator, Taron Chakhoyan, and did nothing to intervene,” said Marianna Gahramanyan, an MP from Strong Armenia. “We will break their arms” — Pashinyan The prime minister told journalists that he had seen footage showing how the incident began. “If anyone thinks they can raise a hand against a member of the National Assembly, hit them or do anything else, we will break that arm. I’m saying this plainly, without beating around the bush.” Journalists asked, “With a chair?” Pashinyan replied: “If necessary, with a chair. They should know their place. There are limits to everything.” Pashinyan said opposition MPs were “reaping what they sow” because they had so far failed to respond appropriately or condemn the behaviour of their fellow MPs. “That is how it will always be from now on. Whenever they behave like this, they will get the same response,” he stressed. “Eradicate violence” — Human Rights Defender The Office of the Human Rights Defender issued a statement on the parliamentary incident. It said that any acts of violence by public officials, including MPs, help justify violence and lead society to regard it as a normal way to resolve disagreements. The Human Rights Defender called for an end to: Behaviour that involves or implies the use of violence. Any statements that justify violence. “This incident must be subject to a proper investigation conducted in accordance with established legal procedures,” Human Rights Defender Anahit Manasyan said. title: New tactical comms system for US ground troops aims to break network silos
body: General Dynamics revealed a new artificial intelligence-enabled, portable communications system on Thursday called the Vion, a Mission Partner Environment solution. Although its basic purpose is to give ground troops a suitcase-sized platform to exchange messages and files, the company said its real value is how it connects allied systems. In an interview with Military Times, Jason Myers, vice president of defense agencies at General Dynamics Information Technology, explained that Vion can help ground troops quickly establish secure connections with a command center and coalition forces from remote environments. Using open architecture and AI, he said Vion will connect with outside networks, adapt to or patch connections and translate written messages, voice memos, videos and more, all while maintaining zero-trust cybersecurity protections . “We wanted to provide an all-encompassing offering, but we didn’t want to lock somebody into an offering or not be able to use where they’ve already invested,” Myers said. He added that most organizations want a custom communications kit, and most companies aim to provide platforms that only work with proprietary equipment and software. But those things can make it challenging and expensive to update or upgrade systems. “What we wanted to do is say, ‘Yes, we’re going to use proven technologies,’ but as new things come out, we are absolutely ripping and replacing those, and how to do that securely, in that modular architecture, is really, really different than how things are being done today,” he said. According to the company, GDIT participated in a Joint Staff J6-led demonstration called Olympus Fires, where the Defense Information Systems Agency , or DISA, explored ways to improve the Coalition Information Environment , or CIE, which it described as “a modernized architecture built on the principles of Zero Trust and data centricity.” At a panel discussion in June, U.S. Army Lt. Col. David Courter, DISA’s Combatant Command Integration and Plans chief, explained the goal of the event was to “broker and federate our environments together without replicating a new environment every time.” Explaining the need for the CIE solutions, Jason Martin, DISA’s Component Acquisition Executive, referenced a friendly fire incident in March , in which Kuwaiti air defenses mistakenly shot down three U.S. F-15E Strike Eagle fighter jets. “We’ve spent the past 50 years building siloed networks, siloed applications and siloed environments to collaborate internally with our own data. We can no longer do that,” Martin said. “We have to converge networks. We have to plug and play. We have to talk to one another … We have to operate and maintain command and control with a single voice.” Myers said GDIT is currently working through the acquisitions process for Vion but declined to say with whom. However, he said he thinks Vion, in terms of service, will “have a very long life in where it can add value to the mission.”

title: Ukraine war latest: 'Russia's mass murder' — Deadly Russian strikes on Dnipro, Chernihiv, Kremenchuk
body:
Russian forces struck a train platform at Dnipro railway station on the morning of Oct. 29, killing at least 14 people and wounding at least 14 more, authorities said.
A passenger train was preparing to depart the platform for Zaporizhzhia when the station was attacked by a Russian jet-powered drone, Ukrainian Railways wrote on social media.
The brazen daytime attack was followed in close succession by deadly strikes against civilians in Chernihiv and Kremenchuk.
The strikes on civilians come not only in the middle of a scheduled local ceasefire in Kherson Oblast, agreed to by Kyiv and Moscow to help evacuate and deliver aid to the residents of the occupied city of Oleshky, but also ahead of the first trilateral "peace negotiations" mediated by the United States since February this year.
According to Ukraine's Air Force, Dnipro was attacked around 11:00 a.m. by four Russian jet-powered drones, three of which were downed by Ukrainian air defense before reaching their targets.
Despite the air raid alert and announcements of a heightened threat, people remained on the platform, Ukrainian Railways said.
Passengers were told to evacuate from the stationary train around ten minutes before the strike, with station and train staff checking each train car one by one.
At 11:29 a.m., Dnipropetrovsk Oblast governor Oleksandr Hanzha reported that medics were already at the scene of the attack, providing first aid.
"A horrific Russian attack on Dnipro train station," President Volodymyr Zelensky wrote on social media in response to the attack. "The Russians used a drone to attack a platform where a regular commuter train and a regular passenger train were standing."
"How many such terrorist attacks has Russia carried out on our people after lifting sanctions on some Russian oligarchs and energy companies instead of de-escalating."
Latvian Foreign Minister Baiba Braze described the attack on Dnipro as "mass murder."
Following the Russian attack on Dnipro, 25,000 people in the city and surrounding Oblast were left without electricity, Hanzha said in the afternoon.
Later in the day, Dnipro Mayor Borys Filatov reported that a Russian drone struck the dormitory of a vocational school in Dnipro, setting the entire fifth floor on fire. There were no injuries, Filatov said, as the students had managed to reach the shelter before the strike.
Throughout the day, Russian attacks across Dnipropetrovsk Oblast injured four more people, including a 15-year-old girl, Hanzha said in an evening statement .
Elsewhere across Ukraine, the cities of Chernihiv and Kremenchuk were also targeted by daytime Russian attacks.
Around noon, Russian forces struck the center of Chernihiv in northern Ukraine with Banderol cruise missiles, killing two 15-year-old girls, regional governor Viacheslav Chaus said.
At least 25 more people were injured in the attack, including four children, the youngest one 10-months-old, Chaus later said .
Meanwhile, in the city of Kremenchuk in Poltava Oblast, at least three people were killed and 32 injured, including six children and two people still in critical condition, after Russian drones struck an apartment building in a residential area, according to local authorities . Oct. 30 has been declared a day of mourning in Poltava Oblast.
Ukraine's Navy destroyed two Russian Su-34 fighter-bomber jets in a strike against the Marinovka military airfield in Russia's Volgograd Oblast, using domestically produced Neptune missiles, the Navy reported on Oct. 29.
The aircraft were destroyed at the base of Russia's 11th Mixed Aviation Regiment near the settlement of Oktyabrsky, according to the Navy. The regiment belongs to the 4th Mixed Aviation Division of Russia's 4th Air and Air Defense Forces Army. The Navy did not provide any visual confirmation of the strike. The Kyiv Independent could not independently verify the claim.
Later on Oct. 29, President Volodymyr Zelensky confirmed the destruction of the two Su-34 jets, adding that Ukrainian forces had also hit a Russian Iskander missile launcher.
The Su-34 is one of Russia's main aircraft used to launch guided aerial bombs against Ukrainian cities, frontline settlements, and military positions. Strikes against these aircraft could weaken Russia's ability to carry out such attacks, while replacing the losses requires significant time and resources.
Russia had approximately 140 Su-34 fighter-bombers of various modifications in service as of Oct. 22, including the modernized Su-34M, Ukraine's military intelligence agency (HUR) reported on Oct. 29.
According to the agency, Russia has lost 43 Su-34 aircraft destroyed and another seven damaged since the start of its full-scale invasion of Ukraine.
"Such losses are quite significant for the aggressor's aircraft fleet, whose restoration requires a lengthy production cycle, substantial financial resources, and specialized industrial cooperation," HUR said.
The agency estimated that Russia can manufacture approximately 14 to 18 Su-34 aircraft annually, meaning the number of destroyed aircraft is equivalent to roughly 2.5–3 years of production.
Demining of designated routes in Russian-occupied Oleshky in Kherson Oblast has been completed, and a humanitarian convoy is ready to depart, Ukraine's Human Rights Commissioner Dmytro Lubinets announced on Oct. 29.
The convoy is expected to arrive at the city's central hospital, where humanitarian assistance will be provided to residents, Lubinets said.
Residents wishing to leave the city will be able to do so until 2:00 p.m. local time, with security measures arranged for their evacuation. Humanitarian aid distribution is scheduled to begin after 2:30 p.m., according to the ombudsman.
Delegations from Ukraine, Russia, and the United States have gathered to coordinate the next steps of the mission, with journalists from all three countries also present, Lubinets said.
The mission is being carried out jointly with Russian Human Rights Commissioner Yana Lantratova, with mediation and coordination by U.S. first lady Melania Trump.
"Our shared goal is to deliver humanitarian aid to civilians and facilitate the safe departure of everyone who wishes to leave the city," Lubinets said.
The operation follows a temporary ceasefire in and around Oleshky, announced by the White House on Oct. 23 and subsequently confirmed by Ukraine and Russia. The pause in fighting, which began on Oct. 27, is expected to remain in effect until Nov. 1 to allow aid deliveries, mine clearance, and civilian evacuations.
Ukrainian forces have struck a Russian military facility used to launch long-range attack drones at Ukraine, the General Staff said on Oct. 29.
The overnight attack targeted the Russian drone base near Navlya in Bryansk Oblast, around 70 kilometers from the Ukrainian border.
According to the General Staff, the strikes damaged a storage facility for Russian long-range Geran-type drones, as well as fuel and lubricant storage facilities and the 'drone port' itself.
Ukrainian media and open-source intelligence (OSINT) groups have tracked Russia's building of several large 'airfields' designed for unmanned systems and built across Russia's western border areas.
The building of these new 'drone ports' reflects Moscow's growing investment in long-range attack drones as a long-term strategic tool, which can be used both against Ukraine or against countries on NATO's eastern flank.
The Oct. 29 attack was the second strike on the Navlya facility, with the first being on Aug. 3, also targeting launch and storage facilities.
The United Nations has appointed a Russian diplomat to a senior position overseeing mine action, drawing criticism from Ukraine as the country continues to clear hundreds of thousands of explosive devices left behind by Russia's war.
U.N. Secretary-General Antonio Guterres announced the appointment of Gleb Desyatnikov as assistant secretary-general for mine action and police in the Department of Peace Operations on Oct. 27.
Desyatnikov has served as Russia's ambassador to Jordan since 2018, including throughout Moscow's full-scale invasion of Ukraine. According to the U.N., he has more than 35 years of experience in international relations and security affairs, including previous positions at Russia's Foreign Ministry.
"Moscow has mined the United Nations," Ukrainian Foreign Ministry spokesperson Heorhii Tykhyi wrote on X on Oct. 29, criticizing the decision.
"Entrusting this responsibility to a representative of the aggressor state is deeply troubling and undermines trust in the United Nations," he added.
The appointment comes as Ukraine faces one of the world's largest demining challenges, with Russian mines and unexploded ordnance threatening civilians and complicating the recovery of agricultural land and infrastructure.
In southern Kherson Oblast, demining teams have neutralized 300,691 explosive devices on the Ukrainian-controlled right bank since the start of clearance operations, according to the regional military administration .
Between Oct. 22 and 28 alone, specialists surveyed 602.8 hectares (1,490 acres) and neutralized 471 explosive devices, the administration reported on Oct. 29. Authorities said 74.5% of the territory designated for clearance on the region's right bank has now been cleared.
A Russian lieutenant general has been charged in absentia with ordering the strike on the Kharkiv Oblast museum dedicated to 18th-century philosopher Hryhorii Skovoroda, the Prosecutor General reported on Oct. 29.
On May 6, 2022, a Russian missile struck the museum, located in the village of Skovorodynivka, some 55 kilometers (about 35 miles) from the regional capital. The strike did not completely destroy the museum, but left it in serious disrepair.
According to the Prosecutor General, the Russian lieutenant general who ordered the attack is originally from the village of Chuhuiv in Kharkiv Oblast and commands Russia's 6th Guards Air and Air Defense Forces Army.
"The (lieutenant) general knew for certain that he was attacking not a military target but a monument of Ukrainian culture. Despite this, he gave the combat order to destroy it," the Prosecutor General wrote .
Skovoroda is considered one of the most influential philosophers in Ukrainian intellectual history. His written works are vital contributions to the Ukrainian Baroque and Enlightenment traditions. The building that housed the museum was once the estate where Skovoroda spent his final years and died in 1794.
Russia has repeatedly targeted Ukraine's cultural heritage since the start of the full-scale war. As of September 2026, 2,161 cultural heritage sites and 2,665 cultural institutions in Ukraine had been damaged or destroyed, according to data collected by the Culture Ministry.
