title: IDF may scale back Hebron presence by weekend after evacuating thousands of Palestinians
body: The IDF may exit or reduce its presence over this coming weekend from the Hebron neighborhood it has occupied since last weekend, The Jerusalem Post has learned.None of this is certain and the situation is highly dynamic, since to date pre-elections, Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu rejected the clear recommendation from IDF Chief of Staff Lt.-Gen. Eyal Zamir to leave the area and allow the at least 2,000 evacuated Palestinians to return to their homes.But there is some increased expectation that Netanyahu may show more flexibility to IDF recommendations now that the election has passed and he feels in a stronger political position than expected.The IDF occupied the area in response to last Friday morning's deadly Hamas terrorist attack and noted that the terrorists were connected to a broader Hamas clan in the neighborhood in question, though the IDF never presented concrete evidence of how most of the 2,000 evacuees could be connected to any specific crime.Already by Sunday-Monday, the IDF was recommending it allow the evacuated Palestinians to return, saying that it had inspected all of the relevant areas, and there was no clear military reason to remain.Why IDF's evacuation of Hebron is differentThe forced evacuations from Hebron appear to be different from other recent incidents.Although in early 2025, Israel cleared areas of Jenin, Tulkarm, and Nur al-Shams in the West Bank, evacuating close to 40,000 Palestinians, those areas had experienced well-documented mass terror incidents dating back to early 2022.The IDF carried out multiple temporary evacuations at that time and even sent in the Palestinian Authority to fight large and organized terror groups before undertaking the mass evacuation and destroying several structures in those areas.In contrast, this time, the IDF provided little information about the offenses of the 2,000 evacuated Palestinians, other than to say that they were familially connected to the Hamas-linked Gaza clan.While during the 2015-2016 stabbing intifada and in earlier years, Hebron had been one of the most violent and unstable areas – and there have been some terror incidents emanating from Hebron over the past three years of war – generally, it has not been one of the leading problem spots.In addition, the IDF said it destroyed illegally built structures that could make security operations harder to carry out. However, the military was extremely vague about what those operations were and why entire buildings needed to be destroyed to carry them out.Pressed about how many of the 2,000 hamula (“clan”) members have records linking them to terror (or at a minimum, to rock throwing), multiple IDF sources did not appear to have any specific information on the topic.Rather, the operation seemed to be motivated by public statements made by Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Defense Minister Israel Katz about clearing or destroying the neighborhood of the two men involved in the terror incident on Friday – apparently a collective punishment measure.While Israel has placed closures on terror-emanating areas in the past, it has not carried out mass evacuations and building demolitions to such an extent without a specific connection to those being impacted.Petition alleges IDF soldiers turned Palestinian homes into military positionsMeanwhile, Adalah petitioned the High Court of Justice on Thursday on behalf of Hebron's municipality and seven residents, seeking to halt what it described as forced evacuations and demolitions during an IDF operation, and secure the return of residents ordered out of their homes.The petition asks for an immediate order barring further evacuations and the demolition of homes, businesses and other civilian buildings while the case is considered. It also seeks safe passage for medical teams, emergency vehicles and municipal workers, arguing that sweeping movement restrictions are cutting residents off from essential services.According to the petition, troops ordered families in the Ein Deir Baha and al-Jalda neighborhoods of western Hebron to leave their homes around 12:30-1 a.m. on the night of October 23-24. Orders were announced over loudspeakers, leaving residents insufficient time to prepare, the petitioners said.Residents were told they could not return until further notice, without being given a timetable or conditions for their return, the petition alleges. It says some families spent the night outside and some residents were unable to take their vehicles with them.Municipal figures cited in the petition put the number of families affected by the operation at 780, which could reach much higher than the original 2,000 estimate, up to 4,969 people, which itself was up from 488 families and 3,171 people earlier. The petition alleges that troops took over some homes and turned them into military positions, while demolishing civilian buildings and requiring traders to remove goods from their businesses at short notice.It says restrictions also affect residents who remain at home, hindering access to medical treatment and the movement of ambulances and emergency vehicles. According to the municipality's figures cited in the filing, blocked access routes had prevented rubbish collection and left approximately 1,200 tons of waste accumulating across the city by Wednesday.Adalah argues that the scale and open-ended nature of the evacuations violate international humanitarian law. Article 49 of the Fourth Geneva Convention permits temporary evacuation where civilian safety or imperative military reasons require it, and requires evacuees to be returned once hostilities in the area have ended. The petitioners contend that no specific justification has been provided for evacuations on this scale. They argue that barring residents' return indefinitely, while damaging or taking over their homes, risks making their displacement lasting.They also invoke the convention's prohibition on destroying property unless military operations make it absolutely necessary, arguing that a general reference to security needs cannot justify demolitions across residential neighborhoods.The petition further alleges collective punishment, citing both the measures imposed on residents and statements by Israeli officials presenting the operation as a means of exacting a price for the shooting. The convention prohibits punishing protected civilians for offenses they did not personally commit. Adalah said it approached the authorities on Sunday and sent a reminder the following day, but had received no substantive response by the time it filed the petition.The case names the defense minister, the head of IDF Central Command, the military advocate-general and the attorney-general as respondents. Alongside an urgent hearing, the petitioners seek immediate protection against further evacuations and demolitions, followed by orders lifting the challenged restrictions and ensuring residents' safe return.Already on Sunday, the Association for Civil Rights in Israel (ACRI) demanded that displaced residents be allowed to return, movement restrictions be lifted, and demolitions carried out as punishment be halted. It also requested the orders authorizing the measures already taken.It argued that public statements by ministers indicated a punitive purpose, including Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich's description of demolitions as serving as deterrence and as exacting a price for the attack.“No attack, however grave, gives the military license to punish an entire city,” ACRI executive director Noa Sattath said.In an initial decision last Friday, Justice Gila Canfy Steinitz directed the state to respond and said she expected it to refrain from changing the existing situation, or demolishing addition buildings, pending a further decision.

title: N.S. university teachers association says premier is using political intimidation
body:
An association representing university teachers in Nova Scotia is accusing Premier Tim Houston of political intimidation after his office complained to a Toronto professor who had commented on a proposed artificial intelligence data centre.
Houston told reporters on Wednesday he’s glad a staffer in his office sent the complaint to the professor, saying his comments about the $10-billion data centre were wrong.
The Association of Nova Scotia University Teachers says it condemns the premier’s response, calling it a threat to academic freedom.
The premier’s office says it disagrees with the characterization and that it has a productive relationship with academic institutions in the province.
The complaint came after Sibo Chen, a communications professor at Toronto Metropolitan University, gave a media interview to CBC News saying that public concerns about the data centre project in Point Tupper, N.S., were valid.
A communications adviser with the premier’s office sent Chen an email describing his comments as slanted and irresponsible, and copied a CBC News reporter and the chair of Chen’s department.
The president of the association of university teachers says the premier’s response raises questions about what consequences Nova Scotia academics could face if they challenge provincial projects.
“Government influence over research grants, board appointments and institutional funding gives that concern real weight,” Mathew Reichertz said. “Faculty should never have to fear that sharing their findings could jeopardize their research support or bring pressure on their employer to discipline them.”
Everwind Fuels announced earlier this month that U.S. AI company Anthropic signed a 20-year lease for the data centre, sparking opposition from members of the public.
A petition to stop the development of AI data centres in Nova Scotia on Change.org had over 24,000 signatures as of Wednesday afternoon.

title: We’re satisfied with Afenyo-Markin’s leadership in Parliament; rules out changes to Minority leadership – NPP
body: The New Patriotic Party (NPP) says it is satisfied with the work of the Minority leadership in Parliament under Alexander Afenyo-Markin and has no plans to replace him. The party’s General Secretary, Justin Kodua Frimpong, said the party had not considered any change in the leadership, dismissing reports circulating on a flyer that another MP had been selected to take over as Minority Leader. Speaking at a media briefing on Thursday, October 29, he said the party’s leadership was happy with the work of the Minority Caucus and would continue to support it. “The party has never thought about even deliberating to change the leadership in Parliament. We have not,” he said. He accused those spreading the reports of attempting to create confusion within the party’s parliamentary caucus and urged the public to disregard the claims. “Those who are busily peddling lies and trying to create chaos or confusion among the leadership in Parliament and the mighty Minority Caucus, they will not succeed,” he said. Mr Kodua said the party’s elected officers were “overwhelmingly satisfied” with the work of the leadership led by Mr Afenyo-Markin. “We are happy with the work they are doing in Parliament and we shall continue to support them. There is no meeting, there is no attempt to change the leadership in Parliament,” he added. He said the party’s support for the Minority leadership was part of its broader efforts to work with its flagbearer towards winning the 2028 general election. Mr Kodua also dismissed speculation about the selection of a running mate for the party’s flagbearer, Dr Mahamudu Bawumia, saying the party had not taken a decision on the matter. Referring to Article 13 of the NPP constitution, he explained that the flagbearer was required to nominate a running mate in consultation with the National Council. He said the constitution did not provide for the selection of a running mate through a contest or campaign, warning party members and supporters against lobbying publicly for the position “Indeed, in selecting a running mate to our flagbearer, our constitution is very clear that the flagbearer, in consultation with the National Council, shall nominate the running mate. There is nowhere in our constitution that says that the running mate is selected through contest or through campaign. So people who are busily edging bloggers, edging people to promote them, the forum is wrong,” the General Secretary added.

title: Who is Levi Salem Musa Marhabi, the Yemeni Jew held hostage by the Houthis?
body: Over the past three years, hundreds of Jewish hostages have been released from captivity across the Middle East, including Israeli hostages held in Gaza and Israeli-Russian researcher Elizabeth Tsurkov, who was released after more than two years in captivity in Iraq. Yet Levi Salem Musa Marhabi, a Jewish man held by Yemen's Iran-backed Houthi movement, remains in captivity, despite a Houthi appeals court ordering his release in 2019.Marhabi was arrested in March 2016 for helping a Jewish family and an 800-year-old Torah leave Yemen. In March 2018, he was sentenced to three and a half years in prison, but remains detained in Sanaa to this day, where Houthi terrorists continue to torture and mistreat him.According to the United States Commission on International Religious Freedom, the Houthis have beaten and electrocuted Marhabi, deprived him of food, and blocked him from communicating with his family.The torture and inhumane conditions have caused his teeth to fall out, worsened his kidney and lung conditions, and he continues to suffer from medical neglect. The American Sephardi Federation reported that the years of mistreatment have also left Marhabi partially paralyzed.Following Hamas's 2023 invasion on Oct. 7, USCIRF said that the Houthis transferred Marhabi to a prison ward with extremists who threatened him. A 10-day prison strike eventually saw the Houthis relocate him to solitary confinement.Marhabi suffers inhumane conditions, loses teeth, sustains kidney, lung damageAsharq Al-Awsat reported in 2021 that the Houthis reached a deal to release Marhabi, exiling the three last Jewish families in Yemen in exchange for his release.“They gave us a choice between staying in the midst of harassment and keeping Salem a prisoner or leaving and having him released,” one of the displaced Jews told Asharq Al-Awsat. “History will remember us as [some of] the last of Yemeni Jews who were still clinging to their homeland until the last moment… We had rejected many temptations time and time again, and refused to leave our homeland, but today we are forced.”

title: Moonshot 2026: ‘Stablecoins here to optimise financial system, not replace it’
body: By Efosa Taiwo Stablecoins could transform cross-border payments by reducing transaction delays, improving liquidity and making money transfers faster and more accessible, speakers at Moonshot 2026 have said. The speakers made the remarks during a panel session titled “The New Payment Backbone: Stablecoins as Core Infrastructure for Global Liquidity” on the Emerging Tech Stage, where industry leaders discussed how stablecoins could reshape payments across Africa and the global financial system. Mercy Emmanuel, Stablecoin & Blockchain Vertical Lead, Flutterwave, said stablecoins could simplify international transfers, which often involve multiple intermediaries and take several days to complete. “Sending money from Lagos to Nairobi goes through a lot. It could take two to five days before it gets to its destination. Stablecoins collapse all these,” Emmanuel said. She likened the technology to a moving train that operates without the restrictions of banking hours and time zones, arguing that it could make payments almost instantaneous and allow businesses to conduct transactions seamlessly alongside their online operations. According to her, stablecoins could also encourage businesses to rethink their payment processes and build more efficient financial operations. “Stablecoins are here to optimise the financial system, not displace the traditional way,” she said, adding that the financial industry was moving towards a system in which the focus would be on how quickly and efficiently money could move from one point to another. Tayo Oviosu, Group Chief Executive Officer of Paga, said widespread stablecoin adoption would require collaboration among financial technology companies, sufficient liquidity and simpler access for everyday users. He argued that consumers were more concerned about the cost and speed of financial services than the underlying technology powering their transactions. “Ultimately, it is giving them what they want: they want to go from fiat to fiat. Stablecoin can be used in between,” he said. Oviosu added that solving liquidity challenges would make stablecoin transactions easier to access and use, stressing that no single company could independently make the technology a mainstream part of everyday financial life. “We want to make it simple. The way you can come to Paga and get a naira wallet, get a stablecoin wallet. That is the part of the user,” he said. He also called for industry players to work together to expand the use of stablecoins, noting that stronger collaboration would be necessary to improve access to the infrastructure and liquidity required to support wider adoption. Ife Johnson, co-founder of JuicyWay, also emphasised the need for shared infrastructure, urging industry players to move away from isolated systems towards solutions that could support the wider financial ecosystem. “The mind shift that needs to happen is moving from silos to shared infrastructure for industry players,” Johnson said. On regulation, Johnson said collaboration between businesses and regulators would be critical to ensuring the technology could develop responsibly. He noted that adoption could take time because of the broader implications of introducing new payment systems into existing financial structures. He expressed confidence that demonstrating responsible implementation and addressing potential concerns would help build regulatory trust and encourage progress. Oviosu also pointed to changing conversations around stablecoins and digital payments in Nigeria, saying engagement between industry stakeholders and regulators had become increasingly encouraging. “Three, four years ago, who could have said CBN will support stablecoins, NCC welcomes the idea? It is interesting to see that dialogue,” he said. He added that Nigeria could help set an example for other African markets if stakeholders maintained constructive engagement and worked together to address the challenges surrounding adoption. Emmanuel similarly welcomed what she described as growing support from the Federal Government, saying cooperation among industry participants and policymakers would be important to the development of the ecosystem. Vanguard News The post Moonshot 2026: ‘Stablecoins here to optimise financial system, not replace it’ appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: Grealish dropped for Everton’s League Cup tie after disciplinary breach
body: Jack Grealish was dropped for Everton’s League Cup fourth round clash against Newcastle on Thursday after “a breach of club discipline”. It was reported that the breach related to Grealish’s unauthorised absence from training. The 31-year-old missed Saturday’s 2-0 loss at Arsenal in the Premier League due to an illness. Grealish, who is on a second season-long loan from Manchester City, had started Everton’s three Premier League matches prior to their defeat against champions Arsenal. The 31-year-old has made six appearances for David Moyes’s side this term, most recently in their loss against Chelsea on October 17. Grealish has been dogged by criticism of his off-pitch behaviour for several years amid reports of nightclub incidents that saw him fall out of favour at City. After playing a key role in City’s treble-winning campaign in 2022-23, Grealish became an increasingly sidelined figure at the Etihad Stadium. Everton are facing Newcastle for a place in the League Cup quarter-finals, with Fleetwood awaiting the winner after their shock victory over Arsenal on Tuesday. title: Russian attack on humanitarian mission bus in Zaporizhzhia region kills woman, injures three
body:
Yevhen Kaplin, head of the Proliska humanitarian mission, announced this on Facebook , Ukrinform reports.
"Today, at around 14:30, a Russian FPV drone attacked a social bus operated by the Proliska humanitarian mission in the village of Bilenke, Zaporizhzhia region. The bus was transporting residents of a frontline settlement to the city of Zaporizhzhia," Kaplin said.
According to him, "preliminary information indicates that it was a drone lying in wait. The attack took place in the center of the settlement, on a stretch of road protected by anti-drone netting. The bus was clearly marked with the Proliska humanitarian mission's insignia on the hood and roof, as well as the words 'social bus.'"
Kaplin said: "This social bus was the only means of transport serving the settlement. Our team launched the service at the request of the regional and local authorities because, after commercial transport operators stopped running, village residents had no way to reach the regional center to access administrative, medical, banking and other essential services, buy food and medicines, or receive pension payments and winter assistance under government and humanitarian organization programs."
According to Kaplin, more than 1,600 people live in Bilenke.
"At the time of the strike, there were 23 passengers and the driver on board. Most of them were elderly people. The drone struck the roof of the vehicle. A female passenger born in 1952 was killed. The bus driver sustained serious injuries and was evacuated to a medical facility. Another passenger, a man born in 1947, sustained multiple shrapnel wounds and was also evacuated to a medical facility. Another woman was injured by broken glass. The other passengers suffered acoustic and blast injuries," Kaplin said.
The injured were evacuated by specialized National Police units and military personnel, accompanied by aerial cover teams because of the threat of further drone attacks.
Kaplin stressed that since Russia launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine, this was the 121st attack on the mission's staff and volunteers while they were providing assistance, as well as on its vehicles, offices and warehouse facilities.

title: INSS outlines recommendations for US, UK to set independent oversight, enforceable 'red lines'
body: A new study by the Institute for National Security Studies (INSS) published on Wednesday urged US political parties to establish binding definitions, independent review mechanisms, and enforceable redlines to address antisemitism among political candidates and elected officials.The analysis, titled “Partisan Antisemitism in the United Kingdom and the United States: Response Mechanisms and Red Lines,” was authored by two INSS researchers: Senior International Security and Foreign Policy Analyst Ariel Cohen and Head of the INSS Antisemitism and Delegitimization Research Team Ofir Dayan.The authors examined how political organizations determine who is qualified to represent them and what consequences should follow when ideological boundaries are crossed. They noted that while political parties grant candidates campaign funds, legitimacy, and institutional infrastructure, responses to antisemitism in the United States often remain ad hoc and contingent on political calculations.They explored the British Labour Party under Jeremy Corbyn's leadership as a primary case study. In the United Kingdom, an accumulation of antisemitic statements by party members, including formal complaints submitted between 2016 and 2018 by the Jewish Labour Movement (JLM) and Campaign Against Antisemitism (CAA), culminated in a formal investigation by the Equality and Human Rights Commission in 2020.The EHRC found Labour responsible for unlawful acts of harassment, discrimination, and political interference in complaints handling, thereby shifting the issue from individual misconduct to institutional failure.The authors highlighted that public pressure, including the March 2018 “Enough Is Enough” protest outside Parliament organized by the Board of Deputies of British Jews (BoD) and the Jewish Leadership Council (JLC), a poll showing 55% of respondents viewed Corbyn as unfit to be prime minister, and an unprecedented pre-election intervention by Chief Rabbi Ephraim Mirvis, turned antisemitism into an electoral crisis.Britain's centralized party structure, combined with EHRC regulatory oversight, allowed Labour to establish an independent complaints process and candidate vetting under Keir Starmer.Cohen and Dayan noted that this framework could serve as a model for parliamentary systems such as Ireland, Australia, and New Zealand.In analyzing the US, the authors found a distinct dynamic shaped by a decentralized party network, primary elections, and First Amendment protections. Because state governments run primaries and no central party organ approves ballot access, US party leadership cannot directly disqualify candidates or prevent them from running.The authors observed that US party leaders often limit themselves to public condemnation without taking concrete action, disavowing candidates only when separate, electorally dangerous scandals emerge.As an example on the Democratic side, the authors cited Graham Platner, a Senate candidate in Maine who maintained party support despite possessing a tattoo associated with the Nazi SS – with senior figures withdrawing support only after he faced unrelated sexual assault allegations.On the Republican side, North Carolina Lt. Gov. Mark Robinson faced criticism for Holocaust denial statements, but senior party figures distanced themselves only after a report linked him to explicit posts on a pornography website.The authors also pointed to incumbent figures who expanded their political standing despite public controversies over antisemitic rhetoric, noting that when Democratic Rep. Ilhan Omar made controversial remarks in 2019, the resulting House resolution was broadened into a general condemnation of hate without censuring her, naming her, or addressing antisemitism as a standalone issue.Likewise, Republicans Minnesota Senate nominee Royce White and Rep. Marjorie Taylor Greene maintained political standing despite promoting antisemitic conspiracy theories.Furthermore, the authors raised concerns regarding political boundary-setting with influential outside figures, citing Democratic candidate Abdul El-Sayed's collaboration with online influencer Hasan Piker, as well as Republican figures and Jewish groups warning against the influence of Tucker Carlson, Candace Owens, and supporters of Nick Fuentes infiltrating conservative activist training institutions.Additionally, a Politico investigation exposing antisemitic messages exchanged by young Republican leaders was cited as evidence of extreme rhetoric seeping into youth pathways.Examining existing US response mechanisms, the authors noted that while parties can withhold funding, endorse primary rivals, or strip elected officials of committee assignments, these tools carry limited impact against candidates with independent fundraising bases, Super PAC support, or strong online followings. Post-election sanctions like committee removal or expulsion require congressional votes that parties are often reluctant to pursue, due to tight voting margins and fear of political retaliation.Condemnation alone fails to define political legitimacyThe authors highlighted The Front Line – a political organization launched in July 2026 affiliated with Republican Sen. Ted Cruz – as a potential vehicle for change. The group seeks to make antisemitism a “disqualifying factor” in Republican primaries by running targeted campaigns against candidates, such as spending $400,000 against Florida gubernatorial candidate James Fishback following his statements on “white genocide” tropes.The study's authors told The Jerusalem Post that public condemnation alone fails to define political legitimacy unless linked directly to structural consequences within political parties.“Both major American parties condemn antisemitism in principle, but too often fail to translate that condemnation into meaningful consequences. On both sides of the aisle, candidates continued to advance after antisemitic remarks surfaced, and were dropped only when a separate scandal made them an electoral liability, signaling that antisemitism alone does not disqualify one from being a public servant,” Cohen and Dayan said.“The British Labour Party's experience demonstrates the importance of treating antisemitism as an institutional challenge rather than a series of isolated incidents.“While American parties cannot simply replicate the British model, they can establish clear standards and enforce them through endorsements, campaign funding, and committee assignments.“Without consistent enforcement, condemnation remains a statement, not a true commitment to protect Jews, ” they told the Post.

title: Judge blocks Trump administration's Medicaid rule forcing sick recipients to prove frailty
body:
A federal judge has ruled that chronically ill people on Medicaid won’t be bound by new work requirement rules that the latest Trump administration guidance requires in order to qualify for “medically frail” exemptions
WASHINGTON -- Chronically ill people on Medicaid won't be bound by new work requirement rules that the latest Trump administration guidance requires in order to qualify for “medically frail” exemptions, a federal judge ruled Thursday.
U.S. District Judge Richard Stearns in Boston gave a partial victory to a coalition of 25 states and the District of Columbia, which sued the Trump administration in June over the new Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services guidance linked to the 2025 law known as the “One Big Beautiful Bill.”
The law says the definition of medically frail must include people who are blind or disabled, have substance use disorders or disabling mental disorders, have certain disabilities that significantly impair daily activities, or have serious or complex medical conditions. But the CMS rule went further, requiring people in those categories to show that their conditions also “significantly impair” their ability to comply with the law’s work requirements.
The plaintiffs argued that the stricter rule would prevent eligible Americans from accessing the care they need — and oversteps the text of the law itself as well.
“The states have met their burden of showing irreparable harm for which monetary damages would provide inadequate compensation — they face the burden of costly and intensive alterations to their eligibility verification systems,” Stearns said in his 16-page ruling.
Notably, while the ruling will make it easier for some Medicaid recipients with qualifying medical conditions to obtain an exemption from the new work requirements, Stearns' decision does not strike down the work requirements as unlawful.
Additionally, Stearns upheld two other federal restrictions on how states can verify medical frailty: including the requirement that states reject proof of patients’ medical frailty if the diagnosis is more than a year old. He also upheld a policy allowing states to accept only one self-attestation per continuous period of enrollment.
Explaining why he upheld the portions in favor of the government, Stearns said “the government provided a non-frivolous rationale for adopting each provision and explained why it did not find the States’ concerns of disenrollment compelling."
Representatives from the Department of Health and Human Services and CMS did not immediately respond to an Associated Press request for comment.
The new Medicaid restrictions are part of Trump’s big tax and policy law in 2025. The change affects those covered through an expansion in most states that gave more lower-income people access to the government’s safety net healthcare program.
Starting Jan. 1, expansion enrollees aged 19 to 64 must show that they work or do community service at least 80 hours a month, or are in school at least half the time. There are exceptions for those considered medically frail or in addiction treatment programs, among others.

title: 2027: Bagos Wins APC Reps Rerun Primary For Jos South/Jos East
body: A former member of the House of Representatives, Dachung Bagos, has emerged as the winner of the All Progressives Congress (APC) rerun primary election for Jos South/Jos East Federal Constituency of Plateau State, defeating his challenger, Esther Bitrus, by a wide margin. Bagos polled 12,181 votes to defeat Bitrus, who secured 2,495 votes in the exercise conducted following a court-ordered rerun in 11 wards across the constituency. The result was announced on Thursday by the Chairman of the Planning Committee for the rerun election, Mr. Simon Karu, at the APC secretariat, Kalwa House, Jos. The rerun followed a judgment of the High Court in Jos, which identified irregularities in the previous primary election in Du, Shen, Zawan ‘B’, Turu, Fobur ‘A’, Fobur ‘B’, Jarawan Kogi, Mai Juju/Doss, Federe, Shere East and Shere West wards. Reacting to his victory while addressing supporters who gathered at his residence in Jos, Bagos expressed gratitude to the people of Jos South and Jos East for their support, prayers and confidence throughout the process. “I want to sincerely thank the people of Jos South and Jos East for standing by me throughout this process. Your support, prayers and confidence in me have given me the strength to continue,” he said. The lawmaker called on party members, supporters and constituents to remain united and work towards securing victory for the APC in the 2027 general election. “I am appealing to everyone to support us in the general election. This victory is not for me alone; it is a victory for all of us and a responsibility to work together for the development of our constituency,” Bagos said. He cautioned his supporters against insults, verbal attacks, and inflammatory remarks against political opponents, stressing the need to preserve peaceful relationships despite differences arising from the contest. “I want to appeal to our people not to insult anybody. Do not abuse your opponents or those who contested against us. Politics should not divide us because after the election, we will still remain brothers and sisters,” the former lawmaker said. Bagos urged his supporters to celebrate the victory with humility and extend a hand of friendship to other aspirants, noting that the primary election was only one stage in the broader political process ahead of 2027. “We must celebrate with humility. Let us not insult or provoke anybody. We have won the primary, but there is still a bigger task ahead of us,” he added. The APC aspirant also commended Plateau State Governor, Caleb Mutfwang, for what he described as the development strides recorded by his administration across the state. “I want to appreciate our Governor, Caleb Mutfwang, for the development strides he has recorded in Plateau State. We recognise the efforts being made by his administration to move the state forward,” Bagos said. He reiterated the need for unity, peace and collective commitment to the development of Plateau State, urging his supporters to focus on the welfare of the people and the task ahead of the 2027 general election. title: Ghana reviews employment policy to identify green job opportunities
body: Ghana is reviewing its National Employment Policy to address emerging labour market challenges and identify opportunities for creating decent jobs through the transition to a greener economy. The review was highlighted at a two-day validation workshop on the Green Employment Diagnostics Report and the National Employment Policy review, held at the Ministry of Labour, Jobs and Employment in Accra from October 27 to 28, 2026. The workshop brought together representatives of government institutions, organised labour, employers and development partners to examine findings and recommendations intended to improve employment outcomes. Delivering opening remarks on behalf of the Ministry’s Chief Director, Director of General Administration, Mrs Joyce Gifty Bosomprah, called for evidence-based employment policies that respond to changing labour market conditions. She identified youth unemployment and underemployment, skills mismatches, informal employment and digital transformation as key challenges that must inform employment planning. Mrs Bosomprah said the Green Employment Diagnostics Report would help identify sectors with significant potential for creating green jobs while assessing how the transition to a sustainable economy could affect workers and businesses. She explained that the review of the National Employment Policy, adopted in 2015, would assess its implementation and determine whether it remained relevant to Ghana’s current and emerging employment challenges. According to her, the shift towards a greener economy could stimulate innovation, support new economic activities, promote skills development and create decent work opportunities. However, she stressed that realising these benefits would require deliberate policy decisions, adequate investment and coordinated action among government, employers, workers and development partners. Mrs Bosomprah urged participants to scrutinise the report’s findings and proposed interventions to ensure the recommendations were practical, achievable and aligned with Ghana’s development priorities. The Ministry also acknowledged the continued technical support of the International Labour Organisation (ILO) in advancing the country’s employment policy agenda. The review is expected to help inform policy responses to changing labour market conditions and the potential employment opportunities associated with Ghana’s transition to a greener economy. title: Israel election results: Netanyahu's Likud biggest party in Israel after all votes counted
body: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's bloc maintained its lead after the final vote count from Tuesday's election with 53 seats in the next Knesset, the Central Elections Committee reported Thursday. The opposition bloc won 48, it said.Both blocs fell short of the 61 seats needed for a Knesset majority. The Arab parties won a record total of 19 seats.The official vote count was announced amid a Shin Bet (Israel Security Agency) investigation into suspicions that foreign entities, potentially including Qatar and Turkey, funneled money into Israel to influence voter turnout in the Arab sector.Central Elections Committee chairman Justice Noam Sohlberg directed Shin Bet Director David Zini to investigate the suspected foreign funding and election interference.The integrity of the vote at polling stations had been maintained, the Central Elections Committee said.The official vote count announced on Thursday included the remaining double-envelope ballots, which were the last to be counted.How many seats does each party have?Netanyahu's Likud is projected to enter with 27 seats, making it once again the largest party in the Knesset. United Torah Judaism and Otzma Yehudit are expected to enter with seven seats, and the Religious Zionist Party and Shas are expected to enter with six seats.Most TV channel polls before the elections showed Likud receiving significantly fewer seats, while other parties in Netanyahu's bloc, including Shas and Otzma Yehudit, were projected to gain more.The opposition bloc, comprising Yashar, B'Yachad, Yisrael Beytenu, and The Democrats, is expected to enter the Knesset with 48 seats.Gadi Eisenkot's Yashar is projected to enter the Knesset with 21 seats. B'Yachad, led by Naftali Bennett, is expected to enter with 12 seats. Yair Golan's The Democrats is expected to enter the Knesset with eight seats. Avigdor Liberman's Yisrael Beytenu is expected to enter with seven.The Joint List was projected to win 11 seats, while Ra'am was projected to secure eight seats in the next Knesset.Most TV channel polling before the elections had shown the opposition bloc in the lead, and Yashar was projected to be the largest party in the Knesset.Ofer Winter's People of Israel party and Yoaz Hendel's The Reservists-Economic party both fell short of the required 3.25% threshold.The prospect of a unity government involving Netanyahu and Eisenkot remains possible, although Eisenkot had previously rejected serving under Netanyahu, including in a rotation government. Other opposition leaders have also ruled out joining a coalition led by Netanyahu.The political deadlock could also ultimately lead to another election, although the parties may still reach an agreement through coalition negotiations.By law, the president is required to consult the Knesset factions before deciding who receives the task of forming a government.President Isaac Herzog on Wednesday called on political leaders to approach coalition negotiations with open minds, warning that Israel must do everything possible to avoid another round.He also called for a full investigation into the Qatari election interference allegations on Thursday amid the Shin Bet investigation and warned against the threat of delegitimizing the voting process.Golan met with Ra'am chairman Mansour Abbas and has called for the opposition bloc to form a government with the Arab parties. He also held separate meetings with Eisenkot and opposition leader Yair Lapid on Thursday.Eisenkot and Bennett met on Thursday and said they had discussed forming a new government as quickly as possible.Meanwhile, Liberman reiterated on Thursday that he would not sit with the Arab parties or Netanyahu, following reports that he was ignoring phone calls from his fellow opposition members.“The only coalition we would consider is one made up exclusively of Zionist parties, including Likud without Bibi [Netanyahu],” Liberman said.All other opposition party leaders except Golan had drawn a redline to Arab parties being part of the government, saying they are not viable coalition partners after the October 7 massacre in 2023.Eisenkot has called for the leader of the largest party in the opposition bloc to become its candidate for prime minister, although no agreement on the arrangement has been announced within the bloc.The political deadlock also raised the possibility of a minority government being formed that could win a Knesset confidence vote without holding an absolute majority of 61 seats. In that scenario, Arab parties could agree to support the opposition bloc. Members of the Arab parties have called to do whatever is possible to prevent Netanyahu from remaining in office.Objections within the opposition bloc to relying on Arab parties could complicate such an arrangement. Liberman had openly rejected such an option ahead of the elections.The recent Shin Bet investigation into Qatari influence in the elections could also reduce the likelihood of such a situation.The investigation prompted Netanyahu's Likud to demand that no Zionist party “cooperate with Ra'am and the Joint List.”The Likud also demanded “immediate action, using all the means at the disposal of the Shin Bet and the police, to investigate these crimes.”Likud had separately accused the Arab parties of allegedly stealing the election through widespread electoral fraud, bribery, intimidation, and ballot manipulation. It demanded an immediate investigation by law-enforcement authorities.All opposition party leaders called on the Shin Bet and Sohlberg to conduct a full and thorough investigation into Qatari influence in the elections.Eisenkot said he was in contact with the relevant authorities and warned against political actors exploiting the situation to influence the swearing-in date of the 26th Knesset.He later accused Netanyahu of launching an organized campaign to delegitimize Tuesday's election results and vowed to prevent any delay in the new Knesset's swearing-in.Abbas said he welcomed the decision to investigate, adding that his party was not involved in any way.Shir Perets and Jerusalem Post staff contributed to this report.

title: Abuja court jails fraudster seven years for defrauding American $205,238
body:
The Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC), has secured the conviction and sentence of Nwachi Chidozie Kingsley for obtaining $205,238 from an American, Nicole Kierulff Sayers, under false pretence.
Justice U.P. Kekemeke of the Federal Capital Territory, FCT, High Court, Maitama, Abuja, convicted Kingsley on Thursday, October 29, 2026, and sentenced him to seven years’ imprisonment on each of the two counts, without an option of fine.
The sentences are to run concurrently at Kuje Correctional Centre, Abuja.
The court also ordered Kingsley to restitute the victim the sum of $205,238 (Two Hundred and Five Thousand, Two Hundred and Thirty-Eight United States Dollars).
Kingsley was prosecuted by the EFCC on a two-count amended charge bordering on possession of a document containing false pretence and obtaining money by false pretence in connection with a purported contract with the Federal Ministry of Works and Housing.
One of the charges accused him of being in possession of a fake notice of intent to award a contract, allegedly issued in his name by the Ministry. The second count accused him of obtaining $205,238 from Sayers under the false pretence that the money was required to finance a government contract, knowing that the claim was false.
While testifying before the court, Sayers, an American lawyer based in the state of Oregon, United States, identified Kingsley as the man who contacted her on Facebook on her birthday.
“I know the defendant. The defendant messaged me on Facebook on my birthday and he said he was a member of the same spiritual organization as me,” she told the court.
According to her, their conversations developed into a romantic relationship, which she said made her trust him and believe his claims.
Sayers told the court that Kingsley subsequently asked her for money to facilitate the award of a contract by the Federal Ministry of Works and Housing. He allegedly claimed that some men were threatening his life because he had not provided the money required to secure the contract.
She said Kingsley supplied her with details of the purported contract, including a logo and other information, which she believed because she had developed an emotional attachment to him.
The witness further testified that Kingsley initially requested $15,000, promising to repay the money within 45 days. She transferred the money to him through a money transfer application.
According to Sayers, Kingsley subsequently introduced her to members of his family during a video call, during which they allegedly thanked her for helping him secure the purported contract.
She told the court that she had transferred approximately $40,000 to Kingsley before travelling to Nigeria to meet him in person.
Sayers said she arrived in Abuja March 2022 and spent two weeks with the defendant at his rented house in Sun City, Abuja. She claimed that she continued the relationship because she wanted to recover her money.
The witness further alleged that Kingsley subsequently requested additional funds for various purposes, including medical emergencies, surgeries, malaria treatment and supplies for the purported government contract.
She told the court that the requests involved more than 125 transactions and that the total amount she transferred was, by her estimate, well over $200,000 within a 12-month period.
Sayers also testified that Kingsley presented her with a document he claimed was proof that he had attempted to transfer $10,000 to her.
According to her, he claimed that the bank had intercepted the transaction because the money was allegedly linked to the misappropriation of government funds, which he said had resulted in his arrest and detention.
She further alleged that Kingsley asked her to provide money for his bail and for bribes connected to the purported criminal case.
Sayers told the court that she repeatedly asked Kingsley to refund her money. According to her, he eventually requested her bank details and promised to transfer the money the following day, but failed to do so.
She said she later realised that he would not repay the money.
At the conclusion of the prosecution’s case, counsel for the EFCC, Fatsuma Muhammad, urged the court to convict and sentence the defendant in accordance with the law.
In his judgment, Justice Kekemeke found Kingsley guilty and sentenced him to imprisonment without an option of fine, with the terms of imprisonment to run concurrently.

title: 2 Colorado college students found dead after going missing during hike
body:
Two Colorado college students have been found dead after going missing during a hiking trip in the Rocky Mountains, according to police.
The Chaffee County Sheriff’s Office said that the bodies of Kaden Matsuda, 19, and Jackson Donlon, 20, were found “near each other” at 3:30 p.m. local time on Wednesday “in a basin of West Apostle Mountain in Chaffee County.”
“Foul play is not suspected, and we will not offer theories as to what may have happened until an autopsy can be completed,” the department said.
A detailed investigation will be completed in partnership with the Chaffee County Coroner’s Office, according to police.
“Our heart aches for Kaden and Jackson’s family and friends. We are very proud of our team’s efforts to find them before this weekend’s coming storm,” Sheriff Andy Rohrich said in a statement.
“Although this is a gut punch, our prayers were answered that we would find Kaden and Jackson, allowing some closure for the family. We ask that everyone give time and distance to family members and friends as they mourn their loss,” Rohrich added.
The students left the Colorado Mountain College Leadville Campus for the hike on Oct. 23 and were reported missing around 10 a.m. local time on Oct. 26 by college staff after they didn’t return to campus, the Chaffee County Sheriff’s Office previously said .
“Family and friends were interviewed, and it was learned that Kaden and Jackson planned on hiking Ice Mountain on the far north end of Chaffee County. Typically, hikers planning this hike would drive near Winfield (County Road 390) and access Mt. Huron trailhead. Deputies responded to the trailhead and located Kaden’s vehicle,” police added.
Matsuda and Donlon’s friends had said that they planned on returning from the hike on Oct. 24 if they didn’t feel safe. If they continued on with the hike of Ice Mountain, their friends said they would have returned on Oct. 25.
Matsuda and Donlon were both experienced hikers and sent their friends a text with a map plot that pinpointed Ice Mountain as their destination, according to police.
“When deputies and search and rescue personnel arrived at the trailhead and located Kaden’s vehicle, they noted that there was about eight inches of snow on the ground but none under the vehicle,” police said on Tuesday. “On Friday when the two ventured to the mountain it would have been raining in the area.”
Police described Ice Mountain as “a very technical climb” and recommended that hikers be “very experienced when trying to tackle it.”
“Chaffee County Search and Rescue (north and south) deployed to the area and began a search mission for the two hikers. The fresh blanket of snow made it easy to watch for tracks but, unfortunately, no human tracks were located,” police said.
Approximately 50 searchers continued their search for the missing hikers on Tuesday from multiple teams including Teller County, Lake County, Chaffee County, Arapaho County and Park County.
“Dogs and arial searchers were used and shortly after 12:00PM a helicopter spotted an object near Lake Ann. A search team was sent in on foot to this area and discovered that the object was the hiker’s tent that had collapsed under the weight of the snow,” police said in an update on Tuesday.
“There was no snow under the tent and there were no visible footprints in the snow which suggested, again, this was all in place before the snow came in. Their sleeping bags, a stove and some clothing were inside the tent, but Kaden and Jackson were not located,” police added.
By Wednesday, the Chaffee County Sheriff’s Office said they still had their search and rescue members searching for the hikers, including helicopter flights and drone teams, as well as canines and handlers.
“Kaden and Jackson’s dorms were searched, and their climbing equipment was not found,” police reavealed. “The equipment was not located in their vehicle at the trailhead nor in their tent, which suggests they were prepared for a more technical climb when they left their tent.”
In another update on Wednesday following the dayslong search , police said, “It is with profound sadness that we report Kaden Matsuda (age 19) and Jackson Donlon (age 20) were located deceased at about 3:30PM today (10-28-26) in a basin of West Apostle Mountain in Chaffee County.”
On Thursday, the Colorado Mountain College (CMC) said it is “mourning the loss of Kaden Matsuda, 19, and Jackson Donlon, 20, two students at CMC Leadville who died during a mountain trip in Chaffee County.”
“The college extends its deepest condolences to Kaden and Jackson’s families, friends, classmates and everyone whose lives they touched. CMC’s immediate priority is supporting those closest to the students and ensuring that the Leadville campus community has the care, counseling and resources needed during this difficult time,” the college added.
Matsuda was studying wildland fire at CMC and Donlon was studying outdoor recreation leadership, according to the college.
“Kaden and Jackson came to Leadville from different parts of the country but found common ground in their love of the mountains. At CMC, that shared passion grew into a friendship and a sense of belonging in the campus community,” the college said.
Ben Cairns, the CMC Leadville vice president and campus dean, said he is “heartbroken by the loss of Kaden and Jackson.”
“They came here to learn, to explore and to build their futures. Along the way, they built friendships and became part of our community. Their lives were full of promise, and their loss is felt deeply by the students, faculty and staff who knew them,” Cairns said.
“We will remember them not for how we lost them, but for who they were and the lives they touched,” he added.

title: Meet Zakon: Ukraine creates its own national font to replace Russian type in state documents
body: (function(w,q){w[q]=w[q]||[];w[q].push(["_mgc.load"])})(window,"_mgq"); For more than 300 years, since Peter I's 1708 script reform , Ukrainian lettering has been shaped by imperial Russian norms. Zakon, presented on 29 October 2026, aims to break that pattern and decolonize the letters of Ukraine's state acts and awards. The national font for official state communication draws on the work of Ukrainian artists, including Heorhii Narbut, who designed a 1918 banknote for the Ukrainian People's Republic, the short-lived independent state that fell to the Bolsheviks. It is meant to replace Izhitsa, Petersburg, and other Russian-origin fonts still often used on honor certificates, letters of thanks, diplomas, battle flags, and signs, adding a visual touch to the country's push to boost its national culture amid the fifth year of Russia's full-blown invasion. Verkhovna Rada Speaker Ruslan Stefanchuk presented Zakon on 29 October, nine months after parliament adopted a resolution that called for a national font and said Russian-origin fonts had no place in official acts or on state awards. The Ministry of Culture developed it with money from the job site Work.ua and its co-owner Artur Mikhno, and the font is still in beta testing, the ministry says . “The letters in which the word ‘Ukraine’ is written are also part of our state identity,” Stefanchuk wrote. “Decolonization should also concern how Ukraine presents itself.” "Ukraine" written in Zakon font. Screenshot from mincult.gov.ua “The creation of a national typeface is an important step toward ensuring that state institutions represent Ukraine through our artistic tradition and contemporary Ukrainian design. [...] We want Ukrainian design to shape the image of our country, and for our cultural heritage to become a source of new solutions,” said Tetiana Berezhna, Deputy Prime Minister for Humanitarian Policy and Minister of Culture. Three typefaces, one of them free for anyone Zakon comes in three versions. Zakon Text is designed for everyday official paperwork and is free for anyone to use; it's available for download here . Zakon Decor, for ceremonial inscriptions, and Zakon Letterpress , for printing the originals of legal acts, have closed licenses. Zakon Text has four styles: regular, italic, bold, and bold italic. The ministry asks users to test it and send feedback before a wider rollout, which Stefanchuk said will be gradual. The designers are Oleksii Chekal, Hennadii Zarechniuk, Dmytro Rastvortsev, and Andrii Shevchenko, with Taras Ishchyk leading the project. Example of an Antiqua font The ministry calls Zakon a “classic Ukrainian antiqua.” Antiqua, or roman, is the family of upright serif letters that grew out of a script Renaissance Italian humanists modeled on Carolingian handwriting, which they took for ancient Roman. The name set it apart from blackletter, the Gothic script, and its forms became the basis of the roman typefaces Nicolas Jenson and Aldus Manutius cut in 15th-century Venice. Built on the lettering of six Ukrainian artists Zakon brings Ukrainian letter forms back to Cyrillic. The Ministry of Culture says that its developers “generalized most of the characteristic features” of six Ukrainian graphic artists’ lettering. Heorhii Narbut (1886–1920) is credited with 13 of the 24 banknotes issued in 1917–1920, the first Ukrainian postage stamps, and an illustrated Ukrainian alphabet he never finished. His letters drew on Cossack baroque motifs and floral ornament. Design of the 100 hryvnia note of the Ukrainian People's Republic. Typography, illustration, ornamentation. Heorhii Narbut, 1918. Vasyl Krychevskyi (1873–1952) drew the trident that became the coat of arms of the Ukrainian People’s Republic in 1918, along with its seals and banknotes. Vasyl Krychevskyi. Coat of Arms of the Ukrainian People's Republic. Poster, 1918. Robert Lisovskyi (1893–1982), a follower of Narbut, made prints, book covers, and emblems, and later led the Association of Ukrainians in Great Britain. Cover of the magazine *For the Unity of the Nation*. Lettering and coat of arms by Robert Lisovskyi, 1955. Vasyl Khomenko (1912–1984) created New Ukrainian, a typeface he worked on from 1963 to 1970. Zakon co-designer Zarechniuk is one of the authors of Homenko, a typeface based on his work. Homenko Font Family developed by Zarechniuk Yakiv Hnizdovskyi (1915–1985) emigrated to the United States in 1949, later settling in New York, and made close to 250 woodcuts, along with book covers and bookplates. Book cover. Calligraphy, ornamentation. Yakiv Hnizdovskyi, 1949, Regensburg. Vasyl Chebanyk (1933–2025) began studying the Ukrainian alphabet in 1971 and in 2001 launched the Rutenia project to restore older Ukrainian forms in a modern shape. Rutenia later grew to more than 60 fonts and won him the Shevchenko National Prize. One of them is on the cover of the ceremonial copy of Ukraine’s Constitution. The Rutenia decorative typeface designed by Vasyl Chebanyk. Illustrative image How Ukraine's state started dropping Russian fonts Russia's full-scale invasion turned fonts into a state matter. On 29 September 2022, days after Russia's sham "referendums" in four occupied Ukrainian oblasts, Anna Yakupova, CEO of ParaType, the Russian studio whose Cyrillic versions of Petersburg and other fonts Ukraine's state institutions still use, congratulated colleagues in a chat that "our country got bigger," prompting a campaign to shun the fonts. In August 2023, MPs from three factions registered bill 9606 to ban the Russian font Izhitsa from Verkhovna Rada documents and move parliament's honor certificates to Volja, a Ukrainian font made in 2022 by Marchela Mozhyna from the lettering of artist Nil Khasevych. A month later, the culture ministry announced plans for a bank of Ukrainian fonts to replace Russian ones. In July 2026, the fight reached Ukraine's money. The National Bank of Ukraine said it would redraw the lettering on its new 2,000-hryvnia note featuring poet Vasyl Stus, after type designer Bohdan Hdal said the denomination lettering resembled an unofficial Cyrillic adaptation of Bickham Script made by a Russian designer. “No Russian shadows on a banknote with a poet whom Russia killed,” NBU Governor Andrii Pyshnyi said. The "Two thousand hryvnias" inscription on Ukraine's new banknote will be redrawn after critics said it resembled a Russian designer's unofficial adaptation of a font Some readers balk at the Z Not everyone liked the name. Among the top comments under Stefanchuk’s post, readers objected that the Latin spelling starts with Z, the letter Russia painted on its vehicles for the full-scale invasion. Others welcomed the font itself.

title: Polymarket suspended trading amid reports of user funds being drained
body:
The prediction markets platform halted trading on Thursday after it reported one of its third party providers had been compromised.
Prediction markets company Polymarket reported its Predictions Trading API had experienced a “major outage,” resulting in the platform temporarily halting trading.
In a Thursday update to its status page, Polymarket said that the platform was in “cancel-only” mode after it had identified and fixed an issue impacting its operations. As of 7:05 pm UTC, the platform reported all its systems were operational.
“One of our third party providers was compromised, and we have referred this to relevant law enforcement,” said Polymarket. “Anyone who has been impacted will be made whole.”
The suspension of trading came as several users claimed online that their Polymarket accounts had been drained of thousands of dollars after their positions were sold without their consent. In June, Polymarket reported that hackers were able to drain more than $2.9 million in user funds by compromising a third-party vendor.

title: Israel extradites Israeli-Russian citizen to US over alleged USD 2.8 million crypto theft
body: Israel extradited Alexander Block to the United States early Thursday to face charges over the alleged theft of about USD 2.8 million in digital assets from cryptocurrency platform Nomad, the State Attorney's Office announced.Block, an Israeli-Russian citizen formerly known as Alexander Gurevich, was transferred to American authorities after extensive legal proceedings in Israel, including an unsuccessful Supreme Court appeal and a subsequent request for a further hearing.The case concerns allegations that he exploited a security flaw in August 2022 to obtain digital tokens - without depositing the assets that were supposed to back them -  and then moved the proceeds between digital wallets to conceal their origin.According to the Supreme Court judgment, US authorities indicted Block in the Northern District of California in August 2023 on eight counts involving computer offenses, transferring stolen property, and money laundering. The US requested his extradition in December 2024.Block was arrested at Ben-Gurion Airport in May 2025 while preparing to travel to Russia. He had changed his surname from Gurevich to Block and obtained a passport in his new name shortly before his arrest.Block identified flaw in crypto platform, withdrew about 2.8m in tokens Nomad, the cryptocurrency platform, operated as a bridge between blockchain networks, allowing users to lock digital assets on one network and receive corresponding tokens on another.According to the American extradition request, Block identified a flaw that allowed him to bypass the check confirming that the original assets had been locked. Prosecutors allege that, after testing the vulnerability, he withdrew about USD 2.8m. in tokens on August 1, 2022, without supplying the corresponding assets.He then allegedly converted the tokens into other cryptocurrencies and transferred them between wallets to obscure the source of the funds.The Jerusalem District Court approved his extradition in July 2025. His appeal challenged whether the alleged conduct constituted criminal offenses under Israeli law and whether the evidence was sufficient to support extradition.Block argues transactions used Nomad functionsBlock argued that the transactions used functions available within Nomad's automated system and that the public record of blockchain transfers undermined the money-laundering allegations.The Supreme Court rejected those arguments, holding that exploiting a programming flaw could constitute unlawful computer intrusion, even where the software technically permitted the action. It also explained that publicly visible transactions did not necessarily identify the people controlling the wallets or rule out efforts to conceal the source of funds.The State Attorney's Office said Supreme Court President Isaac Amit subsequently rejected his request for a further hearing. Thursday's transfer was coordinated by the prosecution's International Department and the Israel Police's operational coordination and Interpol units.

title: Man sentenced to 16 years, 8 months for horrifying Surrey bus attack
body:
WARNING: This story contains disturbing details. Discretion is advised.
A man has been sentenced following a horrifying attack on a Surrey transit bus in 2023.
Abdul Aziz Kawam, 30, assaulted a man with a knife at a bus stop near Fraser Highway and 156th Street before boarding a bus and slashing another passenger in the throat on April 1, 2023. Both men survived.
On Thursday Kawam was sentenced to 16 years and eight months in prison.
With credit for time spent in custody since April 2023, he has just over 11 years left to serve.
Crown had asked for 20 years in the case, while the defence was suggesting seven.
On April 1, 2023, security video obtained by Global News showed Kawam walking onto the bus, followed a few seconds later by his victim, whose identity is protected by a publication ban.
Both stood near the rear exit doors of the bus and rode together in silence for approximately three minutes, not speaking or interacting.
Kawam then suddenly pulled out a large knife and slashed at the victim’s neck three times, intending to kill him, according to the admissions submitted at trial.
As bus passengers are heard screaming in the video, the victim used his body to push Kawam out of the bus.
“He was bleeding out of his neck and he still managed to throw his attacker off the bus,” said Oren Bick, general counsel with the Public Prosecution Service of Canada.
The knife nicked the victim’s vocal cords and missed his main artery by a millimetre, his brother-in-law, who cannot be identified as per the publication ban, told Global News days after the attack.
Crown Prosecutor, Sharon Steele, said on Thursday that this victim “likely saved the lives of other people on that bus with his ability to defend himself so quickly and stay calm and collected and get Mr. Kawam off the bus and it’s likely a credit to him that no one else was injured.”
Some fifteen minutes earlier on April 1, Kawam had used the same knife to attack his first victim across the street.
“Mr. Kawam initially approached him and asked are you Muslim?,” Bick told Global News in an interview.
When the man replied “No,” Kawam went back to the bus stop, prayed for approximately two minutes, and then returned, taking the large knife out of his jacket and attacking the victim, aiming a slashing motion at his neck without making contact.
The victim, who pushed Kawam away and ran, described the blade as being approximately 10 inches, according to the admissions.
“Kawam chased him for some distance, knife still in hand, but (the victim) was ultimately able to escape,” stated the admissions, and was able to call 911 from a gas station nearby.
“This wasn’t a who done it, this was a why did he do it,” said Bick. “There was really no disputing what happened.”
On June 30, 2025, Kawam was convicted of attempted murder and assault with a weapon for the benefit of, at the direction of, and in association with a terrorist group: the Islamic State.

General Motors has agreed to pay $220 million to settle claims that it illegally sold driver and location information to data brokers, as reported earlier by Reuters . The agreement, which resolves a complaint from a coalition of 36 US attorneys general, requires GM to limit the driving data it collects and obtain “express consent” from drivers before collecting their information.
The allegations surround GM’s now-discontinued Smart Driver program , which collected data about driving habits, including acceleration, braking, and trip length. GM allegedly passed this information to data brokers, enabling insurance companies to purchase the data and raise premiums . The states also accused GM of failing to notify drivers that they were enrolled in its Smart Driver program, and that the carmaker was collecting their data.
“This agreement addresses Smart Driver, a product we ended in 2024, and reinforces steps we’ve taken to strengthen our privacy practices,” GM spokesperson Charlotte McCoy said in an emailed statement to The Verge . “Safer, more helpful and personalized experiences are enabled by connected vehicle data, and GM is committed to being clear about what information is used, how it’s protected, and the choices customers have about what they share.”
This settlement comes just months after GM agreed to pay $12.75 million to settle similar claims in California . Oregon AG Dan Rayfield and Washington AG Nick Brown co-led the states’ case against GM, which also included New York, Florida, Michigan, Nevada, Pennsylvania, and many others.
“People bought a car, not a tracking device,” Rayfield says in a press release . “GM told drivers this program would help them drive more safely and promised it wouldn’t share their data with insurers without permission. Our investigation found GM sold that data anyway, and some drivers paid for it with higher premiums.”
