title: EFCC hands over recovered N1.05bn entitlements to 659 disengaged Adamawa teachers
body:
The Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC) says it has handed over N1.05 billion to 659 teachers disengaged in 2014 by the Adamawa State Government.
The commission’s Gombe Zonal Directorate handed over a bank draft worth N1,054,919,532.61 on Thursday. EFCC spokesperson Dele Oyewale made this known in a statement shared with PREMIUM TIMES.
The teachers’ lawyer, Luka Haruna, a Senior Advocate of Nigeria (SAN), received it on their behalf, according to the EFCC.
The EFCC said it began investigating the matter after receiving a petition from Abraham Song in 2024 over the teachers’ unpaid entitlements.
According to the commission, its investigation revealed a risk that the funds could be misapplied. It stated that it took steps to preserve the money, leading to its recovery and handover.
Speaking at the ceremony, the commission’s Acting Zonal Director, Austine Adache, noted that the EFCC was committed to accountability, justice and returning recovered funds to their rightful owners.
Mr Haruna thanked the commission for its efforts, while Mr Song said the recovery would help ease the financial hardship faced by the teachers.
The teachers were employed by the Adamawa State Government in 2012 and worked in secondary schools across the state for 29 months before the government declared their appointments illegal in December 2014.
They challenged their disengagement at the National Industrial Court, which ruled in their favour on 13 June 2018.
The judge N.C.S. Ogbuanya held that the teachers had a valid employment relationship with the state government and were entitled to their outstanding salaries and other benefits.
The court ordered the government to pay about N660 million, including N638.3 million in salary arrears and N22 million as one month’s salary in lieu of notice. It gave the government two months to pay, with interest of 10 per cent per annum accruing on the outstanding sum if it failed to comply.
The government had argued that the teachers were illegally recruited and lacked the required qualifications.
It also explained that they had been dropped after a screening exercise. The court rejected the defence, finding contradictions in the government’s arguments.
The teachers later sought to enforce the judgement through garnishee proceedings involving United Bank for Africa, First Bank of Nigeria, Fidelity Bank, Zenith Bank and Ecobank.
However, in a ruling delivered on 15 May 2025, another judge J.T. Agbadu-Fishim of the National Industrial Court in Yola struck out a garnishee application filed by the teachers.
The judge found that the affidavit supporting the application had been sworn by a litigation secretary in the law firm representing the teachers. He ruled that this did not comply with Section 83(1) of the Sheriffs and Civil Process Act, rendering the application incompetent.
The court discharged the five banks from those proceedings but did not set aside the 2018 judgement.
It noted that the debt had not been fully paid and that the parties disagreed over the outstanding balance, including previous payments and accrued interest.

title: IDF soldier indicted for allegedly spying for Iran, leaking sensitive military intelligence
body: A soldier has been indicted for providing information to Iran, the Shin Bet (Israel Security Agency), Israel Police, and the IDF Spokesperson's Unit, announced in a joint statement Thursday. The soldier was arrested in September in a joint operation by the Shin Bet, the Ayalon District Police Investigations Unit, the Military Police Criminal Investigation Division (MPCID), and the Defense Ministry's security authorities.The official charges filed by the prosecution are providing information to the enemy with intent to harm state security, providing information for the benefit of the enemy, and contact with a foreign agent.The soldier's alleged espionage activities involved encrypted communications, coded messages, cryptocurrency payments, and a cover story designed to conceal his contact with Iranian intelligence. His handler also reportedly offered him a substantial financial incentive to travel to Iran.According to investigators, the soldier maintained contact with Iranian intelligence operatives for approximately a year, fully aware of whom he was communicating with. During that period, he allegedly disclosed sensitive information about his unit's activities, IDF operational readiness, and emergency mobilizations, including details of his own call-up at the outbreak of Operation Roaring Lion.IDF soldier allegedly shared military base coordinates, photos of US aircraft with IranThe information he allegedly provided included the locations and coordinates of military bases, along with photographs of interceptor missiles, military vehicles, and US refueling aircraft stationed at an Israeli airport.Investigators also found that the soldier supplied his handler with personal information about fellow soldiers and commanders in his unit, despite knowing that the Iranian operative intended to use those details to recruit additional individuals for espionage.In exchange, the soldier received payments through cryptocurrency wallets, following instructions from his Iranian handler.The investigation further revealed that the soldier gave his handler access to a Telegram group called "Kal Bakrav," which serves Israelis preparing for military service. The Iranian operative subsequently joined the group.The handler also instructed the soldier to install malicious communications applications that would allow them to exchange encrypted messages. He reportedly suggested that the soldier purchase a basic mobile phone and a handgun.IDF soldier, Iranian handler allegedly used coded messages and cover story to evade detectionTo avoid detection, the two allegedly agreed to communicate using coded language and devised a cover story in case Israeli security authorities uncovered their activities.The Iranian handler also offered the soldier $200,000 to travel to Iran, according to investigators.A military court extended the soldier's detention until November 12, 2026.In their joint statement, the Shin Bet, Israel Police, and IDF described the case as an extremely serious threat to national security and urged the public to remain vigilant against suspected foreign intelligence recruitment attempts."We call on the public to exercise the utmost vigilance. Any suspicious approach by an unidentified individual, request to provide information, or offer of payment in exchange for 'services' must be reported to the security authorities," the agencies said.The security agencies added that they would continue working to prevent espionage and terrorism and pursue legal action against individuals suspected of assisting enemy operatives or endangering Israel's security.

title: Germans will track Russian radars. New tasks for the brigade in Lithuania
body:
The German brigade in Lithuania is set to use electronic reconnaissance for the early detection of military activity in the Kaliningrad Oblast and Belarus. Details were provided to Reuters by Vice Admiral Thomas Daum, head of the Bundeswehr’s Cyber and Information Domain Service.
According to a Reuters dispatch from 28 October, German soldiers will collect information on Russian and Belarusian radars and other military sources of electromagnetic emission. The data will be used to update electronic warfare databases utilised by German and allied forces. This is intended to enable, among other things, the recognition of new radars appearing on the Belarusian side.
The Bundeswehr is also testing drone detection, signal interception, and jamming equipment in Lithuania. Sensors transmitting information from the battlefield to remote analysts are also being trialled.
Daum linked the need to develop these capabilities with Russian activities below the threshold of open armed conflict. In his assessment, previous covert penetration of Western computer networks is giving way to actions aimed at causing damage. “In the cyber and information domain, there is no war yet, but there is no peace either,” he told Reuters.
This marks another step in the permanent presence of German troops in Lithuania. The 45th Armoured Brigade, formally established on 1 April 2025, is responsible for this mission. According to the Bundeswehr, the unit is expected to reach full readiness by the end of 2027 and will number approximately 4,800 soldiers.
The brigade is intended to strengthen the deterrence and defence of the Baltic states. The Bundeswehr also lists the defence of the Suwałki Gap, connecting Poland with Lithuania, among its tasks. The main basing locations for the German forces are being developed in Rūdninkai and Rukla.

title: Farmer Globale earns international recognition for climate-smart rice farming
body: A Ghanaian agribusiness company, Farmer Globale, has earned international recognition at the Africa Sustainable Futures Awards, hosted by the Financial Times in partnership with the World Bank Group’s Multilateral Investment Guarantee Agency (MIGA) in the United Kingdom on October 21 and 22, 2026. The recognition highlights the company’s efforts to transform Ghana’s rice sector through climate-smart farming, support for smallholder farmers and the development of carbon finance opportunities. Farmer Globale is promoting a rice production model that combines environmentally sustainable practices with practical support to help farmers improve productivity, access markets and increase their incomes. At the centre of its approach is Alternate Wetting and Drying (AWD), a water-management technique that reduces water consumption and methane emissions from rice cultivation. The company combines the technology with input financing, mechanisation, agricultural extension services, aggregation, processing and market access to help farmers adopt more sustainable production methods while remaining commercially competitive. Working with more than 20,000 farmers, Farmer Globale is seeking to demonstrate how climate action can support rural livelihoods, strengthen food security and create new investment opportunities in Ghana’s agricultural sector. The company is also developing opportunities for farmers to benefit from carbon credits generated through climate-smart agricultural practices, potentially creating an additional source of income while reducing the environmental impact of rice production. The initiative comes amid growing efforts to make agriculture more resilient to climate change while improving the competitiveness of locally produced food. For the Managing Partner of Farmer Globale, Fred Kukubor, the international recognition reinforces the company’s commitment to ensuring smallholder farmers benefit directly from the shift towards more sustainable food production. “This recognition reinforces our conviction that agriculture can be both commercially viable and a powerful force for climate action and inclusive development. Our ambition is to ensure that farmers are not merely participants in the transition to sustainable agriculture, but among its greatest beneficiaries,” the company said. Farmer Globale says it will continue to expand practical agricultural innovations, strengthen market opportunities and attract investment to deliver measurable benefits for farmers, rural communities and the environment. Its approach seeks to connect sustainable farming practices with stronger value chains, giving smallholder farmers greater opportunities to participate in and benefit from the changing agricultural economy. About Farmer Globale Established in 2017, Farmer Globale is a Ghanaian agribusiness development organisation focused on sustainable agriculture, agricultural technology and inclusive rural development. Through integrated value-chain solutions, market access and climate-smart innovations, the organisation works to improve smallholder farmers’ livelihoods, strengthen agricultural competitiveness and promote sustainable rural development.

title: Number injured in Russian attack on Chernihiv rises to 31 – police
body:
The number of casualties from the strike on the center of Chernihiv has risen to 31, according to Head of the patrol police department Oleksiy Biloshytsky.

"Two dead, 31 injured – the consequences of the enemy shelling of Chernihiv. Four children are among the victims," he said on Telegram on Thursday evening.

Biloshytsky's post is accompanied by footage from the scene of the strike (video from police body cameras).

As previously reported, two 15-year-old girls were killed as a result of a Russian UAV strike on Chernihiv on October 29; the victims included children, notably a 10-month-old girl.

Friday, October 30, has been declared a Day of Mourning in the city for the residents who died as a result of Russian strikes between October 21 and 29.

title: Polish MiG-29s, F-16 Cannon Ammo Reportedly Headed To Ukraine As Bitter Warsaw-Kyiv Rift Heals
body: In a key indication of improving ties between Poland and Ukraine, Warsaw has reportedly agreed to provide two additional MiG-29 Fulcrum fighters, badly needed 20x102mm rounds for Ukrainian Air Force F-16s and artillery shells. Relations between the two countries soured this summer over a political spat between their respective leaders, however they appear to be restoring once-close ties . The aircraft transfer will occur “in the near future,” Lt. Gen. Dariusz Łukowski, director of the Strategy and Defense Planning Department at the Polish Ministry of National Defense, told the Polish Rzeczpospolita ( Rz ) media outlet. “The decision has been made, and two MiG-29s will be handed over.” Of the two Fulcrums, one has reached the end of its service life and may be used for parts while the other is still flying, Rz added. Deputy National Defense Minister Paweł Zalewski confirmed the MiG-29 agreement to another Polish media outlet, TVP Info . “There is an agreement regarding the transfer of two MiG-29s to Ukraine,” Zalewski said. “As regards the remaining MiGs, the matter is ongoing.” Poland had 14 MiG-29 aircraft as of December 2025, of which six to eight were nearing the end of their service life, a Polish official said at the time . It is unclear how many are still on hand. Polish Air Force MiG-29 Fulcrums take part in a NATO Air Force military drill on October 12, 2022 in Lask, Poland. (Photo by Stringer/Anadolu Agency via Getty Images) Anadolu In addition to the jets, Rz reported that “Poland will provide Ukraine with, among other things, a supply of 155mm and 152mm artillery ammunition; 20x102mm combat rounds for the six-barreled cannons on F-16 fighter jets—used, for instance, to shoot down Russian unmanned aerial vehicles—as well as missiles for the Piorun short-range anti-aircraft systems.” Additional MiG-29s are always welcome, as they remain the backbone of Ukraine’s fighter force even though the country has received donations of more modern F-16 Vipers and French Mirage 2000 fighters . Meanwhile, the 20mm cannon ammunition is critically needed. As we have previously reported , Ukraine is struggling to maintain adequate stocks of air-to-air missiles for its fighters. AIM-9 Sidewinders and AIM-120 Advanced Medium-Range Air-to-Air Missiles (AMRAAM) have been heavily used against Russian cruise missiles and drones. As a result, Ukrainian F-16 pilots have reportedly had to ration their missile shots. This has forced them to increasingly rely on their internal 20mm cannon when suitable missiles are not available. Such a tactic is far from an ideal substitute, as you can read about here . Still, Kyiv has reportedly been seeking tens of thousands of additional rounds of 20mm ammunition. Poland is reportedly providing 20mm cannon ammunition for Ukrainian Air Force F-16s. (Ukrainian Air Force) Ukrainian Air Force So far, there has been no official Ukrainian response. We reached out to Zelensky’s spokesman and Polish officials for comment. Reports about the planned Polish weapons transfers to Ukraine mark a turning point in relations between Warsaw and Kyiv, as we noted at the top of the story. For much of this conflict, Poland has been one of Ukraine’s staunchest allies, serving as a logistics hub and providing military assistance. Warsaw’s initial donation of MiG-29s opened the door for the transfer of dozens of others from several NATO nations. That was followed by the eventual provision of the aforementioned Vipers and Mirages. In addition, Sweden has agreed to provide 16 Gripen C/D fighters , with the first aircraft expected in early 2027, while a separate agreement covers the purchase of 16 new Gripen E fighters whose deliveries are not scheduled to begin until early 2029. A Ukrainian Air Force Mirage 2000 takes off from an unidentified airfield in Ukraine. (Ukrainian Air Force) Relations between the two countries reached a nadir in June after Polish President Karol Nawrocki stripped Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky of the Order of the White Eagle. It is Warsaw’s top award and was presented to Zelensky in 2023. That escalated a row between the allies over the memory of WWII. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenski (left) and then-Polish President Andrzej Duda as Zelenski was honored with ”Order of the White Eagle” in Warsaw, Poland on April 05, 2023. (Photo by Foto Olimpik/NurPhoto) Foto Olimpik “Zelensky had infuriated Warsaw this month by naming a military unit after an insurgent army that took part in massacres against Poles in WWII,” AFP reported at the time. After the stripping of the award, the rift grew more bitter, with Poland claiming Ukraine would not transfer drone technology needed to defend against Russian threats. The political kerfuffle culminated with Poland canceling the transfer of additional MiG-29s to Ukraine. Relations between the two nations began to thaw earlier this month. The first sign was Zelensky’s resuming use of Polish airports as a jumping-off point for overseas trips. Ukrainian officials have to travel by train to another country if they want to fly because airspace over Ukraine has been closed to non-military aircraft since the start of the all-out war. After the medal incident, Zelensky opted to use airports in Moldova and Romania . However, on Oct. 14, the Ukrainian leader once again traveled to Rzeszów Airport in Poland. Days later, Zelensky told reporters that stopping at Rzeszów was a signal that his relations with Poland were on the upswing . “Our relations with Poland have indeed improved,” he said. I’m very grateful for this to both Poland and our teams, and I’m grateful to the Prime Minister [Donald Tusk]. I’m grateful to the people of Poland for supporting Ukraine. It’s very important for us to be together right now. There is only one enemy – Russia, which is deeply concerned about a strong alliance between Ukraine and Poland.” “Even very difficult things, we’ll resolve them, I’m sure of it,” the Ukrainian leader added. “These will be mutually beneficial relations, out of respect, because of the importance of security in Europe.” Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky expressed gratitude for Polish support. (Office of the President of Ukraine) Though Polish officials are telling media outlets that deals are in place, there is still a lot that can go sideways before the aircraft and ammunition are in Ukrainian hands. Still, for Kyiv, even suggestions of a future transfer are better than having deals being called off. Contact the author: howard@twz.com The post Polish MiG-29s, F-16 Cannon Ammo Reportedly Headed To Ukraine As Bitter Warsaw-Kyiv Rift Heals appeared first on TWZ .

title: Greek Containership Sunk by Naval Drones Off Bulgaria as Black Sea Attacks Escalate
body:
Essential news coupled with the finest maritime content sourced from across the globe.
The Liberian-flagged container ship CONTSHIP JET, which sank following a naval drone attack off Bulgaria on October 28, 2026. (Photo: Contships Management)
ATHENS/SOFIA, Oct 29 (Reuters) – A Greek container ship has sunk after being hit by naval drones off Bulgaria on Wednesday, the Bulgarian government said, in the latest of a series of strikes in the western Black Sea this month that have raised concerns about the widening scope of Russia’s war in Ukraine.
The Liberian-flagged CONTSHIP JET, loaded with 421 containers, was badly damaged by three sea drones as it passed through Bulgaria’s Exclusive Economic Zone (EEZ) – but outside its territorial waters – en route from Haifa in Israel to Constan?a in Romania.
The crew of 14 Filipinos and four Ukrainians were all rescued and transferred safely to the Bulgarian port of Varna, Contships Management said.
Video footage verified by Reuters showed a sea drone driving alongside the vessel before turning towards its hull. In a separate video, an explosion was seen, causing the ship to eventually list.
It was not immediately clear who had carried out the attack, which added to growing concerns about the impact of Russia’s war in Ukraine on commercial shipping in the area.
Ambrey, a global maritime risk management firm, has analyzed footage, reportedly filmed on a handheld device by a crew member on board, showing a matte black, 5-6 meter-long unmanned surface vehicle (USV) approaching the vessel at high speed.
The USV was likely a variant of a Russian drone, said Tomas Alexa, a senior analyst at Ambrey Analytics, adding that its maneuvers indicated it was controlled remotely.
“Ambrey assessed that the USV was likely a variant of, or derived from, the Russian Murena-300S design,” he told Reuters.
At least six ships have been attacked by drones off Bulgaria this month, and about two dozen seafarers are feared dead, according to government statements. While it is not clear who has carried out the attacks, Bulgaria’s Prime Minister, Rumen Radev, has said that some of them appear to benefit Russia.
Moscow has denied involvement in recent attacks and did not immediately comment on Wednesday’s incident.
Andriy Ryzhenko, a former senior Ukrainian navy officer, said the drone visible in the video does not look similar to any model of Ukrainian naval drone that he is aware of.
Bulgaria, a member of the European Union and NATO, has sought assistance to bolster security off its Black Sea coast.
Bulgarian naval commander Kiril Mihaylov told national television authorities had been alerted to a possible drone attack by a French patrol aircraft, but had been unable to prevent it.
The government said that initial inspections on Thursday had found no visible traces of pollution from the ship, whose cargo included lithium-ion batteries, corrosive liquids and acids and industrial components.
(Reporting by Stoyan Nenov, Alex Lefkowitz, Renee Maltezou and Tom Balmforth; Additional reporting by Aaron McNicholas and Edward Carron; Writing by Angeliki Koutantou; Editing by Kevin Liffey, Edward McAllister, Toby Chopra)

Russia, the world's largest wheat exporter, has turned to an Arctic World War II shipping route to export grain for the first time as the conflict in Ukraine stalls Black Sea trade and officials warn of risks in the NATO-controlled Baltic Sea.
Russia expects to begin regular year-round eastbound shipping along the Northern Sea Route in early 2027, as additional nuclear icebreaker capacity, newer ice-class LNG carriers and pressure to redirect energy exports toward Asia bring the long-delayed ambition closer to reality.
Russia expects cargo transits along the Northern Sea Route (NSR) to more than double in 2026, marking a substantial increase in Arctic shipping despite Western sanctions, although volumes remain far below Moscow’s original ambitions for the route.

title: AFRL Plans to Award $30M for Cislunar Project Starting Next Spring
body: The Air Force Research Laboratory plans to launch its latest technology challenge next month—a project meant to speed up development of systems that can operate beyond geosynchronous orbit. SpaceWERX is leading the effort, dubbed Cislunar Prime. The space innovation hub is looking for commercial capabilities that could put the Space Force on a faster path toward cislunar operations in three focus areas: space domain awareness cislunar communications positioning, navigation, and timing The tentative plan, according to an AFRL spokesperson, is to officially announce Cislunar Prime in December, solicit proposals in January, and begin awarding contracts next spring. The program has $30 million to fund 15 direct-to-phase-two Small Business Innovation Research contracts worth $2 million each. The Space Force defines cislunar as the region of space past GEO and extending to the moon and beyond , hundreds of thousands of kilometers in distance and 1,728 times the volume of space complained within GEO. Conditions there present challenges for satellite operations like PNT and SDA, given its distance from the Earth and its unstable trajectories. Speaking Oct. 21 at AFCEA’s Space Industry Days conference, Portfolio Acquisition Executive for Advanced Programs Maj. Gen. Stephen Purdy said because of these dynamics, the Space Force needs a better understanding of how to operate in cislunar space. “Space is often described as hard and difficult and a fight that we’re not seeing,” he said. “But I would characterize cislunar as even harder and more difficult, and we really don’t see what’s going on in that arena.” The Space Force has a handful of active projects exploring cislunar operations, including AFRL’s Oracle program, which plans to launch its first satellite in December—a pathfinder for efficient cislunar mobility, navigation, and space domain awareness. Over the past year, the service has signaled it plans to ramp up cislunar research and development activities, driven in part by China’s plans to establish a presence beyond GEO and on the moon. Purdy said the Pentagon’s posture toward cislunar operations and planning has shifted significantly over the past year. He cited President Donald Trump’s December 2025 executive order that emphasized the importance of cislunar operations, as well as Chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff Gen. Dan Caine’s acknowledgement of cislunar as a “warfighting domain” during AFA’s Air, Space, and Cyber Conference in September. Now, the service is looking to quickly fund satellites and software that could be ready for operations as soon as 2029 , Purdy said. Beyond Cislunar Prime, the Space Force and its newly established Cislunar Coordination Office have two forthcoming requests for information—the first focused on existing cislunar hardware and software that could fly in the next two to three years, and the second for AI and autonomous processing capabilities. “We’re looking for existing commercial or near-commercial means, non-developmental solutions, hardware with actual relevant evidence behind it, software that doesn’t need a huge amount of work … and ground systems,” Purdy said. “This isn’t a four- or five-year science project. This is about getting capability out soon.” The post AFRL Plans to Award $30M for Cislunar Project Starting Next Spring appeared first on Air & Space Forces Magazine .

title: Israeli parties begin coalition talks with all votes counted
body: Israeli politicians have begun talks on forming a government as the country finished counting votes in its general election, confirming neither Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu nor his main rival Gadi Eisenkot has a clear path to power. With all votes in, Mr Netanyahu's Likud party was the largest with 20.5 per cent of the vote – a better-than-expected result that gives Israel 's longest-serving leader a shot at staying in power despite a host of controversies at home and abroad. However, the 53 seats won by Mr Netanyahu and his current right-wing coalition partners fell short of the 61 needed for a majority in the 120-member Knesset. Mr Eisenkot's Yashar party came second 16.1 with per cent of the vote. Parties seen as backers of the former army general had 48 seats between them, while Arab parties won the remaining 19 seats in a record performance . The final day of counting was overshadowed by claims and counterclaims of interference in the election. Mr Netanyahu has alleged fraud and bribery involving the Arab parties, who on Thursday rejected the “baseless allegations” and accused Likud of damaging the legitimacy of the vote. Qatar also spoke up to deny claims of involvement. The indecisive result sets the stage for what could be weeks or months of negotiations to form a government. Israeli President Isaac Herzog has urged parties to avoid an early second election and enter talks with an “open mind”. Three blocs Of the 53 seats in the Netanyahu camp, Likud had 27 while parties led by controversial ministers Itamar Ben-Gvir and Bezalel Smotrich won seven and six respectively. Two Ultra-Orthodox parties took the rest. The potential Eisenkot bloc has 48 seats, led by Yashar on 21. An alliance of former prime ministers Yair Lapid and Naftali Bennett, won 12 seats. The anti-Netanyahu camp also includes the centre-left Democrats, with eight seats, and the Yisrael Bentenu party, on seven. The Arab Joint List won 11 seats, with the Ra'am party winning eight. There appeared no easy path to 61 seats. Leaders of the Arab parties have offered their support to an anti-Netanyahu government, potentially giving Mr Eisenkot a majority. But relying on Arab support would be hugely contentious in Israel and some members of the Eisenkot bloc had ruled it out during the campaign. Another possibility would be for Mr Netanyahu to peel off members of the Eisenkot camp, some of whom are on the right of Israeli politics. However, all had campaigned on removing Mr Netanyahu, whose policies have been divisive at home and led to allegations of war crimes and genocide against Israel . Talks begin Speaking on Thursday, Mr Eisenkot promised to act “calmly and with determination” but gave no details of how he planned to form a government. He said he would not allow the swearing in of the new Knesset to be delayed “by a single centimetre” despite investigations into the vote. As cross-party talks began, Mr Eisenkot met the leader of the centre-left Democrats, Yair Golan, who was also speaking to former prime minister Yair Lapid and one of the Arab party leaders, Mansour Abbas. “Israeli citizens fired Netanyahu,” Mr Golan said. “We will do everything to establish a government of change and rescue – because that is the will of the voter.” While counting was completed on Thursday, the results are still to be finally ratified. Once they are, President Herzog can select a member of the Knesset to form a coalition. If neither Mr Netanyahu nor Mr Eisenkot can make it to 61 seats, another election is possible early next year. Likud was calling for Israeli security services to investigate the fraud claims. Critics say that by stepping up attacks on Arab parties, Mr Netanyahu may be trying to ensure that Mr Eisenkot ⁠feels unable to form a minority government with Arab help that could remove him from power. Turnout soared in Arab communities, with some voters who had previously boycotted Israeli elections taking part for the first time. Israeli broadcasters said it could have reached 80 per cent. But few would count out Mr Netanyahu, who has survived a long series of scandals and political crises to rule Israel for all but 18 months since 2009. In the meantime, Mr Netanyahu remains in power and there are he will use the interlude to his advantage by launching new attacks on Iran . The US is also said to be considering new strikes after midterm elections next week.

title: Moonshot 2026: ‘Africa must move from content creation to value capture’ — Tech leader Juliet Ehimuan
body: By Efosa Taiwo Juliet Ehimuan, founder of Beyond Limits and former Director of Google West Africa, has urged African creatives and technology entrepreneurs to move beyond content creation to building sustainable businesses that own intellectual property and capture value from their work. Ehimuan made the call while speaking on artificial intelligence (AI) and the future of African creativity at Moonshot 2026 during a keynote speech on Thursday. She said Africa’s creative economy remained underdeveloped, stressing the need to turn the continent’s creative talent into commercially viable enterprises capable of generating greater economic value. “Our creative economy is still less than 2% of GDP,” she said, highlighting the need for a shift from producing content to building businesses around it. According to her, African creators must focus on owning the intellectual property behind their work and exploring different ways to commercialise it. “We need to move from content creation to value capture. We need to move from having creative talents to building enterprises. We should move from content creation to IP,” Ehimuan said. She explained that intellectual property ownership could open up multiple revenue streams, noting that a book could be adapted into a series, while a podcast could generate additional commercial opportunities. “There are so many ways to monetise content if you have the IP for that,” she said, emphasising the importance of owning intellectual property and the infrastructure needed to distribute and commercialise creative products. Ehimuan outlined three priorities for Africa’s creative and technology sectors: adopting and developing AI capabilities, building and owning valuable assets, and establishing businesses capable of reaching wider markets. On AI adoption, she encouraged African businesses to develop their capabilities and stay ahead of technological changes, noting that the technology could improve productivity and create new opportunities across industries. She also urged creators and businesses to protect their rights and permissions while developing distinctive intellectual property that could be commercialised over time. title: Ghana and Poland explore investment opportunities and security cooperation
body: Ghana and Poland have reaffirmed their commitment to strengthening bilateral relations, with discussions focusing on trade, investment, industrial development, technology, education and security. The commitment was reiterated when Deputy Minister for Foreign Affairs, James Gyakye Quayson, met Poland’s Undersecretary of State for Foreign Affairs, Wojciech Zajaczkowski, at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs in Accra on Thursday, October 29, 2026. The meeting provided an opportunity for the two countries to review their longstanding relations and identify areas for deeper cooperation. Mr Zajaczkowski recalled the cordial ties between Ghana and Poland in the 1960s, 1970s and 1980s, particularly in education, technical training, engineering and industrial development. He expressed Poland’s renewed interest in deepening its engagement with Ghana and the wider African continent, citing Ghana’s political stability, economic potential and strategic location in West Africa as factors that make it an attractive partner for Polish businesses seeking to expand into African markets. Mr Gyakye Quayson welcomed the renewed interest and reaffirmed Ghana’s commitment to partnerships based on mutual benefit, economic cooperation and respect for national interests. He also highlighted Ghana’s longstanding policy of non-alignment and its commitment to maintaining friendly relations with all countries, irrespective of ideological differences. He said diversifying international partnerships was important to supporting Ghana’s economic transformation and reducing excessive dependence on any single country or group of countries. The Deputy Minister further highlighted the government’s industrialisation and value-addition agenda, stressing the need to move beyond exporting raw materials towards domestic processing and manufacturing. He encouraged Polish businesses to explore investment opportunities in Ghana, particularly in cocoa and gold processing, agribusiness, food processing, agricultural equipment, pharmaceuticals, information technology and manufacturing. He also pointed to the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA), headquartered in Accra, as an important platform for businesses operating in Ghana to access markets across the continent. The discussions also covered the changing geopolitical and security environment and its implications for international cooperation and economic development. Mr Zajaczkowski expressed interest in exploring cooperation with Ghana in border management and the protection of critical infrastructure. He proposed that Polish experts could visit Ghana to demonstrate relevant technologies and engage with Ghanaian officials. The meeting concluded with both sides expressing confidence that the historical friendship between Ghana and Poland provided a strong foundation for expanding cooperation in trade, investment, technology transfer, industrial development, and other areas of mutual interest.

title: 2027: Tompolo, Oyebanji task Ekiti voters on landslide win for Tinubu, unveil 25 vehicles
body:
Voters in Ekiti State have been urged to ensure that President Bola Tinubu records a landslide win in the 2027 presidential election in the state.
The Grand Patron of the PBAT Door-To-Door Campaign, Government Ekpemupolo, popularly known as Tompolo, made the call on Thursday at the inauguration of the state chapter of the PBAT Door-to-Door Movement, during which he donated 25 vehicles for campaigns across the state.
Tompolo announced the donation through his representative, Kestin Pondi, the managing director of Tantita Security Services Nigeria Limited, even as he stressed the need for the people of Ekiti to massively vote President Tinubu as a highly respected and loved Yoruba son.
He said: “Today, we have an economy that is stable because of President Tinubu. Today, governors have money to pay salaries, pension and they have money to execute projects because President Bola Ahmed Tinubu chose to be bold enough to remove petrol subsidy and to implement the reformative policies he put forward.
“When you come into a person’s house where his brother is contesting elections and you tell the person that you want him for vote for his candidate brother, it could sound insulting.
“President Bola Ahmed Tinubu is your son, brother and in some instances your father, as well as the father of Nigeria, so I would say, we are here to support you to vote for your brother.
“We are here to support you to mobilise to get all the votes that are available for your brother. Part of the support are these vehicles, which are to move from door-to-door, from unit to unit, from ward to ward, from local government to local government, from constituency to constituency and from mosques to mosques and churches to churches.
“Our ultimate goal is to garner votes across the country to ensure the president completes his reformation agenda.”
Tompolo called on members and leaders of the movement to make judicious use of the vehicles as well as other campaign equipment and tools to take the message of President Tinubu’s reelection to the grassroots.
In his speech at the rally, the Ekiti State Governor, Biodun Oyebanji, said victory is sure for the president in his state.
Mr Oyebanji described President Tinubu as the second reason for the success he has recorded as governor, stressing that Ekiti must reward the president with a minimum of 80 per cent of votes come January 2027.
“My plea to Ekiti people is this: that President Bola Ahmed Tinubu will win in Ekiti is not in contention is but by how much?
“In the last election, Ekiti people voted 85.7 per cent in favour of APC. That will be the first time that kind of margin will happen in this state for any political party. And by my own understanding and readings, is that they (voters) did that because this government has served them, and they want a continuity of the government that has served them.
“I consistently to tell Ekiti people, we are 30 years old as a state and there’s no president that has been this fair, this good to Ekiti more than Asiwaju Bola Ahmed Tinubu. If Ekiti people came out and voted in favour of APC in June so that our good works can continue, the only way I’ll be able to continue to serve you is if Asiwaju is reelected. Because everything we have achieved in this state, after God, is the president. I won’t be able to do anything on my own without the support of the president.
“So my plea to you is, chances are that by next year, yes, January next year, Ekiti votes will be the first to be announced as it happened in 2023. But anything less than 80 per cent of total votes cast or total PVC collected will be unacceptable because the only way we can thank the president for what he has done is for us to come out and vote for him.
“And I’m pleading with all of us that the mistake that happened in June should not repeat itself, where people said that either we vote or we don’t vote, ‘Baba’ will win. It’s not going to work in January. So those people that had PVC that did not come out and vote, we have to go and locate them”, the governor stated.
Mr Oyebanji also commended Tompolo for the donation from the Movement and for boldly supporting the president, saying, “on behalf of the government and the people of Ekiti State, we are extremely grateful to you for what you are doing for the country. Because anybody that is campaigning for the re-election of Asiwaju Bola Ahmed Tinubu, loves Nigeria. Whoever doesn’t support his re-election is an enemy of this country. And I sat down there listening to Dr. Pondi, and he was mentioning the members of this movement. And I told myself that this is a big challenge to us in Ekiti”.
Also speaking at the rally, Speaker of the Ekiti State House of Assembly, Adeoye Aribasoye, commended Tompolo for taking the campaign for Tinubu’ reelection across the country. He assured that Ekiti will give Tinubu maiority of its votes.
“In Ekiti State, I will say, coming here is like coming to preach to the converted. For us in Ekiti State, just like our governor has been preaching, that whatever you have seen him doing in the state, these are what President Bola Ahmed Tinubu has enabled him to do and that after God, it’s President Bola Ahmed Tinubu.
“For us in Ekiti we want our governor to continue with his good works and for him to continue with the good work, we must return President Bola Ahmed Tinubu,” Mr Arabisoye stated.
Earlier, the National Coordinator of the PBAT Door-to-Door Movement, Sunday Asuku, called on the people of Ekiti State to turn out massively to vote for Tinubu.
Mr Asuku took time to reel out President Tinubu’s achievements, stressing that the opposition only have fake promises to offer the people.
He said: “It is time to demystify the propaganda being peddled around by the naysayers. If you observe keenly, that is because they have nothing to say. As I usually say, most of them they have held one position or the other in the past. We must learn to ask them questions. While you were in office, what did you do? Give us what you did while you were in office. Tell us, what do you want to come and do? Some of them are acting as if they forgot something in Aso-Rock.
The national coordinator urged members of the Movement to go the extra mile by speaking to voters from door to door, city to city and even at gatherings.

title: Putin highlights Russia’ leading position in grain exports
body:
MOSCOW, October 29. /TASS/. Russia has transformed from a major grain importer in the early 2000s into the world’s largest grain exporter, President Vladimir Putin said at a press conference following the Russia-Africa Summit.
"Not so long ago, in the early 2000s, Russia was an absolute buyer of grain and other agricultural products, but now, we are the world’s number one in terms of grain exports," he pointed out.

title: Senior US general fired, accused of leaking classified information
body: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth has fired U.S. Army Lt. Gen. Brett Sylvia, a senior military planner on the Pentagon’s Joint Staff, over accusations that he leaked classified information to the public, officials said on Thursday. Sylvia’s firing is one of the highest-profile consequences to date from Hegseth’s sweeping hunt for officials suspected of leaking information to the news media as the unpopular Iran war enters its ninth month. Hegseth’s effort includes a Pentagon task force to identify the source of leaks and the widespread use of polygraph exams on senior officials as part of these investigations. Last year, he introduced a media policy that raised legal concerns among press organizations, and revoked the press credentials of journalists who refused to sign it. A senior Pentagon official, speaking on condition of anonymity, accused Sylvia of failing three polygraphs questioning him about leaking classified information. “The extent of his leaking became so critical that Secretary Hegseth took immediate action and fired Sylvia in order to protect national security. Urgent action was needed and could not wait another second,” the official said. U.S. President Donald Trump, who misidentified Sylvia as a woman, said the senior US general has “got problems.” “We’re very much looking for leakers, and she’s going to have big problems, long-term problems,” Trump told reporters. Sylvia could not be immediately reached for comment. Key position Sylvia led the Directorate for Strategy, Plans, and Policy at the Joint Staff, known inside the military as the J5, a key position that helps advise the top US military official, General Dan Caine, the chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff. He previously led the US Army’s 101st Airborne Division. His dismissal was first reported by The Atlantic magazine. His removal comes as the US military plans for a potential resumption of intensive bombings in Iran, something Trump has called “another little Epic Fury.” The Pentagon has fumed about leaks during the Iran war, including about its planning and the expenditure of munitions. Reuters reported on Wednesday that an internal US military analysis estimates it would cost more than $29 billion in munitions alone to restock weapons used against Iran so far. That’s the bulk of the more than $47 billion spent on operations in the war. Sean Parnell, the chief Pentagon spokesperson, said the decision followed an extensive investigation by the Air Force Office of Special Investigations. “This matter, along with others, have been referred to the Justice Department for potential further legal action,” Parnell said, without identifying other officials who may also be targeted. Parnell added: “Our commitment was not an empty promise. We vowed to find you, and we meant it.” A spokesperson for the Joint Staff withdrew an initial statement expressing gratitude for Sylvia’s 32 years of service, saying “we determined the statement did not appropriately reflect the full circumstances.” “Out of respect for the service member and the ongoing personnel process, we will not comment further,” the spokesperson said.

title: ‘One in 4 Nigerian stroke patients under 50’
body: One in four stroke cases in Nigeria affects people below 50, raising concerns about the disease’s growing burden among young adults. Prof. Kolawole Wahab, Head of the Stroke Unit at the University of Ilorin Teaching Hospital (UITH), disclosed this on Thursday in Ilorin. He spoke on the sidelines of a medical rally commemorating the 2026 World Stroke Day, with the theme ‘Every Minute Counts’, which highlights the importance of prompt treatment. Wahab said research published in 2017 had documented the prevalence of stroke among younger Nigerians. “When we talk about stroke in the young, we are talking about those who are below the age of 50. “One out of every four cases of stroke in Nigeria could be a case of stroke in the young. The prevalence is as high as 25 per cent. “We see people who are in their 40s, some in their 30s, coming down with stroke,” he said. The neurologist described the stroke burden in the region as epidemic, adding that UITH’s emergency department receives one or two stroke patients daily. He identified hypertension as Nigeria’s leading stroke risk factor, warning that poor blood pressure control could increase the likelihood of the condition. According to him, up to nine out of every 10 stroke cases have hypertension as an underlying factor. Wahab expressed concern that some patients abandon prescribed medication in favour of unproven remedies, leaving their blood pressure uncontrolled. He also identified diabetes as another major risk factor, noting that some people remain unaware they have the condition. Others, he said, neglect proper diabetes management in spite of knowing their status. “It is until they have suffered from stroke that they become aware they have diabetes,” he said. Wahab listed imbalances in blood fats among other risk factors, explaining that abnormal levels of good and bad fats could contribute to stroke. He warned against smoking, excessive alcohol consumption, hard drugs and sedentary lifestyles, urging Nigerians to adopt healthier habits. The expert also advised people to moderate their salt intake, particularly those diagnosed with hypertension. He cautioned against adding table salt to meals after preparation, stressing the importance of controlling blood pressure. Also speaking, Dr Wemimo Olaofin, a consultant neurologist at UITH, urged Nigerians to check their blood pressure regularly. Olaofin said stroke could occur suddenly at any time, but preventive measures and proper health management could reduce the risk. He encouraged the public to monitor their blood pressure and embrace healthier lifestyles to prevent the condition. Mrs Tejumola Olayinka, Deputy Director of Nursing in charge of UITH’s Stroke Care Unit, said the commemoration aimed to promote awareness and early hospital presentation. “Stroke case is an emergency case that requires timely intervention. We can reduce the number of mortality and also reduce the number of people with stroke,” she said. Olayinka described stroke as a sudden occurrence, “like a slap”, and highlighted facial drooping, arm weakness and slurred speech as warning signs. She urged people displaying these symptoms to be rushed to hospital immediately for medical attention. The nursing director also warned stroke patients against failing to take prescribed medication, noting that some patients did not adhere to treatment in spite of knowing their condition. As part of the commemoration, UITH organised an awareness rally across the hospital and medical outreach programmes at the teaching hospital and Kwara Government House. Two beneficiaries, Mr Jimoh Abdullateef and Mrs Fatima Abdulazeez, commended the medical team for providing free medical services and distributing drugs. title: 2027: Tinubu Doesn’t Have Energy, Competence To Run Nigeria — Obi
body: The presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Peter Obi, has criticised President Bola Tinubu over his governance track record, alleging that the President has spent over 260 days outside Nigeria since taking office but claims he cannot spare 36 days to campaign across the nation’s states. Obi made the remarks on Thursday in Abakaliki, the Ebonyi State capital, during a political meeting. He was reacting to recent statements by President Tinubu, who indicated he might not campaign in all 36 states ahead of the 2027 general elections due to the demands of governance. Declaring himself the leading candidate for the 2027 presidency, Obi asserted that the President lacks the physical energy and administrative competence to manage the country, urging him to step aside. “President Tinubu has stayed over 260 days out of Nigeria, yet he cannot spend up to 36 days going around Nigeria to tell the people what he has been doing for the past three years,” the former Anambra governor said. “He does not have the competence to run Nigeria; he does not have the energy to run Nigeria. He should pack his things, go home, and rest.” Challenging the President to face the electorate directly, the presidential candidate urged Tinubu to visit Ebonyi State and account for his stewardship. “I want President Tinubu to come to Abakaliki to tell the people what he has done in the past three years,” Obi stated. “I want him to come to Abakaliki to tell you what he used the money he has been borrowing to do, and to tell Nigerians what he has used their money for.” Addressing political unity, Obi warned against regional division in the South East, emphasising that his candidacy is anchored on merit and capacity rather than ethnic identity. “Let nobody divide the South East. I don’t want the people of Ebonyi to vote for me because I am from the South East or because I am Igbo,” Obi declared. “My dear people, I want you to vote for me because I am qualified to be the President of this country, and because I am the leading candidate.” Outlining his vision if elected, Obi promised to declare a national state of emergency across seven critical sectors, including security, hunger, education, healthcare, corruption, power, and national unity. “We must unite this country. Our pride should not be based on ethnic considerations. “We will operate the Federal Character principle transparently for all public roles, ensuring every section of Nigeria is included,” he added. “We will declare an emergency on the security of lives and property and deal with insecurity decisively. If kids are in school and someone abducts them into the bush, we will not leave them alone; we will equip our security agencies to defend our people.” “I will fight corruption like nobody has fought it before. Public money must be used for public good; nobody will steal our money again. If you embezzle public funds, you will go to jail, starting from the President.” Speaking further, he said, “We have over 18 million children out of school, and we must reduce that number drastically. On hunger, we have vast arable land; our farmers must safely return to their farms to cultivate food for local consumption and export.” “We will ensure functional healthcare in every political ward across Nigeria. We have the resources required to achieve this.” The post 2027: Tinubu Doesn’t Have Energy, Competence To Run Nigeria — Obi appeared first on Channels Television .

title: Ukraine says Zelensky is ready to discuss territory with Putin in person
body: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky has sent word to Russian President Vladimir Putin that he is ready to discuss territory at an in-person meeting, Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andriy Sybiha told the newspaper Helsingin Sanomat. Finnish President Alexander Stubb and Norwegian Prime Minister Jonas Støre conveyed Zelensky’s position to Putin during a phone call on October 27. Sybiha said the European leaders initiated the call in coordination with Kyiv. Its main purpose was to convey Ukraine’s message: Along with proposing an in-person meeting between the leaders, Ukraine also called for a ceasefire. “We want this meeting and are ready for it. In all likelihood, only a meeting between Zelensky and Putin can change the dynamics of the negotiations. Zelensky is ready to discuss the most difficult and sensitive issues, including territory,” Sybiha said. Stubb’s office had previously said the purpose of the call was to “convey Ukraine’s position on the upcoming peace talks in Abu Dhabi directly to President Putin.” Helsinki provided no details. Putin’s conversation with Stubb and Støre was his first contact with European leaders who support Ukraine since July 2025, when he spoke with French President Emmanuel Macron. title: Stakeholders call for stronger community-security collaboration to prevent extremism
body: Stakeholders have called for stronger collaboration between communities and security agencies to prevent violent extremism and safeguard Ghana’s peace. The call was made on Wednesday, October 28, at a National Dialogue on Civil-Security Engagement in Accra, convened by Catholic Relief Services (CRS) in partnership with the National Security Council Secretariat and the National Peace Council, with funding from the Netherlands Ministry of Foreign Affairs. The dialogue brought together more than 60 participants from government, security agencies, civil society, traditional and religious institutions, and development partners. CRS Ghana Country Representative, Dr. Abena Amedormey, stressed the need for a whole-of-society approach, noting that the organisation and its partners had engaged more than 1,000 stakeholders across Northern Ghana this year to strengthen community resilience. National Security Coordinator, COP Osman Abdul-Razak, also emphasised collective action, while Netherlands Ambassador to Ghana, Hans Akerboom, highlighted the importance of inclusive governance, youth opportunities and community engagement. Chairman of the National Peace Council, Most Rev. Emmanuel Kofi Fianu, called for innovative approaches to youth employment, warning that limited opportunities could increase young people’s vulnerability to extremist recruitment. Participants are expected to use recommendations from the dialogue to strengthen community participation, early intervention, and locally led efforts to prevent violent extremism in Ghana.

title: Zelenskyy: Intelligence reports indicate Russia preparing new ballistic missile strikes
body:
According to intelligence reports, Russia is preparing new ballistic strikes, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has said.
"We currently have intelligence indicating that the Russians are preparing new ballistic missile strikes. And we need the forces to shoot down all this Russian evil. We are awaiting the appropriate decisions," Zelenskyy said in an evening address on Thursday.
The president said he had chaired a meeting of the Supreme Commander-in-Chief's Headquarters, the key issue of which was countering Russian ballistic missiles.
"Sanctions pressure alone is not enough; we need the packages from our partners that we have discussed with them. If we look at key jurisdictions, sanctions can't really impose significant restrictions right away, but only over time – sometimes it takes months of work to achieve this," he said.
Zelenskyy said the longer the sanctions packages against ballistic missiles are delayed, the longer Russia will have the supply chains necessary for production.
He instructed the Ministry of Foreign Affairs to expedite this work with partners.
"We have also identified additional tasks for long-range sanctions, which take effect much more quickly. No public details are available on this yet, but everyone has seen in recent weeks that Ukraine's long-range capabilities are yielding results," he said.

title: Mine clearance completed for Alyoshki humanitarian mission — Russian official
body:
MOSCOW, October 29. /TASS/. Mine clearance has been completed along the routes designated for the humanitarian mission in Alyoshki, and the aid convoy is ready to depart, Russian Human Rights Commissioner Yana Lantratova said.
"Mine clearance has been completed. Thank you to our service members who risked their lives to ensure safe passage along those roads. The convoy will head toward the central district hospital," she wrote on Telegram.

title: GJA pushes for bill to establish minimum wage for journalists
body: The Ghana Journalists Association (GJA) is seeking to lay a private member’s bill before parliament that would consider improving the economic and working conditions of journalists. President of the GJA, Albert Dwumfour, says the national leadership of the association is collaborating with parliament to sponsor a bill that would constitutionally establish a basic minimum wage for both private and state-owned media. Speaking at the Ashanti Media Excellence Award in Kumasi, Mr. Dwumfour noted that engagements are progressing steadily to consider among others ways to improve the welfare and safety of media practitioners. “We’ve also engaged the Speaker of Parliament and leadership of parliament to collaborate with them to sponsor a private member bill on the economic conditions of journalists in this country. We need a bill that can ensure that at least journalists will have a basic minimum wage and also to see how we can improve conditions of journalists. This would be imposed on not only state-owned media but all other private media owners,” he said. Mr. Dwumfuor bemoaned the service conditions of journalists in Ghana, insisting that poor emoluments, job insecurity and insufficient working tools could compromise the quality of journalism. He stressed that a significant number of journalists who are economically vulnerable face a more challenging task of resisting inducement or withstanding external pressure. “Improving working conditions is not merely a welfare issue, but also a matter of professional integrity and media independence and even a threat to national security,” he added. He says a demand for excellence and professionalism must be backed by decent remuneration and working conditions. “We cannot continue to demand excellence from journalists while ignoring the economic realities confronting many of them. Poor remuneration, job insecurity, inadequate working tools, limited opportunities for professional development and difficult working conditions can undermine quality of journalism and expose practitioners to undue pressure,” he said. Mr. Dwumfour disclosed that his administration has initiated processes aimed at engaging relevant stakeholders on ways to improve journalists’ welfare and working conditions. “This requires constructive dialogue with media owners, employers, regulators, government institutions, and other partners. The GJA will continue to improve the conditions while encouraging journalists to demonstrate professionalism, responsibility, and commitment to excellence,” he said.

title: Demining complete, humanitarian convoy ready: Oleshky mission advances as ceasefire holds and Lubinets heads to occupied city
body: (function(w,q){w[q]=w[q]||[];w[q].push(["_mgc.load"])})(window,"_mgq"); Ukraine’s humanitarian mission to Russian-occupied Oleshky in Kherson Oblast has reached a key stage, with mine clearance along designated routes completed and a humanitarian convoy ready to depart, Ukraine’s Human Rights Commissioner Dmytro Lubinets said on 29 October. The mission aims to deliver humanitarian aid to civilians trapped in the occupied city facing humanitarian crisis, and provide a safe way out for those who want to leave. The operation is taking place under a localized ceasefire coordinated with the help of US First Lady Melania Trump. Lubinets said the ceasefire has held for 54 hours without reported violations. Aid convoy prepared, civilian evacuations planned Lubinets said the humanitarian convoy was ready to leave and was expected to reach Oleshky’s central hospital. Residents would receive the assistance they need, he said. Civilians wishing to leave the city would have an opportunity to do so until 2 p.m. local time, with security measures organized for their departure. Distribution of humanitarian aid was scheduled to begin after 2:30 p.m. Delegations from Ukraine, Russia, and the United States had gathered to coordinate the next steps in the mission. Journalists from all three countries were also present, Lubinets said. Lubinets travels to occupied Oleshky Earlier on 29 October, Lubinets said he was still traveling toward Oleshky. He said he wanted to be on the ground to see the situation firsthand and report on the mission’s progress. Lubinets also asked the public to rely on official sources and wait until he returned before raising further questions about the negotiations. The Ukrainian ombudsman said the negotiations had been difficult and lengthy, adding that the mission had reached only the halfway point toward its goals. “If I had to go for the sake of one person, I would go again,” Lubinets said, describing the mission as his duty to help Ukrainians in need. US-mediated ceasefire enables humanitarian operation The mission is being conducted jointly by Lubinets and Russian human rights commissioner Yana Lantratova, with mediation and coordination by Melania Trump . The localized ceasefire took effect on 27 October to allow mine clearance, humanitarian deliveries, and civilian evacuations. Oleshky, on the east bank of the Dnipro River in Kherson Oblast, has been under Russian occupation since 2022. Russian occupation and restrictions on access to the city have left civilians facing severe shortages of food, medicine, and other essential supplies, while access to medical care has become increasingly difficult. The humanitarian mission aims to deliver urgently needed aid and help residents who want to leave reach safety. Explore further Thousands are starving in occupied Oleshky. People have no food, no way out, and Russian forces bomb incoming aid Lubinets thanked Melania Trump and the Ukrainians and US citizens who helped bring attention to the situation in Oleshky and support the negotiations. He said the mission’s priority remained delivering assistance and helping civilians leave safely.
