title: Why did Russia agree to the Oleshky ceasefire?
body:
An aerial view of Russian-occupied Oleshky, Kherson Oblast, Ukraine in a photo published on Sept.16, 2026. (Dmytro Lubinets / Telegram)
Moscow's consent to a temporary ceasefire in Russian-occupied Oleshky seems like a long-overdue and welcome concession from a country that has repeatedly rejected or violated ceasefire proposals during the full-scale invasion of Ukraine.
So why is the Kremlin so on board with Oleshky ? Experts, as well as information from Oleshky itself, suggest Russia's motives go far beyond addressing the humanitarian catastrophe it created itself.
Instead, the highly publicized ceasefire brokered by U.S. First Lady Melania Trump presents several opportunities for Moscow to manipulate facts on the ground, an international audience, and — crucially — the White House, all as it positions itself ahead of a new round of peace talks.
"They know exactly what they're doing," John Foreman, a former U.K. defense attache in both Kyiv and Moscow, told the Kyiv Independent.
Oleshky has been under Russian occupation since the early days of Russia's full-scale invasion. Located across the Dnipro River from Kherson , the city has been effectively blockaded by Russian forces, which have prevented humanitarian aid from reaching residents.
Residents have faced severe shortages of food, water, and electricity. Mined roads and constant drone attacks have made safe evacuation virtually impossible, and civilians trying to flee on the only roads in and out of the city have frequently been targeted by drones.
Russian President Vladimir Putin on Oct. 29 accused Ukraine of "creating a humanitarian catastrophe" in Oleshky, despite the fact that Russian forces have been in control of the city since 2022.
Military analyst Vasyl Pehno said on Oct. 27 that Russia had created the humanitarian crisis in Oleshky and is now presenting itself as "heroically rescuing civilians."
The evacuation of residents from Oleshky provides the Kremlin with the opportunity to convince the world that Ukrainians under occupation would rather live in Russia than go back to Ukraine.
The Russian-installed head of occupied Kherson Oblast, Volodymyr Saldo , claimed on Oct. 27 that residents will have a choice — either to stay in Russia or to travel to Ukrainian-controlled territory "to reunite with their families."
But a source familiar with the events unfolding on the ground, speaking to the Kyiv Independent on condition of anonymity, said on Oct. 29 that Russia was already taking steps to ensure as few people as possible left for Ukraine .
They said that patients at the city's only functioning hospital were being registered and told they faced filtration if they left, Russian forces had refused to go house-to-house to inform sick and immobile people that the evacuation was happening, and those living in outlying villages had been told they could be shot if they approached the assembly point.
Some residents expressed fears in local Telegram chats that they could be taken to "concentration camps."
Footage broadcast by Russian state media channel TASS also appears to show civilians being moved with only Russian forces present and before the agreed-upon date of departure, Oct. 30.
Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha previously warned that Russia is preparing to stage "dozens" of videos, and President Volodymyr Zelensky said on Oct. 25 that Russia will likely "do everything it can to clear the roads in such a way that these people head toward Russia and remain there."
Despite efforts by the United Nations, the International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC), and even Pope Leo XIV, a ceasefire agreement has only come about since the intervention of Melania Trump.
The first lady facilitated the ceasefire arrangement after she learned about the crisis during the United Nations General Assembly week, her senior adviser, Marc Beckman, told the Kyiv Independent on Oct. 28.
He added that her involvement in the Oleshky ceasefire was " wanted very much " by Putin, something Foreman said betrays obvious political motives.
"Allowing Melania to take the credit bolsters (Russia's) credentials to the MAGA base as peacemakers before the midterms," he said.
Foreman argued that the temporary truce could help Putin placate Trump as he continues to blame Ukraine for blocking the peace process.
"(It's the) same Kremlin approach for the diesel deal , agreeing to three-way talks, and releasing a hostage in return for pausing new sanctions," he said, adding that each time Russia has gained something substantial without "conceding anything significant."
Petro Andriushchenko, head of the Center for the Study of the Occupation, told the Kyiv Independent that Moscow wants to give Trump another opportunity to claim he has helped stop a war.
Russia is unlikely to violate the ceasefire this time, he said, not out of concern for civilians, but because the Kremlin would not want to jeopardize its relationship with Trump ahead of the U.S. midterm elections .
Despite this, the Beckman is adamant that Russia is acting in good faith.
"It's my understanding and my belief in being very close to all of these negotiations and knowing all of the parties for a long time, that everybody, the Russians included, is working in good faith," Beckman said.
"It's understood that this is a humanitarian crisis in Oleshky, and these elderly people need to be saved."
While the Kremlin agreed to the Oleshky ceasefire, it remains silent about the dire humanitarian situation across other occupied territories.
Daria Rabinovitsch, co-executive director at Helping to Leave, a charity that helps civilians leave the occupied territories , told the Kyiv Independent that calculating how many settlements are isolated is nearly impossible due to broken communications and missing internet access, but at least three other areas are known to be suffering from isolation.
These include the Kinburn Spit , settlements in the Polohy District of Zaporizhzhia Oblast where drivers refuse to go, and Enerhodar , where access has become hazardous due to intense air attacks along transport routes.
Such enclaves frequently appear when the front line shifts and Russia gains more territory, Rabinovitsch said. In some places, Russian military personnel relocate residents from active combat zones deeper into occupied lands, she added.
While the ceasefire might facilitate temporary relief efforts in Oleshky, it leaves systemic problems facing Ukrainians under Russian control unaddressed.
Across all occupied territories, civilians face failing water and electricity systems, shortages of qualified doctors, deteriorating municipal services, and mass depopulation, while specific problems differ from one occupied region to another.
"Oleshky is not the only community on the temporarily occupied territories that is experiencing a humanitarian catastrophe, and while we are happy and hopeful for the people there, we know that this evacuation will not resolve the systemic problems facing Ukrainians in the Russian occupation," Rabinovitsch said.
According to Ukraine's human rights ombudsman, Dmytro Lubinets, the initial 30 hours of the ceasefire proceeded without incident. While Kherson Oblast had a brief chance for respite, Russian forces continued striking other Ukrainian regions and killing civilians.
As Lubinets headed to Oleshky on the morning of Oct. 29, Russian troops attacked the railway station in Dnipro, Dnipropetrovsk Oblast, with a jet-powered drone, killing at least 13 people.
Yuliia Taradiuk is a Ukrainian reporter at the Kyiv Independent. She has been working with Lutsk-based misto.media, telling stories of Ukrainian fighters for the "All are gone to the front" project. She has experience as a freelance culture reporter, and a background in urbanism and activism, working for multiple Ukrainian NGOs. Yuliia holds B.A. degree in English language and literature from Lesya Ukrainka Volyn National University, she studied in Germany and Lithuania.

title: West fails to inflict strategic defeat on Russia — Putin
body:
MOSCOW, October 29. /TASS/. The West failed to achieve its goal of inflicting a strategic defeat on Moscow and it is unlikely to succeed by 2030, Russian President Vladimir Putin said at a press conference following the Russia-Africa Summit.
"Many are only talking about preparing for war by 2030. Is that the right thing to do? We are prepared but we do not want any kind of war with Europe," he stressed.
"As for them, if someone wants it, let them prepare. However, they failed to inflict a strategic defeat on Russia this time and it is unlikely to become possible by 2030," Putin added.

title: Falana seeks recovery of $123bn in oil funds
body: Human rights lawyer, Femi Falana, SAN, has called for the recovery of more than $123 billion and N66.4 billion allegedly owed to the Federation Account by the Nigerian National Petroleum Company Limited (NNPCL) and other oil and gas companies. Falana, in a letter dated October 28, 2026, addressed to the Senate President and copied to the Speaker of the House of Representatives, urged the authorities to initiate measures to recover the funds, which he said comprised outstanding oil royalties, proceeds of alleged crude oil theft, unpaid dividends, taxes and other revenues. The senior lawyer warned that failure to initiate recovery measures within 14 days of receiving the letter would prompt his firm to institute legal proceedings at the Federal High Court to compel the relevant authorities to act. The letter, signed by Falana, outlined five categories of alleged outstanding funds and cited court judgments, government reports and legislative investigations in support of the demand. On royalties, Falana said an estimated $62 billion had remained uncollected from international oil companies over 18 years following the non-implementation of provisions of the Deep Offshore and Inland Basin Production Sharing Contracts Act. He cited a Supreme Court consent judgment delivered on October 20, 2018, directing the Federal Government to collect outstanding royalties under the law and pay oil-producing states their 13 per cent derivation entitlements upon recovery. According to the letter, the Federal High Court subsequently entered judgments in favour of Akwa Ibom and Rivers states for a combined $3.3 billion, while Bayelsa State obtained a separate judgment for $951 million. Falana alleged that the Federal Government had yet to comply with the judgments. On alleged crude oil theft and undeclared exports, he cited findings attributed to a team of Nigerian lawyers engaged by the Nigerian Maritime Administration and Safety Agency, which reportedly identified about 60.2 million barrels of crude oil, valued at $12.7 billion, allegedly discharged at a port in Philadelphia, United States, between 2011 and 2014. He also referred to a House of Representatives ad hoc committee’s investigation into undeclared crude oil and liquefied natural gas exports during the same period. According to the letter, the committee found that oil and gas exports worth $17 billion had been shipped without proper records. Falana urged the authorities to pursue the recovery of the combined $29 billion from the companies allegedly involved, while acknowledging that civil cases filed by NIMASA were pending before the Federal High Court. The lawyer further alleged that NNPCL had failed to remit $23.1 billion in dividends attributable to the Federal Government’s 49 per cent stake in Nigeria LNG Limited to the Federation Account. He said NLNG had paid more than $47 billion in dividends to its shareholders over 26 years, with the Federal Government’s share channelled through NNPCL. Falana argued that the alleged failure to remit the funds contravened Section 162 of the 1999 Constitution, as amended. He added that resolutions of the Senate and House of Representatives calling for the remittance had not been implemented. The letter also cited the Nigerian Extractive Industries Transparency Initiative’s 2022/2023 oil and gas industry report, which reportedly put outstanding collectible revenues due to the Federal Government at $6.071 billion and N66.4 billion as of June 2024. Falana urged the National Assembly to support NEITI in recovering the outstanding amounts. On refinery rehabilitation, he called for the recovery of about $2.9 billion paid under contracts for the rehabilitation of the Port Harcourt, Warri and Kaduna refineries. He said the Federal Executive Council approved a $1.5 billion contract in April 2021 for the rehabilitation of the Port Harcourt refineries and another $1.48 billion in August 2021 for the Warri and Kaduna facilities. Citing NNPCL’s subsequent announcements about the refineries’ operational status, Falana alleged that the foreign contractors had breached the terms of their contracts and urged the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission to investigate and pursue recovery of the contract sums. He argued that recovering the money would enable the Federal Government to engage competent contractors to undertake the rehabilitation projects. Falana said the recovery of the alleged outstanding revenues would reduce the need for further foreign borrowing by the Federal Government and state governments. He also argued that his firm had sufficient grounds to pursue legal action, citing its involvement in preparing a bill to amend the Deep Offshore and Inland Basin Production Sharing Contracts Act. The bill, he said, was subsequently adopted, modified and passed by the National Assembly. The letter’s stated totals, however, contain an apparent discrepancy: while its heading and opening paragraphs cite $123.17 billion, the concluding paragraph refers to $118.67 billion, alongside N66.4 billion. The figures were presented as claims requiring recovery and were not independently verified for this report. The post Falana seeks recovery of $123bn in oil funds appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: Ukraine, NATO create conditions for new opportunities in joint technology development, testing – Alliance HQ
body:
Ukraine and NATO's Defence Innovation Accelerator for the North Atlantic (DIANA) have signed a Memorandum of Understanding that opens up new opportunities for the joint development and testing of technologies, as well as for deepening cooperation between Ukraine's and NATO's innovation ecosystems.
According to the Alliance's press service, the document was signed on Thursday, October 29, at NATO headquarters.
The press release explains that the partnership is based on the principle of reciprocity. "Ukraine has developed an extraordinary innovation ecosystem while confronting the realities of modern conflict, rapidly testing, adapting and improving technology under the most demanding conditions, as a result of Russia's war of aggression. DIANA offers an established pathway connecting innovators with NATO's defence and security expertise and infrastructure," the statement reads.
The Memorandum also lays the foundation for further cooperation, "helping Ukrainian innovators navigate NATO requirements, explore testing opportunities and tackle barriers to scaling promising technologies." "For NATO, closer cooperation could broaden the community of innovative suppliers and technologies contributing to the security of the Alliance, while strengthening the industrial base on which collective security depends," NATO said.
NATO said that at a time when "Allies need both to replenish critical capabilities and build a stronger, more innovative industrial base for the future, DIANA's model is designed to connect promising companies with real defence and security problems and create pathways for technologies to move towards operational capability."
Commenting on the signing, Acting Managing Director of DIANA Jyoti Hirani-Driver said: "This Memorandum of Understanding is a beginning. A door is opening. Now our job is to walk through it together. We have an enormous amount to learn from Ukraine."
The signed agreement is the first of its kind between DIANA and a NATO partner. "[The agreement] marks a practical step towards strengthening mutual security through innovation. It also builds on the broader NATO-Ukraine cooperation across their innovation ecosystems, which has developed significantly since Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine," the press release notes.

Now you can generate, preview, and edit PDFs, Google Docs, Google Sheets, slide decks, Markdown files, TXT files, and code directly within Google Gemini . The new file editing capabilities are available starting today for all Gemini users, and while PDF previews/editing works on both the web and mobile, all other file formats are only in the web version for now.
Google added support for generating and downloading files in Gemini earlier this year, but now you can tweak those files without leaving the Gemini app. Google says you can expand documents to edit them in full-screen mode and highlight text in files to ask Gemini questions or prompt it to make changes to the file, like highlighting a table and asking Gemini to turn it into a graph.
You could already use Gemini to edit files with its integrations in Google’s Workspace apps, like the Gemini bar in Google Docs . Anthropic also launched a feature earlier this year that allows users to generate and edit documents and presentations in Claude chats.

title: Number injured in Kremenchuk attack rises to 32, incl six children – administration
body:
The number of casualties resulting from the enemy attack on Kremenchuk in Poltava region has risen to 32 people, including six children, according to Head of Poltava Regional Military Administration Vitaliy Diakivnych.

As of 17:30 on Thursday, three people had died, and nine injured individuals had been admitted to hospital wards. Two of those hospitalized are in critical condition – a 16-year-old boy and a 72-year-old man – while seven others are in moderate condition.

"As a result of the enemy attack on the city of Kremenchuk, three people were killed and 32 were injured, including six children… All are receiving the necessary medical care," the head of the regional administration said on his Telegram channel.

Earlier, Diakivnych reported 28 casualties from the attack, including three children. The death toll at that time stood at three.

title: WAFU-B: Edo Queens petition CAF after losing disputed final to Ampem Darkoa
body:
Nigeria Women’s Football League champions Edo Queens have petitioned the Confederation of African Football ( CAF ), seeking to overturn their 3-2 extra-time defeat to Ghanaian champions Ampem Darkoa Ladies in the disputed final of the 2026 WAFU-B Women’s Champions League.
In a petition dated after Thursday’s encounter, Edo Queens asked CAF to declare the continuation of the final, played on 29 October, null and void, citing alleged irregularities in the venue change, match arrangements and eligibility of players.
The Nigerian club also urged the continental governing body to suspend confirmation of the regional qualification slot for the CAF Women’s Champions League pending the determination of its complaint.
The fresh protest follows a contentious sequence of decisions that overturned Edo Queens’ initial victory in the regional final and gave both teams another opportunity to contest the title.
Ampem Darkoa secured the WAFU-B title after defeating Edo Queens 3-2 following extra time in the rescheduled conclusion to the final.
The encounter followed the original meeting between the sides on 5 September in Ouagadougou, Burkina Faso, which ended 2-2 after 90 minutes.
Edo Queens subsequently won the penalty shoot-out 4-1 and initially appeared to have secured the regional championship and qualification for the continental competition.
However, Ampem Darkoa challenged the outcome, prompting CAF’s Organising Committee to rule on 26 September that the penalty shoot-out had no sporting effect.
The decision, subsequently upheld by the CAF Appeal Board on 16 October, directed that the match resume from the beginning of extra time with the score still at 2-2.
When play eventually continued on Thursday, Ampem Darkoa struck the decisive blow just two minutes into extra time to secure the 3-2 victory.
The Ghanaian champions thereby claimed the WAFU-B title and the zone’s qualification place for the 2026 CAF Women’s Champions League.
The triumph marks Ampem Darkoa’s return to the continental competition for the second time in their history, having previously featured in 2023 in Côte d’Ivoire.
In its petition, Edo Queens identified three principal grounds for challenging the continuation of the final.
First, the club questioned the relocation of the match from Ouagadougou to Cairo, Egypt, alleging that the move occurred without the required confirmation from the West African Football Union Zone B (WAFU-B), as stipulated in the CAF decision.
Second, the Nigerian side alleged that sporting conditions had not been properly restored before the continuation of the match.
The club claimed it was prevented from fielding eligible players who had participated in the original encounter. It also raised concerns about the accommodation provided for its delegation, alleging that members were housed at a military base rather than a conventional hotel.
Third, Edo Queens complained about what it described as inadequate official communication concerning the venue, kick-off time and other match arrangements, arguing that the alleged shortcomings could have affected its preparations.
These allegations are contained in the club’s petition and have not been independently established.
Beyond seeking the annulment of Thursday’s result, Edo Queens has asked CAF to direct WAFU-B to produce documents relating to the disputed fixture.
These include the required venue confirmation, match sheets, substitution records, player eligibility lists and disciplinary records.
The Nigerian club is also seeking an order for a full 90-minute replay under properly regulated conditions, with eligible players and at the original venue.
Alternatively, if a replay cannot be completed before the start of the 2026 CAF Women’s Champions League on 1 November, Edo Queens wants CAF to declare it the winner of the WAFU-B tournament.
The requested remedies remain proposals by the club, and no decision on the fresh petition was included in the information provided.
Meanwhile, Ampem Darkoa are preparing for the continental tournament in Egypt, where they have been drawn in Group B alongside Morocco’s AS FAR, Uganda’s Kawempe Muslim Ladies and Mali’s USFAS Bamako.
The CAF Women’s Champions League is scheduled to run from 1 to 15 November, leaving a narrow window for any further intervention that could affect the regional qualification outcome.

title: Russian forces strike student dormitory in Dnipro, two teenage girls injured
body:
Oleksandr Hanzha, head of the Dnipropetrovsk Regional Military Administration, announced this on Telegram , Ukrinform reports.
"Russian forces continue to attack Dnipro. They struck a dormitory at one of the vocational schools with a drone. Several rooms on the top floor caught fire," the statement said.
Later, Hanzha reported on Telegram that two girls had been injured in the Russian attack on the vocational school dormitory.
According to him, the girls are 15 and 16 years old.
They suffered acute stress reactions. Medical personnel provided them with all necessary assistance at the scene.
Dnipro Mayor Borys Filatov said on Telegram that more than 50 windows had been shattered in the building of Vocational School No. 17, which has now come under Russian attack for the second time.
"Young people staying there will be relocated to other dormitories today. Some have decided to go home. It's just an ordinary vocational school where students train to become machine-tool operators, cooks and welders," the mayor said.
Earlier reports said that tomorrow would be a day of mourning in Dnipro for those killed in the attack on the Dnipro railway station. The attack claimed 14 lives.

title: AFU strike Iskander launcher – Zelenskyy
body:
The Armed Forces of Ukraine (AFU) carried out two missile strikes, resulting in the destruction of two Russian Su-34 fighter-bombers, as well as an Iskander launcher, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has said.

"I just received a report. We carried out two missile strikes, destroying two Russian Su-34s, and also hitting an Iskander launcher. I thank you, guys, for the result," Zelenskyy said in an evening address on Thursday.

Earlier, the press service of the AFU Ukrainian Navy said that two RussianSu-34 fighter-bombers were destroyed as a result of a missile strike by Neptune coastal missile system on the aircraft's location at Marinovka airfield in Russia's Volgograd region.

title: Anyaoku condemns xenophobic attacks in South Africa
body: By Emma Ujah, Abuja Bureau Chief Former Commonwealth Secretary-General, Chief Emeka Anyaoku, has condemned the reported xenophobic attacks against African nationals in South Africa, describing them as distressing and regrettable. Anyaoku expressed sadness that South Africans, who endured years of apartheid and received support from across Africa in their struggle for liberation, were now turning against fellow Africans from other countries. The 94-year-old statesman spoke in an interview on the sidelines of the MasterClass on Penetrative Leadership in an Increasingly Chaotic World Order in Abuja. He recalled his role in efforts to end apartheid and facilitate negotiations between the former white-minority government and the country’s black majority, saying the current attacks were particularly painful given the sacrifices made by other African countries. “The attacks are regrettable,” Anyaoku said, recalling how he worked to secure support from Commonwealth leaders for efforts to facilitate negotiations in South Africa following the release of Nelson Mandela in 1990. He recounted that Mandela visited Abuja in May 1990 for a meeting of Commonwealth foreign ministers responsible for South Africa and attended his first official dinner as secretary-general. Anyaoku said the visit marked the beginning of a friendship with Mandela and his then-wife, Winnie Mandela. He explained that in 1991, he secured a mandate from Commonwealth Heads of Government to visit South Africa and explore ways to help the country’s then-president, F.W. de Klerk, organise talks aimed at ending apartheid. According to him, his meeting with de Klerk on November 1, 1991, focused on rebuilding confidence among South Africa’s major ethnic groups. Anyaoku said de Klerk initially questioned how the Commonwealth could assist South Africa, given its support for sanctions against the apartheid government. He said he explained that the Commonwealth could help build confidence among the country’s black, white and Asian communities, using the diversity of his delegation as an example. Anyaoku added that he intervened when the negotiations threatened to collapse, helping to keep the process on course. He recalled that the agreement concluding the negotiations was signed at 3:30 a.m. on November 17, 1993, in his presence. Shettima warns against misinformation At the event, Vice-President Kashim Shettima urged Nigerian elites to exercise restraint in the narratives they promote about the country, particularly in the age of social media and artificial intelligence. Represented by his Special Adviser on Economic Matters, Dr Tope Fasua, Shettima said the rapid spread of digital information made it necessary for citizens to verify claims before sharing them. “Digital success is an asset. It gives Nigerian businesses access to customers, young people access to opportunities and citizens access to information. But it also places a greater responsibility on all of us to distinguish reliable information from manipulation,” he said. Adesina stresses national reputation Also speaking, Group Managing Director of Sahara Power Group, Mr Kola Adesina, said reputation was built on three pillars: performance, character and goodwill. He urged Nigerians to pay greater attention to how their actions and public communications shape the country’s image. Adesina said younger generations could learn valuable lessons from experienced leaders such as Anyaoku, particularly by studying their responses to crises and avoiding past mistakes. He also cautioned against the tendency to share information instantly without verifying its accuracy. “Your reputation is a matter of choice; it’s a decision,” he said. The post Anyaoku condemns xenophobic attacks in South Africa appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: Wallenius Wilhelmsen Orders Up to 12 LNG-Powered Car Carriers in $1.5 Billion Fleet Expansion
body:
Essential news coupled with the finest maritime content sourced from across the globe.
Rendering of a Wallenius Wilhelmsen Shaper Class car carrier. The company is expanding its fleet renewal program with an order for four additional LNG dual-fuel vessels and options for eight more. (Image: Wallenius Wilhelmsen)
Wallenius Wilhelmsen is expanding its fleet renewal program with an order for four new dual-fuel car carriers and options for eight more, potentially adding 12 vessels in a deal valued at approximately $1.5 billion.
The Norwegian shipping and logistics group announced Wednesday that it has reached an agreement with China’s Jinling Shipyard (Jiangsu) for the construction of four 9,900-car-equivalent-unit (CEU) pure car and truck carriers (PCTCs), with deliveries beginning in mid-2030.
The agreement includes options for four additional vessels in 2031 and another four in 2032. If all options are exercised, total capital expenditure is expected to reach approximately $1.5 billion.
The ships will be equipped with dual-fuel LNG engines and built to Wallenius Wilhelmsen’s Shaper Class design , which features hoistable decks, heavy-duty ramps and flexible cargo spaces capable of accommodating passenger vehicles, trucks and other rolling equipment.
The latest order expands the company’s fleet renewal program to 26 vessels, including options, extending a newbuilding campaign launched in 2023 that Wallenius Wilhelmsen describes as the largest in its history.
“We continue to see attractive opportunities in the segments we serve and want to ensure we have the capacity, flexibility and efficiency needed to support our customers well into the next decades,” said Xavier Leroi, chief operating officer of shipping services at Wallenius Wilhelmsen.
“Expanding our newbuilding program with deliveries from 2030 reflects our confidence in the long-term fundamentals of the market,” he added.
The newbuilding agreement follows a private placement completed earlier this month as the company continues investing in its long-term fleet requirements.
Wallenius Wilhelmsen has already begun taking delivery of vessels under its existing Shaper Class program, with the new ships intended to modernize its fleet while providing additional capacity across its global shipping network.
The company said the vessels’ flexible cargo configurations will allow it to respond to changing customer demand across the automotive and high-and-heavy equipment markets.
The investment also reinforces the company’s shift toward alternative-fuel-capable vessels. LNG dual-fuel propulsion offers a pathway to reducing certain emissions compared with conventional marine fuels, although its overall climate benefits depend in part on methane emissions and fuel sourcing.
Headquartered in Oslo, Wallenius Wilhelmsen operates approximately 130 vessels across 15 trade routes serving six continents. Its broader logistics network includes vehicle processing centers, inland distribution operations and marine terminals.
The company said the expanded newbuilding program will help maintain capacity and operational flexibility as it prepares for shipping demand into the next decade.

title: Zelenskyy calls on USA not to remain silent about killings of Ukrainians
body:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy called on the United States not to remain silent about Russia's killings of Ukrainians and emphasized the need to extend the humanitarian principles observed by the Defense Forces during the operation in Oleshky to the entire territory of Ukraine.

"It is important that America, too, not remain silent about the killings. This is very important. They are ongoing," Zelenskyy said in a video address on Thursday evening.

According to him, Ukraine is working to ensure the success of the humanitarian operation in Oleshky, and Ukrainian forces are maintaining a ceasefire. At the same time, the president emphasized that humanitarian considerations must extend beyond a single section of the front line.

"We must act in such a way, and turn the situation around, so that Russia agrees to de-escalation – and so that this applies to our entire country, not just Oleshky," Zelenskyy said.

title: Maya Gebala released from hospital 262 days after Tumbler Ridge shooting
body:
Tumbler Ridge shooting victim Maya Gebala has been released from hospital.
In an update provided by her dad, David, he posted on X on Thursday morning that it has been 262 days since that fatal day in Tumbler Ridge.
“It’s been 262 days since you were airlifted to BC Children’s Hospital,” David wrote, adding “262 days since we were told, ‘We did everything we could, but we don’t think she’s going to make it through the night.'”
David said that since then he has watched his daughter fight for every single one of those days.
He said it was 251 days ago that Maya opened her eye, moved it and shifted her leg, only to be rushed into emergency surgery again for hydrocephalus.
It was 238 days ago when Maya was extubated and breathed on her own for the first time, David said, and 230 days when Maya was able to feel the sun on her face.
It’s been 262 days since you were airlifted to BC Children’s Hospital. 262 days since we were told, “We did everything we could, but we don’t think she’s going to make it through the night.”
Since then, I’ve watched you fight for every single one of those days.
— David Gebala (@DavidGebala) October 29, 2026
David chronicled the progress his daughter has made since she was shot inside Tumbler Ridge Secondary School on Feb. 10.
The small mining community of Tumbler Ridge was left reeling after the devastating mass shooting that killed eight people , as well as the shooter, and left dozens of others injured.
Maya and another victim, Paige Hoekstra, were airlifted to B.C. Children’s Hospital following the shooting.
David said it was 213 days ago that he wrapped his hands around Maya for the first time since the morning he left for work on Feb. 10.
He said 145 days ago, Maya intentionally smiled while they played thumb war and 140 days ago he wheeled Maya off hospital grounds for the very first time.
Forty days ago they celebrated Maya’s 13th birthday at the Foo Fighters concert.
It warms my heart to watch these two interact whenever they see each other. ❤️ #mayastrong pic.twitter.com/1L35aEgv6h
— David Gebala (@DavidGebala) August 3, 2026
“There was never a day I stopped believing we would get here,” David wrote.
“The road ahead is still long, but this is a milestone no one thought we would reach. Maya, you are the bravest person I know. You are an inspiration to so many people. Giving up was never an option for me, and it clearly never was for you either.”
David thanked the incredible nurses, doctors and therapists who helped their family reach this milestone.
“Now it’s time to leave these hospital walls behind and keep moving forward, Maya Bear,” David wrote.

title: NDC’s Tanko Computer dismisses NPP denial of alleged plot to remove Afenyo-Markin
body: The National Democratic Congress (NDC) has dismissed the New Patriotic Party’s (NPP) denial of reports that it is planning to change its Minority leadership in Parliament, describing the response as “fire fighting”. Speaking on JoyNews’ Top Story , NDC member Rashid Tanko Computer said the alleged plan to remove Minority Leader Alexander Afenyo-Markin had been discussed since the 2024 general elections. He insisted that the governing party was not seeking to influence the NPP’s leadership decisions but maintained that the opposition party was responding to mounting pressure following the reports. “Are they not fire fighting? That’s what they are doing. We are not determining for them. We are not telling them they should change their leaders or not. From the outset, they wanted to remove him,” he said. Mr Tanko Computer added that the NPP had been forced to address the issue publicly because details of the alleged plan had emerged. Asked how he knew about the alleged plot, Mr Tanko Computer said it was widely known within political circles. He linked the reported discontent to the NPP’s presidential primary, which elected former Vice President Dr Mahamudu Bawumia as the party’s flagbearer. He claimed that tensions over Mr Afenyo-Markin’s position had emerged after the Minority Leader lost heavily in his constituency during the 2024 elections. “After the conference that elected Alhaji Mahamudu Bawumia, his excellency, the former vice president, didn’t you see what they were doing? He lost in the Afenyo-Markin constituency. He lost heavily. From that day, they wanted him out,” he said. Mr Tanko Computer further claimed that social media posts from individuals associated with Dr Bawumia’s camp had called for Mr Afenyo-Markin’s removal. He said the NDC was monitoring developments but was not concerned about the reported internal disagreement within the opposition party. He also criticised the NPP Minority Caucus for what he described as an overreliance on press conferences to communicate its positions on national issues. The comments follow reports that some NPP members are dissatisfied with Mr Afenyo-Markin’s performance and are considering changes to the party’s Minority leadership. The NPP has denied the reports, maintaining that it is satisfied with Mr Afenyo-Markin’s work and that no meeting has been scheduled to remove or replace the Minority leadership.

title: 2027: Obi pledges 10,000 MW of power, declares emergency on corruption
body: By Chinedu Adonu Presidential candidate of the National Democratic Congress, NDC, Mr Peter Obi, has pledged to generate, transmit and distribute at least 10,000 megawatts of electricity if elected president in 2027, promising to tackle insecurity, corruption, unemployment and other challenges confronting the country. Obi, who made the pledge during a Town hall meeting in Enugu, also promised to declare emergencies in education and the fight against corruption, while ensuring access to primary healthcare in every ward across the country. He said Nigeria needed a leader with the competence, capacity, compassion, commitment and character to address its economic and security challenges and restore public confidence in governance. According to him, the country is currently battling widespread hunger, unemployment and insecurity, making the 2027 presidential election critical to its future. “Today, our country is suffering. Today, people are hungry. Today, our children do not have employment. Today, Nigeria is not secure,” Obi said. He urged Nigerians to elect a president capable of uniting the country, securing lives and property, and creating an environment for economic growth and development. The former Anambra State governor said his administration would take decisive action against insecurity, insisting that the government must confront criminal elements wherever they operate. “As president of Nigeria, I will unite Nigeria. As president of Nigeria, I will secure Nigeria. We will deal with security,” he declared. On corruption, Obi said public funds must be deployed for the benefit of citizens, promising greater transparency and accountability in government expenditure and borrowing. “People must stop stealing public money. Public money must be used for public good. That is why I am making my commitment. We will be accountable, we will be open,” he said. He added that Nigerians would be informed about the purpose of government borrowing and how borrowed funds were spent. On education and healthcare, the NDC presidential candidate promised to ensure that children had access to schooling and that every ward in the country had primary healthcare services. Obi also identified electricity as a major priority of his proposed administration, arguing that reliable power supply was necessary to revive industries, create jobs and stimulate economic activities. “As I promised, we will generate, transmit and distribute at least 10,000 megawatts of electricity, because we want industrial work,” he said, urging Nigerians not to lose hope in the country’s future. Obi challenges Tinubu to account for borrowing The presidential candidate also challenged President Bola Tinubu to campaign across the country and explain his administration’s performance over the past three years, including the utilisation of borrowed funds. Obi argued that Nigerians deserved to hear directly from those seeking their votes and assess their records and policy proposals before making their electoral choices. He questioned the president’s reported extensive foreign travels, demanding explanations on government expenditure and the purpose of the loans obtained under the administration. “We are asking him: ‘Please spend at least 36 days and go round Nigeria and tell them what you have been doing for the past three years,’” Obi said. He further challenged the president to explain how the money borrowed by the Federal Government had been utilised. “We must go round Nigeria and tell them what he used nearly $100 billion he borrowed for,” he said. Obi maintained that presidential candidates should engage citizens across the country rather than remain in Abuja and expect Nigerians to support them without sufficient public engagement. He also called on other presidential aspirants to travel across the country, understand the challenges confronting ordinary Nigerians and present their plans for addressing them. Utomi backs Obi-Kwankwaso combination Meanwhile, renowned political economist, Prof. Pat Utomi, called for political change, arguing that corruption, criminality and disunity had undermined Nigeria’s development aspirations. Utomi expressed confidence in the proposed combination of Obi and former Kano State governor, Senator Rabiu Kwankwaso, saying their partnership could offer Nigerians an alternative political direction. “We come before you to say to you that we have done our research and I know, that I know, that I know, that a combination of Peter Obi and Rabiu Kwankwaso will deliver Nigeria,” he said. He, however, urged Nigerians to take an active role in the electoral process by turning out to vote and protecting their votes. “All that is left is for all of us to ensure that the people come out massively, vote, defend their votes and a new Nigeria will begin,” Utomi said. The professor, who recalled celebrating his 60th birthday at the same venue on February 6, appealed to Nigerians to make the next year’s anniversary memorable by supporting the emergence of a new political direction. “Give me a birthday present on the 6th of February next year and let a new Nigeria begin,” he said. The post 2027: Obi pledges 10,000 MW of power, declares emergency on corruption appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: Russia wants to avoid Hormuz scenario in Baltic Sea — Putin
body:
MOSCOW, October 29. /TASS/. Moscow does not want a situation similar to that in the Strait of Hormuz and the Persian Gulf to develop in the Baltic Sea, Russian President Vladimir Putin said at a press conference following the Russia-Africa summit.
He said Baltic security had come up during telephone talks with Finnish President Alexander Stubb and Norwegian Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Store. The discussions touched on Finland’s and many other European countries’ efforts to uphold international maritime law and their hope that all international actors would do the same.
"We support that approach. What is the alternative? A situation similar to the one in the Strait of Hormuz. Does anyone want the Baltic Sea to face the same situation as the Persian Gulf or the Strait of Hormuz? I do not know. We do not want that," Putin said.

title: Russia does all it can to keep humanity from repeating previous global tragedies — Putin
body:
MOSCOW, October 29. /TASS/. Russia remembers all the tragic pages of history well, including the lessons of both world wars, and is doing everything in its power to ensure that nothing like this happens to the humanity again, President Vladimir Putin said at a press conference after the Russia-Africa summit.
"History is something that has already happened, and nothing can be improved here," the president noted. "But knowing history, knowing the tragic pages of history, we can make attempts to ensure that nothing like what happened to the humanity in previous decades or centuries, nothing that the humanity experienced during some major conflicts, armed conflicts, so that none of this happens again.
"We in Russia remember all this well, including the lessons of the WWI and WWII. And we are doing everything to ensure that nothing like this happens on a global scale."

title: CIBN to honour Alakija, Lagos Deputy Chief of Staff, other leaders at Fellowship Investiture
body:
The Chartered Institute of Bankers of Nigeria ( CIBN ) said it would honour distinguished leaders from the banking and finance industry, government and public sector, private sector, academia and other critical sectors of the economy at its 2026 Fellowship Investiture.
The 2026 Fellowship Investiture is scheduled to take place on 31 October at Harbour Point, 4 Wilmot Point Road, off Ahmadu Bello Way, Victoria Island, Lagos.
The investiture ceremony is organised to confer the Institute’s highest honour, Fellowship, on deserving prominent individuals who have excelled in their fields of endeavour.
CIBN added that the award honours industry leaders who have contributed immensely to the growth and sustainability of the banking profession in Nigeria and globally.
At the Fellowship Investiture, the keynote address will focus on the theme, “Bank Recapitalisation: Leveraging New Bank Capital for Nigeria’s Industrial Transformation,” and will be delivered by D’Tayo Aduloju, Chief Executive Officer of the Nigerian Economic Summit Group (NESG).
The Executive Governor of Lagos State, Babajide Sanwo-Olu, and the Honourable Minister of State for Budget and Economic Planning, Doris Uzoka-Anite, are expected to be the Special Guests of Honour at the event.
Among the distinguished honorary fellows to be recognised are Sam Egube, Deputy Chief of Staff, Lagos State; Thompson Oludare Sunday, Managing Director/Chief Executive Officer of the Nigeria Deposit Insurance Corporation; Ibrahim Stevens, Governor of the Bank of Sierra Leone; Afolabi Olorode, Managing Director/Chief Executive Officer of Quest Merchant Bank; and Emmanuel Ikazoboh, Chairman of Dangote Cement Plc and former Group Chairman of Ecobank Transnational Incorporated.
The honourees also include Folorunsho Alakija, Vice Chairman of Famfa Oil Limited; Tokunbo Talabi, Secretary to the Ogun State Government; and Olubunmi Kuku, Managing Director/Chief Executive of the Federal Airports Authority of Nigeria.
CIBN will also honour Siraju Salisu, Managing Director/Chief Executive Officer of Summit Bank Ltd; Lady Ada Chukwudozie, Chairman of Keystone Bank Limited; Mohammed Mustapha Bintube, Chairman of Jaiz Bank Plc; Akin Ogunranti, Executive Director of Zenith Bank Plc; Segun Ogunsanya, Chairman of the Nigeria Sovereign Investment Authority; and Tosin Runsewe, Founder/Chief Executive Officer of AfyA Care.
Iyinoluwa Aboyeji, Founding Partner of Future Africa, and Faith Tuedor-Matthews, Chief Executive Officer of TEKLA Factoring & Finance Limited and former Managing Director/Chief Executive Officer of Mainstreet Bank Limited, top the list of eminent bankers who will be formally conferred with the Fellowship of the Institute.
Other members who will be elected Fellows of the Institute include Nixon Iwedi, Managing Director/Chief Executive Officer of Signature Bank Ltd; Osiyemi Oluwaseun, Honourable Commissioner for Transportation, Lagos State; Oyeneyin Hakeem, Founder of FelDams Ltd and Chairman of Visiblevalue Chain Ltd; and Olatunbosun Ajala, Deputy Director at the Central Bank of Nigeria.
Ben-Obi Onyewuchi, Deputy Director at the Central Bank of Nigeria, will also be elected a Fellow of the Institute.
Those to be invested as Honorary Senior Members of the Institute include Oluwayemisi Olorunshola, Board Chairman of Wema Bank Plc; Samson Oyetunde, Executive Director of the African Development Bank; Ishaku Polycarp, Director at the Central Bank of Nigeria; and Usman Garba of the Nigerian Navy/Nigerian Navy Microfinance Bank.
Of the 755 awardees to be honoured at the event, 18 will be named Honorary Fellows, 460 Associates will become Elected Fellows, and 277 senior management staff of banks and members of academia will become Honorary Senior Members of the Institute.
The Institute’s Team Lead for Corporate Communication and Brand Management, Taofik Sanni, said the honours recognised the awardees’ meritorious service and commitment to upholding ethics and professionalism.
He added that the honourees were being recognised for their valuable contributions to the banking industry and the economy, both in Nigeria and globally.
The hybrid event, which will be chaired by Bello Maccido, the Wakil-Sokoto and Chief Executive Officer of Crosse Pointe Capital & Advisory Ltd, is expected to attract stakeholders from within and outside the industry, including top government functionaries, members of the diplomatic community, captains of industry, decision-makers, top management staff of banks, members of the academic community, professional bodies and members of the Institute.
The President/Chairman of Council of the Chartered Institute of Bankers of Nigeria, Dele Alabi, will be the Chief Host of the occasion, supported by Mojisola Asieru-Sweet, First Vice President/Chairman of the Board of Fellows and Practice Licence, and Akin Morakinyo, Registrar/Chief Executive.

title: Israel’s exit polls may have ‘fundamental problem’ after Netanyahu bloc surprise, pollster says
body: Israeli pollsters significantly underestimated Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's political bloc in the latest election, Dr. Menachem Lazar, CEO of Lazar Research and Maariv's pollster, acknowledged in an interview with Nissim Mishal and Anat Davidov on 103FM, as he attempted to explain the discrepancies between the polls and the election results.According to Lazar, there is no room for doubt."The pollsters were wrong, all of them. Some more than others, but there was a mistake. A serious mistake. I could argue that the last poll I conducted was on the Thursday before the election and that things happened between then and the election, but that is not really the reason. We were wrong. We saw a picture that ultimately turned out to be different. We gave the opposition a majority, and we saw that the Netanyahu coalition had a majority."Lazar elaborated on the extent of the polling failure."We will have to conduct a full assessment of what happened once we see the final results. We need to wait another day. We underestimated the Netanyahu bloc, underestimated Benjamin Netanyahu's strength. We saw more or less the same thing in the 2015 election, how on the final day of the election he managed to increase Likud's strength."He then explained how election polling is conducted and what the discrepancies might indicate about Israeli voters."There are two things that need to be done correctly with an exit poll: correctly distribute the polling stations, thoroughly examine how the exit poll polling stations were selected, look at the difference between the nationwide distribution and the distribution of those polling stations, and conduct another examination of the gap between the exit poll ballot box and the actual ballot box next to it."The exit poll ballot box is supposed to represent the actual ballot box beside it. This is not the first time. There may be a fundamental problem here, either with the polling stations and how the exit polls are positioned and constructed, or with how the Israeli public behaves ahead of elections."'Neither side won'Addressing accusations that the polls were intended to manipulate public opinion, Lazar said:"Clearly, everything will head in that direction. There are more serious things we will need to examine. We examine ourselves after every election campaign. There is no election in which we produce results that match the parties' results exactly. Generally, we produce much better results when it comes to the blocs. There was the 2015 election, when there was also a similar discrepancy. We corrected ourselves in the election campaigns that followed. We will examine, correct, and hope that in the next rounds it will work better."Lazar also addressed the issue of double-envelope ballots and the changes they could bring to the final distribution of Knesset seats."In my assessment, apart from the fact that the Arab parties have a smaller share of the overall vote, this should reflect what we are seeing in the Jewish sector. It could push the Reservists' Party and the Economic Party above the electoral threshold. They are short by around 40,000 votes, and they may reach that number."There is a certain chance that it could instead go to the Jewish Home party and Naftali Bennett, who were short by 1,400 votes, or Meretz, which was short by several thousand votes. Once again, a party could be on the threshold. We need to wait."Lazar explained that the remaining ballots could also affect the balance between the political blocs, although he believes the overall election picture is relatively clear."The Arab parties could lose one or two seats, and there could be movement between the blocs. There are also the surplus-vote agreements. I think the overall picture looks fairly clear. Neither side won, and the entire argument is about who lost less. Now the question is how to form a government with this situation, or whether to go to new elections, where there are also assessments of what might happen."

title: FAA proposes safety rules for Embraer’s automatic takeoff system
body: The FAA has proposed new safety requirements for an Embraer system that would automatically raise a jet’s nose for takeoff and control its initial climb. The proposal covers the Embraer Enhanced Takeoff System, or E2TS, on the E195-E2. E2TS engages when pilots advance the thrust levers to the takeoff setting. The crew steers the aircraft along the runway centerline, while the system keeps the wings level and handles the rotation and initial climb. Pilots monitor the automatic rotation using the calculated takeoff speed. Embraer unveiled the technology at the Farnborough International Airshow in July 2024. The Brazilian manufacturer says more precise control during takeoff can reduce the runway distance required and allow aircraft to carry more weight or fly farther from airports where takeoff performance limits operations. At the announcement, Embraer identified London City, Florence and Rio de Janeiro’s Santos Dumont as airports that could benefit. It said the system could add 350 nautical miles of range from London City. The company also said automating the maneuver would reduce pilot workload. The takeoff system was announced alongside other E2 improvements, including lower fuel consumption, increased range and cabin changes. The FAA said existing takeoff rules assume a human pilot raises the aircraft’s nose. Its proposed requirements would account for the automatic system’s sensor inaccuracies and operating tolerances. Embraer will have to demonstrate safe performance across different aircraft weights, loading conditions, temperatures and airport elevations, including takeoffs with an engine inoperative. The FAA is accepting public comments on the porposal through November 27, 2026. The post FAA proposes safety rules for Embraer’s automatic takeoff system appeared first on AeroTime .

title: I bleached my skin to get movie roles — Nollywood actress Habibat Jinadu
body: By Enitan Abdultawab Nollywood actress Habibat Jinadu has revealed that she bleached her skin to secure acting roles, saying dark-skinned and slim actresses struggle to get opportunities in the film industry. Jinadu made this known in an interview with BBC Yoruba, where she recounted how pressure to meet the industry’s preferred physical appearance influenced her decision to bleach her skin. “I bleached my skin because if you were dark-skinned, then you would not get a role. Also, if you were not chubby but slim, you would not get a role,” the actress said. Explaining how she responded to the situation, Jinadu said she decided to bleach her skin and wait for the acting opportunities she believed would follow. “So, I went ahead, bleached my skin and started expecting to get roles. And indeed, I started getting roles,” she said. However, the actress disclosed that the change in her complexion made it difficult for people to recognise her outside the screen, despite her growing acting opportunities. “But people could not recognise me any longer. If I stepped out to buy something, people would go like, ‘You look familiar,’ ‘You look like an actress,’ and all sorts,” she recounted. Jinadu said she was unhappy with the experience but continued bleaching her skin as she tried to establish herself in the industry. “I was not happy with it, but I kept on pushing,” she said. The actress also revealed that she began experiencing injuries and skin tears from minor bruises while working on movie sets. “Then, I started sustaining injuries and tears from minor bruises on sets and all,” she said. According to Jinadu, the reality of her situation became clearer in 2023 when she became pregnant and had to stop bleaching her skin. “It all dawned on me when I got pregnant in 2023. And when you are pregnant, you cannot bleach your skin,” she said. She explained that stopping the practice brought another challenge, as people began criticising her appearance after her complexion changed. “When I eventually stopped, people started abusing me and calling me all sorts of names,” she said. title: The cost of the gospel: A story that should humble every generation (2), By Ayo Akerele
body:
Charles Colson, in his important book, “ The God of Stones and Spiders ,” recounts the story of Armando Valladares, a Cuban poet who was arrested by the regime of Fidel Castro in 1960. Castro imprisoned Armando for twenty-two years. In Colson’s words: “During one three-month period, Armando Valladares and some condemned Christian prisoners were given showers of human urine and excrement by sadistic prison guards. In the middle of the night, Armando would hear from his prison cell the measured footsteps of condemned Christian men being marched outside.
The persecution of faithful Christians has more than doubled around the world and it will still multiply in the years ahead. The future of the Church in Africa, and indeed globally, now rests, to a significant degree, in the hands of the young Christians of today. But the question that must keep every spiritual leader awake at night is this: Will the youths of today, who are drinking from the wells dug by the fathers, take up their swords and sharpen them for the battle ahead?
“So it came about, on the day of battle, that there was neither sword nor spear found in the hand of any of the people who were with Saul and Jonathan. But they were found with Saul and Jonathan his son.” (1 Samuel 13:22).
What a tragedy beyond measure. On the day it mattered most, the day of actual battle, no sword was available in the hands of the people of God. The fathers carried swords, but the children carried none. The Sword, of course, is the Word of God. A sharpened sword is the sharp, undiluted, uncompromising truth of God’s Word. But how will our children and the children of our children confront the moral rot, spiritual recklessness, and doctrinal confusion of their generation without a Sword?
“But all the Israelites went down to the Philistines, to sharpen every man his share, and his coulter, and his axe, and his mattock.” (1 Samuel 13:20).
This passage serves as a sobering allegory for the next generation of the Church. The Philistines should have been coming to the Israelites for everything, the Church was meant to be the light, the standard-bearer, the shaping force over culture. Instead, it was God’s own people who descended to their enemies for sharpening. It was the reverse of what God intended. Rather than scripture shaping culture, culture is increasingly shaping scripture in the minds of many who sit in our pews. The present generation of young and teenage believers face the very real danger of not following the Lord wholeheartedly in their own generation.
Many of them have not been prepared to carry swords. Many have never been shown what a sword truly is. The Sword is the genuine, unadulterated Word of the Lord, the very nucleus of the gospel. If the present generation of Christian leaders does not urgently assemble a solemn gathering to train and thoroughly equip the youths of today with the undiluted truth of God’s Word, these youths will inevitably descend to the Philistines to sharpen their own, and in truth, many of them are already mingling with the Philistines in the land.
Many are boldly and unselfconsciously singing the Lord’s song in a strange land, entirely unaware of the spiritual danger they are in. Our children must be rescued. If they are not, they will be subdued by the world and the spiritual forces of darkness that are intensifying in this end time. They will carry no fire and distribute no fire. They will be vulnerable, weak, and without passion. It is time for the Church to rise, to contend earnestly for the faith, to rescue its own soul, and to fight without retreat for the souls of the next generation.
What does the next generation truly know about intercession? What do they know about sanctification? What do they know about discipleship? What do they know about genuine repentance, not the performance of it, but the reality of it? What do they know about authentic love and compassion for the poor? What do they know about faithfulness and self-control? What do they know about the gifts of the Holy Spirit and the fruits of the Holy Spirit, and the critical difference between them?
At that time, Armando Valladares was not himself a committed believer. But having witnessed the unshakeable faith and fearless trust in Christ demonstrated by those condemned Christian men, even as they walked calmly toward death, he emerged from Castro’s prison after twenty-two long years as a transformed man, carrying a renewed and burning commitment to follow Christ passionately for the remainder of his life.
What do they know about eternity and eternal rewards? What do they know about purpose and God-given vision? What do they know about the charge of evangelism? The walls of the gospel of Christ are being systematically broken down, and the next generation of believers stand on the very edge of apostasy, unless they are called back to God with surgical urgency and unwavering love.
“And there arose another generation after them, which knew not the Lord.” (Judges 2:10).
The present generation of mature believers and spiritual leaders must therefore begin with great intentionality to build bridges and demolish every wall that stands between God and the next generation. We must return to the uncompromising truth of God’s Word, a truth stripped clean of greed, egocentrism, post-modernism, and the subtle infiltrations of new age philosophies. We must come together with unified purpose to fulfil the prophetic vision given to David: “One generation shall praise Thy works to another, and shall declare Thy mighty acts.” (Psalms 145:4).
For by doing this we will be able to place sharp swords into the hands of the next generation, and when we have gone to our reward, they will be strong and bold enough to confront the Philistines of their own lands. They will grow tall and deep-rooted in God, and they will succeed in passing those same swords to their children, and this gospel of the Kingdom shall be preached to all nations, and then shall the end come.
Sometimes, we need to sit with the weight of what Christians in other nations and in other generations have endured in their faithfulness to Christ, not merely to admire them from a distance, but to allow their stories to deepen and demand more of our own commitment.
Charles Colson, in his important book, The God of Stones and Spiders , recounts the story of Armando Valladares, a Cuban poet who was arrested by the regime of Fidel Castro in 1960. Castro imprisoned Armando for twenty-two years. In Colson’s words: “During one three-month period, Armando Valladares and some condemned Christian prisoners were given showers of human urine and excrement by sadistic prison guards. In the middle of the night, Armando would hear from his prison cell the measured footsteps of condemned Christian men being marched outside. Then he would hear their voices rise in a final defiant shout of ‘Viva Cristo Rey’, Long live Christ the King, just before the exploding rifles of the firing squad shattered those voices into eternity.”
At that time, Armando Valladares was not himself a committed believer. But having witnessed the unshakeable faith and fearless trust in Christ demonstrated by those condemned Christian men, even as they walked calmly toward death, he emerged from Castro’s prison after twenty-two long years as a transformed man, carrying a renewed and burning commitment to follow Christ passionately for the remainder of his life.
Friends, the prices that generations of Christians have paid in defense of their faith are prices that most of us have not begun to contemplate. Christianity has never been, and was never designed to be, a cost-free, comfort-centred experience. Jesus Himself declared without ambiguity: “If anyone will come after Me, let him deny himself and take up his cross daily and follow Me.” (Matthew 16:24) You cannot be a genuine follower of Christ and simultaneously live with reckless self-indulgence and spiritual carelessness.
Let us return, with urgency and with tears if necessary, to the essence of Christianity and ministry. Let us focus on what matters most: becoming genuine disciples of Jesus Christ, and in so doing, faithfully producing the next generation of disciples who will carry the fire further than we ever could. The scars on Pastor Joseph’s back demand nothing less.
This is precisely why it is absolutely essential that we collectively de-emphasise church membership as the primary measure of Christian life, and begin wholeheartedly promoting, modelling, and living out the demanding but life-giving virtues of discipleship. This means deliberately building spiritual stamina and deep scriptural capacity for the increasingly difficult days that lie ahead. It means prioritising intimacy with God, a depth of relationship with the Holy Spirit, and genuine spirituality over carnality, both in the way we teach and in the way we live, so that our children and our spiritual sons and daughters have a solid platform upon which to stand when the storms of their generation break against them.
Above all, let those who have been stealing, whether of God’s resources, of people’s trust, or of their own integrity, steal no more. Let hypocrisy in leadership come to an end. The younger generation stands at a crossroads of defining decisions. Dr Billy Graham has gone to his eternal reward. Kenneth E Hagin has gone ahead. The next generation is marching toward war without swords. Some are already descending to the Philistines to sharpen what they have.
They will self-destruct if we do not act. If we do not live our truth but only speak it, if we do not model what we preach, they will not catch the flame, much less ignite a fire of deep, consuming love and passion for Jesus Christ in their own generation. Churches must repent and return to God in genuine, not performative, repentance.
Pastors and leaders must wake up and take seriously the sacred responsibility of helping our children know, love, and faithfully serve the true and living God.
We live in a generation that has become dangerously obsessed with signs and wonders and supernatural spectacle, yet Jesus Himself issued a sobering warning: “A wicked and adulterous generation seeks after a sign.” (Matthew 16:4) The genuine move of the Holy Spirit never contradicts the fruit of the Spirit, love, joy, peace, patience, humility, self-control.
God does not compromise His own nature to satisfy our appetite for excitement and performance. It is infinitely better to fail quietly with the fruit of the Spirit than to succeed spectacularly through the works of the flesh. Gifts may impress crowds for a season, but only godliness, deep, hidden, costly godliness, sustains a ministry, a family, a church, and a generation.
Let us return, with urgency and with tears if necessary, to the essence of Christianity and ministry. Let us focus on what matters most: becoming genuine disciples of Jesus Christ, and in so doing, faithfully producing the next generation of disciples who will carry the fire further than we ever could. The scars on Pastor Joseph’s back demand nothing less.
Ayo Akerele is the senior pastor of Rhema Assembly and the founder of the Voice of the Watchmen Ministries in Ontario, Canada. He can be reached through [email protected] .
