title: Russia, Africa are natural allies in building new fair world — Putin
body:
MOSCOW, October 29. /TASS/. Russia and African countries are natural allies in forming a new and fair world order, Russian President Vladimir Putin said at a press conference after the Russia-Africa summit.
"Our countries are natural partners in the process of forming a new, more fair multipolar world," Putin said.
"We maintain close foreign political coordination and work proactively over bilateral and multilateral channels - in the United Nations and other international organizations," the head of state added.

title: Police arrest two masquerades over alleged extortion, others in Akwa Ibom
body: Police in Akwa Ibom State have arrested two Ekpo masquerade participants over allegations of extorting money from residents and assaulting members of the public in Ikot Ekpene. The suspects were arrested at about 6pm on Monday, October 26, along the Ukana/Abak highway during an operational show of force, the police said. The state police spokesperson, Timfom John, identified the suspects in a statement on Thursday as Ine Isong, 29, of Ukana Ikot Esoh Village, and Emmanuel Ekpenyong, 20, from Ikono Local Government Area. John said the suspects were allegedly found in possession of Ekpo masquerade costumes and attire, machetes, spears and arrows. “Preliminary reports indicate that the suspects and other persons allegedly involved in the activities had been terrorising residents and extorting money from unsuspecting members of the public,” the statement said. It added that some people, particularly women, were allegedly assaulted during the activities. John said investigations were ongoing to establish the circumstances surrounding the alleged offences and identify other persons who might be involved. The Commissioner of Police, Baba Azare, warned that the command would not tolerate the use of cultural practices or masquerade activities as a cover for criminality, intimidation, extortion or violence. “While respecting lawful cultural traditions, the command remains resolute in ensuring that no individual or group takes the law into their own hands or threatens the peace and security of residents,” Azare said. The post Police arrest two masquerades over alleged extortion, others in Akwa Ibom appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: U-17 WWC: Flamingos beat Mexico, set up Quarter-Final clash with Venezuela
body:
Nigeria’s Flamingos have advanced to the quarter-finals of the 2026 FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup after defeating Mexico 2-1 in their Round of 16 encounter on Thursday.
Goals from Oluebube Umejiaku and Mary Dunstan secured victory for the Nigerian side at the Mohammed VI Football Complex in Salé, Morocco, as they continued their pursuit of a second appearance in the competition’s semi-finals in the last four years.
Umejiaku opened the scoring in the 40th minute, giving Nigeria a deserved advantage before the break.
The Flamingos maintained their lead into the second half and doubled their advantage in the 71st minute when Dunstan found the net to put the Nigerian girls in a commanding position.
Mexico, however, refused to surrender without a fight. Emily Delgado scored in the 90th minute of stoppage time to reduce the deficit, but Nigeria held on to secure their place in the last eight.
The victory extends the Flamingos’ campaign following their impressive 3-1 triumph over defending champions DPR Korea in their final group match.
That result ended DPR Korea’s run of 18 consecutive matches without a defeat in regulation time at the U-17 Women’s World Cup, dating back to 2018.
Nigeria began their Group B campaign with a 2-1 loss to Poland before responding with a 2-0 win over Puerto Rico.
They finished second in the group with six points from three matches, scoring six goals and conceding four.
Against Mexico, the Flamingos built on the confidence gained from their victory over DPR Korea, producing the goals needed to navigate a potentially difficult knockout encounter.
Mexico had also recovered from an opening 2-0 defeat to Spain, beating Chile 3-1 and Australia 1-0 to finish second in Group F with six points.
Their progress to the Round of 16 suggested they would provide a stern test for Nigeria, but the Flamingos proved more clinical when it mattered.
Thursday’s victory keeps alive Nigeria’s hopes of improving on their previous performances at the competition. The Flamingos won bronze at the 2022 edition in India after reaching the semi-finals.
Nigeria will face Venezuela in the quarter-finals on Sunday, 1 November, at the Mohammed VI Football Academy, Pitch 4, in Salé. Kick-off is scheduled for 7 p.m. Nigerian time.
Venezuela secured their place in the last eight with a major upset, defeating reigning European champions Germany.
The South Americans will present another test for the Flamingos, who must maintain their attacking efficiency and defensive discipline to progress further in Morocco.
With Mexico now behind them, Nigeria will turn their attention to a Venezuelan side that has already shown it can upset the tournament favourites.
For the Flamingos, Sunday’s encounter offers a chance to move within one victory of another semi-final appearance and strengthen their title bid.
Tunde Eludini is a graduate of the Obafemi Awolowo University Ile-Ife, Nigeria where he studied International Relations. He is a Senior Correspondent coordinating the sports section for PREMIUM TIMES. Twitter : @tundeyeludini

title: UN needs reform, but don't throw baby out with bathwater — Putin
body:
MOSCOW, October 29. /TASS/. The UN needs to be reformed, but not completely destroyed, Russian President Vladimir Putin said at a press conference after the Russia-Africa summit.
"Of course, almost all major international structures, including the United Nations, are subject to reform due to the drastic changes in the world," he announced the Russian position. "The only question is that these decisions should be made on the basis of, as we say, broad consensus and that we should not throw the baby out with the bathwater. Not to destroy universal international instruments, such as the United Nations, which are perhaps rightly criticized today, but are singularly unique.
"Humanity does not have a similar organization. Yes, maybe it doesn't work the way we would like it to work, but it still exists, it works, it is a platform where positions are coordinated."

title: Humanitarian mission in Oleshky: Route demining completed, convoy ready to depart – Lubinets
body:
Demining of the routes for the humanitarian mission in Oleshky (Kherson region) has been completed, and the humanitarian convoy is ready to depart, Verkhovna Rada Commissioner for Human Rights Dmytro Lubinets reported from the scene.
"Preparations for the humanitarian mission in Oleshky are entering the final stage. Demining of the designated routes has been completed. The humanitarian convoy has been assembled and is ready to depart," he said on Telegram on Thursday evening.
According to Lubinets, the convoy is expected to arrive at the central hospital. All citizens will be provided with all necessary assistance.
Lubinets also reported that those wishing to leave will be given the opportunity to do so until 14:00. All necessary security measures will be in place. The distribution of humanitarian aid will begin after 14:30.
"Currently, delegations from Ukraine, the Russian Federation, and the United States of America have gathered to coordinate further actions as part of the humanitarian mission. Journalists from the three countries are also present," Lubinets said.
According to Lubinets, the humanitarian mission is being carried out jointly with Yana Lantratova, the Russian Human Rights Commissioner, through the mediation and coordination of U.S. First Lady Melania Trump. "I am grateful to U.S. First Lady Melania Trump for her personal involvement, mediation, and coordination of efforts, thanks to which we were able to reach important humanitarian agreements. We continue to work with Yana Lantratova on their implementation. Our unwavering priority is the lives and safety of the civilian population," the Ukrainian ombudsman added.

title: Russia ready to respond to any challenge in Baltic Sea — Putin
body:
MOSCOW, October 29. /TASS/. Moscow is ready to respond to any challenge in the Baltic Sea but does not want tensions to rise there, Russian President Vladimir Putin said at a press conference following the Russia-Africa summit.
He said Baltic security had come up during telephone talks with Finnish President Alexander Stubb and Norwegian Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Store. Russia does not want a situation similar to that in the Strait of Hormuz and the Persian Gulf to develop in the Baltic Sea, Putin added.
"We do not want that. But we will respond to any challenge," he noted.

title: Ukrainian, US, Russian representatives arrive at site from which aid will be delivered to Oleshky
body:
Davyd Arakhamia, head of the Servant of the People parliamentary faction, announced this on Telegram , Ukrinform reports.
"A delegation of representatives of Ukraine, the U.S. and Russia has reached the site from which aid will be delivered to Oleshky tomorrow," Arakhamia said.
According to him, "media representatives from all three countries are present at the site to ensure the humanitarian mission's next stage is carried out with maximum transparency."
As Ukrinform reported, U.S. First Lady Melania Trump said she had secured a local ceasefire between Russia and Ukraine applying only to the Russian-occupied city of Oleshky in the Kherson region. According to the White House press service, the parties agreed to temporarily suspend all military activity in Oleshky to allow humanitarian aid to be delivered and prepare for the evacuation of civilians through an agreed safe corridor.
The ceasefire in the Oleshky area will remain in effect from October 27 until 22:59 on Sunday, November 1.
President Volodymyr Zelensky said he did not know which direction people would choose to go during the evacuation from Oleshky, but understood that it would be easier for them to leave for areas deeper inside the territory temporarily occupied by Russia. However, he said, many people wanted to return to territory controlled by the Ukrainian government.
Oleksandr Pavlichenko, executive director of the Ukrainian Helsinki Human Rights Union, noted that Russia was interested in keeping some of the population in Oleshky, as this would allow the occupying forces to use them as a human shield against Ukraine.
On Thursday, October 29, a Ukrainian delegation led by Verkhovna Rada Commissioner for Human Rights Dmytro Lubinets set off toward temporarily occupied Oleshky to monitor the humanitarian operation.

title: QatarEnergy Continues LNG Buying Spree to Hedge Future Hormuz Disruptions
body:
Essential news coupled with the finest maritime content sourced from across the globe.
Stock Image: Shutterstock/Oleksandr Kalinichenko
DOHA, Oct 29 (Reuters) – QatarEnergy is buying long-term supplies of liquefied natural gas from the US and other producers as part of a trading strategy designed to generate revenue if exports through the Strait of Hormuz are disrupted in the future, CEO Saad Sherida Al-Kaabi told Reuters on Thursday.
“In a scenario where you have a closure of the strait, which is the true contingency that we’re looking to have, you’d immediately see a spike in gas price and you’ll be able to generate revenue for QatarEnergy that otherwise wouldn’t be generated,” Kaabi, who is also the minister of state for energy affairs, said of the plan.
Kaabi’s remarks reveal for the first time how Qatar, one of the world’s largest LNG producers, plans to offset lost income from the Iran war and protect revenue against future disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz.
The company signed a 20-year agreement on Thursday to buy 3 million metric tons per year (mtpa) from Woodside’s US facilities. Last week it signed two agreements with Cheniere Energy for up to 4 mtpa through 2054 from its Sabine Pass and Corpus Christi plants. Together, the deals amount to 7 mtpa in the past two weeks.
“There’s more to come,” Kaabi said. Cheniere deliveries are not expected to begin until 2031.
Kaabi, appointed CEO of the state energy giant in 2014, said the strategy was his idea and took shape about three months ago after QatarEnergy studied and ruled out pipeline options.
“As we have seen, pipelines and pump stations or compression stations can be also targets.”
The strategy builds on QatarEnergy’s LNG expertise, trading operation and shipping fleet. It requires no capital spending and is far cheaper than building pipelines or extra LNG trains, he said.
“In normal circumstances you’d make a reasonable return and in critical circumstances — however that comes out and how long it is — you have actual proof today of what you could make.”
QatarEnergy halted LNG production in early March after several days of Iranian missile attacks on Qatar. It declared force majeure to affected buyers on March 4.
Qatar accounts for around a fifth of global LNG exports, all of which pass through Hormuz. The company has extended force majeure until the end of 2026.
Kaabi said being unable to ship volumes had taken a heavy toll on revenue.
QatarEnergy believes it can leverage its fleet of about 200 LNG tankers, the world’s largest, as well as QatarEnergy Trading, which Kaabi said will soon become the world’s largest gas trading platform.
“When you have the arbitrage capability that we have, the volume, number of ships, all the capabilities that we have, that’s why you can do it,” Kaabi said.
The hedge targets a market transformed after Iran responded to a war launched by the US and Israel on February 28 by effectively closing the Strait of Hormuz, a vital chokepoint through which a fifth of the world’s oil and LNG shipments pass.
QatarEnergy can profit from the gap between lower US gas prices and higher European prices, Kaabi said.
“You can imagine the arbitrage you can make, and that would make up some of the loss.”
Kaabi said he expects QatarEnergy to sign more 20- to 25-year supply agreements with US and other producers this year.
The company’s target is “much higher” than 7 mtpa, though Kaabi declined to give a figure. He said QatarEnergy was in talks with “everybody,” including Venture Global, and would buy from whichever supplier offered the best commercial terms. Reuters reported last week that Venture Global is in advanced talks to supply 3 mtpa.
Kaabi said QatarEnergy cannot offer US volumes to long-term customers as a backup to Hormuz disruptions because long-term customer contracts are point-to-point — requiring deliveries from specific export terminals to specific destinations. He added that customers had been understanding of the disruption.
Iranian missile strikes on QatarEnergy’s main Ras Laffan gas processing facility in March damaged two of its 14 LNG trains, affecting combined capacity of 12.8 mtpa and knocking out about 17% of Qatar’s export capacity. QatarEnergy said in March the damage would cost about $20 billion a year in lost revenue.
Kaabi said on Thursday that repairs to the two trains would take about three years. The Pearl gas-to-liquids plant, a joint venture between QatarEnergy and Shell that was also damaged in the attack, should return to service by the first quarter of 2027, he said.
He said Qatar could restart full LNG production within a week of a peace deal, provided ships were available. Output would be limited to about 83% of pre-war levels until the damaged trains return.
Kaabi said no announced project had been canceled. Ras Laffan has capacity of 77 mtpa, and Qatar’s plan to expand LNG output to 142 mtpa remains unchanged, with all contracts awarded, he said. North Field East, South and West are all proceeding. The first North Field train is expected to start up in the first quarter of next year, although production would require a US-Iran peace deal to be in place.
Kaabi said he had met Iran’s acting petroleum minister twice in recent weeks to explore oil and gas cooperation once the war ends.
(Reporting by Andrew Mills in Doha and Maha El Dahan in Dubai. Editing by Mark Potter)

title: ‘If things go too far, there will be no winners’: Putin warns Europe, says Russia is ready for war but doesn’t want one
body: Russian President Vladimir Putin said Moscow is ready for war with Europe but does not want one. Many [in Europe] talk about nothing but preparing for war [with Russia] by 2030. title: Estêvão will ‘have his moment’ at Chelsea — Alonso
body: By Adegboyega Adeleye Chelsea head coach Xabi Alonso has promised Brazilian teenager Estêvão will get his opportunity this season, despite the winger’s limited playing time and omission from the Blues’ Carabao Cup quarter-final defeat to Liverpool. Alonso said he understood the 19-year-old’s frustration after he was an unused substitute in Wednesday’s penalty shootout loss, insisting it was his responsibility to manage the youngster’s development and involvement in the team. “I understand his situation and that he could be happier for sure,” Alonso said at his post-match press conference. “Every player wants to play, wants to be part of the team. We have had some intense games, and there will be moments for everything. “I’m sure Estêvão will have his moment. It’s my responsibility, and we need to deal with that.” Estêvão has played only 172 minutes across eight appearances for Chelsea this season, starting just twice under Alonso. His lack of opportunities attracted attention after he remained on the bench against Liverpool, despite Cole Palmer and João Pedro being unavailable for the cup tie. The Brazilian featured in two of Chelsea’s four matches since the latest international break, coming on as a substitute on both occasions. His reduced role follows a promising debut campaign in which he scored eight goals and provided three assists in 36 appearances before his season was cut short by injury. Estêvão also missed the 2026 World Cup because of a hamstring injury, adding to the challenges surrounding his recent progress. The teenager has yet to register a direct goal contribution in the 2026-27 campaign, although he has attempted seven shots, created six chances and completed five of his 14 dribbles, according to the supplied statistics. Alonso’s comments suggest the winger remains part of Chelsea’s plans despite his limited involvement so far. Chelsea will return to Premier League action on Saturday when they host Manchester United, offering Estêvão another opportunity to feature as the London club look to respond to their cup exit. The Blues are also scheduled to face Sunderland before the November international break. The post Estêvão will ‘have his moment’ at Chelsea — Alonso appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: Army pilots are trying virtual reality to stay more alert in flight
body: The 101st Combat Aviation Brigade is testing a virtual-reality headset to see if it can make helicopter pilots more alert. For the next eight months, the unit will incorporate the Oculus -based NeuroTrainer into their flight-training regimen, to measure whether pilots’ reaction times improve. “In the 101st Combat Aviation Brigade, our pilots operate in unpredictable environments where split-second decisions dictate mission success,” Col. Anthony Marston, the unit’s commander, told Defense One. “By putting our aviators through the targeted exercises using the NeuroTrainer, we want to see if it can measurably improve their processing abilities.” Pilots will do three headset sessions a week, playing two games for at least six minutes. One game requires them to catch orange balls while dodging projectiles, and the other challenges them to identify a robot teammate outside of their immediate field of view, then swat a ball in that teammate’s direction. “All the VR-based exercises are designed to challenge and improve reaction time, situational awareness, and quick-decision making,” said Capt. Drew Lightsey, a spokesman for the 101st CAB. During the initial phase of the program, unit pilots will do a round on the NeuroTrainer and then get in a helicopter simulator to measure their cognition, a news release said. “It had a little bit of a learning curve to start,” said Chief Warrant Officer 2 Eric Low, a CH-47 Chinook maintenance test pilot. “Once you start to get the hang of it, it felt like a video game. I like how it challenged different aspects of hand-eye coordination and the ability to track multiple objects at the same time.” The second phase begins at week 15, when 70 pilots will be evaluated on their long-term results. “Evaluators will consider the speed at which aircrews perform emergency procedures in the simulator and a qualitative assessment asking open-ended survey questions on how participants felt they improved after using the system over time,” Lightsey said. Down the line, the NeuroTrainer could become a tool for pilots to use on days when they aren’t flying, or for staff pilots who don’t fly frequently but need to keep their skills sharp. “I think this device could bring awareness to some of the underlying issues affecting our pilots,” said Victor Rodriguez, cognitive performance specialist for the 101st CAB’s Holistic Health and Fitness program. “The performance results could help us recognize when to discuss stress, oversaturation, or emotional regulation with them to help them improve.” The press release said that similar headset tests are taking place at Navy Fighter Weapons School, Air Force Special Operations Command, and the 75th Ranger Regiment. ]]>

title: Shettima seeks deeper interfaith collaboration to strengthen peace, national unity
body: ‎–.Urges religious leaders to support Tinubu’s reforms, national development agenda ‎ ‎By Johnbosco Agbakwuru ‎ ‎ABUJA—Vice President Kashim Shettima has called for deeper collaboration among religious leaders and faith-based organisations to strengthen peaceful coexistence, national unity and collective efforts towards Nigeria’s economic development. ‎He said religious leaders have a critical role to play in fostering understanding across communities, promoting responsible citizenship and mobilising support for initiatives aimed at addressing the nation’s social and economic challenges. ‎ ‎The Vice President made the call when he received a delegation of the Community and Youth Development National Network at the Presidential Villa, Abuja. ‎ ‎The organisation is a coalition of Islamic religious bodies dedicated to youth empowerment, peaceful coexistence and leadership development. ‎ ‎It also maintains an interfaith platform comprising Christian leaders and other stakeholders working to advance shared interests across religious and social boundaries. ‎ ‎Commending the composition and outreach of the organisation, Senator Shettima described its members as people of considerable intellectual capacity, influence and moral standing who could contribute meaningfully to shaping public attitudes and promoting national cohesion. ‎ ‎”A look around the composition of the membership of this group shows men and women of values, people who have the intellectual capacity and candour to shape narratives, acceptability and positive spiritual and moral conduct of Nigerians,” he stated. ‎ ‎The Vice President urged the delegation to sustain engagement with Christian leaders and other religious stakeholders, stressing that dialogue and cooperation remain essential to building trust and strengthening peaceful coexistence. ‎ ‎He also appealed to the group to support the Federal Government’s efforts to address Nigeria’s economic challenges, noting that national development requires a shared sense of responsibility. ‎ ‎”I urge you to be partners in our national progress. Remain undeterred and focused, and let us ensure that whatever binds us supersedes that which divides us. This nation must be seen as a collective responsibility, a collective patrimony which deserves all our loyalty and service,” Senator Shettima said. ‎ ‎The Vice President expressed confidence in the economic reforms being implemented by President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, describing them as necessary measures to address longstanding structural challenges and reposition Nigeria for sustainable growth. ‎ ‎He acknowledged that the reforms had been difficult but maintained that they were laying the foundation for improved economic performance and greater prosperity. ‎ ‎Senator Shettima urged religious and community leaders to contribute to national development by promoting public understanding, encouraging constructive engagement and supporting initiatives that improve citizens’ welfare. ‎ ‎Earlier, the delegation, led by the National Coordinator of the Community and Youth Development National Network, Mallam Ibrahim Shekarau, who also serves as the organisation’s Vice Chairman II, outlined its commitment to religious tolerance, youth development and peaceful coexistence. ‎ ‎The organisation emphasised the importance of strengthening cooperation among religious groups and other stakeholders to promote national stability, responsible leadership and inclusive development. ‎ The post Shettima seeks deeper interfaith collaboration to strengthen peace, national unity appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: Iran expert says second Israeli election would be ‘the best thing' that could happen to Tehran
body: The results of Israel's elections have raised concerns within the Iranian regime, particularly over the possibility that Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu will remain in power, although continued political instability in Israel could ultimately serve Tehran's interests, Iran expert Beni Sabti of the Institute for National Security Studies (INSS) said.Sabti discussed how Iran is analyzing the election results, its fears of Netanyahu, and its preparations for another military confrontation. He also criticized the Trump administration's handling of the Islamic Republic.According to Sabti, political divisions in Israel and the United States provide Iran with a significant advantage."The Iranians are mainly hearing multiple voices. That is the biggest problem on the Western side when facing Iran, and it is what serves Iran the most. We are in a state of instability, with questions about the government and whether an order will be given or not. This greatly strengthens the Iranians. They don't understand democracy. That's the problem. It's not that we're doing something wrong. They don't understand it."Addressing the possibility that Netanyahu will continue serving as prime minister, Sabti said: "The Iranians' worst nightmare has come true. From their perspective, the best thing would have been for Netanyahu to leave the political scene and for a new coalition to emerge, one that would take time to understand Iran. As far as they are concerned, Netanyahu is the strong man, and he can attack.""To their credit, they analyze everyone and understand everyone. They see them all as demons. They understand that one was a chief of staff (Gadi Eisenkot), while another was prime minister for a short time (Naftali Bennett). But during that short period, I remember that every two or three weeks, an Iranian officer or scientist would disappear. That was during Bennett's time."He continued: "They do analyze these people, but Netanyahu is the one credited with the wars, and that is why he frightens them the most. They compare it to their own mentality. When the Iranian leader has ruled for 37 years, and Netanyahu has been around since 1996, that's also 30 years. In the Iranians' eyes, he is someone like them, and that is why he scares them more."I'll say it again, this is all from their perspective. The very possibility of a change in leadership is already better for them. Incidentally, a second election would be the best thing that could happen to Iran. Instability, chaos."The American sideSabti also addressed contacts between Washington and Tehran, arguing that divisions within the US administration are sending the wrong message to Iran."On the American side, there are also disagreements. The worst thing that happened last night was the American misunderstanding. The vice president is sending what amounts to a plea, which is how the Iranians are describing it this morning.""JD Vance sends a message to the secretary of Iran's National Security Council and says, 'Let's agree on various things,' 'We'll open the straits,' 'You'll receive medicine.' The Iranians see this as the enemy's surrender.""There is no such thing as a humanitarian gesture in Iran. It's like the trucks going to Hamas. When you want to help the other side's poor, they interpret it as you not wanting to destroy them. To this day, we are still sending trucks and money to Hamas."Turning to Iran's economic and social situation, Sabti described worsening conditions and growing tensions."The situation is very bad. Yesterday, they raised the price of bread. In a single day, the price of bread jumped by 55%. People are lining up for fuel, and the sounds of war are growing louder."The voices coming from the US are voices of despair. The Iranian public sees a letter from the American vice president saying, 'Let's talk.' The Iranians are at a point where another medicine or another Acamol [painkiller] won't help them. They need surgery to actually remove the regime."There are millions of Iranians who want to overthrow the regime. That sentiment is there. It's a shame the Americans started something and then seemed to lose faith in it. That is the most ridiculous thing that has happened here. There is no benefit to an attack if they are not going to see it through to the end."Finally, Sabti addressed the possibility of renewed protests against the Iranian regime, pointing to the symbolic significance of the birthday of Cyrus the Great."Today is the birthday of King Cyrus. Iranians are desperate to go out and demonstrate against the regime on such a day. Nobody is calling on them to do so; nobody is talking to them about it. October and November are protest months in Iran, and there is real potential right now."If President Trump had called on the Iranian people, perhaps we would be in a different situation. Unfortunately, President Trump has done half the job on many things."

title: Northrop Grumman to supply propulsion systems for 12 Virginia-class submarines, CEO says
body: The order covers main propulsion units and ship service turbine generators, Warden told analysts during Northrop’s October 20 earnings call. She identified the company’s support for shipbuilding as a source of future growth alongside the B-21 bomber and Sentinel missile programs. “We also definitized the Virginia-class Block VI submarine procurement for an additional 12 shipsets of main propulsion units and ship service turbine generators,” Warden said. “The award value adds $1.4 billion to backlog, supporting our partnership with the Navy through 2032.” Chief Financial Officer John Greene said higher marine systems volumes contributed to a 2% increase in third-quarter sales at Northrop’s Mission Systems division. Increased activity on restricted airborne radar programs also helped drive that growth. The submarine equipment award comes as Northrop’s total backlog reached a record $110 billion during the quarter. Warden said existing contracts and backlog gave the company strong visibility through 2028, while the timing of government appropriations and new contracts would influence its growth.

title: 2027: Makinde visits South-east, speaks on Peter Obi, Igbo’s votes
body:
The presidential candidate of the Allied Peoples Movement (APM) and Oyo State Governor, Seyi Makinde, has appealed to the people of the South-east to reject all visions across tribal lines and desist from voting with ethnic and religious sentiments in 2027.
He said Igbos should not be influenced by ethnic and religious sentiments during the forthcoming election because Peter Obi comes from the South-east.
Mr Obi, a former governor of Anambra State, is the presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress.
Mr Makinde spoke during the South-east APM Town hall meeting in Enugu on Thursday.
The APM candidate said he decided to visit the South-east to deliver a message of his Reset Agenda for Nigeria despite his initial discouragement of visiting the region because Mr Obi comes from there.
“When we were coming here, we were almost discouraged because this is the zone of my friend and brother, Peter Obi and the South-east is totally for him,” he said.
The Oyo governor then urged Igbos to remove unhealthy sentiments during the forthcoming general election.
“My message to you today is: reject all visions across either religious or ethnic lines.
“The challenges we are faced with do not know religion, do not know ethnicity,” he said.
Mr Makinde explained that despite criticism from his opponents he had delayed releasing his campaign manifesto until he had concluded his town hall meetings across the six geopolitical zones of the country.
He said the town hall meetings afforded him the opportunity of listening to the people and knowing their needs in order to craft the manifesto in line with the yearnings of Nigerians.
“So, this is the last of the town hall meetings. Over this weekend we will be walking around the clock with our team to get our manifesto ready and it will be launched on the 4th of November 2026,” he declared.
Mr Makinde said his Reset Agenda for Nigeria has four major pillars built on economy, security, education and socio-polity.
The APM candidate said he would serve with sincerity which he argued has the capacity to solve at least 30 per cent of Nigeria’s problems.
“So, we will ensure that we bridge the trust deficit between the leaders and the citizens,” he said, stressing that he did similar things in Oyo State.
He also promised to train youths on skills to boost job creation and reduce the country’s unemployment rate.
“The job of the government is to create an atmosphere conducive for businesses to thrive and that is exactly what we will do,” he assured.
Earlier, the South-east Coordinator of the Makinde-Duara Presidential Campaign Organisation, Okechukwu Obiechina, said Nigeria has been going through difficult moments for several years due to bad leadership.
Mr Obiechina, however, expressed confidence that Mr Makinde would rescue the country if elected president.
“People are finding it difficult to eat three square meals a day, they’re finding it to fuel their vehicles or even pay school fees for their children.
“His Reset Agenda will reset Nigeria. For him, there’s no sacrifice that is too much to be paid for Nigeria,” he said.
Also speaking, the National Chairman of the APM, Yusuf Dantalle, claimed President Bola Tinubu had failed to deliver on his promises to salvage Nigeria since his election in 2023.
Mr Dantalle stressed that Mr Makinde was well qualified to succeed Mr Tinubu to complete the turn of Southern Nigeria.
The national chairman also said Mr Tinubu was too old to govern Nigeria and then urged South-easterners to support 58-year-old Mr Makinde because he represents the youth population.
“Today, we are calling on President Tinubu to support a new direction and step aside from the 2027 race to allow Makinde complete the remaining four years of the Southern term,” he said.
On his part, the APM’s vice-presidential candidate, Lawal Daura, said the party was determined to tackle Nigeria’s challenges through its 16-point agenda.
Mr Daura stressed that the party was committed to reforming the system for the benefit of all Nigerians.
“We are Resetters, volunteers, and we are here to sacrifice for the good of the nation. We are serious about this mission. We are not here to joke, to steal or to lie,” he said.

title: The morning after: Israel’s election leaves more questions than answers
body: Israelis went to the polls expecting clarity. What they got instead was a political puzzle no one seems able to solve. On the latest episode of The Deep Dive, host Jacob Laznik and Knesset correspondent Keshet Neev unpack a whirlwind week in which months of polling were overturned almost overnight.With more than 97% of votes counted, Benjamin Netanyahu's Likud emerged as the largest party at around 27 seats, and his bloc leads the opposition 53 to 48, yet neither side has a path to 61.Arab parties make the differenceThe kingmakers in this deadlock are the Arab parties, which won a record 19 seats on the back of turnout above 80%, well past their previous high of 15. That surge also raised the electoral threshold and wiped out every small party that had dominated months of pre-election speculation.The conversation moves quickly through the scenarios now being whispered in the Knesset corridors. Could a unity government bring together Netanyahu, Gadi Eisenkot and Naftali Bennett? Laznik floats a provocative “200 IQ” scenario for how it might play out, and both hosts explain why the parties' policy promises may make such a coalition unworkable, pointing to the Gantz precedent as a cautionary tale. They also examine the Arab parties' unusual new posture, now focused less on longstanding red lines and more on ousting Netanyahu, alongside Avigdor Liberman's role as the opposition's wild card.Then there is the story that broke publicly later: a Shin Bet investigation into possible foreign interference, with Qatar and Turkey reportedly under scrutiny. Qatar has denied involvement, and the Central Elections Committee says the integrity of the vote remains intact.The hosts also look beyond Israel's borders. They discuss how next week's US midterms could reshape Washington's approach to Iran, why reports of Donald Trump's views on far-right ministers might push Netanyahu toward a broader coalition, and what it means that Netanyahu used election night to name toppling the Iranian regime as his first priority. They also reflect on what these first post–October 7 elections reveal: a Netanyahu bloc still in the lead, but noticeably weaker than before the war.Neev offers viewers a practical guide for cutting through the deliberate noise of the coming weeks. As Laznik puts it, anyone claiming to know what happens next is lying.

title: La residents petition Mahama over Laboma, Kajano and Labadi Beach demolitions
body: Hundreds of protesters from La communities have petitioned President John Dramani Mahama over the demolition of businesses at Laboma, Kajano and Labadi Beach, demanding compensation and government intervention to address the loss of livelihoods. The demonstration, dubbed “Aaagbe Wɔ”, meaning “They are killing us”, was organised by the Ga-Dangme Progressive Front on Thursday, October 29, 2026. The protesters, including affected business owners, residents and supporters, marched to Jubilee House to demand justice, engagement with stakeholders and clarity on the future of the demolished sites. They said the demolitions had destroyed businesses built over several years, leaving owners, workers and their families facing economic hardship. Among those affected was a business owned by former New Patriotic Party (NPP) National Chairman Freddie Blay, who joined the demonstration in solidarity with the affected communities. Mr Blay condemned the demolitions, describing them as “unnecessary demolition” and criticising what he called the “unfriendly and extremely reckless actions of government agents”. He said the exercise had disrupted businesses that residents had operated for years and which contributed to Ghana’s hospitality industry. “Overnight, you have broken them down, rendered about three to four thousand people homeless and jobless,” he said. Mr Blay called for greater consideration of the economic consequences for the affected communities, arguing that the destruction had dealt a severe blow to people whose livelihoods depended on the businesses. The protesters are demanding compensation for affected business owners, consultations with relevant stakeholders and clear information about plans for the demolished sites. Presidency receives petition Dr Bernard Okoe Boye, the Greater Accra Regional Chairman of the NPP, presented a petition to the Presidency on behalf of the Ga-Dangme Progressive Front. The petition called on the government to engage the affected communities and address their concerns. A representative of the Presidency received the document and assured the demonstrators that it would be conveyed to President Mahama, who was out of town at the time. “We appreciate you for exercising your constitutional right and we promise that the petition is duly accepted and will be presented to the President of the Republic,” the representative said. The representative also commended the protesters for demonstrating peacefully. The petition places the concerns of the affected communities before the Presidency, with protesters awaiting a response on compensation, the future of the demolished sites and possible measures to address the loss of livelihoods.

title: Putin certain about Africa’s ability to achieve success
body:
MOSCOW, October 29. /TASS/. African nations will achieve success by drawing upon their cultural roots, determination, and industriousness, Russian President Vladimir Putin told a news conference following the Russia-Africa summit.
He thanked the leaders of the African nations for their collaborative efforts and wished them success.
"I am confident that our African friends will achieve this success by relying on their determination, their industriousness, their traditional cultural roots, and the aspiration of their peoples to improve their standard of living and to secure a more equitable place in the global hierarchy. Russia, within the scope of its capabilities and through its traditional means, will provide every possible form of support," Putin emphasized.

With its playful design, versatility, and relatively affordable price, the Ikea Varmblixt quickly became one of my colleague Jennifer Pattison Tuohy’s new favorite smart light products when she tested it in April . Now, the donut-shaped lamp is on sale for $79.99 ($20 off) through November 11th at Ikea .
Don’t let us tell you where you can or cannot put your Varmblixt. But it’s meant to sit on a table or be mounted on a wall (it can hang from a drilled-in screw, nothing fancy). The newer model lets you cycle through 12 preset colors, including shades of pink, blue, green, and white, as opposed to just orange with the predecessor. You can also use the remote to control other compatible Ikea lights.
For those who want to embed the Varmblixt into their smart home setup, the lamp supports Matter, allowing it to work with compatible smart home platforms including Apple Home, Google Home, and Amazon Alexa. In addition to letting you control the lights with your voice, this gives you access to hundreds more colors, lets you set lighting schedules and sleep or wake-up routines, and allows you to connect the lamp with motion sensors and other smart lights you may have. You can unlock those features with Ikea’s Dirigera hub , as well, which also offers a feature through its Home Smart app that gradually adjusts the shade of white throughout the day akin to natural daylight.

title: Arsenal lose appeal against Dowman red card in shock Fleetwood defeat
body: Arsenal have lost their appeal against Max Dowman’s red card in their stunning League Cup loss at Fleetwood after an independent commission ruled against the Premier League champions. The teenage rising star was sent off for kicking out at Harrison Neal following a strong challenge in the 85th minute of the tie, which the Gunners lost on penalties following a 1-1 draw. Arsenal appealed but England’s governing Football Association announced Thursday an independent commission had dismissed claims of both wrongful dismissal and excessive punishment for Dowman. The 16-year-old Dowman will now begin an immediate three-game ban for violent conduct, starting with Arsenal’s match away to Liverpool in the Premier League on Sunday. Mikel Arteta’s men, level on points with league leaders Manchester City, travel to Anfield looking to bounce back from a huge upset, with fourth-tier Fleetwood now set to face another top-flight side in either Everton or Newcastle in the quarter-finals of the League Cup. title: Russia opens treason case against 76-year-old former Communist faction leader over alleged Ukrainian intelligence ties
body: Gennady Stepakhno, a former deputy speaker of the Murmansk Regional Duma, is under criminal investigation for treason, the regional branch of Russia’s Federal Security Service (FSB) said. The agency said Stepakhno, whom it described as “an opponent of the special military operation ,” had cooperated with Ukraine. The FSB alleges that the former lawmaker used his position to collect documents about the Murmansk regional government’s work and unspecified engineering facilities in the region and pass them to Ukrainian military intelligence. The agency believes this information “could be used to undermine Russia’s security.” Sources cited by the news outlet Arktichesky Obozrevatel believe the investigation into Stepakhno began after he told a relative living abroad that a pharmaceutical plant was being built in the Murmansk region with India’s involvement. A court has already ordered Stepakhno, 76, held in pretrial detention. His detention first became public on October 9. Stepakhno is a veteran Communist lawmaker in the Murmansk Regional Duma. He served four terms from 2007 to 2026 and led the Communist Party faction. He did not return to the regional legislature for its new term.
