title: Petrol price to drop by 3.51%, while diesel will go up by 1.50% from Nov. 1 – COMAC
body: Petrol prices are expected to fall by up to 3.35% per litre from November 1, 2026, while diesel prices could rise by 1.50%, according to the Chamber of Oil Marketing Companies (COMAC). Liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) prices are also projected to increase by 0.81% per kilogram during the November 1–15 pricing window. Data from JoyBusiness indicates petrol could sell at GH¢17.02 per litre, while diesel could reach GH¢18.99 per litre. Actual pump prices will vary between marketing companies. Why the mixed pricing outlook? COMAC attributes the outlook to movements in international petroleum prices, the cedi’s appreciation, and continued government–industry support that moderates diesel price increases. Crude oil prices declined by 1.90% during the review period. However, refined petroleum product prices moved in different directions. International petrol prices fell by 4.97%, while diesel rose by 3.54%. LPG recorded the largest increase at 21.33%. Meanwhile, the cedi appreciated by 0.70% to GH¢11.7326 per US dollar, based on average bank rates between October 12 and October 27, 2026. According to COMAC, the Ghana Gold Board’s foreign exchange interventions over the past three weeks have provided modest support for the currency. It also cited a planned US$1.5 billion injection to support the cedi’s recovery and stability ahead of the festive period. The chamber said the projected pump price adjustments reflect both international refined-product prices and the stronger cedi. Government–industry intervention is also expected to cushion consumers against the full increase in diesel prices. Adjustments to the Energy Sector Shortfall and Debt Repayment Levy (ESSDRL) and selected statutory margins in the diesel price build-up remain in place for one month. “The total value of the intervention remains unchanged, maintaining the Government–industry burden-sharing arrangement introduced on 16 April 2026 to moderate increases in diesel prices at the pumps,” COMAC said. NPA’s price floor The National Petroleum Authority (NPA) has also set new minimum price floors for the pricing window beginning November 1. Market data obtained by JoyBusiness shows the petrol floor fell from GH¢16.09 to GH¢15.39 per litre. The diesel floor has increased from GH¢17.09 to GH¢17.41 per litre. The LPG floor has declined from GH¢13.89 to GH¢13.73 per kilogram. These figures are minimum price floors, not final retail prices. According to the NPA, they exclude premiums charged by International Oil Trading Companies, operating margins of Bulk Import, Distribution and Export Companies, and margins charged by Oil Marketing Companies and LPG Marketing Companies. The respective companies will determine these charges independently under the prescribed Petroleum Products Pricing Formula.

title: If it comes to war between Russia and Europe, 'there will be no winners' — Putin
body:
MOSCOW, October 29. /TASS/. "There will be no winners" in a war between Russia and Europe, President Vladimir Putin said at a press conference after the Russia-Africa summit.
The West has not achieved its goal of inflicting a strategic defeat on Russia, and it is unlikely that this will be possible by 2030, Putin said.
"And if it goes too far, there will be no winners at all. Let no one forget about it," he said.

title: HII Celebrates ROMULUS USV Production Progress for U.S. Navy
body: NEW IBERIA, La. — On Tuesday, Oct. 27, HII, America’s largest military shipbuilder and the global leader in autonomous seapower, celebrated a milestone in the production of Romulus unmanned surface vessels for the U.S. Navy during a ceremony in Louisiana, highlighting the state’s vital role in delivering the next generation of autonomous maritime capabilities. Louisiana Gov. Jeff Landry joined Vice Adm. Michael Wosje, deputy chief of naval operations for Warfighting Requirements and Capabilities (N9); HII President and CEO Chris Kastner; and Breaux Brothers Enterprises President Brannon Breaux for the celebration, which featured the ceremonial installation of a commemorative hull plaque on the first-in-class Romulus 151 USV. The event celebrated the continued progress on HII’s production of Romulus USVs for the U.S. Navy’s medium unmanned surface vessel (MUSV) program and honored the skilled workforce, regional shipbuilding partners and advanced manufacturing capabilities supporting construction of the vessels. The U.S. Navy recently awarded HII a contract to build 10 Romulus 151 vessels under the MUSV program, reinforcing the importance of the Louisiana and Gulf Coast maritime industrial base in delivering advanced defense capabilities, sustaining skilled shipbuilding jobs and strengthening national security. “Louisiana is the powerhouse of the maritime industry, and today we solidified that legacy. Working with Breaux Brothers and HII, we are committed to ensuring the next generation of maritime technology is built by Louisiana hands on Louisiana soil,” Landry said. “We are proud to play an important role in helping the U.S. Navy remain the most powerful and capable of any military in history. This is a great day for Louisiana and a great day for America’s national security.” “Building and fielding the Medium Unmanned Surface Vessel is an essential tailored offset within the CNO’s Hedge Strategy, expanding distributed lethality, and maritime domain awareness across contested waters. Leveraging rapid commercial acquisition paths coupled with agile fleet Introduction, we are integrating combat-ready autonomous capabilities into the Fleet to provide Combatant Commanders with asymmetric options…and we are going to do it fast!” Wosje said. Romulus is a modular family of AI-enabled USVs built on HII’s open-architecture Odyssey Advanced Autonomy Solutions and designed to meet current and emerging requirements for the U.S. Navy, U.S. Marine Corps, joint forces, and allied partners. The platform supports a wide range of missions, including intelligence, surveillance and reconnaissance (ISR); mine countermeasures; strike operations; counter-unmanned systems; and the launch and recovery of unmanned underwater and aerial vehicles. The U.S. Navy’s selection of the Romulus 151 USV represents a significant step in the transition from unmanned maritime experimentation to operational deployment at fleet scale. The program combines HII’s decades of shipbuilding experience with proven autonomous technologies and a distributed production strategy designed to deliver reliable, mission-ready vessels efficiently and at scale. “Louisiana has builders who have been turning aluminum into hard-working boats for generations.” Kastner said. “And when the U.S. Navy put us to the test in the Gulf, Romulus met all the Navy requirements. That’s the kind of team we like to assemble, one that can be trusted to compete and win.” Louisiana Shipbuilders Power the Future of Autonomous Seapower HII’s Romulus USV production strategy draws on the expertise of established Gulf Coast maritime partners, including Breaux Brothers Enterprises, Halimar Shipyard and Bayou Metal Supply & Manufacturing in Louisiana. The Romulus USV was developed in partnership with Beier Integrated Systems and Incat Crowther. “For four generations, our family has built vessels right here in Louisiana, and today we are proud to put that experience to work in support of the United States Navy,” Breaux said. “Building HII’s Romulus USV is an opportunity to serve our country in a way that means a great deal to me personally and my shipbuilders. Our craftsmen have spent decades building custom, reliable, aluminum vessels that can perform in the toughest conditions, and now we are bringing that same expertise to the next generation of naval technology.” In 2025, HII began securing the partnerships, production capacity, supplier network and infrastructure needed to accelerate Romulus USV construction. Those early investments helped establish a production-ready approach designed to reduce risk and support the U.S. Navy’s growing demand for autonomous maritime platforms. Proven Autonomy, Built for U.S. Navy and Allied Operations At the core of Romulus USVs is HII’s Odyssey Autonomous Control Solutions (ACS), a combat-tested, modular, open-architecture autonomy suite designed to enable trusted, coordinated operations across maritime environments. Odyssey enables unmanned vessels to perceive their surroundings, navigate, manage onboard systems and payloads, coordinate with manned and unmanned platforms, and execute complex missions with limited human intervention. Its open architecture also supports integration of emerging sensors, command-and-control technologies and artificial intelligence capabilities. HII, alongside partners Applied Intuition, Greenroom Robotics and Rodi Marine, successfully completed the MUSV program’s evaluation phase, demonstrating Odyssey ACS capabilities during 13 days of U.S. Navy-monitored testing in the Gulf of America. The evaluation included a demanding long-endurance mission simulation in which HII’s autonomy system successfully completed a 420-nautical-mile mission over 28 hours, meeting all established success criteria and demonstrating the reliability and endurance required for sustained maritime operations. The Louisiana celebration underscored the importance of pairing proven autonomous technologies with the nation’s shipbuilding workforce and industrial capabilities to accelerate delivery of the U.S. Navy’s future unmanned fleet. From HII, Oct. 28, 2026 The post HII Celebrates ROMULUS USV Production Progress for U.S. Navy appeared first on Seapower Magazine .

title: Ottawa to invest up to $1.6B in Canadian AI firm Cohere
body:
Prime Minister Mark Carney said Thursday his government will invest up to $1.6 billion in Canadian AI company Cohere.
He made the announcement in Montreal as he welcomed European Union leaders to a summit aimed at forging closer ties.
“We are not waiting for the future of AI to be decided somewhere else by those we don’t know or by whom we don’t trust. We’re building it right here in the right way,” Carney said.
In April, Cohere announced it would merge with Germany’s Aleph Alpha and said the company would be “anchored in” Germany and Canada.
On Thursday, Carney called the partnership a concrete example of what Canada and Europe can build together.
He also said that, under the agreement, Cohere will stay Canadian.
Carney said the government is making the announcement on “a commercial basis, alongside private investors including Nvidia, Bell, and Germany’s Schwarz Group.”
Cohere CEO Aidan Gomez said at the announcement that the company, which was founded seven years ago, is now “one of the very few companies in the world building frontier AI technology at a global scale.”
He added that it’s the largest AI company outside the U.S. and China.
In a press release issued Thursday, the government said the funding would be provided in stages, with regular reporting on commitments made by the company.
Those commitments include creating at least 1,000 “new high-paying Canadian technical jobs” and committing at least $1.7 billion to building more computing infrastructure by 2030.
The government says Cohere will also maintain its Canadian headquarters and incorporation, invest in research partnerships, create opportunities for students and graduates and continue working with the Canadian AI Safety Institute.
“Cohere will now be able to develop far more advanced models and products, scale up its computing infrastructure, and expand its Canadian workforce to serve more businesses and governments in Canada and around the world,” the press release said.
“Building this capability at home ultimately means that Canadian businesses and governments will have more choice in how they adopt AI and greater control over their sensitive information.”
In 2024, the government announced it would provide up to $240 million to Cohere to boost its computing capacity. In 2025, Ottawa signed an agreement with the company to identify areas where AI can enhance public service operations.
Artificial Intelligence Minister Evan Solomon has often pointed to Cohere as an element of Canada’s strength in AI, saying Canada is one of only a few countries around the world with a large language model.

title: Russell Brand’s wife tells jury he is a ‘wonderful’ father during rape trial
body:
Russell Brand’s wife, Laura Gallacher, told London’s Southwark Crown Court Thursday that her husband, who is on trial for rape and sexual assault allegations , is “caring, kind and a wonderful father” to their children, according to U.K. media reports.
Gallacher, 39, told the jury that “the way he treats me is to know me,” and that she feels seen by Brand and loves him “very much,” the BBC and The Guardian report.
Brand, 51, is facing seven charges including three counts of rape, three counts of sexual assault and one count of indecent assault. The charges involve six women and alleged offences between 1999 and 2009. The trial is expected to last up to 10 weeks.
The actor and media personality has pleaded not guilty to all charges.
Brand and Gallacher got married in 2017, but had split up in the past over his disinterest in monogamy, Gallacher told the court, according to The Guardian.
“I wasn’t interested in having a relationship with him if he was sleeping with other people,” she said, the U.K. outlet reported.
They first began dating in 2006 after meeting at the Edinburgh Festival in Scotland. She described him then as being “very caring,” and willing to take things “totally at my pace.”
“I was not experienced; I had only had one partner before Russell, and I felt entirely cared for and looked after by Russell,” she continued, The Guardian reports, adding that she told the court she was aware he “liked women” and that he was “engaging” with other women within the first year of their relationship.
His infidelity eventually led to their split in 2007, but they reconciled in 2015 after Brand ended his marriage to Katy Perry — who has been in a relationship with former Canadian prime minister Justin Trudeau since July 2025. Gallacher said that during their time apart, she and Brand remained friends and would talk about his promiscuity.
She went on to describe their marriage as “honest” and “clear.”
Brand, who took the stand on Wednesday, acknowledged that he had engaged in “reckless” sexual activity for much of his life.
“I have been persuasive, seductive, begging and flirting, and have dedicated a ​lot of my life to what seems now beyond reckless philandering and idiocy,” he told the court towards ⁠the end of about four hours of evidence, Reuters reported.
“I was in a position of fame. As I became more successful and famous, I was ​very comfortable allowing that to facilitate sexual access, which I agree was wrong,” he added.
The jury has previously been told how all the complainants came forward ​to detectives after a documentary was broadcast in 2023, along with several newspaper articles in which anonymous allegations were made by other women who are not involved in the trial.
Prosecutors allege that Brand ‌raped a ⁠woman after meeting her at a fringe event for a Labour Party conference in 1999, forced a woman to give him oral sex in the toilets of a London bar in 2004, and molested another woman at a radio station in 2004 or 2005.
He is also accused of trying to drag a woman into the men’s toilets at MTV Europe, in London, where she was working in 2001, and of anally raping a ​woman in 2009.
The final ⁠allegation is that he assaulted a woman while they were involved in a recording project.
“Consent is fundamental, essential, necessary and indeed more important than sex itself,” Brand told the court while discussing the first rape allegation.
While he said he did not ​remember incidents involving three of the alleged victims, he did recall details about the other alleged rapes, saying both women had either consented or the incident ​was not as ⁠they portrayed, Reuters said.
During the trial’s opening statements earlier this month, the prosecution described Brand as a “ruthless” sexual predator who was “indiscriminate and voracious” in his pursuit of sexual contact at the time of the alleged assaults and said he viewed women as a “means to an end.”

title: APC rejects court ruling, insists Uzodimma is Senatorial candidate
body: The All Progressives Congress (APC) in Imo State has rejected a Federal High Court ruling recognising former governor Rochas Okorocha as its candidate for Imo West Senatorial District in the 2027 general elections, insisting that Governor Hope Uzodimma remains its flagbearer. The party said Uzodimma emerged victorious in its senatorial primary with the overwhelming support of its members, adding that its legal department would study the court’s decision before determining its next course of action. The position was contained in a statement issued on Thursday by the APC State Publicity Secretary, Onwuasoanya Jones, following the ruling by Justice Obiora Egwuatu of the Federal High Court, Abuja. The court had ordered the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) to publish Okorocha’s name as the APC candidate for the senatorial district ahead of the January 16, 2027 election. It also directed Uzodimma to stop presenting himself as the party’s candidate for the election. However, the APC maintained that the governor remained its duly nominated candidate, citing the outcome of the party’s primary election. “The Party wishes to state without any confusion that His Excellency Distinguished Senator Hope Uzodimma, CON, remains the candidate of our Party for Imo West Senatorial District, having won the primaries of our great Party with the overwhelming support of the majority of our Party members,” the statement said. The party said it would examine the court’s decision before taking further action on the dispute. “The Party’s legal department shall study the outcome of a legal intervention in this matter and act accordingly,” it added. The APC also called on its members and supporters to remain committed to the party’s political objectives and work towards securing victories across Imo State in the 2027 elections. The dispute stems from the APC senatorial primary held on May 18, 2026, in which Uzodimma was declared the winner with 230,464 votes, while Okorocha was credited with 1,098 votes, according to the results recognised by INEC. Dissatisfied with the outcome, Okorocha approached the court to challenge the process and the recognition of Uzodimma as the party’s candidate for the district. In its ruling on Thursday, the court held that Okorocha was the lawful winner of the primary and ordered the APC to submit his name to INEC for publication as its candidate. The court also questioned inconsistencies in documents submitted by the party in support of Uzodimma’s nomination.

title: Jobberman Launches ‘Her Next Move’ Campaign to Advance Female Inclusion Through Free Skills Training
body: Jobberman Nigeria, Nigeria’s leading career development and recruitment solutions company, has launched ‘Her Next Move’, a campaign designed to empower young Nigerian women with practical skills and confidence to pursue career opportunities and participate more fully in the workforce. Through free online training, the initiative supports women aged 18 to 35 as they prepare to enter the workplace, advance into better roles or explore freelance and gig work. Built around the message ‘Your Future. Your Skills. Your Move’, the campaign places female inclusion at the centre of career development, encouraging women to take an active role in shaping their professional futures. It connects the ambition to progress with an accessible starting point: learning skills that can help women prepare for their next opportunity. ‘Her Next Move’ recognises that career progress looks different for every woman. For a graduate, it may mean preparing for a first job. For a woman already working, it may involve developing the skills to take on greater responsibility or pursue a new role. For another, it may mean understanding how to navigate freelance work and participate in the global gig economy. The campaign brings these aspirations together through a shared emphasis on learning, preparation and action. This Initiative by Jobberman in partnership with Mastercard Foundation promotes two courses: Jobberman Soft Skills Training and Becoming a Successful Global Gig Worker. Both courses are free, with a free certificate upon successful completion. Jobberman Soft Skills Training focuses on workplace readiness, helping participants build the professional skills needed to navigate work and prepare for career progression. Becoming a Successful Global Gig Worker introduces participants to the demands and opportunities of freelance and gig work, supporting women interested in exploring career paths beyond traditional employment. By making the training and certification available at no cost, ‘Her Next Move’ reduces the financial barrier to participation and encourages more young women to invest in their professional development. Its focus extends from raising awareness of learning opportunities to helping participants follow through and complete their chosen course. To bring the campaign to life, Jobberman is working with young creators who are sharing personal stories about ambition, career transitions and the role of learning in their journeys. Through videos, social media posts and follow-up conversations, the creators encourage young women to reflect on their own goals and identify the practical steps they can take towards them. These stories are intended to make career development relatable, connecting everyday aspirations with opportunities to learn. Across the campaign, the question “ What is your next move?” invites women to define progress for themselves and begin preparing for it. ‘Her Next Move’ reinforces Jobberman’s and Mastercard Foundation’s commitment to supporting career development and expanding access to learning for young Nigerian women. By combining free skills training with relatable storytelling and encouragement to take action, the campaign seeks to help more women feel prepared to pursue their ambitions.

title: Putin cites Russia-Africa summit motto 'For Peace, Security and Development'
body:
MOSCOW, October 29. /TASS/. The motto of the third Russia-Africa summit, held in Moscow, was "For Peace, Security and Development," which set the course of the discussions, Russian President Vladimir Putin said at a news conference following the summit.
"It is certainly gratifying that 21 African leaders, high-ranking delegations from the overwhelming majority of countries on the continent, and heads of almost all leading African integration organizations took part in the Moscow summit. The motto of this summit is ‘For Peace, Security and Development,’" the Russian leader said.
As Putin emphasized, this motto essentially determined the course and topics of the discussions.

title: Abuja Job & Career Fair 2026 Connects Talents With Employers, Advances Inclusive Access to Employment
body: The Fair brings together government, employers and development partners to expand employment opportunities, strengthen workforce readiness and promote inclusive hiring. The Federal Ministry of Labour and Employment (FMLE), with the support of the Mastercard Foundation in partnership with Jobberman Nigeria and the GIZ SEDEC Cluster, has convened the Abuja Job & Career Fair 2026 to strengthen connections between talents and employers, improve workforce readiness and expand access to employment opportunities. Held under the theme ‘ Opportunities, Connections and Impact,’ the Fair features employer engagements, career counselling, CV reviews and training sessions on employability and skills development, with a focus on expanding access for women, persons with disabilities and other underserved groups. “The Abuja Job & Career Fair is about more than bringing talents and employers into one space. It is about creating connections that lead to employment and giving participants a clearer pathway to dignified and fulfilling work,” said the Country Head of Programmes at Jobberman Nigeria, Olamide Adeyeye. She noted that physical career fairs remain vital, as many young people still face barriers to online opportunities, adding that more than 150,000 people secured jobs through job fairs, career events and job centres in the past year. Opening the Fair, the Minister of Labour and Employment, Dr. Muhammadu Maigari Dingyadi , pledged to expand access to jobs through public job centres and the National Electronic Labour Exchange (NELEX), the ministry’s digital job-matching platform. He identified skills mismatches and weak links between job seekers and employers as key challenges and urged employers to look beyond academic qualifications. Delivering a goodwill message on behalf of Dr Markus Wagner, Country Director, GIZ Nigeria and ECOWAS, Oladoyin Olawaiye noted that GIZ and the ministry have established 11 job centres across five states under the Skills Development for Youth Programme, serving over 65,000 people, more than half of them women. For participant Victory Izevbizua, the Fair delivered on both fronts. She came hoping to meet employers in Customer Service and Data Analytics and met several, but her highlight was a Jobberman career counselling session, where a counsellor reviewed her CV and gave her clear, actionable advice on tailoring it for different roles. “The job seekers I have met here are innovative, willing to work and enthusiastic about what they do. With talents like these, we believe we can change the narrative of healthcare in Nigeria,” said Anomiri Chidozie-Pascal, Founder and CEO of Big Panda Medicare (PandaCare), which is recruiting for administrative, public health, data analysis, social media and digital marketing roles. The Fair is supported by the Mastercard Foundation, through its Young Africa Works Programme, and international development partners, including the European Union (EU), the German Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development (BMZ), the Swiss Development Cooperation (SDC) and the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Denmark.

title: NASS to conclude state police law before December – Senate Leader
body:
The Senate Leader, Opeyemi Bamidele, has said the two chambers of the National Assembly will review state assemblies’ resolutions on the proposed state police system and conclude the process before December.
Mr Bamidele, who represents Ekiti Central Senatorial District, said the lawmakers would review resolutions passed by state Houses of Assembly on the proposed constitutional amendment before transmitting the final resolution to President Bola Tinubu for assent.
He spoke on Thursday while delivering a lecture at the Senior Executive Course 48 programme organised by the National Institute for Policy and Strategic Studies ( NIPSS ) in Kuru, Plateau State.
“We have set a clear timeline for ourselves. We intend to conclude all these legislative stages — consideration of reports, passage of resolution, and transmission for presidential assent — on or before December 2026,” he said.
The Senate and the House of Representatives passed the proposed state police framework in September, and it was transmitted to state Houses of Assembly for consideration as part of the process of amending the 1999 Constitution.
The proposal seeks to establish state police services that would operate alongside the existing federal police system.
Under the proposed framework, state governors would appoint police commissioners, subject to confirmation by their respective Houses of Assembly. Governors would also be empowered to direct state police on matters relating to insecurity.
While the Inspector-General of Police would continue to head the federal police, a commissioner appointed by the state governor and confirmed by the state House of Assembly would head each state police service.
The proposal, however, stipulates that existing local security outfits cannot be converted into state police services or exercise police powers under the new framework. It also prohibits such outfits from bearing firearms.
Such outfits include Amotekun in the South-West, Ebube Agu in the South-East, and Hisbah in parts of northern Nigeria.
Under Section 9 of the 1999 Constitution, a proposed constitutional amendment must be approved by at least two-thirds of the 36 state Houses of Assembly, which means 24 states. before the National Assembly can proceed with the final stages of the amendment process.
About 30 state assemblies have reportedly approved the proposal, exceeding the required threshold and paving the way for the National Assembly to consider their resolutions and proceed with the remaining legislative stages.
Mr Bamidele said the state assemblies’ approvals had brought the country closer to establishing state police after more than 15 years of efforts to introduce the system.
He said the development demonstrated the National Assembly’s commitment to prioritising the security of lives and property.
“What this means is that State Police is no longer a campaign promise or a subject of endless debate. It is now a constitutional reality. It means that the security of lives, private property and public assets occupies a prime place in the legislative agenda of the 10th National Assembly,” he said.
He said the proposed system would enable Nigeria to develop a policing structure that understands local terrain, speaks local languages, respects local realities and remains accountable to local communities.
“It is not about creating state armies, but about creating state-led, community-anchored policing within clear constitutional safeguards, operational standards, oversight mechanisms and human rights protections,” he said.
Mr Bamidele added that the National Assembly, under the leadership of Senate President Godswill Akpabio, remained committed to establishing state police.
“The National Assembly, under the leadership of the President of the Senate, Senator Godswill Akpabio, remains committed to delivering on the establishment of State Police. We will not falter until every Nigerian, whether in Kuru, in Iyin-Ekiti, in Gusau or in Yenagoa, can sleep with both eyes closed,” he said.

title: Gunmen kill farmer, injure pastor in Plateau attack
body:
Gunmen have killed a 36-year-old farmer and injured a pastor in an attack on a farm in Lamor community, Pushit District, Mangu Local Government Area of Plateau State, while another man has been reported missing.
The attack occurred on Wednesday afternoon, according to a community youth leader, Bulus Nehemiah, who confirmed the incident.
Mr Nehemiah identified the deceased as Steven Bala and the injured cleric as Apollos Charly, the owner of the farm where the attack occurred.
He said a 57-year-old man, Danbaba Libet, was also missing following the incident.
“During the attack on Pastor Apollos Charly’s farm, Steven Bala, aged 36, was killed by the gunmen. The pastor himself was injured, while another man, Mr Danbaba Libet, aged 57, is still missing,” Mr Nehemiah said.
He alleged that armed men suspected to be members of a militia had repeatedly attacked communities in Pushit District in recent weeks, disrupting farming activities during the harvest season.
“In the past few weeks, the gunmen have been terrorising our communities in Pushit, attacking and killing our people. They have prevented us from going to our farms, especially now that it is harvest season,” he said.
Another community leader, John Sabo, condemned the attack and called on security agencies to investigate the incident, apprehend those responsible and strengthen security in the area.
“We condemn this senseless attack in the strongest terms. No community should be subjected to this kind of violence, and innocent people should not continue to lose their lives,” Mr Sabo said.
He urged security operatives to increase their presence in the affected communities to prevent further attacks and reassure residents of their safety.
Efforts to obtain confirmation from the Plateau State Police Command were unsuccessful as the police spokesperson, Alfred Alabo, did not respond to calls or text messages sent to his phone.
The latest attack adds to security concerns in parts of Mangu Local Government Area, where community members have raised concerns about violence and restrictions on access to farmland.

title: Question about rivalry has nothing to do with Russia, colonialism alien to it — Putin
body:
MOSCOW, October 29. /TASS/. Russia has never been a colonial power, this is why the question of the possible use of African territory for rivalry with anyone directed at Moscow is misplaced, President Vladimir Putin said at a press conference after the Russia-Africa summit.
"As for the fact that the countries of the African continent can remain or be the subject of rivalry between large states, this is not the right question. Russia has never considered the countries of Africa as some kind of objects for rivalry," he noted.
"For Russia, the African countries have always, throughout history, been only friends. We were not engaged in colonial policy. On the contrary, we helped African countries to free themselves from colonial dependence."

title: UN appoints Russian diplomat to oversee mine action, as Ukraine clears over 300,000 explosives in Kherson Oblast
body:
The United Nations has appointed a Russian diplomat to a senior position overseeing mine action, drawing criticism from Ukraine as the country continues to clear hundreds of thousands of explosive devices left behind by Russia's war.
U.N. Secretary-General Antonio Guterres announced the appointment of Gleb Desyatnikov as assistant secretary-general for mine action and police in the Department of Peace Operations on Oct. 27.
Desyatnikov has served as Russia's ambassador to Jordan since 2018, including throughout Moscow's full-scale invasion of Ukraine. According to the U.N., he has more than 35 years of experience in international relations and security affairs, including previous positions at Russia's Foreign Ministry.
"Moscow has mined the United Nations," Ukrainian Foreign Ministry spokesperson Heorhii Tykhyi wrote on X on Oct. 29, criticizing the decision.
"Entrusting this responsibility to a representative of the aggressor state is deeply troubling and undermines trust in the United Nations," he added.
The appointment comes as Ukraine faces one of the world's largest demining challenges, with Russian mines and unexploded ordnance threatening civilians and complicating the recovery of agricultural land and infrastructure.
In southern Kherson Oblast, demining teams have neutralized 300,691 explosive devices on the Ukrainian-controlled right bank since the start of clearance operations, according to the regional military administration .
Between Oct. 22 and 28 alone, specialists surveyed 602.8 hectares (1,490 acres) and neutralized 471 explosive devices, the administration reported on Oct. 29. Authorities said 74.5% of the territory designated for clearance on the region's right bank has now been cleared.
In December 2022, Human Rights Watch (HRW) confirmed that Russia was using 13 models of anti-personnel and 13 models of anti-vehicle landmines in its invasion of Ukraine, and that approximately 30% of the country — an area twice the size of Austria — had been "contaminated" with mines.
Among them are also PFM-1 "Butterfly" anti-personnel mines. The mines are green or olive in color, and recognizable by their distinctive shape, similar to the "propellor" seeds that spiral down from maple, ash, and sycamore trees. During the Soviet invasion of Afghanistan, they became better known for their injurious effects on the curious children who would find them while out playing.
Speaking to the Kyiv Independent nine months later, HRW Associate Director Mark Hiznay, explained the near impossibility of keeping that figure current. What is known is that Russia, at the beginning of the full-scale invasion, had a stockpile of 26 million mines —the largest in the world, according to various estimates.

title: Mission To Breed And Replicate Umo Enos
body: By Anietie Usen Ndifreke Akpekong is a cassava farmer in Eket, Akwa Ibom State. Four years ago in 2022, he was operating as a struggling farmer in a local community in the hinterland of his LGA. The only trouble was that Akpekong was dealing with severe capital limitations that prevented him from expanding his cassava farming. This restriction kept profit margins thin and limited his scope of operations. But his story changed after he received a grant of N500,000 from IBOM IGNITE, an NGO set up by Pastor Umo Eno, six years before he became the Governor. With the half-a-million Naira grant, according to reports in THE GATHERING, Akpekong “successfully cultivated a 0.7-hectare cassava plantation and directly expanded his local economic footprint by employing over 15 persons both directly and indirectly within the community”. Udofia Emmanuel, a metal fabricator and another beneficiary of IBOM IGNITE told his story to journalists covering the 2025 edition of the programme. “I was struggling to meet customer demands because I lacked the specialized gear. Winning the ₦250,000 grant completely changed my trajectory. I was able to acquire a brand-new specialized machine for my metal fabrication yard. Not only did it increase my capacity, but I have also been able to hire two additional staff to join my business.” So are the stories of Ruth Bassey, founder of Enriched Bakery, Uyo; Tochukwu Lorenzo, fine artist and interior decorator; Uyo; Mary Ekpo, fashion and apparel designer, Eket; Blessing Udofot, fashion designer inEket; Pastor Church Mfon Monday, a manufacturer of cosmetics and household products in Etim Ekpo; Ikemesit Awak, a producer of cleaning products and liquid soap; to mention a few. Before the grant of N500,000, Bassey, a chemical engineering graduate was trying to break into the bakery business. She was constrained by low-capacity of domestic baking tools, which restricted her market reach and daily output. After the grant, she said she “upgraded her workflow by acquiring a commercial mixer and an additional industrial oven”. She also initiated her formal NAFDAC product registration and scaled up her operations to hire five permanent staff. For Pastor Monday, another graduate of the University of Uyo, “the IBOM IGNITE grant in addition to my savings helped me to purchase a brand new 30KVA; four cylinder sound proof diesel generating plant, to expand my soap production factory from manual method to a fully automated soap factory…” Tochukwu Lorenzo, a creative artist and decorator got a grant of N500,000. Before the grant, he was relying on sporadic, raw commissions without the machinery or high-grade supplies needed to tender for corporate interior design projects. After the grant, Lorenzo secured commercial studio gears, allowing him to transition his artistic talent into a formal business structure capable of handling large-scale commercial decoration contracts across Uyo and Eket. It is virtually the same story for more than 10,000 trainees who have successfully gone through the IBOM IGNITE programme since inception in 2017. Over the years, beneficiaries of the IBOM IGNITE Conference have shared overwhelming testimonials, describing the programme as the critical turning point for their businesses. Beyond the financial seed funding, past participants consistently highlight the mindset shift, practical financial prudence, and the ability to structurally design a business vision as the most valuable takeaways that helped them transition from ideas to surviving local enterprises. IBOM IGNITE is one programme that reflects the deepest desires of Governor Eno to, in his words, ‘produce after its own kind’, a Biblical phrase that establishes the biological and spiritual law that every living thing reproduces offspring matching its exact species or nature. As the NGO is taking stock of its last six years, all is set also for the take off of the IBOM IGNITE CONFERENCE 2026, scheduled for October 27 and 28, 2026, at Ibom Hall, IBB Avenue, Uyo, Akwa Ibom State. Launched as a private, faith-based, youth-focused empowerment platform by Pastor Eno way back in 2017, six years before he became the Governor of Akwa Ibom State, the annual capacity building and entrepreneurial empowerment programme draws from the Eno example and background as a self-made entrepreneur, who built the Royalty Group and a fortune from a small 5-room hotel in Eket. Since then, the IBOM IGNITE Conference has evolved from a local faith-based youth initiative into one of the most influential state-backed youth entrepreneurship and leadership movements in Nigeria’s South-South region. The maiden conference took place in Eket, Akwa Ibom State, drawing around 2,000 young leaders and featuring prominent local business mentors. Over the years, the annual conference shifted to the capital city of Uyo. Following Pastor Eno’s election as Governor, the platform seamlessly aligned with his Administration’s ARISE Agenda, cementing its role as a premier gateway for human capital development and startup financing in Akwa Ibom State. This year’s stanza of the programme is featuring a blend of administrative leaders, spiritual mentors, and seasoned strategy consultants; including Pastor Eno himself, a highly successful entrepreneur who is bringing to the table practical business experience together with his hands-on background and track record in governance. Other resource persons include Apostle Joshua Selman, the highly influential founder of Eternity Network International (ENI) and host of Koinonia. He is globally recognized for his teachings on principles of personal development, mindset shifts, and leadership strategy; Sir Charles Sebastian Udoh, a seasoned media, communications, and brand management executive who has served as a state commissioner, bringing public relations expertise to the panel and Ime Uwah, the Senior Special Assistant on Entrepreneurial Development to Governor Eno. Hanson Johnson, a prominent digital ecosystem builder and country director behind local tech hubs, focusing heavily on fueling software development and youth digital empowerment across the South-South region; as well as Dr. Maxwell Ubah, an elite corporate strategist, leadership expert, and CEO of Strategy House Limited, who specialises in restructuring businesses and training executives. They will all focus on the theme: “REINVENT: Rethink, Reimagine, Redesign, Become”. The target is 1,500 young leaders, entrepreneurs, and innovators, selected on merit through a public, digital application pipeline that operated on a strict, first-come-first-served basis. Applicants were filtered into two distinct streams based on their intent: those registering strictly as general conference attendees to participate in leadership training, and those applying for the IBOM IGNITE Entrepreneurship and Innovation Grant. For participants seeking a portion of the ₦50 Million funding pool, an additional layer of selection was implemented. Out of the registered pool, 470 applicants were selected to advance to a mandatory physical screening and live pitching assessment held at the IBOM-LED Complex on October 24, 2026. The final winners in both the Startup and Existing Business categories will be unveiled live during the wrap-up event of the IBOM IGNITE Conference on October 28, 2026. According to Governor Eno the initiative maintains an over 60% success rate, verified by trackable testimonials of beneficiaries who used early seeds to build functional, surviving businesses. Across its distinct annual cycles, the program has collectively trained, upskilled, and mentored over 10,000 Akwa Ibom youths in corporate leadership, digital innovation, agribusiness, and financial prudence. By drawing down global industry leaders, tech CEOs, and national visionaries (like Apostle Joshua Selman and Obafemi Banigbe), it bridges the gap between grassroots local entrepreneurs and national economic pipelines. Beyond the financial seed funding, past participants consistently highlight the mindset shift, practical financial prudence, and the ability to structurally design a business vision as the most valuable takeaways that helped them transition from ideas to surviving local enterprises. Ikemesit Awak who emerged as the standout winner last year in the highly competitive Business Startup Category and walked away with a ₦2 Million startup capital grant after delivering a masterful pitch, said her business fortunes and trajectory are now irreversible. “This grant helped me achieve one of my major business goals, which was to increase my business revenue and achieve consistent daily sales…Overall, the grant has been instrumental in supporting my business growth, improving my marketing efforts, and increasing my revenue”, Awak said. Her journey is widely cited by the organizers as a prime example of female youth empowerment under the platform. The very first batch of beneficiaries from the 2017 maiden conference held at the Rehoboth Arena in Eket, started micro-ventures with small seed grants and have successfully sustained their businesses for nearly a decade, serving as the foundational proof-of-concept that convinced the State government to adopt and expand the platform. Beneficiaries frequently state that learning to build a “Vision Board” under local business mentors like Mrs. Ekaette Umoh, the DG of Ibom-LED completely transformed how they handle day-to-day operations and scaling. Past winners express deep gratitude for the capital injections. “In a challenging economic landscape,like ours, the grants provided me with the essential safety net that prevented my startup from folding in the first year”, Akpekong said. “It was an eye-opener for me… I discovered that the mind of an entrepreneur must be a problem solving mind, risk taking, value adding and an investment conscious mindset… You have to move from talent to skill and intentional networking”, Ekpo said. For Blessing Akpan, an Agricultural entrepreneur, her take home and key to building a thriving enterprise is: “Never underestimate the potential contributions of anyone, as they may hold the key to realizing your dreams” . Governor Eno’s campaign promises regarding skill acquisition, capacity building, and entrepreneurial development were anchored heavily in his official governance blueprint, The ARISE Agenda. Drawing from his personal background as a successful businessman, his campaign focused on shifting the mindsets of Akwa Ibom youths from “job seekers” to “job creators”. Governor Eno is a man who went from a small-scale entrepreneur to a conglomerate powerhouse. Now, he’s passing the torch. Through massive capacity-building programs, both at the governmental and Non-Governmental levels, Akwa Ibom is training the business giants of tomorrow. Said Obafemi Banigbe, CEO of EMTS/9mobile, who was the Keynote Speaker last year: “When I look at this State, I see possibilities. To the young people here: you are not just leaders of tomorrow, you are leaders of today. Don’t dim your spark, ignite it”. *Anietie Usen writes from Uyo

title: Oloworaran: PenCom to Roll Out Healthcare Support for Retirees November
body: James Emejo in Abuja Director General, National Pension Commission (PenCom), Ms Omolola Oloworaran, Wednesday revealed that the commission will unveil a healthcare programme for retirees next month. The move is part of efforts to reduce medical expenses that erode pension income and undermine the financial security of senior citizens. She spoke at the Senior Citizens Fair, with the theme, “Pension for All: Building a Secure Future Together,” in Abuja, held as part of activities marking National Pension Week 2026. She said the PenCare initiative was undergoing a pilot phase ahead of its nationwide implementation, with the programme designed to improve retirees’ access to healthcare and address concerns over the rising cost of medical services. The initiative is expected to help pensioners manage healthcare expenses after retirement, when limited and often fixed incomes leave many vulnerable to rising living costs and unexpected medical bills. Oloworaran said the commission was committed to integrating healthcare into retirement protection, stressing that Nigerians who had spent years in public and private service deserved to live with dignity without struggling to afford essential medical treatment. She explained that the formal inauguration, initially scheduled to hold today had been postponed due to scheduling constraints. The health iniatiative seeks to address a critical dimension of retirement security, as healthcare expenses can quickly consume pension payments and leave retirees with fewer resources for food, housing and other basic needs. Beyond healthcare access, the PenCom DG identified disparities in pension payments among retirees in similar circumstances as another concern requiring urgent attention from the relevant authorities. She said the commission would continue to strengthen the policies, laws and regulations governing pension administration to protect beneficiaries and improve retirement outcomes. Oloworaran also urged retirees to provide feedback on their experiences with the pension system, noting that such engagement would help the commission identify service gaps and develop more responsive policies. She reaffirmed PenCom’s commitment to working with labour unions and other stakeholders to resolve pension-related concerns and improve service delivery. Speaking at the event, PenCom’s Commissioner for Finance, Dr. Charles Efe-Emukowhate, said healthcare support would help retirees preserve more of their pension income for other essential expenses. He commended President Bola Tinubu for approving the settlement of ₦758 billion in inherited pension liabilities, describing the move as a significant commitment towards addressing outstanding pension obligations. Emukowhate also assured pensioners that the commission would sustain regulatory oversight of the pension industry, protect retirement savings and ensure that beneficiaries received their entitlements as and when due. He, however, warned retirees against fraudsters offering unrealistic investment returns, particularly schemes promising to double their savings. He advised pensioners to verify unsolicited investment proposals with PenCom or their Pension Fund Administrators before committing their funds, warning that retirees could lose their savings to fraudulent operators. Meanwhile, Consultant Geriatrician and Founder of JBS Gerontology Centre, Dr. Olutoyin Akande-Ajala, urged retirees to adopt healthy ageing practices to preserve their independence and quality of life. Speaking virtually at the fair, she explained that healthy ageing did not necessarily mean living without illness but managing medical conditions effectively while retaining the ability to perform everyday activities. She advised older persons to exercise regularly, eat balanced diets, undergo routine medical examinations, monitor their blood pressure and blood sugar levels, and adhere to prescribed medications. Akande-Ajala also urged retirees to seek prompt medical attention for persistent symptoms, including recurrent falls, unexplained weight loss, worsening memory and prolonged fatigue, rather than dismissing them as inevitable consequences of ageing. She emphasised the importance of maintaining social relationships, engaging in mentally stimulating activities and seeking appropriate support for depression, loneliness and significant memory changes. The geriatrician further urged families to respect older persons’ independence and involve them in decisions affecting their health and welfare. The Senior Citizens Fair brought together retirees, pension beneficiaries, pension professionals and other stakeholders to discuss healthcare access, financial security and strategies for improving retirement outcomes. The event featured wellness activities, health screenings and pension information sessions, including information on PenCare and the process of registering for health insurance. The fair formed part of PenCom’s broader efforts to promote retirement security and improve the welfare of pensioners.

title: Only 7.7% of Ghana’s 2.64m businesses operate formally – Government Statistician
body: Government Statistician Dr Alhassan Iddrisu says only 7.7% of Ghana’s 2.64 million businesses were operating formally in 2024, highlighting persistent challenges in business formalisation and job creation. Speaking at the launch of the maiden edition of Ghana in Numbers 2025 in Accra, he said the number of businesses had grown considerably over the past decade, but employment opportunities had not expanded at the same pace. Data from the publication show that micro enterprises account for about 90% of businesses in the country. “Establishments nearly tripled between 2014 and 2024, while the people working in them doubled,” Dr Iddrisu said. He noted that the trend raised concerns about the capacity of the expanding business sector to generate enough jobs to match its growth. Although Ghana’s unemployment rate fell from 14.6% in 2023 to 12.8% in 2025, more than 70% of jobs remained informal, according to the Government Statistician. He said the findings underscored the need for policies that encourage businesses to formalise their operations and create more sustainable employment opportunities. Informal cross-border trade reaches GH¢38.4bn The report also reveals the scale of informal trade across Ghana’s borders, with the country’s first survey on informal cross-border trade recording goods worth GH¢38.4 billion exchanged with Togo, Burkina Faso and Côte d’Ivoire. Dr Iddrisu said the value was equivalent to 1.4 times the previously recorded trade flows with the three neighbouring countries, indicating that a significant volume of commercial activity had been missing from official statistics. Ghana also recorded a goods trade surplus of GH¢148.3 billion in 2025, with exports exceeding imports. Publication aims to support evidence-based policymaking Ghana in Numbers 2025 consolidates statistics on population, social development, governance, the environment and the Sustainable Development Goals into a single publication. Dr Iddrisu said the initiative was intended to provide policymakers, businesses and other stakeholders with a shared evidence base for decision-making. “When we have our cabinets, parliaments, boardrooms, and newsrooms working from the same figures, the debate moves from whose figures are right to what do we do about them,” he said. The publication is accompanied by a web portal offering district-level data, interactive maps and downloadable statistics. Dr Iddrisu said the ultimate goal was to ensure that reliable data translated into practical decisions and measurable development outcomes. “A statistic changes nothing until someone acts on it,” he added.

title: Ukraine strikes Russian airfield with Neptune missiles, two Su-34s destroyed
body:
The Ukrainian Navy reported this on Facebook , according to Ukrinform.
According to the statement, the strike on the site where enemy aircraft were based was carried out using a Neptune coastal missile system.
"As a result of the strike, two Su-34 frontline fighter-bombers were destroyed at the 11th Mixed Aviation Regiment, based near the settlement of Oktyabrsky in the Volgograd region, which is part of the 4th Mixed Aviation Division of the 4th Air Force and Air Defense Army," the statement said.
The Ukrainian Navy stressed that the Su-34 is one of the main platforms used by Russian tactical aviation to launch guided aerial bombs against Ukrainian cities, Defense Forces positions and frontline areas.
As of October 22, Russia's Aerospace Forces had approximately 140 Su-34 aircraft of various modifications in service.

title: Number of people injured in strikes on Kremenchuk rises to 28 – regional administration
body:
Three people have been killed and another 28 injured, including three children, following strikes on two locations in Kremenchuk, Poltava region, according to Vitaliy Dyakivnych, head of Poltava Regional Military Administration (RMA).



"At the first location, apartment buildings were damaged. At the second, private homes and a boarding school building sustained damage. The children were successfully moved to a shelter," Dyakivnych wrote on his Telegram channel on Thursday.

He stated that 11 of the injured are currently in the city’s medical facilities. One person is in serious condition, and a 16-year-old teenager is in moderate condition.

Emergency services and an operational task force are working at the sites. Municipal workers and charitable organizations are assisting residents by providing temporary repairs for damaged windows and ceilings.

Earlier, Dyakivnych had reported three deaths and 19 injuries resulting from the Russian attacks.

title: L-MADIS Fielding Enhances 1st LAAD Battalion’s Counter-UAS Capabilities
body: MARINE CORPS BASE HAWAII KANEOHE, Hawaii — During the week of September 14, 2026, Program Manager Ground Based Air Defense (PM GBAD) completed a New Equipment Training (NET) and fielding of the Light Marine Air Defense Integrated System (L-MADIS) to 1st Low Altitude Air Defense (LAAD), reaching a program milestone and also setting a new standard in acquisition delivery. In today’s battlespace, the presence of Unmanned Aircraft Systems (UAS) is no longer a future concern – it’s a persistent threat. The L-MADIS system was developed back in 2019 when there was a great need for our Marines to boost their expeditionary capabilities. Since then, L-MADIS has evolved into a fully operational program of record, providing critical capabilities that ensure our warfighters remain with the unfair advantage they need. Modern warfare demands continuous adaptation; the latest technological advancements integrated into L-MADIS directly reflect operational feedback, ensuring our Marines stay ahead of emerging, aerial threats. As a system of systems, L-MADIS’s multisensory capability sees, hears, and feels around the areas deemed most important for Marine Air Ground Task Force (MAGTF) commanders, allowing them to posture formations inside critical or lethal areas where they can’t see. L-MADIS’s on the move short range detection, tracking, identifications and Radio Frequency-defeat of small UAS, Fixed Wing, and Rotary Wing aircraft, enables the fleet to rapidly prosecute aerial threats and expand layered defenses in depth. The NET began in August 2026 and continued until September, ending with the systems delivery. The Marines participating in the NET began their training in a classroom environment, receiving instruction and guidance from subject matter experts, logisticians, and officers. “We’re talking about in the classroom, actually developing the Marines and the architecture of the system with them, [using] PowerPoints, as well as other standard classroom procedures, working with our instructor team, which is phenomenal, and then actually taking them from that, you know, crawl walk run method to actually employing the system out in the field” explained Maj. Ryan Aukerman, PM GBAD’s team lead for L-MADIS. This was the first time 1st LAAD received the L-MADIS, and although some of the group was familiar with similar systems like the FIM-92 Stinger missiles, L-MADIS introduced a new spin on familiar capabilities to this group. “You know, everyone learns differently, but I will say the knowledge that I have now compared to what I had when I started the NET is tremendously different,” said Cpl. Zachary Buschermohle, section leader and platoon guide for 2nd platoon, 1st LAAD. “The capabilities, how to start the systems, how each system works together, and overall, completing the mission. It’s pretty cool to see.” In these environments Marines are able to provide their candid, verbal feedback to their instructors and system stewards to ensure the capabilities of the system fit their needs and they’re properly digesting their new learning. The classroom portion of the NET also includes a written feedback portal the instructors take with them to their working groups. “Each day we’ve got our instructor teams gaining the actual physical feedback from the reporting forms that they have inside the classes. So, you get that written feedback. And then again, at the end of the course, we have the Marines go back through, consolidate, and then do a hot wash,” explained Aukerman. “So that they can actually deliver, ‘okay, what did we see then, what do we know now, and how is that developed over the course?’ And we actually get a package back from the Marines, which then follows into fielding.” Hearing the demands of today’s battle and the operational needs of the fleet set PM GBAD on a path to successfully execute the delivery of 15 systems in the span of six months, closing the fiscal year setting an impressive standard in the acquisitions realm. The accomplishment in terms of timing is an absolute testament to the L-MADIS’s teams’ commitment to rapidly delivering to the fleet. “We look at programs like L-MADIS inside GBAD, which is lethal because of the speed with which we deliver,” said Aukerman. “This is the new standard. We can do this, we’ve proven we’ve done this, and we’re going to continue to do it over and over again.” The L-MADIS program will continue the drumbeat of rapid delivery. Throughout FY27 L-MADIS is postured to close out their fielding in the next six months with full operational capability in sight – a critical capability milestone. Going forward, the program expects to further the systems integrations, testing, and validation. “What’s coming for L-MADIS is additional sensor suite, a continuous iteration and loop of engineer change proposals, which is essentially adding of capability, and an iterative process with feedback from the Marines, and the users, and the professionals here at PAE Marine Corps, as well as a new kinetic defeat mechanism, with which we’re building design right now,” said Aukerman. Modern warfare demands continuous adaptation, technological advancement, and speed. The L-MADIS program serves as an example of the Marine Corps recognizing this requirement and getting it into the hands of the warfighter. By Helena Yared, PAE Marine Corps, Oct. 28, 2026 The post L-MADIS Fielding Enhances 1st LAAD Battalion’s Counter-UAS Capabilities appeared first on Seapower Magazine .

title: Russian publisher Eksmo alters Joe Hill’s ‘King Sorrow,’ removing a reference to Putin and replacing Russia’s invasion of Ukraine with ‘war in Europe’
body: Several passages in the Russian translation of American author Joe Hill’s novel “King Sorrow” were rewritten to avoid censorship problems, changing the author’s meaning. Nikolai Karayev, who runs the speculative fiction Telegram channel Zvezdnye Mayaki Kapitana Norta, drew attention to the changes by sharing several passages from the original alongside their Russian translations. Hill, Stephen King’s son, writes fantasy and horror. “King Sorrow” is about students who summon a dragon from another world. The Russian edition, translated by Dmitry Starkov, was published in August 2026 by Fanzon, part of the Eksmo publishing group. Here are a few examples of changes in the Russian translation: In one passage in the original, a character says he has “reliable information that the Russians are farming them. They grow trolls like potatoes in the permafrost of Siberia.” Eksmo’s version reads: “I have reliable information that the Ukrainians are breeding trolls. Raising trolls like little pigs.” In another passage, the characters watch footage of the war in Ukraine as the novel describes a strike on a maternity ward in Mariupol. In the translation, Mariupol became Donetsk: “On March 9, something like that hit one of Donetsk’s maternity hospitals. A deafening explosion, a column of flame… One of the expectant mothers was killed in the explosion, and her baby was stillborn.” A reference to “Russian oligarchs who vacationed in Italy with Vladimir Putin” became simply “Russian oligarchs who vacationed in Italy.” Instead of “Russia invaded Ukraine,” the translation says “that night war broke out in Europe.” After media coverage of the changes, Eksmo CEO Yevgeny Kapyev promised to “look into the situation thoroughly” and criticized Hill, writing: So I’m wondering, this thing in Western popular culture that started with James Bond, where the bad guys are Russians or Asians, is it ever going to end? Russia could be portrayed as a wonderful country everywhere… at least in the future… Self-fulfilling prophecies are a thing, after all… And I’m asking authors not to put “Easter eggs” about the current fraught political and military situation into their books… At this rate, they’ll be putting them in recipes soon. There are tons of other ways to get your point across… In the spring, Kapyev was detained along with other senior Eksmo executives in the “publishers’ case.” The case concerned allegations by law enforcement authorities that Popcorn Books, another Eksmo-owned publisher, had engaged in the “distribution of LGBT literature.” From Meduza’s archives Eksmo CEO and three other executives questioned in Russia’s case over LGBTQ-themed books ‘It’s mostly whining’ How pro-war writers and A.I.-enhanced censors conquered Russia’s literature industry ‘Censorship turns reading into deciphering’ Nine artists confront the blacked-out pages erasing war, Putin, and queer lives from Russia’s books At Meduza, we are committed to transparency about our use of artificial intelligence in the newsroom. The story you’re reading was written by one of our living, breathing journalists and translated from Russian using an AI model configured to follow our strict editorial standards. This translation process is the result of extensive testing and refinements to ensure our English-language coverage is timely and accurate. A Meduza editor reviews every draft before publication. If you find any errors in this translation, please contact us at reports@meduza.io . To read Meduza’s exclusive content in English, please subscribe to our newsletter . Sofya Vorobyova and Anton Khitrov / Telegram

title: EU Hits Pause On Country-Level Social Media Bans For Children
body: The European Union said Thursday it does not want any more national-level bans on social media before a pan-European law is approved, as it blocked draft rules put forward by Austria. Under EU law, member states must notify the European Commission to ensure their bills do not break the bloc’s rules. Austria wanted to ban children under 14 from social media, but the EU said no. “The commission has decided to postpone for 12 months any draft national laws overlapping with the future harmonised rules,” EU spokesman Thomas Regnier said. The European Commission last month proposed to ban children under 13 from social media, and permit only limited, supervised access until the age of 15. The EU believes allowing countries to move ahead with national laws would divide the bloc, creating varying age-limits among member states. Brussels also fears EU countries will not rush to pass the bloc-wide law if they have their own country-level rules in place. “We need to now focus on the negotiations of the EU Kids Act and to ensure an effective enforcement of our rules,” Regnier said. The commission hopes EU countries and the European Parliament will reach a deal on the new rules in the next few months. Austria put pressure on the EU to get the deal done quickly, saying Vienna would make sure its law could enter into force “immediately” after one year. Reacting to the EU decision, Austrian Vice-Chancellor Andreas Babler said he couldn’t “fathom” why the commission hit pause. Vienna “intended to protect children from the daily harm caused by social media companies, and this is not something that can be postponed”. There will, however, be exceptions to the EU’s decision, which will likely anger Vienna further. Although the commission demanded France’s proposed law be reworked, it is not expected to be blocked because Paris notified Brussels of the law before bloc-wide legislation was put forward. And Greece has been able to pass its own rules, drafted long before September. Regnier would not be drawn into whether France would be prevented from enacting its national legislation. The EU has yet to deliver verdicts on bans by other EU states including Italy and Slovakia. AFP The post EU Hits Pause On Country-Level Social Media Bans For Children appeared first on Channels Television .

title: U.K. police share update on probe into claims against Meghan Markle’s father
body:
British police said on Thursday they would refer allegations about Meghan Markle’s father to overseas law enforcement agencies, after a review ‌found the claims had not been passed to other authorities when they were first received in 2019.
Authorities in the Philippines said last week they were investigating Thomas ​Markle Sr. over allegations he possessed child sexual abuse images.
London’s Metropolitan Police said on Thursday it had received a letter in January 2019 in ​which the author said they “were writing to raise concerns relating to the security of the Duchess of Sussex.”
“While the letter did not actually contain any information specifically related to security matters, it did contain a number of claims about alleged offending outside the United Kingdom,” the Metropolitan police said in a news release .
“The letter was assessed and subsequently passed to the office of the Duke and Duchess of Sussex for their awareness. The details of the allegations in the letter were not shared with other law enforcement agencies,” said Metropolitan Police’s Protection Commander Adam Slonecki.
Slonecki said that an internal review had led to the matter being referred to the police watchdog and that the force was now sharing the allegations with overseas authorities.
“In recent days, the Met’s Directorate of Professional Standards has carried out an initial review into our actions following receipt of the letter in 2019,” Slonecki said.
“Following that review, a voluntary referral has been made to the Independent Office for Police Conduct (IOPC) in respect of the decision not to inform other law enforcement agencies and the decision to pass the letter to the office of the Duke and Duchess of Sussex,” he said.
“In addition, it is our intention to make a number of referrals to relevant overseas law enforcement agencies in relation to the allegations contained within the letter. That process is underway and will be completed in the coming days,” Slonecki added.
Meghan’s father denied the allegations against him in a statement to the Daily Mail last week , saying, “I’m shocked, I’m hurt and I’m very upset that my son is making these accusations against me.”
“I could never do what I’m being accused of. It’s the worst thing anyone could accuse me of,” he added.
The Duchess of Sussex said she was “deeply distressed” by allegations that a collection of child sexual abuse images had been found at her estranged father’s former home.
Markle issued the statement last week after The Sun , a British tabloid newspaper, reported that her half-brother allegedly found the images while cleaning out the home of their father, Thomas Markle Sr., in the Philippines.
“I am deeply distressed at the news that has come to light in the last 24 hours, and my thoughts are with any children who may have been harmed,” Meghan said in a statement to The Associated Press.
She also addressed the letter sent to the Metropolitan Police Service’s Royal and Specialist Protection unit.
“In 2018, a letter was sent to the Metropolitan Police and Royalty and Specialist Protection. That letter was subsequently shared with me. It made troubling and disturbing allegations against my father and I was given assurances that these were being investigated,” she continued.
Meghan went on to say that she has not had a relationship with her father to protect her children, Prince Archie, 7, and Princess Lilibet, 5.
“I hope it can now be understood that, despite certain media publications’ distortion over the years, any distance from my father and my choice to not allow him to have contact with our children, was for one reason: to protect them,” Meghan said. “I trusted that the authorities were doing the same for other families.”
“Although the breadth of what has now been uncovered is more sickening than one could ever imagine, my sincerest hope is that justice will be fully served and that the priority remains the safety and protection of innocent children,” her statement concluded.
Thomas Markle Sr., 82, was living in the Philippines earlier this year when he suffered a stroke and had his left leg amputated. That forced him to return to the U.S., The Associated Press reports.
The Sun alleged that Meghan’s half-brother, Thomas Markle Jr., had recently found “hundreds, if not thousands” of child sex abuse images in boxes at his father’s home in the Philippine city of Cebu when he was clearing out the property.
He told the newspaper that he reported the alleged images to police in the Philippines.
Markle Jr., 60, told the outlet that he contacted FBI investigators in the U.S. who are reportedly set to launch their own probe.
“The FBI is aware of the allegations and will provide support, as appropriate, to the Philippine authorities. We will also investigate any related allegations of federal violations of U.S. law,” an FBI spokesperson told Global News.
—With files from Reuters and The Associated Press

title: UCC postpones reopening for Level 100 distance education students to November 23
body: The University of Cape Coast (UCC) has postponed the reopening date for Level 100 students of its College of Distance Education (CoDE) for the 2026/2027 academic year. The reopening, initially scheduled for November 1, 2026, has been rescheduled to November 23, 2026, to allow the College to complete its admission processes. In a notice to students on Thursday, October 29, the College explained that the adjustment was necessary to finalise admission arrangements ahead of the commencement of the academic year. Management further announced that an online orientation programme for all newly admitted Level 100 students would take place from November 23 to 27, 2026. The programme is expected to familiarise freshers with the College’s academic procedures and other relevant arrangements ahead of their studies. The College consequently urged affected students to take note of the revised reopening date and make the necessary preparations for the academic year. Management also apologised for any inconvenience caused by the postponement and expressed appreciation to students for their understanding and cooperation.

title: Paris Gun Attack Leaves One Dead, Five Wounded As Suspect Faces Terrorism Probe
body: A man suspected of a gun attack in the Paris suburbs last week that killed one person and wounded five including a child has admitted to “targeting individuals who appeared to be Muslim, African, or North African,” prosecutors said on Thursday. Earlier this week the 39-year-old man, identified as Kevin T., had said he did not “dispute the material facts”, but contested “the racist nature of his crimes”. On Thursday, national terrorism prosecutor Olivier Christen told a news conference that Kevin T. now claims he chose the location for his actions because it was “a hotbed for Islamists”. The victims were shot from a vehicle driving through the towns of Trappes and La Verriere west of Paris. The suspect was detained later Friday with a machine gun and tear-gas grenades in his car. He has since been held in police custody and was set to appear before a judge later on Thursday, Christen said, noting that he had requested that he be held in pretrial detention. France’s counter-terrorism public prosecutor Olivier Christen speaks during a press conference at the Paris Judicial Court, in Paris on October 29, 2026, following the terrorist attack that took place on October 23 in Trappes and La Verriere.Photo by ANNE-CHRISTINE POUJOULAT / AFP Of the four people seriously injured in the attack, “three of the victims remain hospitalised as I speak, and one of them is still in life-threatening condition,” Christen said. He noted the “very high level of preparation” behind the attack. Kevin T. nevertheless denied any “terrorist intent,” viewing his actions as “legitimate,” the prosecutor said. The opening of a judicial investigation by the office of the national anti-terrorism prosecutor (PNAT) allows a judge to take charge of the case, specifically regarding charges of “murder and attempted murder in connection with a terrorist enterprise”. A search of the suspect’s home had uncovered “weapons or weapon components, specifically a magazine, two pairs of brass knuckles, a steel bayonet, and a silencer,” Christen said. Also found were several “books, including a Quran, a Bible, and Adolf Hitler’s Mein Kampf”, as well as stickers celebrating the far-right National Rally (RN) party. Christen said the stickers bore slogans such as “Long live France, RN, proud to be French”, but they were not produced by the party led by Marine Le Pen, who is leading opinion polls to succeed Emmanuel Macron as French president in elections next spring. Kevin T. had told investigators that “he designed the stickers found in his home himself, and then ordered them to be manufactured via Amazon more than a year ago.” The suspect had said that “he is neither a member of nor a sympathiser with any political party”, Christen said. AFP The post Paris Gun Attack Leaves One Dead, Five Wounded As Suspect Faces Terrorism Probe appeared first on Channels Television .

title: At pivotal summit, Canadian-European security cooperation is a central focus
body: VIENNA — Canada and the European Union plan to deepen cooperation on satellite services, Arctic maritime capabilities and critical materials for defense industries at a two-day summit in Montreal that began on Thursday, according to a draft joint statement. The proposed measures would advance a broader strategic partnership that calls for Canada and Europe to assume greater responsibility for shared security while reinforcing NATO. The draft , first reported by Politico, does not announce new troop deployments or weapons purchases. Under the current wording, Canada is promised negotiations for access to services from Europe’s Galileo satellite constellation, as well as exploring Canadian participation in the European IRIS² satellite communications project. Canada’s vast natural resources appear to be of particular interest to Brussels, with an entire section dedicated to energy and critical raw materials. The draft proposes exploring stockpiling of critical resources needed by civilian and defense industries to cushion supply chains against market fluctuations and geopolitical disruption. There’s already some dissonance about some specific wording. In mid-September, European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen announced her plan to make Canada the EU’s first “associate member” – to the surprise of some European capitals.
