title: Iran cancels execution for woman who 'filmed burning shop' during protests
body: A woman condemned to death in Iran for what supporters say was nothing more than filming a burning shop during protests has had her sentence overturned by the Supreme Court. Prosecutors had claimed Leila Abolhasani, 43, was involved in setting the shop on fire during anti-regime protests in January that were met with a violent crackdown. Ms Abolhasani, a nail technician with two children, was arrested in the city of Shahin Shahr, becoming one of an estimated 25,000 to 50,000 people detained in Iran during the protests. She was found guilty of moharebeh, or enmity against God, and sentenced to death in August. Campaigners outside Iran said she was merely taking videos of the unrest. "When Ms Abolhasani was present at the protest site, one of the Ofogh Kourosh chain stores in Shahin Shahr was burning and she was filming the scene," the organisation Human Rights Activists in Iran quoted a source close to her family as saying. It said she had been held at a prison in Isfahan. On Thursday, however, it reported that the Supreme Court had overturned her sentence and sent the case back to a lower court for retrial, in a rare victory for campaigners. Activists say no court ruling or evidence has been made public. Iran has executed at least 34 people in cases linked to the January protests, Amnesty International said this month. Others have been put to death on espionage charges during the US and Israeli war on Iran . A UN-backed fact-finding mission said last month that the response to the protests amounted to crimes against humanity. The unrest began in late 2025, triggered by high prices and the weakness of Iran's currency, before broadening into one of the biggest anti-regime revolts since the 1979 revolution. Government personnel responded by firing into crowds from rooftops, trapping demonstrators in alleys with tear gas and carrying out killings in all 31 provinces of Iran, the UN mission said.

title: USS Washington Undocks at Portsmouth Naval Shipyard on Schedule
body: PORTSMOUTH NAVAL SHIPYARD, Maine — The Virginia-class attack submarine USS Washington (SSN 787) was successfully undocked on schedule Oct. 27, marking a major milestone in its scheduled maintenance and modernization availability moving the Washington into its next phase of operational testing. Completion of a submarine’s docking period is a critical first step in its return to the fleet and directly supports the Navy’s focus on combat-ready platforms, increasing operational availability and contributing to credible, sustained deterrence. “Washington’s undocking is an achievement that represents a coordinated effort across the shipyard to return a renewed and combat-ready submarine back to the fleet,” said Capt. Jesse Nice, shipyard commander. “This team overcame every obstacle through our traditional shipyard grit combined with cutting-edge deckplate innovations led by our expert tradespeople. Today, we stand taller, tougher, and poised for the next phase to preserve the Navy’s mandate to build and maintain combat-ready forces.” Washington has undergone extensive mechanical and electrical system upgrades, scheduled maintenance, and structural inspections utilizing deckplate innovation such as additive manufacturing. This comprehensive overhaul enhances the submarine’s capabilities, modernizes critical systems, and equips Sailors — the Navy’s decisive warfighting advantage — with an advanced, reliable platform ready to meet the Navy’s operational demands to deliver peace through strength. “I’m proud of the incredible work done between our crew and the project team, whose exceptional collaboration and vigilance led us to this undocking on time,” said Cmdr. Keith Turnbull, commanding officer, USS Washington (SSN 787). “Through this monumental collective effort, we are laying the groundwork that will ultimately deliver the ‘Blackfish’ as a fully mission-capable, cutting-edge submarine operated by a highly skilled crew that will stand ready to answer our Nation’s call.” As America’s leader for attack submarine maintenance, repair, and modernization, Portsmouth Naval Shipyard delivers the decisive edge required to master an era of evolving threats. It stands at the forefront of America’s commitment to peace through strength, delivering combat-ready submarines that are lethal, resilient, and prepared to win. The work performed at Portsmouth Naval Shipyard directly contributes to national security, ensuring the U.S. Navy remains the most dominant maritime force anywhere in the world. From Alana Demo. Oct. 29, 2026 The post USS Washington Undocks at Portsmouth Naval Shipyard on Schedule appeared first on Seapower Magazine .

title: Avenger Triad 26 assesses command-and-control gaps in large-scale European combat scenario
body: Nearly 100 Joint Modernization Command personnel conducted the assessment during Avenger Triad 26. The wider exercise brought together 2,000 U.S. service members and 2,000 multinational personnel at command posts in France, Germany, the Netherlands and Poland. “I’d say the majority of our insights addressed command and control overmatch,” said Lt. Col. Zachary Quintana, the assessment team lead. “That is a well-defined gap.” The work included Multi-Domain Command–Europe, created at the beginning of 2026, alongside the Theater Strike Effects Group and Theater Information Advantage Detachment. Planners assessed how those formations, their concepts and their technology could improve command and control against an opponent. “We looked at how do these formations, concepts, and capabilities tie to our warfighting gaps, looking to inform the Army on how a particular formation, utilizing a particular technology, can achieve command and control overmatch and give us an advantage against the enemy,” said Maj. Javoria Collier, a JMC experimentation planner. The assessment was guided by the Army’s recently published “How the Army Fights” document. The team also beta-tested an upgraded dashboard designed to connect findings across experiments and give leaders real-time access to assessment information. JMC’s Data Science Solutions Team and Operations Research / Systems Analysis team are developing the tool. “Joint Modernization Command is working alongside Army organizations and joint partners to identify, assess, and help close critical warfighting gaps, ensuring formations are better prepared, more integrated, and ready to succeed against future threats,” said Brig. Gen. Jennifer Mykins, the command’s commander. Findings will be shared with Army modernization organizations and incorporated into further experiments. Quintana said the assessment drew on lessons from Operation Epic Fury in Iran and the Russia-Ukraine conflict. Electronic warfare, space capabilities and protection against unmanned aircraft were among the areas informing the work.

title: Ashanti Regional GJA secures land waiver for proposed press centre
body: The Ashanti Regional Branch of the Ghana Journalists Association (GJA) has secured a waiver on land allocated by Asantehene Otumfuo Osei Tutu II for the proposed Ashanti Press Centre, marking a significant milestone in efforts to establish a permanent office for journalists in the region. Chairman of the association, Kofi Adu Domfeh, announced at the Ashanti Media Excellence Awards 2026, where he called on corporate institutions, development partners, philanthropists and individuals to support the next phase of the project. Mr. Domfeh described the proposed centre as more than a physical structure, indicating it would serve as a hub for professional training, collaboration, media development and the advancement of journalism in the region. He expressed profound gratitude to Otumfuo Osei Tutu II for the gesture and acknowledged Access Bank Ghana and Fidelity Bank Ghana for providing seed capital to support the project’s take-off. However, he noted that additional resources would be required to move the project from planning to construction. He therefore appealed for financial contributions, building materials, technical expertise and other forms of practical assistance to help realise the vision. “The Ashanti Press Centre must become our collective legacy. We invite you to be part of it,” he said. The chairman’s appeal comes at a time when the media landscape is undergoing rapid transformation, driven by digital platforms, artificial intelligence and growing concerns about misinformation and declining public trust. The proposed Ashanti Press Centre is expected to provide a dedicated institutional space to support journalists and strengthen the media profession in the region. Beyond serving as a physical base for the Association, the project is intended to create opportunities for professional development, collaboration and improved journalistic practice. Credibility remains journalism’s greatest asset Additionally, Mr. Domfeh highlighted the importance of credibility, ethical conduct and accountability in journalism. He observed that artificial intelligence was creating new opportunities for research, production and storytelling, while also making it easier to generate fake images, fabricate audio, manipulate videos and circulate misinformation. In such an environment, he argued, credibility would remain the defining difference between professional journalism and the growing volume of online content. “AI can generate content, but journalists must provide verification, context, judgement and accountability,” he said. He urged journalists to embrace technological innovation without compromising accuracy, ethics or the public interest. The GJA Chairman also stressed the importance of credible journalism in addressing challenges confronting communities in the region, including illegal mining, environmental degradation, unemployment, public health concerns and governance deficits. He called on journalists to investigate critical issues, ask difficult questions, amplify neglected voices and hold those in positions of authority accountable.

title: Zamfara First Lady Supports 150 Women Farmers With Inputs, Cash
body: The Zamfara State First Lady, Hajiya Hurriya Dauda Lawal, has provided farm inputs and financial assistance to more than 150 women farmers to boost agricultural production and food security. The support was announced during the 2026 World Food Day celebration organised by the Nigerian Women for Agriculture Progressive Development Initiative (NWAPDI) at the Ministry of Agriculture in Gusau. Hajiya Hurriya commended Governor Dauda Lawal for prioritising the welfare of farmers and supporting efforts to improve agricultural production in the state. She said the initiative was aimed at supporting women farmers to increase food production and contribute to food security. The state coordinator of NWAPDI, Hajiya Shafa’atu Tsafe, urged the beneficiaries to make judicious use of the farm inputs and financial assistance to improve their agricultural output.

title: ‘They’ll expand opportunities for future generations’, Tinubu defends Fresh loans
body: President Bola Ahmed Tinubu has responded to criticism from opposition leaders over the Federal Government efforts to access fresh loans from international institutions and banks. In a piece entitled “From reforms to delivery: Our infrastructure investment and growth strategy”, Tinubu said, “The real question is not how much we borrow, but what we build, what value we create and what future we leave behind.” Tinubu identified the Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway, Sokoto-Badagry Superhighway, Trans-Sahara Superhighway, electricity grid upgrades and the modernisation of key commercial ports in Lagos as major projects expected to strengthen Nigeria’s productive capacity. He said the projects, alongside investments in healthcare, education and vocational training, would connect economic regions, reduce logistics costs, unlock agricultural and industrial potential and attract private investment. According to the piece made available to journalists on Thursday, the Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway is expected to cut logistics costs along its corridor by 15 to 20 per cent. ” It could add up to two per cent to Nigeria’s GDP through expanded trade, tourism, and industrial activity. “The project is also projected to generate about 100,000 direct jobs in construction and engineering, alongside more than 150,000 indirect jobs in logistics, materials and related services.” “We are not simply building highways. We are opening economic corridors, connecting markets, unlocking industries and reshaping Nigeria’s economic geography,” the President said. He said the administration’s ambition to build a $1 trillion economy by 2030 would require sustained infrastructure investment to support higher productivity, industrialisation and trade. “We cannot build a USD 1 trillion economy with infrastructure designed for an economy a fraction of that size,” Tinubu said. He said improving economic indicators and growing international investor confidence are creating opportunities for Nigeria to attract long-term investment and expand critical infrastructure. The President said the economic reforms his administration introduced in May 2023 helped restore macroeconomic stability, strengthen public finances, and improve the country’s standing in international financial markets. He said a $1 trillion economy would not emerge by declaration alone but must be built through sustained investment, higher productivity, industrialisation, and trade, stressing that infrastructure development would be critical to achieving the target by 2030. Tinubu said real Gross Domestic Product growth reached 4.43 per cent in the second quarter of 2026, while headline inflation fell to 14.63 per cent in September from 20.98 per cent a year earlier. He also said gross external reserves rose to $55.1 billion as of October 9, 2026, including about $46 billion in net reserves, while the tax-to-GDP ratio increased to 12.5 per cent from seven per cent. Tinubu said real Gross Domestic Product growth reached 4.43 per cent in the second quarter of 2026, while headline inflation fell to 14.63 per cent in September from 20.98 per cent a year earlier. The President attributed the improvements to measures including petrol subsidy removal, exchange rate unification, tax reforms and coordinated efforts to tackle inflation.

title: Eisenkot accuses Netanyahu of attempting to delegitimize election results
body: Yashar party chairman and opposition bloc leader Gadi Eisenkot accused Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on Thursday of launching an "organized campaign to delegitimize" the results of Tuesday's Knesset election, vowing to prevent any attempt to delay the swearing-in of the new parliament.Eisenkot also pledged to prevent Netanyahu from using the government for his "own personal needs," declaring that those days were over."I will not allow the Knesset's swearing-in to be delayed by even a single centimeter from its scheduled date," Eisenkot said.He added that his team was preparing for a vote when the new Knesset convenes."I intend to act as I always have, calmly and with determination," Eisenkot concluded.Allegations of foreign interference by Qatar in Israel's elections emerged on Thursday, The Jerusalem Post reported.Qatar denies election interference allegations, accuses Israeli figures of disinformationQatari Foreign Ministry spokesperson Majed al-Ansari categorically denied the allegations, accusing Israeli politicians and media figures of conducting a disinformation campaign against Doha."We categorically deny allegations that Qatar has interfered in Israeli elections or funded any activities intended to influence their outcome," he said.In his statement, Eisenkot claimed that Netanyahu and Likud had prepared their statements and briefings in advance, accusing them of attempting to delegitimize the election results because they had lost and lacked a Knesset majority.Shin Bet investigates the allegationsThe Shin Bet (Israel Security Agency) is investigating suspicions that foreign entities, potentially including Qatar and Turkey, funneled money into Israel to influence voter turnout in Arab communities. The investigation follows a directive from Central Elections Committee Chairman Supreme Court Justice Noam Sohlberg to examine allegations of foreign funding and election bribery, the Post reported Thursday. Shin Bet chief David Zini is expected to brief most of Israel's political party leaders on the investigation into suspected foreign interference in Tuesday's Knesset election, having already updated several of them on Thursday. The investigation is expected to conclude in the coming days.The Shin Bet will present its findings to Sohlberg once the investigation is complete.The investigation initially began covertly and progressed to its next stage only after investigators gathered a critical amount of intelligence described as "solid information."The investigation is being conducted in full coordination with Sohlberg and the Central Elections Committee.KAN News reported Thursday, citing a senior Central Elections Committee official, that even if all suspicions of foreign interference were substantiated, the alleged activity would not have been extensive enough to alter the election results.Yair Lapid says election results are not in jeopardy despite interference allegationsFormer prime minister Yair Lapid said Thursday that Israel's election results were not in jeopardy and that nothing would prevent the swearing-in of the new Knesset, following a meeting with Shin Bet chief David Zini at the agency's headquarters."I spoke today with representatives of Justice Sohlberg on the Central Elections Committee and met with Shin Bet chief David Zini," Lapid said, adding that "there is no risk to or challenge to the election results, and there is no obstacle to swearing in the Knesset."Ra'am Chairman Mansour Abbas denied on Thursday allegations that it was involved in an election-interference scheme via Qatar, and apparently backed the launch of an investigation into the matter."Ra'am welcomes the decision of Central Elections Committee Chairman Justice Noam Sohlberg to investigate suspicions of an attempt to improperly influence the elections through foreign funding," said Abbas.President Isaac Herzog called Thursday for a thorough investigation into the election interference allegations, stressing that "election integrity is a supreme democratic value" and that those responsible must be prosecuted to the fullest extent of the law. At the same time, he warned against undermining the legitimacy of the electoral process, saying, "We must avoid tarnishing an entire public that sought to exercise its right to vote and take an active part in democracy."Jonah Davidov, Croinne Baum, Jerusalem Post staff, contributed to this report.

title: Zamfara to Commission Over 70 Projects for 30th Anniversary
body: The Zamfara State Government says it will commission more than 70 completed projects across the state as part of activities marking the 30th anniversary of its creation. The projects cover healthcare, education, infrastructure, commerce, sports, security and public administration. The state was created in 1996. According to a statement issued by the Ministry of Information and Culture on October 20, Governor Dauda Lawal will commission the projects as part of activities marking the anniversary. In the health sector, the projects include the rehabilitation of general hospitals in Gummi, Kasuwar Daji in Kaura Namoda and Shinkafi, as well as the construction and equipping of the General Hospital in Talata Mafara. Others are the rehabilitation of the Women and Children Hospital in Kaura Namoda, including staff quarters, and the remodelling and furnishing of administrative blocks at the Drugs and Medical Consumables Agency. In education, the projects include the renovation of the Smart School in Gusau, construction of a safe school in Anka, and rehabilitation of Government Secondary School, Maru, and Government Science Secondary School, Gusau. The government also listed hostels and a clinic at the College of Education, Maru; hostels at Abdu Gusau Polytechnic, Talata Mafara; and a Faculty of Education, clinic and store at the state university in Talata Mafara. Other projects include classroom and office blocks at the Federal University Gusau, alongside an administrative block and rehabilitated classrooms at the Zamfara College of Arts and Science (ZACAS), Gusau. Under infrastructure and commerce, the government listed the Fanna Bridge, a 300-metre surfaced approach road and the Magami link road. The projects also include the first phase of an ultra-modern market in Gusau, comprising 165 shops, 25 bus stops across the metropolis and parking facilities at the J.B. Yakubu Secretariat Complex. In the sports, recreation and cultural sector, the Sardauna Memorial Stadium in Gusau has been upgraded. Other projects include the rehabilitation of Gusau Amusement Park, construction of a monument sculpture at Gada-Biyu Roundabout, a small city garden and renovation of the Sambo Dan Ashafa Juma’ah Mosque in Yardole. The statement further listed renovation, remodelling and furnishing works at several ministries, departments and agencies, including the Ministry of Information and Culture, Zamfara State AM Radio Station, Ministry of Agriculture, Ministry of Women Affairs, Civil Service Commission and Office of the Auditor-General. Other institutions covered include the Bureau of Statistics, Teaching Service Board, State Pension Board, Hospital Services Management Board, ZAROTA, Ulama’u Council, and state housing and electrification agencies. At Government House in Gusau, the projects include the renovation of chalets and one-bedroom suites, remodelling of the Chief of Staff’s office, rehabilitation and automation of the auditorium conference hall, and renovation of the First Lady’s office and 38 staff offices. The government also listed the construction of a central kitchen, recreational centre and perimeter fence at the Government House. In the security and justice sectors, completed projects include the remodelling of the police command headquarters, construction of an ammunition depot and administrative block at the Nigerian Army Cantonment in Gusau, and rehabilitation of the residence of the 1 Brigade Commander. Other works include the renovation of a High Court judge’s residence, fencing of the Group of Courts and construction of a doctors’ quarters block at the Federal Medical Centre, Gusau. The government said the projects were aimed at improving public service delivery, expanding access to healthcare and education, boosting economic activities and strengthening security. The Commissioner for Information and Culture, Mahmud Muhammad Dantawasa, urged the media and the public to cooperate with the anniversary planning committee. He added that the schedule for the commissioning would be announced later.

title: Trilateral Delegation Arrives Ahead of Oleshky Aid Delivery as Newsmax Observers Draw Scrutiny
body:
A delegation of Ukrainian, US and Russian representatives has arrived at the site from which humanitarian aid will be delivered to Russian-occupied Oleshky on Friday, Oct. 30.
Davyd Arakhamia, who leads President Volodymyr Zelensky’s Servant of the People party in parliament, said on Thursday, Oct. 29 that journalists from all three countries had also reached the location. Their presence, he said, is meant to make the next stage of the humanitarian mission as transparent as possible.
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official .
The truce, which marked a rare instance of de-escalation in Russia’s fifth year of war, initially began clouded by confusion as Chief of the Russian General Staff Valery Gerasimov announced a “silence regime” along the Kherson front beginning Oct. 27 – two days earlier than the Oct. 29 date set by the White House.
Despite fears of possible sabotage that Moscow’s unilateral announcement widely raised, the ceasefire is still holding as no incident has been reported for more than 64 hours.
On Wednesday, Oct. 28 US First Lady Melania Trump, who mediated the agreement, announced that four journalists from the US conservative broadcaster Newsmax would be embedded with Ukrainian and Russian humanitarian officials in Oleshky.
She described them as “neutral observers” who would independently document the mission.
Shortly before, Kremlin’s economic envoy Kirill Dmitriev wrote on X that Russia was welcoming the Newsmax journalists to report firsthand on the mission; a post that Melania Trump shared.
Michael Bociurkiw, a global affairs analyst and senior fellow at the Atlantic Council, questioned the arrangement, as the Newsmax crew essentially represents the American delegation instead of US authorities, who are reportedly not expected on the ground.
54+ hours into the Oleshky ceasefire, the First Lady amplifies Putin envoy Kirill Dmitriev and bills a Newsmax crew as "neutral observers." With no US officials on the ground, that crew is effectively the American presence. The US side is reportedly coordinated by Marc Beckman,… https://t.co/SebejBf2Vr
Dmitriev heads the Russian Direct Investment Fund (RDIF), which the US Treasury sanctioned in 2022, under the previous Biden administration as it is closely connected to Russian President Vladimir Putin.
Since US President Donald Trump struck a diesel arrangement with Putin on Oct. 9, Dmitriev has become not only Moscow’s main economic channel to the Trump administration, but possibly a key negotiator in the ceasefire.
The Trump administration is currently reviewing a request to lift sanctions on the fund, which helped arrange Russian diesel shipments to the US. Only a week prior, US special envoy Steve Witkoff confirmed that the US Treasury was working with Dmitriev directly.
Zelensky said that it was Ukraine’s idea to bring American journalists to the site, citing Kyiv’s distrust of the Russian side.
According to Ukrinform , he did not know which direction residents would choose when leaving. Moving deeper into Russian-occupied territory would be easier due to the routes available, he acknowledged, but many people in Oleshky want to reach Ukrainian-controlled areas.
“I know how technically the evacuation to Ukraine can take place, but I don’t know what will really happen,” Zelensky said.
Ukrainian human rights advocates have warned that Moscow may try to keep part of the population in place.
Oleksandr Pavlichenko, executive director of the Ukrainian Helsinki Human Rights Union, told Ukrainian Radio that Russia sees civilians in frontline Oleshky as a human shield against Ukrainian fire, Ukrinform reported earlier on Thursday, Oct. 29.
According to Pavlichenko, there was no information available yet on whether Russian forces would subject evacuees to filtration, but warned that the risks existed. So far, he said, further details about international observers, including their number and access, remain unclear.
Saving the children from what Ukrainian senior authorities previously called a “death trap” remains a priority.
Petro Andriushchenko, head of the Center for the Study of Occupation, said Russian forces would almost certainly use the truce to move and rotate their units, adding that such activity could also take place on the Ukrainian side of the Dnipro River.
Oleshky, located on the left bank of the Dnipro River in Ukraine’s southern Kherson region, roughly 5 kilometers (3 miles) southeast of Kherson city, has faced severe shortages of food, clean water and medicine for months, with the last food delivery reported on May 26.
According to Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha’s estimates, roughly 1,700 people remain in the city from a prewar population of 24,000, including 47 children.
Ukraine’s human rights commissioner Dmytro Lubinets, who leads the humanitarian operation, earlier said that about 6,000 people, including some 200 children, remain across Oleshky and the surrounding settlements. In his view, up to 2,000 people could remain in Oleshky itself.
However, neither figure could be independently verified, particularly because Russian occupation authorities narrowly restrict access to information from the area.
Lubinets said on Sept. 16 that the residents had started escaping on foot independently across mined fields and under threat of constant Russian drone attacks, simply because they saw no other way out.
Before the truce was officially announced, Pope Leo XIV held a telephone discussion with Russian President Vladimir Putin on Oct. 16, urging him to agree to an immediate ceasefire and allow the delivery of food and medical assistance to the city.
The pontiff then spoke to Zelensky on Monday, Oct. 19, reiterating his earlier request for a humanitarian ceasefire.
On Oct. 20, European Parliament Vice President Pina Picierno declared a hunger strike in protest over the starvation of civilians in Oleshky.
Kyiv Post is Ukraine’s first and oldest English news organization, reporting since 1995. Its international reach – 90% of readers are outside of Ukraine – make it truly Ukraine’s global voice.

title: Beskrestnov: Russia produces more ballistic missiles than the entire world produces Patriot interceptor missiles
body:
Russia is producing ballistic missiles in volumes that exceed the global production capacity for Patriot interceptor missiles, stated Serhiy Beskrestnov (Flash), an advisor to the President of Ukraine on defense technologies.

title: Putin notes specific nature of challenges facing African regions
body:
MOSCOW, October 29. /TASS/. The challenges facing various regions of Africa are unique and specific, yet many of these threats require collective solutions, Russian President Vladimir Putin said following the Russia-Africa summit.
"The challenges encountered by these regions and subregions are unique and specific; however, many regional threats are often universal in nature and require collective solutions," he said.
Putin noted that the summit provided a valuable opportunity for all participants to hear African leaders discuss the pressing issues facing their respective regions - specifically the Sahara, the Sahel, and Northern, Central, and Southern Africa.

title: Zamfara Hails MSF Over Support Against Diphtheria Outbreak
body: The Zamfara State Government has commended Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF) for supporting efforts to contain the diphtheria outbreak in the state. The Commissioner for Health, Dr Nafisa Muhammad Maradun, gave the commendation during a visit to the Infectious Diseases Hospital (IDH) to assess response activities being implemented by MSF. She said collaboration between the state government and development partners was crucial to strengthening the outbreak response, preventing further transmission and ensuring that affected persons received appropriate medical care. The commissioner urged residents to cooperate with response teams and promptly report suspected cases of diphtheria to the nearest health facility for assessment and treatment. She stressed that community participation, early detection and prompt medical attention were essential to controlling the spread of the disease and protecting public health. Maradun reaffirmed the state government’s commitment to working with relevant partners and stakeholders to strengthen disease surveillance, improve case management and protect residents across Zamfara. Also speaking, the Emergency Project Coordinator of NIMERT, Abdoulaye Mahmoudoune, commended the state Ministry of Health and relevant authorities for their support and commitment to improving health outcomes. Mahmoudoune expressed satisfaction with the efforts to contain the outbreak, strengthen disease surveillance and build local capacity to respond effectively to public health emergencies.

title: Six lanes and metro line under fire: Kyiv prepares about $22 million for backup river crossings after Russian strike on Southern Bridge
body: (function(w,q){w[q]=w[q]||[];w[q].push(["_mgc.load"])})(window,"_mgq"); The Ukrainian government has instructed Kyiv to establish alternative routes after Russian attacks stopped traffic on one of the capital’s main bridges. The city authorities will bear the cost of the new crossings, with Kyiv Mayor Vitali Klitschko saying the city needs an additional $22 million. This year, Russia has launched tactics to spread panic among civilians and trigger more people to leave the country. In the latest attack, several Russia's ballistic missiles struck the Southern Bridge, used for vehicle and metro traffic, breaking a huge hole and paralyzing all the pathes. The bridge was closed. Now, there is a fear that more bridges can be targeted this way, dividing Kyiv in two parts. The situation is urgent, as Ukrainian Transport Minister Mykola Kalashnyk says about 600,000 vehicles cross the Dnipro in Kyiv every day. What is Kyiv’s response to the winter terror? According to Klitschko, Kyiv convened the capital’s Defense Council on 28 October to find an answer to this difficult question. The agenda included implementing a project to build combined water crossings over the Dnipro River and access roads to them. “The military command will determine the locations, with approval to be granted, among others, by the Kyiv City Military Administration,” Klitschko said. Under the government’s recommendations, the Kyiv city authorities must find $22 million for the project. Klitschko had previously faced heavy criticism after it emerged that the city lacked sufficient shelters and last winter exposed serious shortcomings in preparing infrastructure for Russian attacks. These included a lack of alternative energy supply routes, poorly distributed energy, burst heating pipes that flooded apartments, and the inability of people with disabilities to reach shelters without elevators. The mayor himself said the problems stemmed from the central government withholding funding, which had stalled numerous energy resilience projects and delayed their implementation. The latest announcement also indicates that Kyiv has once again taken on the financial burden itself. Meanwhile, Ukraine has been working with Japan on backup crossings. Tokyo has already delivered 720 meters of prefabricated bridge structures to Ukraine. The two sides are currently exploring how this equipment could be used to establish alternative crossings. Step two: strengthening existing infrastructure Another option is to reinforce existing bridges. City specialists are developing additional technical solutions to protect bridges across the Dnipro River, Klitschko said in his statement on 27 October, adding that proposals from the military had also been heard. The issue of installing mobile shelters was also raised on the same day, the mayor of Kyiv said in a separate statement on his Telegram channel on 27 October. Despite intensifying Russian attacks and about, as Radio Svoboda reported in its article on 30 September, $11 million set aside in 2025, Kyiv still has only a handful of mobile shelters: LB reported in December 2025 that district tenders failed. Donors paid for the first one at a bus stop, the Kyiv City State Administration said on 15 October. Klitschko raised the issue of shelters again after a court on 12 October ruled that local authorities must urgently install mobile shelters in public areas, including near public transport stops, parks, and squares, according to Kyiv’s Prosecutor’s Office. Russia hits the Southern Bridge again On 2 October, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said in an interview with the Financial Times that Russian ruler Vladimir Putin had ordered the lifting of previous restrictions on airstrikes. Among new targets, according to him, were bridges, data centers, internet, mobile networks, hospitals, kindergartens, schools, and universities. The night of 26–27 October showed what that looks like. Russia launched ballistic missile attacks in a few waves, and the second of them hit the Southern Bridge and the metro infrastructure on it, Klitschko said . The structure carries six lanes of road traffic and two metro tracks. Rescuers work beside a fence pocked by shrapnel in Kyiv after the Russian attacks of 26–27 October 2026. title: Nigerian states record 27% rise in tax revenue – Official
body:
Nigeria recorded a 27 per cent increase in tax revenue collected by 23 states in the first half of 2026, as the government’s new tax regime takes effect and efforts intensify to curb multiple taxation.
The Executive Secretary of the Joint Revenue Board (JRB), Olusegun Adesokan, disclosed this on Wednesday in Abuja, saying the revenue collected by the 23 states between January and June was higher than their earnings in the corresponding period of 2025.
Mr Adesokan said the increase was recorded alongside provisions intended to reduce personal income tax for low- and middle-income earners, arguing that the reforms were designed to improve revenue collection without placing an excessive burden on ordinary Nigerians.
“The vision is to tax prosperity, not poverty. Tax the fruit, not the seed. We should tax returns, not investments,” he said.
According to figures presented by the board, the 23 states generated about N2.2 trillion in the first half of 2026, compared with N1.75 trillion in the same period of 2025.
Mr Adesokan attributed the growth to efforts to improve tax administration, widen the tax base and ensure that those with greater financial capacity contribute appropriately.
He said the board’s data showed that about 92 per cent of income earners in the states covered by the figures were paying lower personal income tax or no personal income tax under the new regime.
The figures cover only the 23 states that submitted returns to the board and do not represent the tax performance of all 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory.
Mr Adesokan also disclosed that 21 states had adopted the model harmonised taxes and levies law developed by the JRB in collaboration with the Presidential Committee on Fiscal Policy and Tax Reforms.
The legislation is intended to address multiple taxation at the subnational level, where businesses and individuals sometimes face overlapping demands from different government authorities.
The framework consolidates more than 100 taxes, levies and charges into nine categories, with the aim of making the system easier to understand and comply with.
“One of the things it addresses is the issue of multiple taxation at the subnational level, and it’s a major problem,” Mr Adesokan said.
“Sometimes, the state government will collect the same thing. So what we have done is we have harmonised all the multiple taxes into just nine.”
He stressed that the reforms were not intended to introduce additional taxes but to simplify existing levies, improve accountability and make revenue administration more consistent across states.
The 21 states that have adopted the framework are Kebbi, Kaduna, Zamfara, Ekiti, Enugu, Abia, Anambra, Gombe, Adamawa, Yobe, Borno, Niger, Plateau, Benue, Kogi, Kwara, Nasarawa, Akwa Ibom, Bayelsa, Delta and Ondo.
The remaining 15 states are yet to adopt the model legislation.
Mr Adesokan said the process required legislative approval and consultations with stakeholders, rather than directives from state governors alone.
He expressed confidence that more states would adopt the framework as implementation progresses.
The Nigeria Tax Act 2025, which took effect on 1 January 2026, introduced a revised personal income tax structure, including an exemption on the first N800,000 of annual taxable income. Higher income bands attract progressively higher rates, up to 25 per cent on taxable income above N50 million.
Mr Adesokan said the changes were intended to leave more money in the hands of eligible low- and middle-income earners while ensuring that higher earners contribute according to their capacity.
He noted that the reforms would be judged not merely by the number of taxes removed or consolidated, but by whether businesses could expand, jobs were created and households experienced improved economic conditions.
“The success of tax reform will continue to be measured not by taxes being removed, but by businesses being able to grow, jobs being created and prosperity being shared,” he said.
The revised system also provides for eligible deductions, including pension contributions and certain housing-related expenses, in calculating taxable income.
The board has urged employers and payroll administrators to apply the new provisions correctly when calculating workers’ tax deductions.
The board is also working with the police and state revenue authorities to curb illegal levies and unauthorised collections along highways and transport routes.
Mr Adesokan said such practices increase the cost of transporting goods, with the additional expenses often passed on to consumers through higher prices for food and other essential commodities.
“You can’t just be stopping and harassing people,” he said, calling for greater use of technology and stronger enforcement against illegal collectors.
He acknowledged that ending the practice would take time because roadside collections had become entrenched in some areas.
The JRB has also announced measures against the sale of revenue stickers and emblems, roadblocks for revenue collection and unauthorised cash payments.
Mr Adesokan urged taxpayers to verify revenue demands with the appropriate authorities and avoid paying money into private accounts or accounts belonging to consultants without proper confirmation.
He said informal-sector traders who qualify for income tax exemptions should not be subjected to income tax demands, although other lawful charges may still apply.
Mr Adesokan said the board was working with the Nigeria Revenue Service (NRS) and state internal revenue services to link existing taxpayer identification records to a national Tax Identification Number system.
The unified system is intended to help revenue authorities verify taxpayers’ records across state boundaries, reduce duplicate documentation and prevent repeated income tax demands arising from poor coordination.
He said taxpayers would be able to retrieve their Tax IDs through designated online platforms using their personal details.
The board said it is also planning joint tax audits involving the NRS and state revenue authorities to reduce repeated inspections and disruptions to businesses.
Mr Adesokan urged Nigerians with complaints about tax administration to seek redress through the appropriate channels, including the Office of the Tax Ombud, which he said provides a free avenue for resolving taxpayer complaints.
The JRB, formerly known as the Joint Tax Board, received an expanded mandate under the Joint Revenue Board (Establishment) Act 2025. Its responsibilities include coordinating tax administration, harmonising taxes and levies, resolving disputes between tax authorities and improving the sharing of tax-related data.
Mr Adesokan said the ultimate test of the reforms would be whether they improve compliance, reduce the burden on businesses and support economic growth.
He added that the government’s objective was to build a tax system that is fair, equitable, accountable and transparent, without imposing demands beyond what taxpayers can reasonably bear.

title: Zamfara Inducts 632 Newly Recruited Nurses, Midwives
body: The Zamfara State Hospital Services Management Board (HSMB) has organised a three-day induction programme for 632 newly recruited nurses and midwives as part of efforts to strengthen the healthcare workforce and improve service delivery. The programme was designed to familiarise the new health workers with the policies, regulations, professional ethics and operational procedures guiding healthcare delivery in public hospitals. Speaking at the event, the Executive Secretary of the board, Alhaji Mustapha Abdulkadir Marafa, commended Governor Dauda Lawal for his commitment to revitalising the health sector, particularly through the recruitment of additional personnel to address manpower shortages in public health facilities. Marafa described the recruitment of 632 nurses and midwives as a significant step towards strengthening the existing workforce and improving the quality of healthcare services across the state. He said the recruitment would help ensure that patients received timely and professional medical attention. The executive secretary urged the newly recruited health workers to demonstrate dedication, discipline, compassion and professionalism in the discharge of their duties. He also advised them to apply the knowledge and skills acquired during the induction programme to their daily responsibilities. The three-day programme featured sessions on professional conduct, hospital administration, patient care, infection prevention and control, teamwork and other essential aspects of effective healthcare delivery.

title: Syria hands life sentence to Jerusalem Brigades terrorist linked with IRGC, state media announces
body: A Syrian court sentenced Abdul Jabbar Ghazi Arziq to life imprisonment after convicting him of joining an armed group affiliated with Liwa al-Quds, aka Jerusalem Brigades, a predominantly Palestinian militia that supported the Assad regime and has been linked to Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC), Syrian state media reported on Wednesday.Jerusalem Brigades members were largely recruited from the Bab an-Nayrab Palestinian Refugee Camp, east of Aleppo. According to the think tank Foundation for Defense of Democracies, the group has light arms, mortars, and short-range rockets, as well as close connections to both the Popular Front for the Liberation of Palestine (PFLP) and the IRGC.In April 2023, Jerusalem Brigades claimed responsibility for the multiple rockets launched from Syrian territory toward the southern part of the Golan Heights, targeting the Israeli towns of Netur and Avni Eitan, according to the Hezbollah-affiliated Al Mayadeen network in Lebanon.The courts found that the group had aimed to incite civil war, promote sectarian violence, and seize cities, classifying the acts as war crimes and crimes against humanity, given the human rights abuses of the Assad regime.Life sentence due to gravity of acts, threat to civilians, lawyer saysLawyer Radif Mustafa, director of the Accountability and Justice Department at the National Commission for Transitional Justice, told the Syrian Arab News Agency [SANA] on Wednesday that the gravity of the acts and the threat they posed to civilians and social peace were among the considerations underpinning Azriq's life sentence.The court rejected the defendant's claim for mitigating circumstances and ruled that he would not be eligible for a general or a special amnesty in the future.Mustafa told SANA that the ruling confirmed that political changes or changing circumstances would not erase crimes, adding that more will be done to ensure victims of the Assad regime receive justice.

title: Carney says Cleveland-Cliffs making ‘mistake’ by not respecting obligations
body:
Prime Minister Mark Carney said Thursday that Cleveland-Cliffs would be making a “mistake” by not respecting its obligations and commitments, as the U.S.-based owner of Stelco faces potential legal action from the federal government over their laying off of up to 500 Canadian steelworkers.
The comments came at an event in Ottawa when Carney was asked by a reporter if, given what has transpired in recent weeks, the federal government felt it was a mistake to allow Cleveland-Cliffs to acquire Stelco in 2024.
“The mistake here would be Cleveland-Cliffs not respecting the obligations, the commitments that they made in the acquisition,” Carney said in response.
The agreement from 2024, of which only a summary has been shared publicly, includes several legally binding commitments Cleveland-Cliffs and Stelco must maintain, including for employment to be at or above levels measured at the time the agreement was created until 2029.
When pressed for more on Thursday, Carney declined to comment further because there is now a legal process heading before the courts. He added that he would reserve his comments for “some other time.”
This comes just hours after Global News obtained a letter, dated Oct. 29, from Industry Minister Mélanie Joly and addressed to Stelco’s president, Paul Simon. In the letter, Joly said she expects a “concrete and credible plan for re-engagement with these workers.”
While arguing the company has not broken its agreement with the federal government, Cleveland-Cliffs has also argued they “should not be responsible for impacts of external factors beyond their control,” including U.S. tariffs on Canadian steel.
Speaking to reporters Thursday, Joly reiterated that Cleveland-Cliffs and its CEO, Lourenco Goncalves, have actively supported the U.S. tariffs and must “face the consequences” they have on the Canadian market.
Joly said she reviewed an interim compliance report that was provided by Stelco on Oct. 26 but said the report was “far from satisfactory.”
“It does not alter my belief that Stelco and Cleveland-Cliffs are not in compliance with their undertakings under the Investment Canada Act as set out in my October 22 section 39 demand,” she said in the most recent letter.
According to the union representing Stelco’s laid-off workers, about 175 have been let go so far, but an internal memo said that could increase to about 500.
Separately, Cleveland-Cliffs CEO Lourenco Goncalves reportedly told The Canadian Press Wednesday that laid off Stelco workers could be recalled by the holidays provided sales of Canadian steel increase.
“It will depend on Canadian customers buying Canadian steel, made by Stelco,” he said in a statement, adding: “If our plan works, my intention is to call back all the 175 workers before Christmas.”
– with files from Global’s Rachel Morgan, Mackenzie Gray and The Canadian Press

title: Air Force again requires flu vaccine for select personnel
body: The Air Force restored the annual influenza vaccine mandate for select personnel once again, following the service’s exception request from the Pentagon’s optional policy. The flu vaccine is a requirement for all active duty, reserve components and civilian personnel of the Department of the Air Force that fall under certain designated categories, according to a memo signed last week by the Assistant Secretary for Manpower and Reserve Affairs Richard Anderson. For those required to vaccinate, the department lists recruits, training populations and congregate living; rapid deployment forces and “no-fail” missions; deployed forces; healthcare personnel; civilian personnel in child services programs; and Air Mobility Command aircrew in support of transportation taskings and en route care as well as executive airlift personnel. “While the influenza vaccination is voluntary for the broader military and civilian populations, the annual vaccination remains a readiness requirement for Airmen and Guardians, as well as designated civilian personnel, within the following six specific categories,” an attachment to the memo reads. Failure to comply with the requirement as a service member within the designated populations can result in administrative or disciplinary action under the Uniform Code of Military Justice, the memo says. Effective immediately, recruits, healthcare and child center personnel are required to be vaccinated, while deploying forces will adhere to pre-deployment timelines, per the guidance. Other personnel included in the policy must be vaccinated no later than Dec. 15 annually. The memo first circulated on social media on the unofficial Air Force amn/nco/snco Facebook page. An Air Force spokesperson confirmed its authenticity to Military Times. Both military and civilian personnel can submit religious accommodation and medical exemption requests. If requests are denied, personnel have an opportunity to comply with the vaccination requirements. The updated guidance comes six months after Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth scrapped the flu vaccine requirement, calling it “overly broad and not rational,” and instead opted to make it optional. Two months later, nearly 300 trainees at Lackland Air Force Base, Texas, contracted the flu, resulting in four hospitalizations and one death. Following the Pentagon’s optional policy, military services expressed the desire for exemptions. The Under Secretary of Personnel and Readiness Anthony Tata granted the exceptions to policy, or ETPs, to the Department of the Army, Department of the Navy, Department of the Air Force, National Security Agency and Defense Health Agency. Since the Marine Corps and Space Force are under the Department of the Navy and Department of the Air Force, respectively, they are also included in the policy exceptions. Although the Air Force initially declined to say when the ETP was granted, the recent memo lists June 11, during the time there was the localized outbreak at Lackland. “The DAF requested an exemption to the voluntary policy to protect mission-critical and high-risk populations,” the memo’s attachment says. “The mandatory vaccination for these select groups [is] deemed essential to preserve force readiness, prevent illness, minimize lost duty days, and ensure the successful execution of DAF missions.” Service members and civilian personnel who are deployed for longer than 30 consecutive days to the U.S. Central Command area of responsibility are required to get the annual flu vaccine as well, according to a separate memo circulating on the unofficial Air Force amn/nco/snco Facebook page, signed by Tata late last month.
