title: Can inertial navigation make ground-robot swarms real?
body: Two startups, working together for just under a week, may have found a way around the biggest obstacle to deploying swarms of ground robots: the need for GPS-free navigation in a small package. Swarmbotics AI, which makes 100-pound autonomous robots, is teaming up with TERN, whose navigation software doesn’t need GPS, the companies announced Wednesday. The Army has been seeking alternatives to the spoofable, jammable satellite-based system for years. “The current environment has taught us that GPS is the first thing that gets canned on the battle space,” William Shuart, a program manager for the Army’s Pathfinder3D program, told Army magazine in January. So the service is fielding jam-resistant GPS cards for munitions and is also working on ALTNAV , which uses a different satellite constellation. But its plans for a robot-forward ground force require a position-navigation-timing system that can get by without a satellite signal at all. The self-driving car industry, with its reliance on GPS and unstealthy LiDAR, hasn’t been much help. Enter TERN, whose PNT system needs no signals from space, and Swarmbotics AI, an Arizona robotics company whose four-wheeled FireAnts fit roughly into a two-foot cube. “Our teams integrated the TERN system on site here in Phoenix into the FireAnt in less than a week, which I think is really impressive. So we went from never having really spoken to these guys on a technical level at least to having the system fielded in a week,” said Drew Watson , co-founder and CTO of Swarmbotics AI . TERN’s Independently Derived Positioning System, or IDPS, combines input from the vehicle’s own sensors, including “wheel speed, steering angle, and 3D motion data,” with onboard map data. “We’re using the motion of that vehicle all the way down to something as as compact as a FireAnt, and through that successive motion, we're able to output latitude and longitude at the same rate that GPS could, or twice a second,” said Shaun Moore , co-founder and CEO of TERN . Next up: sharing that information, which Watson described as “a building block to something else.” The team wants to move toward coordinated swarm maneuvering, with teams of robots sharing data with one another in a mesh network. If each member of the swarm understands where it is and where its teammates are, that data can add value to other sensor data, such as camera or radar feeds about threats. “The way that's working is that each one of these FireAnts is giving a line of bearing to an enemy tank, for instance. Those are triangulated into a position of that enemy tank via multiple firings. The quality of that identification, the position of that enemy tank, is based on the position of the firings…It improves the automatic target recognition,” said Watson. Both companies have already drawn Army attention. TERN received a $11.26 million contract in September, and both have participated in the service’s Operation Jailbreak tech demonstrations. ]]>

title: Day of mourning declared in Chernihiv for Oct 30 following Russian strikes
body:
Friday, October 30, has been declared a day of mourning in Chernihiv for city residents killed in Russian strikes between October 21 and October 29.
According to Chernihiv City Council website, the corresponding order was signed on Thursday by Viktor Geraschenko, Deputy Head of Chernihiv City Administration.
"As a sign of grief for those who have died, the State Flag of Ukraine, adorned with a black ribbon, shall be flown at half-mast on the buildings and facilities of state executive authorities, local self-government bodies, as well as enterprises, institutions, and organizations throughout the city. Entertainment and concert events within the city are to be restricted, and the playing of entertainment music in markets, retail establishments, restaurants, and on public transport is prohibited," the document states.
It is reported that on October 21, a 61-year-old man was killed in a Russian strike on Chernihiv. On October 23, a 68-year-old man died following an attack on an enterprise. On October 29, two 15-year-old girls were killed in another Russian strike on the city.
"Chernihiv urban territorial community expresses its sincere condolences to the families and loved ones of those who have died. We share the pain of the families who have lost their dearest ones," the message reads.

title: 2027: David Mark urges ECOWAS to warn FG, INEC against poll crisis
body: By Luminous Jannamike ABUJA – The National Chairman of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), Senator David Mark, has urged the Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS) to warn the Federal Government and the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) against actions that could trigger a crisis over the 2027 general elections. Mark made the appeal in Abuja on Thursday when he received an ECOWAS delegation on a pre-election fact-finding mission, stressing that the credibility of Nigeria’s elections was critical to peace and stability across West Africa. According to a statement by the ADC National Publicity Secretary, Mallam Bolaji Abdullahi, the party said it had raised concerns over INEC’s preparedness, alleged government control of state institutions, including the judiciary, and threats of violence it attributed to the ruling party. Mark said credible elections were essential to preventing electoral conflict. “The best way to prevent conflict, especially in relation to elections, is to ensure that it is free, fair and transparent,” he was quoted as saying. He urged ECOWAS to join the ADC in pressing Nigerian authorities to ensure a credible electoral process. Mark said, “We in the ADC have committed ourselves to the highest standards of peaceful conducts before, during and after the elections. But we need ECOWAS to join us in insisting on a credible election now. “This is why you must tell the Federal Government and the INEC that they must not do anything that could plunge Nigeria into needless crisis. This must form a part of your early warning signals.” The Head of Mission and former Vice-President of Sierra Leone, Mr Victor Bockarie Foh, said the delegation would report the ADC’s concerns, alongside those of other stakeholders, to the regional body. Foh said the mission was assessing Nigeria’s preparedness for the elections and the political atmosphere ahead of the polls, stressing that peace and stability in Nigeria were important to the entire West African region. Other members of the delegation included Francess Piage Alghali, ECOWAS Commissioner for Political Affairs, Peace and Security; Julius Fofanah Sandy, representing the ECOWAS Permanent Representatives’ Committee; and Segrine Mamadou, Head of the Electoral Assistance Division. The post 2027: David Mark urges ECOWAS to warn FG, INEC against poll crisis appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: Billing disputes: LASCOPA recovers N26.2m refund for Ikeja Electric customers
body: .Resolves 528 cases By Olasunkanmi Akoni Lagos State Consumer Protection Agency (LASCOPA) has resolved 528 complaints against Ikeja Electric Distribution Company (IKEDC) and secured credit adjustments and refunds totalling N26,243,758.75 for affected consumers between January and September 2026. The General Manager, LASCOPA Afolabi Solebo, Esq., revealed this on Thursday. Solebo explained that 556 complaints were received against Ikeja Electric during the nine months, with 528 resolved and 28 ongoing, representing about a 95 per cent resolution rate. He reaffirmed the agency’s commitment to promoting fairness, accountability, transparency and improved service delivery in the electricity distribution sector. According to Solebo, the agency facilitated refunds and credit adjustments worth N26.2m, underscoring the importance of regulatory intervention and mediation in securing redress for consumers. Head of Complaints and Mediation Department, Mr Yusuf Musiliu, said the agency receives and analyses complaints through online and offline channels, while stakeholders’ parley provides a platform for Ikeja Electric officials and affected consumers to discuss grievances and reach amicable resolution. Musiliu therefore urged aggrieved consumers to follow established procedures rather than resorting to self-help, advising them to submit relevant documents, including electricity bills, payment receipts and other evidence when filing complaints for timely investigation. He disclosed that LASCOPA’s stakeholders’ parley with Ikeja Electric holds on the last Thursday of every month, providing a regular platform for consumers to present unresolved complaints and engage directly with the distribution company. Musiliu encouraged consumers to promptly report billing disputes, estimated billing, overbilling, electricity supply issues and other unfair practices. The agency reiterated its commitment to protecting consumers and promoting accountability in line with Lagos State Consumer Protection Law 2025 (as amended), urging residents to contact the agency through the toll-free helpline 080 0005 2726 on weekdays or email lasgcopa@gmail.com to report complaints. The post Billing disputes: LASCOPA recovers N26.2m refund for Ikeja Electric customers appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: PFIPC: ICPC Arraigns Adeyemi For Alleged Forgery, Impersonation
body: The Independent Corrupt Practices and Other Related Offences Commission (ICPC) has arraigned Adeniyi Adeyemi, the director-general of the Presidential Foreign Investment Promotion Council (PFIPC), alleged to be fake, at the Federal Capital Territory High Court, Abuja. The ICPC charged Adeyemi with 22 counts of alleged forgery and impersonation. The ICPC alleged that about March 8, 2024, in Abuja, the defendant forged a document, a letter referenced SH/COS/209/A/3456, purportedly signed/issued by the Chief of Staff to the President, Femi Gbajabiamila, appointing him as the director-general of the PFIPC. The prosecution said this is punishable under Section 364 of the Penal Code Cap. 532, Laws of the Federation of Nigeria (Abuja) 1990. The ICPC also alleged that the forged document was presented by the defendant to obtain government recognition and legitimacy for the purpose of carrying out his fraudulent activities. Counsel for the ICPC, Fatima Bardi, prayed the court to fix a date for the prosecution to open its case against Adeyemi Counsel for Adeyemi, Ibrahim Angulu, SAN, prayed the court for bail in the form of an oral application. ​ The trial judge, Justice Halilu Yusuf, however, directed Angulu to file a written bail application Angulu consented but informed the court that Adeyemi had spent 155 days in detention and had some health concerns. He said he was in possession of a report from the police clinic where his client had been receiving treatment. Meanwhile, Justice Halilu adjourned the matter until November 9 for trial and possible hearing of the defendant’s bail application. More to follow… The post PFIPC: ICPC Arraigns Adeyemi For Alleged Forgery, Impersonation appeared first on Channels Television .

title: Inquest into death of Regis Korchinski-Paquet on hold for investigation: coroner
body:
A coroner’s inquest into the death of a Toronto woman who fell from a 24th-floor balcony while police were in her home was put on hold indefinitely Thursday just as it reached the final stretch of the proceedings.
“I know everyone has been working extremely hard during this inquest. Unfortunately, I will be adjourning the inquest until further notice,” said Dr. David Cameron, the coroner presiding over the inquest into the death of Regis Korchinski-Paquet.
“The reason for this is that we have some quite unanticipated investigation that needs to be done before we can continue.”
The coroner gave no details on the nature or focus of the investigation but said jurors and the public would be informed when the inquest was ready to resume.
The inquest finished hearing evidence on Wednesday and was set to reconvene Thursday afternoon so that lawyers for about a dozen parties could make their closing remarks and suggest recommendations to the jury.
Korchinski-Paquet, a 29-year-old woman of Afro-Indigenous and Ukrainian descent, died on May 27, 2020 after police were called to the west-end apartment she shared with relatives.
The inquest was temporarily thrown off course after her mother, Claudette Beals, made a new allegation against police, who were cleared of wrongdoing by a watchdog agency.
Beals alleged officers pushed her daughter toward the balcony, causing the inquest to go on an extended break so that lawyers could figure out a way forward.
Two officers who were in the apartment had previously testified that Korchinski-Paquet was allowed into the apartment to use the bathroom, then introduced to a paramedic. Korchinski-Paquet moved quickly to the balcony, knocking over an air conditioning unit in the process, they said.
The Special Investigations Unit, one of Ontario’s police watchdog organizations, found she died while trying to move from her apartment’s balcony to the one next door. The SIU did not participate in the inquest, and its investigation is outside the scope of the proceedings.
Jurors in coroner’s inquests do not assign blame or legal responsibility, but they may make recommendations aimed at preventing similar deaths in the future.
The inquest has focused largely on Korchinski-Paquet’s history of seizures from epilepsy as well as education and training around epilepsy and postictal delirium or psychosis, mental states that can occur after seizures and lead to uncharacteristic behaviour.
Korchinski-Paquet had experienced two seizures earlier in the day, hours before police were called over a fight involving knives. Korchinski-Paquet, her mother and her brother each called 911 and mentioned her diagnosis and seizures to the call taker, jurors heard.

title: Summits like Russia-Africa summit have become good tradition, Putin says
body:
MOSCOW, October 29. /TASS/. Hosting large-scale events such as the Russia-Africa summit has become a good tradition: these gatherings reaffirm a commitment to further strengthening multifaceted ties in the spirit of genuine partnership, Russian President Vladimir Putin stated at a news conference following the summit.
At the beginning of his opening remarks, he noted that the third Russia-Africa summit had just concluded.
"On behalf of the participants, Mr. Evariste Ndayishimiye - the President of the Republic of Burundi, which currently holds the chairmanship of the African Union - and I would like to offer an assessment of the work we have accomplished together and the decisions adopted today," Putin said.
"I would like to emphasize that this is the third Russia-Africa summit. Holding such large-scale events has become a good tradition; it clearly demonstrates the firm resolve of both Russia and the African nations to continue strengthening and expanding their multifaceted ties - in a spirit of genuine partnership and mutual respect - for the sake of universal growth and prosperity," Putin pointed out.

title: Borno community to Tinubu, Zulum: Bring our 78 children home
body: By Luminous Jannamike & Kehinde Folarin ABUJA – The Margi community in Borno State has urged President Bola Tinubu and Governor Babagana Zulum to intensify efforts to rescue 78 schoolchildren and a teacher abducted from Mussa and Lassa communities in Askira/Uba Local Government Area. The community said the victims’ continued captivity had plunged their families into anguish, urging the authorities to step up rescue efforts and provide regular updates on their whereabouts. Briefing journalists in Abuja on Thursday, the community’s Secretary, Malla Gadzama, said 43 pupils were abducted from Mussa on May 15, 2026, while 35 students and a teacher were taken from a secondary school in Lassa on June 26 as they prepared for national examinations. “Our message is simple and clear: our children must not be forgotten,” Gadzama said. He called on Tinubu to mobilise the necessary security and intelligence resources and ensure effective coordination among security agencies. “Mr President, these children are Nigerians. Their lives matter,” he added. Gadzama also urged Zulum to make the rescue a priority and establish a reliable channel for keeping affected families informed without compromising security operations. “Development must also be measured by the safety of our children and the well-being of their families. Infrastructure cannot compensate for the continuing anguish of parents whose children remain in captivity,” he said. The community appealed to Senator Ali Ndume and other elected representatives from Askira/Uba to use their positions to sustain pressure on the authorities. It also called for better security around vulnerable schools and medical, psychological and educational support for the victims upon their return. Citing Section 14(2)(b) of the 1999 Constitution, which identifies the security and welfare of the people as the primary purpose of government, Gadzama said the authorities must fulfil their constitutional responsibility. “We are not asking for favour from government. We are just asking the government to fulfil its primary responsibility to the people,” he said. The community urged Tinubu, Zulum and security agencies to sustain rescue efforts until the children and their teacher were safely reunited with their families. “Bring Mussa schoolchildren, Lassa schoolchildren and their teachers safely home. That is our demand,” Gadzama said. The post Borno community to Tinubu, Zulum: Bring our 78 children home appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: Ghanaian neuroscientist honoured at Millennium Excellence Awards USA for Alzheimer’s blood test discovery
body: Thomas Karikari, associate professor of psychiatry and clinical and translational science at the University of Pittsburgh’s School of Medicine in the United States, was a proud recipient of the Excellence in Scientific Research award at the recent Millennium Excellence Awards ceremony in Washington, DC, under the royal patronage of Otumfuo Osei Tutu II, the Asantehene. When young Dr. Thomas Karikari entered his laboratory in Sweden years ago for his research program, one question lingered on his mind: “Why don’t we have a good blood test kit for Alzheimer’s dementia?” This was a question that not only developed into a hypothesis for research, but one that was ready to transform biomedical research in neuroscience and enhance medical care for people living with the condition. Many scientists had attempted in their might to understand how the disease could be easily tested without an invasive procedure, but failed at it. Dr. Karikari was nearly discouraged in his quest for answers. “I was told you don’t talk about it. Companies have spent millions; they couldn’t do it. People have spent years, but they couldn’t do it. So, just shut up,” he recounted. But, burning with the desire, the neuroscientist was poised to develop his question into a groundbreaking practical solution to testing the neurological disorder with blood samples. ‘And I set out to do it as my side project. I wasn’t even doing it as my main project because no one believed it would work,” he noted. For decades, diagnosing Alzheimer’s required invasive procedures such as spinal taps or expensive brain scans. These tests are often inaccessible in many regions of the world, especially in low-resource communities. Dr. Karikari’s experience with limited diagnostic capacity in Ghana fueled the need for a solution. So, when he was headhunted to lead a clinical research program in diagnostic medicine at the University of Pittsburgh in the United States of America (USA), he was bent on dedicating most of his career to developing, improving, and validating the clinical performance of blood tests that could simplify Alzheimer’s diagnosis. After grueling years and sleepless nights at the lab, he finally found a means to detect the disease. Dr. Karikari has about 300 publications to his name. He has published multiple seminal works in leading medical journals describing major innovations in high-performance blood tests for the neurological disorder. He also holds several patents and pending patents to that effect. Last year, Dr. Karikari was recognized by Clarivate as among the top 1% of scientists worldwide. The high-impact journal Nature also named him as a Rising Star in Ageing research, an accolade that was bestowed on only three investigators. These accomplishments have earned Dr. Karikari global respect and recognition as a leading figure in biomedical research. His achievements were celebrated at the just-ended Millennium Excellence Awards USA, spearheaded by the Asantehene, Otumfuo Osei Tutu II. “I am so proud that today I have made that contribution. A contribution that would change the face of how we treat diseases for a long time. This is just a stepping stone,” he gladly noted. Dr. Thomas Karikari’s groundbreaking research has led to the development of multiple blood tests for Alzheimer’s disease and other forms of dementia. In his acceptance speech, Dr. Karikari further noted that two new blood tests for Alzheimer’s disease have been approved by the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA). This adds to two already approved by the authority over the last two years. Dr. Karikari’s mission is beyond scientific discovery—he wants diagnostics to reach everyone, including people in places like his home village of Manfo. He says a parcel of land has been acquired back home in his late mother’s hometown of Achinakrom near Ejisu in the Ashanti region to continue with the groundbreaking scientific discoveries in Ghana. He is poised to establish a research center to help advance biomedical research on the continent. “Everything we do must get back to our people,” he said.

title: Bandits Attack: Reps seek security, humanitarian intervention in Taraba
body:
The House of Representatives has called for urgent security and humanitarian interventions following a deadly bandit attack on Binnari community in Karim Lamido Local Government Area of Taraba State, which reportedly left between 57 and 60 people dead.
The lawmakers also urged the federal government to complete the abandoned Wase-Karim Lamido road project to improve security operations and enable the rapid deployment of security personnel to affected communities.
The resolutions followed a motion of urgent public importance moved by Mohammed Audu (APC, Taraba) during Thursday’s plenary.
Presenting the motion, Mr Audu said the attack occurred on 23 October when traders and residents gathered at the community market.
He said the attackers opened fire, killing 10 people at the scene, while the ensuing panic caused several people to jump into a river, bringing the reported death toll to between 57 and 60.
According to the lawmaker, the attackers allegedly came from forested areas in Plateau State, including Dutsen Zaki in Wase Local Government Area, Kukawa in Kanam Local Government Area and areas around the Yankari Game Reserve and Gwana Mountain in Alkaleri Local Government Area of Bauchi State.
He said these areas shared boundaries with communities in Karim Lamido, making improved road access and coordinated security operations necessary to prevent further attacks.
Mr Audu described the incident as unprecedented in its scale in Karim Lamido, adding that the affected communities had suffered considerably because of the lack of access roads.
“This type of deadly attack has never taken place in Karim Lamido Local Government; the people of Karim Lamido have suffered a lot. No access road leading to all these areas,” he said.
He also reported another attack on 26 October in neighbouring Gomben Dela community, where the assailants allegedly looted food items and seized vehicles. No deaths were reported in the second incident.
The lawmaker asked the House to observe a minute of silence for those killed in Binnari and neighbouring villages.
He further urged the federal government to strengthen intelligence sharing among security agencies in Taraba, Plateau and Bauchi states to prevent a recurrence.
Mr Audu also called on the North-East Development Commission (NEDC), the National Emergency Management Agency (NEMA), the National Commission for Refugees, Migrants and Internally Displaced Persons and other humanitarian agencies to provide relief materials to affected communities.
He listed building materials, food, blankets, mattresses and mats among the items needed to support survivors and affected families.
The motion also commended the Taraba State Governor, security commanders and other security agencies for their response to the attack.
Contributing to the debate, the Minority Leader, Fred Agbedi, expressed concern over the recurring attacks on communities across the country, questioning whether the government was doing enough to protect lives and property.
He said the House had repeatedly been confronted with reports of killings and destruction of property, often followed by motions and minutes of silence.
“I remember that in 2016, on this same floor, I rose to say that the life of a Nigerian is just now worth a one-minute silence,” Mr Agbedi said.
He acknowledged the efforts of security personnel but argued that the scale of the attacks demanded a stronger response, particularly through the deployment of modern technology.
According to him, attackers often invade communities, carry out killings and leave before security agencies respond.
“The situation where criminals will go to a community, attack the community, and there is no response. They finish. They will leave, and then we start reacting. It’s like medicine after death,” he said.
Mr Agbedi questioned whether the country had adequately deployed technological tools to identify attackers and trace their movements.
He also raised concerns about the funding and implementation of security budgets, urging relevant House committees to move beyond resolutions and take practical steps to improve national security.
He said lawmakers serving on security-related committees had a responsibility to work closely with security agencies and ensure that the necessary measures were implemented to protect Nigerians.
Another Taraba lawmaker, Jaafaru Yakubu, said the state and neighbouring areas had experienced coordinated criminal activities, including banditry and kidnapping.
Mr Yakubu said the Binnari attack was followed by another assault in which the attackers allegedly took food items and destroyed facilities belonging to the federal government.
Presiding over the plenary, Deputy Speaker Benjamin Kalu acknowledged the concerns raised by Mr Agbedi but defended the federal government’s efforts to tackle insecurity.
Mr Kalu said the House’s resolutions had contributed to measures taken by the government and that the legislature should not be seen as merely holding sessions without achieving results.
He cited figures he attributed to government reports, including more than 13,000 terrorists reportedly killed in the preceding year and an 81 per cent reduction in violent deaths since 2023.
He also said more than 124,000 fighters and their family members had surrendered since 2023, while over 104,000 people had been processed through the Safe Corridor programme in collaboration with the Multinational Joint Task Force.
The deputy speaker further said the number of local government areas under insurgent control had declined from 17 in 2022 to six, citing data from 2025.
On weapons recovery, he said more than 19,000 illegal weapons had been destroyed.
Mr Kalu also highlighted an increase in security spending, saying the allocation rose from ₦2.98 trillion in 2023 to ₦3.25 trillion in 2024, ₦4.91 trillion in 2025 and ₦5.4 trillion in 2026.
He added that the government had recruited 30,000 additional police personnel and expanded electronic policing initiatives.
The deputy speaker said the figures demonstrated that the government was acting on the legislature’s interventions and that security operations were producing results.
He maintained that the minute of silence was intended to honour victims, while the government continued efforts to reduce insecurity.
“Your resolutions here, your motions here, do not end only with one minute silence. The one-minute silence is to honor those who have lost their life, but the number is shrinking by the day because the government is deliberate in making sure that the issue of insecurity is reduced, and we must give kudos to whom kudos is due. This administration has been doing tremendously well,” he said.
The House subsequently adopted the motion through a voice vote and observed a minute of silence in honour of those killed in the attacks.
Mr Kalu referred the matter to the House Committees on the North-East Development Commission, Works and NEMA for further legislative action.
The referral to the works committee is expected to facilitate consideration of the abandoned Wase-Karim Lamido road project, which the lawmakers said would improve access for security personnel responding to emergencies.
The committees are expected to pursue the House’s resolutions on road access, emergency response and assistance to communities affected by the attacks.

title: FGN’s CREDICORP showcases consumer credit access for over 1,000 Abians, pilots SPARK
body:
The Nigerian Consumer Credit Corporation (CREDICORP) concluded its CREDICORP for All – Abia State Edition beneficiary showcase at the Prime Time Event Centre, Aba, Abia State, in Nigeria’s South East, highlighting affordable credit opportunities for over 1,000 Abians. The event brought together beneficiaries, participating financial institutions, local vendors and government representatives to demonstrate how consumer credit can improve everyday livelihoods.
At the showcase, market women and traders participated in live credit-access activities, while young Nigerians engaged with YouthCred and transport operators were showcased as beneficiaries of credit-backed tricycles. Together, the activities put real people and the practical value of consumer credit at the centre of the event.
A major highlight was the pilot of SPARK, a first-of-its-kind USSD-based entry-level credit product, designed to enable Nigerians, particularly first-time borrowers, to access credit and begin building their formal credit histories. By establishing repayment records through responsible borrowing, beneficiaries can progressively improve their credit profiles and create pathways to greater financial opportunities.
The product, which simplifies credit access through basic mobile phones without requiring smartphones or internet connectivity, is expected to become more widely available to Nigerians before the end of 2026.
The showcase also featured locally assembled tricycles made available on credit through CREDICORP’s S.C.A.L.E. (Securing Consumer Access for Local Enterprises) initiative. The programme connects consumers with Nigerian manufacturers and vendors through affordable credit, supporting local production, enterprise development and job creation.
YouthCred also featured at the event, connecting eligible young Nigerians, including serving NYSC corps members, with affordable credit opportunities intended to support their financial journeys and responsible borrowing habits.
Representing the Executive Governor of Abia State, Dr Alex Otti, Mr Chinenye Mba-Uzoukwu, Chief Principal to the Governor, welcomed the initiative and highlighted the steps taken by the Abia State Government to create an environment in which responsible consumer credit and enterprise can thrive.
“Under Governor Alex Otti’s leadership, Abia State is putting the conditions in place for businesses to grow, investments to flourish and responsible credit to reach more of our people. By strengthening the enabling environment for enterprise, we are making it easier for initiatives such as CREDICORP to support traders, young people and hardworking families across the state.”
The Managing Director of MOFI and Board Member, CREDICORP, Dr Armstrong Ume Takang, described the showcase as an example of translating Federal Government policy into practical economic opportunities for Nigerians.
“The Federal Government’s consumer credit initiative reflects President Bola Ahmed Tinubu’s commitment to building an economy where more Nigerians can access the tools and opportunities needed to improve their lives. Through CREDICORP, we are seeing how well-structured public investment can stimulate enterprise, support local manufacturers and deliver measurable economic impact directly to citizens.”
Speaking on CREDICORP’s expanding national footprint, Managing Director/CEO Uzoma Nwagba emphasised that the Corporation’s mission is to take consumer credit beyond financial institutions and into the hands of everyday Nigerians.
“Consumer credit should not be a privilege reserved for a few. It should be an opportunity available to every working Nigerian. Today in Aba, Abia State, in Nigeria’s South East, we are demonstrating what that means in practical terms: credit for market women, a financial head start for young people, productive assets for transport operators, and with SPARK, asimple way for Nigerians to begin building their credit histories. This is how we make credit work for the people.”
The Abia showcase builds on CREDICORP’s engagements across Lagos, Abuja, Ondo, Osun, Ogun, Rivers and Adamawa, reflecting the Corporation’s growing nationwide reach.
Since commencing operations, CREDICORP has enabled over ₦53.5 billion in consumer credit for more than 351,000 Nigerians, with women representing approximately 59 percent of beneficiaries.
Established under President Bola Ahmed Tinubu’sadministration, CREDICORP is advancing the Federal Government’s objective of expanding consumer credit access to at least 50 percent of working Nigerians by 2030.
From market women accessing credit to young Nigerians beginning their financial journeys, and transport operators acquiring income-generating assets, the Abia showcase demonstrated how consumer credit can move beyond policy into practical opportunities that improve everyday lives.
CREDICORP for All. Credit for Every Nigerian.

title: European Solidarity office staff member injured in Russian strike on Chernihiv
body:
Yulia Mekhed, a staff member at the Chernihiv office of the European Solidarity party, was among those injured in a Russian drone attack on the center of Chernihiv, according to party leader and Member of the Ukrainian Parliament Petro Poroshenko.
"Following strikes on Dnipro, Zaporizhia, and Kremenchuk, there are now fatalities and injuries in the very center of Chernihiv. Our colleague from European Solidarity, Yulia Mekhed, was among those affected in Chernihiv. The Russian strike hit while she was inside our party office. She is currently receiving medical attention. We sincerely hope for her speedy recovery," Poroshenko wrote on Facebook .
He noted that Ukraine is in urgent need of additional air defense systems from its partners. "But we also need our own solutions, our own production, and our own technologies to protect our cities. Yet, in the 2027 budget... there is no proper financial priority given to systematically strengthening the protection of our cities. This is unacceptable," Poroshenko emphasized.
As previously reported, a Russian drone strike on Chernihiv on Thursday resulted in the deaths of two 15-year-old girls, while 23 local residents sustained injuries, including three minors, among them a 10-month-old baby girl.
Friday, October 30, has been declared a day of mourning in the city for the residents who lost their lives in Russian strikes between October 21 and October 29.

title: Stretford Hill Executes Structural, MEP Works for Canary Points Headquarters
body: Stretford Hill Limited has executed the structural and mechanical, electrical and plumbing (MEP) works for Canary Points Headquarters, a five-storey commercial building in Lekki, Lagos, commissioned on October 27. The commissioning ceremony was attended by Lagos State Deputy Governor, Dr Kadri Obafemi Hamzat; Chairman of Canary Point Holdings, Kayode Lambo; the company’s Group Managing Director, Idris Ibrahim; and other government officials, business leaders and industry stakeholders. As the main contractor for the structural and MEP works, Stretford Hill handled the building’s structural construction from foundation to roof slab, as well as the installation of its mechanical, electrical and plumbing systems. Other aspects of the development, including interior finishing, were undertaken by specialist contractors, alongside the contributions of consultants and other project stakeholders. Speaking on the project, Stretford Hill’s Chief Executive Officer, Engr. Lakunle Runsewe, said the successful execution of commercial developments depended on engineering precision, coordination and collaboration among project teams. “On a project like this, the structural elements and building services must work together to ensure the building functions as an integrated facility. Achieving that requires careful planning, effective coordination and consistent attention to quality,” he said. “At Stretford Hill Limited, we remain committed to demonstrating the capabilities of indigenous construction expertise through sound engineering, professional accountability and the consistent delivery of quality work.” The commissioning adds to the portfolio of commercial developments delivered with the involvement of indigenous construction firms.

title: Fishing is a key issue in Alaska's tight U.S. Senate race
body:
Alaska's U.S. Senate race is embroiled in an emotional fight over fish. Many in the state rely upon salmon to feed their families but those fish and others are increasingly hard to find.
JUANA SUMMERS, HOST: President Trump is trying to preemptively block election results in Alaska if the Republican incumbent loses. But in that state, the big issue in the Senate race has been an emotional fight over fish. And that's because the salmon that have long sustained Indigenous people are not returning to some Western Alaska rivers. While people living in remote villages feel the loss of salmon most acutely, the issue could ultimately affect the balance of power thousands of miles away in Washington, D.C. Alaska public media's Liz Ruskin reports. (SOUNDBITE OF DOG BARKING) LIZ RUSKIN, BYLINE: Evon Waska lives at the water's edge, where he says his parents settled when they gave up their nomadic life. EVON WASKA: Well, this is my smokehouse, and this is where we make smoke, right? RUSKIN: Waska's drying racks should be filled with salmon, but they're empty. Most years now, too few salmon return from the Bering Sea to his river, the Kuskokwim. To conserve fish, government agencies often close the river to fishing, even to those like Waska who fish to feed their families. Waska blames trawlers, industrial fishing boats miles offshore. WASKA: They don't close the trawlers. They close me and my people first. RUSKIN: Waska is up against a $1 billion industry, much of it based in Seattle. Picture a sock-shaped net that's a quarter mile long with an opening as wide as a football field. That's what trawlers tow to catch pollock. The white fish is served to you as imitation crab in McDonald's Filet-O-Fish. But also scooped up in those nets are prized king salmon and other fish. They're caught by accident and wasted, a problem known as bycatch. Alaskans are increasingly angry about it. Now, in a year where Alaska could decide the balance of power in the U.S. Senate, fish are all over political ads here. (SOUNDBITE OF MONTAGE) UNIDENTIFIED NARRATOR #1: Senator Sullivan is championing legislation to reduce bycatch and strengthen Alaska's fisheries. Call Senator Dan Sullivan. Thank him and tell him to keep fighting for Alaska fishermen. UNIDENTIFIED NARRATOR #2: Dan Sullivan is taking big money from out-of-state corporate trawlers. UNIDENTIFIED NARRATOR #3: Mary Peltola tells a lot of fish tales to get votes. RUSKIN: Republican Senator Dan Sullivan has been an ally of the pollock industry. But this year, he's touting a new bill. (SOUNDBITE OF ARCHIVED RECORDING) DAN SULLIVAN: It's the most comprehensive bycatch legislation ever to reduce bycatch, protect seafloor habitat. RUSKIN: Democratic Senate challenger Mary Peltola is Indigenous, from the Kuskokwim. She says she'd ban factory trawlers, the largest of the pollock fleet. She calls Sullivan's bill an election year ploy. (SOUNDBITE OF ARCHIVED RECORDING) MARY PELTOLA: Dan Sullivan reeled in over $300,000 from trawlers and waited until the 11th hour for a half-hearted and half-baked solution. RUSKIN: Heather Mann (ph) leads a trawlers association. She says scapegoating the pollock fishery won't help western Alaska. HEATHER MANN: Even if you were to eliminate pollock, the chances of salmon runs being restored, what the science shows us is it would have a minimal impact. RUSKIN: So far this year, pollock trawlers say they've caught 40,000 Alaska salmon. The waste is a tiny percentage of the massive pollock harvest. (SOUNDBITE OF MACHINE WHIRRING) RUSKIN: But in the Kuskokwim River village of Kwethluk, it's galling. (SOUNDBITE OF MACHINE RUMBLING) RUSKIN: Subsistence fishing is the main occupation here and the backbone of the culture. Tribal president Mary Nikolai steps into a neighbor's cold smokehouse. It pains her to see it was unused all summer. MARY NICOLAI: Most of the smokehouses are like this. And it's like a slow trend of closing our workforce out. RUSKIN: Regardless of who wins, she hopes this close Senate race tells the world of the threat they face. For NPR News, I'm Liz Ruskin in Kwethluk, Alaska. Copyright © 2026 NPR. All rights reserved. title: Alternativa Film Festival Opens 2027 Entries, Expands to Africa
body: Vanessa Obioha Alternativa Film Festival has opened submissions for its 2027 edition, marking its first expansion to Africa, with $120,000 in prize money across seven award categories. The announcement was made on Thursday at MIP Africa, as the festival, founded and supported by global mobility company inDrive, invited filmmakers from Africa, Asia and Latin America to submit feature films for the competition. Short film submissions, however, are restricted to African filmmakers, reflecting the continent’s status as the festival’s focus region for 2027. All entries must have been completed after January 1, 2026. Three of the seven awards are reserved for African filmmakers: the $20,000 Focus Award and two Short Film Awards worth $10,000 each. African filmmakers are also eligible for the remaining categories. Directors whose films are selected for the competition will be invited to attend the festival and awards ceremony, with travel and accommodation covered by the organisers. Scheduled for late 2027, the festival’s host country, city and exact dates are yet to be announced. Submissions are free and close on March 1, 2027. Alternativa champions impact-driven cinema from the Global South, a region home to roughly five-sixths of the world’s population but which remains underrepresented on screen. Its expansion into Africa comes as the initiative broadens its efforts to improve the reach of films from the region. Earlier this year, it launched Alternativa Distribution, a non-profit model designed to reinvest in filmmakers and local film industries. The distribution arm offers upfront minimum guarantees for non-theatrical rights, funds subtitling and dubbing, and shares revenue after recovering direct distribution costs. “Exceptional filmmaking can come from anywhere, but access to international audiences is still hindered by a deeply unequal system,” said Arsen Tomsky, founder and chief executive officer of inDrive. “Alternativa Distribution was created to challenge that imbalance.” Its catalogue includes Nepal’s ‘Elephants in the Fog,’ the country’s 2027 Oscar submission and winner of the Un Certain Regard Jury Prize at Cannes in 2026; ‘No Good Men,’ Afghanistan’s co-production and the opening film of the 2026 Berlin International Film Festival; Malaysia’s ‘Lost Land,’ which won the Orizzonti Special Jury Prize at the 2025 Venice Film Festival; and Tunisia’s ‘Four Daughters,’ a 2024 Oscar nominee. Films selected for the 2027 festival may also be considered for inclusion in the distribution catalogue. Alternativa began its festival journey in Almaty, Kazakhstan, in 2023, before moving to Yogyakarta, Indonesia, in 2024, and Medellín, Colombia, in 2026. The itinerant festival moves to a new region with each edition. The Medellín edition received 1,831 submissions from 55 countries, attracting 11,000 attendees, 107 international guests and more than 60 partners, making it the festival’s largest edition to date. “With each edition, Alternativa Film Festival grows,” said Liza Surganova, head of Alternativa. “Not only in reach and scale, but also in the connections it creates and the opportunities it opens up for filmmakers.” She said the African edition would build on the festival’s previous achievements while introducing new initiatives for its community. “Africa is home to an extraordinary diversity of cultures, perspectives, and cinematic voices, and we believe this new chapter will deepen our understanding of what transformative cinema can be and help us forge valuable new connections,” she added. The 2027 programme will feature public screenings, discussions and other events exploring the social issues addressed in selected films. An awards ceremony will recognise films that combine artistic excellence with the potential to drive social change. The festival will also hold Industry Days, a professional programme that connects filmmakers, producers, industry experts and social impact leaders from across the Global South. Elise Shick, a Malaysian producer of ‘Lost Land,’ which won the Nativa Award at the 2026 edition, said the festival had helped foster international collaboration. “Here, we have already formed a co-production project involving nine countries. We hope to screen it as the opening film of the next Alternativa Film Festival in Africa,” she said. The festival is open to fiction, documentary, animation and hybrid films across all genres. Eligibility requirements, the list of qualifying countries and details of the award categories are available on the festival’s official website.

title: ‘No country developed in less than 30 years’, Kashifu defends Tinubu
body: .As TMS unveils new platform By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA: Director General of the National Information Technology Development Agency NITDA, Kashifu Inuwa Abdullahi, has defended the reforms of President Bola Tinubu, saying no country has developed in less than 30 years. Kashifu, who is also Chairman, Board of Trustees and National Coordinator of the Tinubu Movement for Sustainable Governance Foundation (TMS), spoke on Thursday in Abuja at the group’s inaugural training workshop. “No country in the world developed in less than 30 years. The fastest developed country is South Korea. It took 30 years. To develop, you need the right policies first. That is the foundation Mr President is laying. Then you build on it to get investors,” he said. The programme, themed ‘Empowering Every Nigerian to be Heard’, also saw the Movement launch its official website, http://tmsnigeria.ng, where citizens can engage and verify information. The event was convened to educate citizens on the Renewed Hope Agenda and to give Nigerians a platform to contribute ideas on how to move the country forward. Kashifu said the thrust of the reforms is a change in what government spends its money on. “We spend most of our resources trying to subsidise consumption. When President Bola Ahmed Tinubu came on board, he looked at it: Is it consumption we should subsidise, or production, innovation, and investment? That is what the reforms are all about,” he said. According to him, the President built the Renewed Hope Agenda around eight priority areas. They are reforming the economy for sustained growth; strengthening national security; boosting agriculture for food security; unlocking energy and natural resources; enhancing infrastructure and transportation; focusing on health, education and social investment; accelerating diversification through industrialisation, digitalisation and creative industry; and improving governance through efficient service delivery. The NITDA chief pointed to the integration of digital skills into formal education, the introduction of Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) by the Ministry of Education, and the Student Loan scheme, which he said ensures no Nigerian is left behind because of economic circumstances. He added that NITDA is promoting digital literacy through Digital Literacy for All, the training of over 19,000 National Youth Service Corps (NYSC) champions in markets and motor parks, and the Three Million Tech Talent programme, which prepares young Nigerians to work remotely for global companies. Kashifu said the reforms are already attracting investors, citing the Dangote Refinery, a $1 billion data centre investment by a South African firm announced this week, and JP Morgan’s decision to open operations in Nigeria. “Reform is a journey; it is not a one-off event. The essence of this movement is to enlighten Nigerians on these reforms, so that Nigerians can understand what is in it for them. You are the ultimate beneficiary,” he said. He urged participants at the roundtable to propose ideas on how to sustain the reforms and to state what government needs to do more, including inputs for the approved National Youth Conference. A member of the TMS Board of Trustees, Olujonwo Obasanjo, said the Movement was set up to close the information gap between government and citizens and to showcase progress being recorded through projects across the country. He described the creation of regional development commissions by President Tinubu, and his commitment to local government autonomy affirmed by the Supreme Court, as deliberate steps to fast-track inclusive development and bring governance closer to the people. “Nigeria’s development challenge has never been lack of ideas, but policy discontinuity. There is the need for sustained, uninterrupted reforms to consolidate gains, drive economic growth and ensure that ongoing investments translate into lasting prosperity,” Obasanjo stated. The Director-General of TMS, Marcel Ngogbehei, said the workshop was conceived to empower and educate ordinary Nigerians and give them a credible platform to be heard on national issues. He explained that the training combined civic education with practical engagement, including role-play sessions in which participants set public expectations of governance against what the Tinubu administration is already implementing. Ngogbehei acknowledged that reforms come with initial pains, but maintained that continuity is critical to attracting long-term investment and ensuring the benefits eventually reach every household. He urged Nigerians to move beyond rhetoric and demand substance from political actors. “Instead of following rhetoric, we should encourage Nigerians to ask the opposition a simple question: What alternative are you offering that President Bola Ahmed Tinubu is not already doing?” he said. title: Mahama appoints 15 officers of the Ghana Prisons Service
body: President John Mahama has appointed 15 officers of the Ghana Prisons Service, elevating seven Deputy Directors of Prisons to Directors of Prisons and eight Assistant Directors of Prisons to Deputy Directors of Prisons. In a statement issued on Thursday, October 29, it said the appointments, which took effect on July 1, 2026, were made in accordance with Article 207 of the 1992 Constitution, on the advice of the Prisons Service Council. The seven officers appointed to the rank of Director of Prisons are Abraham Nii Moi Allotey, David Ofosu Addo, Thompson Otsyokpo, Edward Ashun, Joseph Asabre, Alfred Moses Cudjoe and Samuel Fiifi Dontoh. Mr Allotey is the Western Regional Commander and Officer-in-Charge of Sekondi Central Prison, while Mr Ofosu Addo serves as Head of Government Business at Prisons Headquarters. Mr Otsyokpo is the Bono-Ahafo Regional Commander and Officer-in-Charge of Sunyani Central Prison. Mr Ashun serves as Greater Accra Regional Commander and Commanding Officer at Prisons Headquarters, while Mr Asabre is the Central Regional Commander and Officer-in-Charge of Ankaful Maximum Security Prison. Mr Cudjoe serves as General Staff Officer at Prisons Headquarters, while Mr Dontoh is Head of Procurement at the headquarters. The eight officers appointed from Assistant Directors of Prisons to Deputy Directors of Prisons are Joseph Aggrey-Graham, Gandaa Bekanuo Zunuo, Aaron Agbenyegah Agbo, Michael Osei Akoto, Forson Odei, Naja Daniel Donkor, Nasom Kwabena Bawah and Matilda Nyampong. The Ghana Prisons Service congratulated the officers and wished them success as they take on their new responsibilities. The Service reaffirmed its commitment to professionalism, discipline and effective leadership, as well as its mandate of ensuring the safe custody, welfare, reformation and rehabilitation of prisoners.

title: Egypt rejects citizenship application by Hamas negotiator’s daughter on ‘security grounds’
body: The Egyptian Interior Ministry has rejected a citizenship application by Asmaa Hamad, the daughter of senior Hamas political bureau member and negotiating team official Ghazi Hamad, citing “security grounds,” Egypt's Official Gazette reported earlier this week.Hamad submitted her application while living in Egypt but has since relocated to Qatar with her husband, according to Egyptian media reports.A source close to the Hamad family said the rejection was “surprising,” Egypt's Al Manassa news site reported, adding that three of Asmaa Hamad's siblings had previously obtained Egyptian citizenship through their mother.Ministerial Decree No. 1630 of 2026, published in Wednesday's edition of the Official Gazette, formally confirmed the rejection. The decree cited Article 3, Paragraph 2, of Law No. 154 of 2004, which amended provisions of Egypt's Nationality Law No. 26 of 1975, and based the decision on “security grounds.”Article 3 grants individuals born to an Egyptian mother and a non-Egyptian father before the enactment of Law No. 154 of 2004 the right to notify the Interior Ministry of their desire to obtain Egyptian nationality.Asmaa Hamad, born in 1989, falls under the provision, which gives the ministry the legal authority to reject an application within one year of its submission.Hamad served as Hamas political officialGhazi Hamad is a senior Hamas political official who has served as a spokesperson for the terrorist organization and previously oversaw Gaza's border crossings.The US Treasury Department sanctioned Hamad in November 2024, citing his senior position in Hamas and his role in supporting the group's fundraising efforts and weapons smuggling into Gaza.Hamad became a prominent public figure during the Israel-Hamas War after the October 7 massacre and participated in hostage-ceasefire negotiations in Doha, where he currently resides.The Egyptian Embassy in Tel Aviv did not respond to a Jerusalem Post request for comment.

title: Ukraine destroys 2 Russian Su-34 bomber jets in Neptune missile strike on airfield, Navy says
body:
Ukraine's Navy destroyed two Russian Su-34 fighter-bomber jets in a strike against the Marinovka military airfield in Russia's Volgograd Oblast, using domestically produced Neptune missiles, the Navy reported on Oct. 29.
The aircraft were destroyed at the base of Russia's 11th Mixed Aviation Regiment near the settlement of Oktyabrsky, according to the Navy. The regiment belongs to the 4th Mixed Aviation Division of Russia's 4th Air and Air Defense Forces Army. The Navy did not provide any visual confirmation of the strike. The Kyiv Independent could not independently verify the claim.
Later on Oct. 29, President Volodymyr Zelensky confirmed the destruction of the two Su-34 jets, adding that Ukrainian forces had also hit a Russian Iskander missile launcher.
The Su-34 is one of Russia's main aircraft used to launch guided aerial bombs against Ukrainian cities, frontline settlements, and military positions. Strikes against these aircraft could weaken Russia's ability to carry out such attacks, while replacing the losses requires significant time and resources.
Russia had approximately 140 Su-34 fighter-bombers of various modifications in service as of Oct. 22, including the modernized Su-34M, Ukraine's military intelligence agency (HUR) reported on Oct. 29.
According to the agency, Russia has lost 43 Su-34 aircraft destroyed and another seven damaged since the start of its full-scale invasion of Ukraine.
"Such losses are quite significant for the aggressor's aircraft fleet, whose restoration requires a lengthy production cycle, substantial financial resources, and specialized industrial cooperation," HUR said.
The agency estimated that Russia can manufacture approximately 14 to 18 Su-34 aircraft annually, meaning the number of destroyed aircraft is equivalent to roughly 2.5–3 years of production.
Despite the losses, Russia continues to manufacture and modernize the aircraft to maintain its fleet and sustain aerial attacks against Ukraine.
The latest strike follows an Oct. 15 attack on the Borisoglebsk military airfield in Russia's Voronezh Oblast that destroyed four Su-34M bomber-jets and damaged two more. The attack was also carried out using Neptune missiles.
The Ukrainian ground-launched Neptune cruise missile is best known for sinking Russia's Black Sea flagship, the Moskva , in 2022. Ukraine has since developed a longer-range version capable of striking targets up to 1,000 kilometers (620 miles) away.

title: Beskrestnov: Evacuating Kyiv is impossible; there is no precedent for this anywhere in the world
body:
Evacuating Kyiv is not a viable solution; instead, every effort must be made to protect the city from potential Russian attacks on critical infrastructure—specifically water supply, sewage, and energy systems—says Serhiy (Flash) Beskrestnov, an advisor to the President of Ukraine on defense technologies.
"Evacuating Kyiv is nonsense—complete nonsense—because there is no precedent for this anywhere in the world. Even if we were talking about evacuating a thousand or ten thousand people, we simply lack the infrastructure to carry it out. Therefore, we must do everything possible to ensure Kyiv holds firm," he told reporters on Thursday, according to an Interfax-Ukraine correspondent.
According to Beskrestnov, Russia could target water supply and sewage systems, combined heat and power plants, electrical substations, and power generation facilities in an attempt to trigger a collapse in the capital.
He believes that preparations for potential attacks should have begun more actively back in the summer, specifically by installing protected generators, drilling additional artesian wells, and setting up stationary heating points.
Beskrestnov also pointed to the examples of Zaporizhia and Kharkiv, where, he noted, active work is underway to prepare for potential disruptions in heat and electricity supplies.
At the same time, he warned that deploying mobile boiler units will not, by itself, solve the problem, as their thermal emissions could make them visible to Russian drones equipped with thermal imaging cameras.
Beskrestnov urged Kyiv residents to prepare for potential disruptions to utility services, specifically, by stocking up on batteries and a small supply of fuel.

title: Turkey-Russia ties owe strength to Erdogan-Putin friendship — ambassador
body:
MOSCOW, October 29. /TASS/. The friendship between Turkish President Tayyip Erdogan and Russian leader Vladimir Putin has played a major role in building strong ties between Ankara and Moscow, Turkish Ambassador to Russia Tanju Bilgic said at a Republic Day event.
"Turkey and Russia currently cooperate actively on many issues, both bilaterally and in multilateral forums, and are carrying out major joint projects. Undoubtedly, much of the credit for the strength of relations between Turkey and Russia goes to the personal friendship between our President Recep Tayyip Erdogan and Russian leader Vladimir Vladimirovich Putin," the ambassador said.
Mutual respect and a spirit of cooperation, underpinned by the firm political will of the two leaders, form the foundation of bilateral relations, he said. "This enables close, sincere exchanges and cooperation across all areas," he added.

title: 2027: Tinubu’s daughter mobilises market women, launches Iyaloja movement
body: By Johnbosco Agbakwuru ABUJA — President Bola Tinubu’s daughter and Iyaloja-General of Nigeria, Dr Mujidat Folasade Tinubu-Ojo, has launched the Iyaloja General Movement (IGM) to mobilise market women and other grassroots voters for her father’s re-election in 2027. The movement, inaugurated on Thursday at Eagle Square, Abuja, comprises mainly market women from the 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory, with structures reportedly established across the country’s 774 local government areas and various electoral wards. The group pledged to mobilise 10 million votes for Tinubu and the All Progressives Congress (APC) in the 2027 general election. Speaking at the inauguration, Tinubu-Ojo said the movement would sensitise market leaders, traders and members of the informal sector about the forthcoming elections and encourage them to support candidates they consider capable of providing effective leadership. She said the group had coordinators and other officials at the state, local government and ward levels to drive its mobilisation efforts. According to her, market women and other informal-sector operators constitute an important voting bloc because of their presence in communities across the country. “What we are putting together as market leaders is to encourage our people and sensitise them on the next election — on which direction they should follow — so that they will not derail. And to inaugurate my own movement, the Iyaloja General Movement,” she said. Tinubu-Ojo urged voters to consider the direction of the country under the current administration, warning against electing candidates whose policies, in her view, could reverse the gains she attributed to the Tinubu administration. She expressed support for the President’s economic policies, acknowledging that they had imposed hardships on Nigerians but arguing that the expected long-term benefits justified the difficulties. “President Tinubu has done well. He has policies that will enhance the country and make our country boom again. We know what he has been doing,” she said. “What he is doing right now is like a pregnant woman going through labour. We are labouring now. Almost all Nigerians are feeling what he is doing now. The policies are painful, but the end result will justify the means.” The Iyaloja-General also defended the removal of the petrol subsidy, saying the additional revenue available to the three tiers of government had helped them execute projects and meet financial obligations, including the payment of workers’ salaries. She urged voters not to support a candidate who had promised to restore the subsidy, arguing that the revenue generated following its removal had enabled governments to undertake infrastructure projects. “We don’t want any person who will drive us back. If we vote somebody else now, that person will come with his own ideas. Somebody has said he is going to return the fuel subsidy, and we can see the impact of the fuel subsidy removal in the states,” she said. “We can see what the three tiers of government are doing. Workers are getting their salaries paid on time, and infrastructure is in place.” Tinubu-Ojo said the movement would work to sustain support for the President by engaging market associations and grassroots communities ahead of the election.
