title: Ronaldo thanks fans after winning greatest Ballon d’Or award
body: By Adegboyega Adeleye Cristiano Ronaldo has appreciated his fans and supporters around the world after his 2008 Ballon d’Or-winning season was voted the best in the history of the prestigious individual football award in a public poll organised to celebrate its 70th anniversary. The Ballon d’Or announced Ronaldo as the winner of its “Ballon d’Or of All Time” (BOAT) vote on Wednesday, after fans had their say in a poll that made them choose their favourite Ballon d’Or-winning season. In a post on X today, Ronaldo appreciated his fans, as he dedicated the award to them. He wrote: “Football belongs to the fans! Thank you to all the fans around the world, the Ballon D’Or of All Time is also yours.” Football belongs to the fans! Thank you to all the fans around the world, the Ballon D’Or of All Time is also yours. pic.twitter.com/S0sLDNiUUY — Cristiano Ronaldo (@Cristiano) October 29, 2026 Ronaldo’s message followed his victory in the inaugural Ballon d’Or of All Time (BOAT) public vote, organised by France Football. Fans chose their favourite Ballon d’Or-winning season, and Ronaldo’s 2008 campaign finished ahead of Lionel Messi’s 2012 season. The 41-year-old winning season came with Manchester United in 2007–08, where he scored 42 goals in all competitions, including 31 in the Premier League and seven in the Champions League. United won both the Premier League and Champions League, with Ronaldo scoring in the final against Chelsea. His league tally earned him the European Golden Shoe, and he went on to win his first Ballon d’Or later that year. The Portuguese legend subsequently won the award four more times, in 2013, 2014, 2016 and 2017, taking his career tally to five. Lionel Messi’s 2012 season finished second in the poll, with Ronaldo’s 2017 campaign third. Messi’s 2023 season took fourth, while Ronaldo’s 2016 campaign rounded out the top five. The top ten also includes Ronaldo’s 2014 and 2013 seasons, plus Messi’s 2015, 2011 and 2009 campaigns. The BOAT vote was a fan poll celebrating the award’s 70th anniversary, rather than a new Ballon d’Or trophy. Voting opened on October 1 and closed on October 27, with the result announced on October 28. The post Ronaldo thanks fans after winning greatest Ballon d’Or award appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: Attack on Chernihiv city center leaves two dead and raises injury toll to 25
body:
According to Ukrinform, Vyacheslav Chaus, head of the Chernihiv Regional Military Administration, reported this on Facebook .
"An absolutely brutal strike on the center of Chernihiv. Two children were killed—Russia killed two girls. Twenty-five people were injured. Among the injured are four children—the youngest girl is only 10 months old, another girl is 10 years old, and the boys are 16 and 17. Two children —a brother and sister—are in critical condition,” he wrote.
It is noted that a total of eight people are currently in hospitals. The rest received medical care on the scene or are being treated on an outpatient basis. All emergency services are operational and continue to deal with the aftermath of the attack.
Friday, October 30, was declared a Day of Mourning in Chernihiv for the city’s residents who died as a result of Russian strikes between October 21 and 29, according to Chernihiv City Council Order No. 90-r dated October 29, 2026.
“To honor the memory of those who died as a result of enemy strikes carried out by the armed forces of the Russian Federation against the city of Chernihiv between October 21 and 29, 2026, and pursuant to Article 59 of the Law of Ukraine ‘On Local Self-Government in Ukraine’: October 30, 2026, is hereby declared a Day of Mourning in the city of Chernihiv,” the document states.
It is noted that, as a sign of mourning for the deceased, the National Flag of Ukraine with a black ribbon will be flown at half-mast on the buildings of state authorities, local self-government bodies, enterprises, institutions, and organizations.
On this day, entertainment and concert events are prohibited, as is the broadcast of entertainment music in markets, retail establishments, restaurants, and on public transportation, the city council added.
As reported by Ukrinform, on October 29, a Russian drone attacked the center of Chernihiv, resulting in fatalities and injuri es.

title: Iran received letter from US's Vance, Trump claims message about medical supplies
body: Tehran has received a letter from US Vice President JD Vance, but it has not responded to it yet, Iran's semi-official Tansim news agency said on Thursday, after the Wall Street Journal reported on Wednesday that Vance sent a letter to Iranian Security Chief Mohsen Rezaei in a bid to revive peace negotiations.Tehran insists on its seven conditions being met by the US and "any position that contradicts this framework is unacceptable," the agency added.US President Donald Trump said that Vance's outreach to Iran was about helping the country get medical supplies.The Wall Street Journal reported that Vance sent the letter at Trump's direction. When asked by reporters later on Wednesday if he directed Vance to reach out to Iran to restart peace negotiations, Trump said: "No.""What that is is they need help with medical supplies and various things. He (Vance) asked me what I thought. I said, if you want to do that, that's okay. Basically, it's getting supplies in to help people that are not well," Trump told reporters.Iran's mission to the United Nations in New York did not immediately respond to a request for comment on the letter and Trump's remark. Vance's office did not immediately respond to a request for comment.The United States and Israel launched a war against Iran at the end of February. The US has also since imposed a naval blockade on Iran to starve it of oil export revenue and escalated efforts to economically isolate Iran.Iran blames US for lack of medical suppliesIran has long blamed US sanctions for hindering civilian access to medical supplies.In an August letter to the UN Security Council, Iran accused the US of intentionally depriving civilians "of access to food, medicines, medical equipment, energy and other necessities, with grave consequences for their rights to life, health, food and a decent standard of living."Qatari mediators presented Iran with a new draft deal on Sunday to end the war, but a senior Iranian official said Doha had only put forward unacceptable ideas that did not amount to an offer.The war's impact on global energy costs has also weighed on support for Republican candidates and hurt Trump's approval ratings ahead of the US midterm elections that decide control of Congress. Trump's Republican Party holds a narrow majority in both chambers of Congress.

title: More than 80% of domestic workers worldwide remain in informal employment – ILO
body: More than four in five domestic workers worldwide remain in informal employment, often without effective labour and social protection, despite progress in many countries, a new report by the International Labour Organisation (ILO) has found. The report, The State of Domestic Work in 2025: 15 Years After Convention No. 189, estimates that 66.5 million domestic workers, representing 83.1 per cent of the global workforce in the sector, are informally employed. The figure is 5.1 million higher than in 2019, reflecting the growing concentration of domestic workers in countries where informality remains persistently high. The report, released 15 years after the adoption of the ILO Domestic Workers Convention, 2011 (No. 189), estimates that 80 million people aged 15 and above were employed as domestic workers worldwide in 2025, up from 75.6 million in 2019. Domestic work accounts for 2.2 per cent of total global employment and 4.4 per cent of employees. Africa records highest informality rate The ILO found that informality in domestic work declined or remained stable in 91 of the 140 countries with comparable data between 2019 and 2025. These countries account for nearly 70 per cent of domestic workers worldwide. However, informality increased in the remaining 49 countries, which represent about 30 per cent of the global domestic workforce. Africa recorded the largest increase in the number of domestic workers during the period, adding 4.2 million workers between 2019 and 2025. The report estimates that 93.3 per cent of domestic workers in Africa are informally employed, while informality is nearly universal in the Arab States. Asia and the Pacific has the largest domestic workforce, with 40.2 million workers, accounting for about half of the global total. Europe and Central Asia recorded the lowest regional informality rate, although more than one in three domestic workers in the region remain informally employed. Domestic workers earn less Despite providing essential household services, including cleaning, cooking and care for children, older people and persons with disabilities, domestic workers continue to face significant wage inequalities. According to the report, domestic workers earn an average of 53.3 per cent of the monthly wages of other employees. For those in informal employment, the figure drops to 48.7 per cent. The relative wage gap has widened since 2019, when domestic workers earned 56.4 per cent of the average monthly wages of other employees. The ILO explained that this does not necessarily mean domestic workers’ wages have declined. In many countries, their wages increased but at a slower rate than those of other employees. Women, who make up 77.2 per cent of domestic workers globally, face particularly significant disadvantages. They earn an average of 48 per cent of the monthly wages of other employees, compared with 65.8 per cent for men in domestic work. Long working hours also remain a concern. The report estimates that 35.2 per cent of domestic workers work at least 49 hours a week, including 14.6 per cent who work 60 hours or more. Others work very short hours, which the ILO says may reflect underemployment or jobs spread across several households. ILO calls for stronger protection Patrick Belser, Chief of the ILO’s Informal Work Branch, said progress in several countries showed that reducing informality was possible, but more action was needed to improve conditions for domestic workers. “We cannot claim to value care while undervaluing the people who provide it,” he said, calling for fair wages, social security, decent working conditions and effective protection for all domestic workers. The ILO is urging governments and other stakeholders to strengthen the implementation of Convention No. 189 and Recommendation No. 201. Its recommendations include making worker registration and social protection more accessible, enforcing minimum wages, improving working-time protections, investing in decent care jobs and strengthening labour inspections and collective bargaining. The organisation says improving working conditions for domestic workers will become increasingly important as demographic changes, migration and digital transformation reshape the labour market and increase demand for care services. It argues that effective protection for domestic workers is essential to advancing gender equality, building sustainable care systems and promoting social justice.

title: Africa seeks expanded Russian investment, industrial partnerships — AU Chairman
body:
MOSCOW, October 29. /TASS/. African states are interested in expanding investments by Russian companies and establishing joint industrial production facilities on the continent, African Union (AU) Chairperson and President of Burundi Evariste Ndayishimiye announced at the plenary session of the third Russia-Africa Summit.
"We invite Russian enterprises to invest more in Africa, form partnerships within the industrial sector, develop projects with our local partners, and facilitate the transfer of expertise," he said.
According to the AU Chairperson, African countries seek to move away from an economic model where the continent primarily exports raw materials and imports finished goods.
"We need to develop our own industrial capacity, modernize our agriculture, strengthen our energy infrastructure and logistics networks, and invest more in research and technological development," Ndayishimiye stressed.
He noted that Africa possesses significant natural resources, a growing market, and a young population, while Russia can offer technologies, industrial capabilities, and expert knowledge--a combination that opens up broad prospects for mutually beneficial cooperation.
The AU Chairperson also underscored the need to establish domestic value-added production chains on the continent.
"Our continent must become a genuine hub for production and sales, rather than remaining merely a consumer market," he declared.
Ndayishimiye added that developing productive investments and industrial partnerships, alongside facilitating mutual market access for Russian and African enterprises, should be a priority for the Russia-Africa Partnership Forum’s 2027-2029 action plan.

title: UAE weather: Rain and hail forecast in some areas until Monday
body: UAE residents can expect rain in some parts of the country until Monday, with temperatures reaching 38°C, according to the National Centre of Meteorology. As hail and heavy showers hit several areas this week, the weather centre recorded the highest rainfall at 38mm in Masafi. Heavy rain hit parts of Sharjah, Fujairah, Ajman, Dubai and Al Dhafra, with showers also affecting northern and eastern areas. The NCM forecasts clouds in the north – Ras Al Khaimah, Umm Al Quwain, Ajman and northern Sharjah, as well as Fujairah and Dibba in the east. This may extend inland and bring more rain. Hail is also expected in some eastern and northern areas. On Friday, skies will be fair to partly cloudy, with a chance of convective clouds bringing rain to eastern and northern areas. Humidity is expected to rise overnight and on Saturday morning in western areas, with mist possible. Colder weather is forecast in some eastern and northern regions. Saturday will bring similar conditions, with further rain possible in the east and north. Winds will be light to moderate, strengthening at times and potentially raising dust. Gusts could reach 45kph. On Sunday, rain may continue in eastern and northern areas, while humid conditions overnight and early on Monday could bring fog or mist to some coastal and inland areas. Convective clouds may bring further showers to eastern areas on Monday. Humidity will increase overnight, with another chance of fog or mist early on Tuesday. Temperatures are forecast to reach 33°C to 37°C along the coast and on islands, 35°C to 38°C inland, and 26°C to 32°C in mountainous areas. Residents are urged to follow authorities' updates and warnings, particularly when travelling through areas affected by rain, blowing dust or reduced visibility.

title: Finland launches third Pohjanmaa-class corvette, with all four ships due for completion by 2029
body: The third vessel will now undergo outfitting, while work continues on the first two ships. The fourth has been under construction since before its keel was laid in August. “The launch of the third vessel reflects the progress made through long-term, persistent effort,” said Rear Admiral Tuomas Tiilikainen, commander of the Finnish Navy. “This is a major undertaking that brings together the future capabilities of the Finnish Navy, domestic industrial expertise, and close cooperation between various stakeholders.” RMC Defence Oy, a subsidiary of Rauma Marine Constructions, is building the corvettes under the Squadron 2020 programme. The Finnish Defence Forces Logistics Command commissioned the project, which RMC says accounts for more than 3,600 person-years of direct employment in Finland. “As the project moves forward, we have been able to utilise the experience from each vessel in the building of the next ones,” said Mika Nieminen, RMC’s president and chief executive officer. “This is reflected in the evolution of the building processes, increased efficiency of production and stronger capabilities in warship building.” The ships are designed for year-round operations in the Baltic Sea and are intended to serve well into the 2060s. They will form a core part of Finland’s maritime defence and support operations alongside NATO allies. “The launching of the third vessel testifies to the excellent learning curve in the key project on maritime performances,” said Brigadier General Engineering Juha-Matti Ylitalo, deputy chief of the Finnish Defence Forces Logistics Command. “The continued development of cooperation between the Rauma Shipyard, SAAB as the supplier of weapon systems, and the Finnish Navy as the performance owner ensures the achievement of the projected performance.” The overlapping construction programme allows lessons from each vessel to be applied to those that follow. The Navy said the work would strengthen Finland’s ability to design, build and maintain sophisticated warships domestically.

title: Ukraine heads for first economic decline since 2022 as Russian strikes take their toll
body:
Intensified Russian attacks on Ukrainian businesses have pushed the economy into decline for the first time since 2022’s invasion shock, choking key industries as inflation hits a three-year high.
Ukraine’s National Bank said on Oct. 29 that the country’s economy will shrink by 0.4% this year, after revising its previous forecast of 1.8% growth. The last time Ukraine’s economy contacted was the year of Russia’s full-scale invasion, which saw its gross domestic product (GDP) plummet by an astonishing 30% before gradually recovering the following year.
The bank said the decline was caused by Russia’s months-long blockade of seaports and escalating attacks on logistics and production facilities. The metallurgy industry has particularly suffered, with steel production shutting down across the country amid the heightened risk of deadly Russian strikes.
Meanwhile, Ukraine's Agriculutral Ministry said that farmers wont see any profits from crop production this year, as they cannot export goods via the Black Sea, while costs for autumn sowing, fuel, fertilizers, and land rental payments have increased.
The attacks, combined with the fuel crisis caused by the war in the Middle East, have also caused inflation to surge to double digits, jumping to 10% in September, the bank said.
The NBU predicts that annual inflation will reach 12.5% by the end of 2026 — a three-year high. To help cool the economy, the bank hiked its benchmark interest rate from 16% to 16.5%, the highest level since October 2023. The rate is expected to remain in place until spring 2027, the NBU said.
"Taking the consequences of the destruction into account, the NBU forecasts a slow recovery in economic growth in 2027-2028," the bank said.
"Economic activity will be supported, in particular, by public and private investment in the defense industry, the localization of weapons production financed through the Ukraine Support Loan, and projects to restore critical infrastructure."
The bank predicts that next year, Ukraine’s foreign partners will provide $52 billion in direct budget support and $37 billion for defense needs through the EU’s Ukraine Support Loan program, after the country passed several laws this month to unlock funding from the EU and the International Monetary Fund (IMF).
The funding will help Ukraine cover core budgetary needs, although the country faces a projected deficit of nearly Hr 1.7 trillion ($37 billion) next year.
This year has been one of the hardest for Ukraine’s economy, with businesses expected to lose some $10 billion in the wake of the attacks, creating a Hr 70 billion ($1.5 billion) tax shortfall.
As Russia shows no sign of slowing its attacks, the country is adapting to a new phase of the war. Ukraine’s Economy Ministry is developing support programs for companies, including a multibillion-dollar war risk insurance fund to help cover businesses starting in January.

title: 90% of Tatarstan’s enterprises use domestic software — Minnikhanov
body:
KAZAN, October 29. /TASS/. About 90% of Tatarstan’s industrial enterprises currently use Russian software, the republic’s Head Rustam Minnikhanov said at the plenary session of Kazan Digital Week 2026.
“Digital technologies and artificial intelligence are already widely used in the republic. A total of 658 digitalization projects are being implemented at industrial enterprises. About 90% of enterprises use Russian software. More than 1,400 robots are employed in industry,” Minnikhanov said.
As examples, Minnikhanov cited projects by Tatneft, KAMAZ and Setevaya Kompaniya. According to him, the goal is to move from individual digital projects to the systematic application of technologies that improve management quality and economic efficiency.
The international Kazan Digital Week 2026 forum is taking place in Kazan from October 29 to 31. Its business program includes more than 100 sessions, with over 1,000 speakers scheduled to take part. Representatives from more than 70 countries are attending the forum. The program is organized around 10 thematic areas. Experts will discuss, among other topics, digital technologies in public administration, education, culture, healthcare and agriculture, as well as cybersecurity, financial technology and intelligent mobility systems. The forum was first held in 2020.
TASS is the forum’s general information partner.

title: EU frees up over 20 billion euros to potentially help Ukraine's defense
body:
BRUSSELS, Belgium — EU countries were invited to pitch 20 billion euros' ($22 billion) worth of defense projects on Oct. 29, and the European Commission emphasized that those plans should ideally prioritize Ukraine.
The 21.3 billion euros ($23.8 billion) on the table is part of the Security Action for Europe (SAFE) instrument, which includes 150 billion euros ($167.5 billion) in favorable loans freed up in May 2025 that EU countries can draw on to help them beef up their defense and support to Ukraine.
The scheme proved quite successful, with 19 countries submitting proposals for the loans.
However, the full 150 billion euros was not used, chiefly because Italy and Hungary scaled down their borrowing plans, allowing the Commission to issue its new call.
"Along with their needs and national defense priorities, member states are also encouraged to use the funds from this second call to strengthen cooperation with Ukraine," a European Commission press release reads.
For the Commission, that means EU countries engaging in joint defense procurement with Ukraine and spending to address Ukraine's "urgent needs," for example, in "air and missile defense systems, drones and counter-drone systems, and ammunition and missiles."
That new call for submissions also comes as Ukraine-EU defense cooperation has gained momentum.
Among the spending plans already foreseen for the SAFE loans are many plans for joint production with Ukraine, even for countries seen as less pro-Ukraine in the bloc, such as Bulgaria , which has a plan to co-produce drones.
The EU has since then also launched its EU-Ukraine drone alliance , which brings together manufacturers from both sides to deepen cooperation, and the bloc has moved forward on five pan-continental defense projects , in which Ukraine has been deeply embedded.
The same day the European Commission issued the new call for SAFE proposals, EU-Ukraine defense cooperation was a key topic at Brussels' annual defense and security conference , organized by the consultancy Logos.
Panu Routila, CEO of Finnish defense manufacturer Patria, told the Kyiv Independent he is excited about a new joint venture between his company and Ukrainian drone producer General Cherry.
For Routila, the cooperation will allow the two companies to advance together on first-person view (FPV) drones and interceptor technology.
Patria is now looking for "direct collaboration" with Ukrainian companies across a range of "emerging capabilities," following that first positive collaboration, Routila told the Kyiv Independent.
Former Prime Minister and head of the Kyiv Security Forum Arseniy Yatsenyuk told the Kyiv Independent at the same event that his message for defense manufacturers in Europe is simple.
"Press your national governments to support Ukraine and to provide more," Yatsenyuk said.
He characterized the situation as a win-win, because if countries provide financial support to Ukraine, it can continue to procure from European defense manufacturers.
The SAFE loans are a concrete line of funding through which national governments could boost financial support at low borrowing costs.

title: October 30 declared day of mourning in Dnipro
body:
October 30 has been declared a day of mourning in Dnipro to honor those killed on October 29 in a drone attack on a civilian train, as well as all other victims of Russian attacks throughout the month of October.
An order to this effect was issued by the head of Dnipro, Borys Filatov, who shared a screenshot of the document on his Telegram channel on Thursday.
"In memory of the 14 victims killed by Russia this morning at the railway station, and for nine other fellow residents whose lives were taken by these Russian bastards over the past month," Filatov wrote in his Telegram post.
"The wounded are currently recovering in city hospitals—following hours-long surgeries, stabilization on ventilators, and the removal of dozens of pieces of shrapnel from their bodies. We are hoping for the best," Filatov added.
According to the order, flags will be flown at half-mast across Dnipro on the day of mourning. Businesses and institutions are encouraged to join in honoring the victims by displaying national flags adorned with black ribbons.
As previously reported, Russian forces carried out a targeted strike using a jet-powered drone against the railway station. The enemy drone struck one of the platforms, where a suburban electric train (No. 866, Dnipro–Zaporizhia) was stationed and people were present. This massive attack resulted in the deaths of 14 civilians, with more than 10 others sustaining injuries—many of whom remain in serious condition.

title: Kaduna Deputy governor swears in 3 commissioners, 18 advisers
body: By Ibrahim Hassan-Wuyo KADUNA — The Deputy Governor of Kaduna State, Dr Hadiza Balarabe, has urged newly appointed commissioners and special advisers to serve faithfully, uphold integrity and discharge their responsibilities without fear or favour. Balarabe gave the charge on Thursday after swearing in three commissioners, 18 special advisers, a Deputy Chief of Staff (Administration) and a Counsellor on Infrastructure. She reminded the appointees of the significance of the Oath of Allegiance and Oath of Office prescribed by the Seventh Schedule of the Constitution, saying the oaths carried obligations to the government and people of Kaduna State. “The Oath of Allegiance and Oath of Office are not mere words because they bind you before God and the people of Kaduna State, to serve faithfully,” she said. The deputy governor described the swearing-in ceremony as more than the conferment of titles, saying it represented a call to service and a responsibility that required humility, integrity and commitment to the people. She said the appointments reflected Governor Uba Sani’s confidence in the appointees’ abilities, experience and capacity to contribute to the state’s development. Balarabe urged them to regard their appointments not merely as recognition of past achievements but as an opportunity to deliver greater results in the service of the people. Addressing concerns about the timing of the appointments during an election season, she said the government’s responsibilities to citizens continued irrespective of the electoral calendar. “Elections have their calendar, but the needs of our people do not wait for it,” she said. According to her, Governor Sani remains committed to fulfilling his promises to the people of Kaduna State, irrespective of their political, ethnic or religious affiliations. She said the administration’s objective was to build a peaceful, prosperous and inclusive state where no community would be left behind. Highlighting the administration’s achievements since May 2023, Balarabe said communities previously divided by conflict were reconciling under the Kaduna Peace Model, while farmlands were reopening and markets becoming active. She also said more than 500 schools previously closed because of insecurity had reopened, while over 300,000 out-of-school children returned to classrooms in 2025 alone. The deputy governor added that hundreds of classrooms had been constructed, others renovated and thousands of teachers trained. In the health sector, she said 255 primary healthcare centres had been upgraded to Level Two, while improvements were ongoing at general hospitals across the state. On infrastructure, Balarabe disclosed that about 160 road projects, covering approximately 1,335 kilometres, were being implemented across the state’s 23 local government areas. She also cited the proposed light rail and bus rapid transit projects as part of the administration’s plans for the state’s future transport system. The deputy governor urged the newly sworn-in officials to serve as a link between the government and communities at the grassroots. “Let your performance be the argument that convinces the sceptical and the proof that justifies the trust of the supportive,” she said. The three commissioners sworn in were Hon. Benjamin Dalhat Solomon Kure, for Sports Development; Hon. Amina Akilu Dalhat, for Special Duties I; and Abdullahi Garba Abbas, for Special Duties II. Dr Haliru Musa Soba was sworn in as Deputy Chief of Staff (Administration), while Engr. Balarabe Muhammad Bello took the oath as Counsellor on Infrastructure. Eighteen special advisers were also sworn in. The post Kaduna Deputy governor swears in 3 commissioners, 18 advisers appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: African nations seek to expand cooperation with Russia in multiple sectors — CAR President
body:
MOSCOW, October 29. /TASS/. African nations are looking to Russia for assistance in developing their industrial, agricultural, energy, and transport infrastructure sectors, Central African Republic (CAR) President Faustin-Archange Touadera announced at the plenary session of the third Russia-Africa summit.
"We wish to develop cooperation with Russia in a variety of areas," he said. In particular, the CAR President pointed to agriculture, the extraction and processing of mineral resources--including copper and uranium--solar and general energy development, and the creation of transport corridors to provide access to seaports. He also underscored the importance of digital cooperation and technology transfer.
According to Touadera, African states intend to move away from an economic model where the continent serves primarily as a raw material supplier, while processing and value-added production take place abroad. In this regard, he called for developing local manufacturing, attracting investment, training specialists, and expanding international market access for African products.
The CAR President also thanked Russia for its security assistance.
"Your support in technology and the assistance provided to our national armed forces enabled us to achieve stability and peacefully hold elections in December 2025," he noted, adding that the focus must now shift toward economic development. "The time has come to translate the peace achieved into concrete projects."
He expressed confidence that the summit should serve as a starting point for concrete initiatives, including the construction of industrial facilities, roads, schools, and hospitals. Such cooperation, he emphasized, must be based on respect for sovereignty, non-interference in internal affairs, equality, and transparency.
Touadera also noted Russia’s support for the African position on reforming international institutions to ensure broader representation for the continent.

title: AGFUND to expand development initiatives in Africa, seeks Nigerian partners — Saudi Prince
body:
The Chairman of Arab Gulf Programme for Development (AGFUND), Prince Abdulaziz bin Talal bin Abdulaziz Al Saud, says the fund is seeking partnerships with governments, local organisations and non-governmental organisations (NGOs) to expand its development initiatives across Africa, including Nigeria.
The Saudi Arabia Prince made the remarks on Wednesday during a press conference with journalists in Armenia.
When PREMIUM TIMES asked what specific investments or programmes is AGFUND willing to prioritise in Nigeria to support young entrepreneurs, smallholder farmers and community-led development, and how can Nigeria access this support, the Saudi Arabian Prince said the organisation is looking to work with local partners to identify development challenges in different African countries and develop solutions tailored to their needs.
The AGFUND Chairman also disclosed the organisation’s development priorities, including efforts to tackle unemployment by supporting small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs), entrepreneurs and financial inclusion initiatives.
Nigeria, Africa’s most populous country, continues to grapple with the unemployment challenge, amid government efforts to create sufficient employment opportunities for its growing population, particularly young people entering the labour market to address the soaring rate of young talents leaving the country, which is commonly known as “japa” in the Nigerian parlance.
According to the National Bureau of Statistics (NBS), Nigeria’s official unemployment rate is pegged within the range of 4.3 to 4.9 per cent. Although under the older NBS methodology used prior to 2023, the reported unemployment rate was much higher, it was about 33.3 per cent in late 2020. A vast majority of the Nigerian workforce operates in the informal sector, with the informal employment rate estimated at roughly 92.8 per cent.
On Wednesday, a Nigerian climate technology and agritech startup, D-Olivette Labs, emerged as one of four winners of the 2025 Prince Talal International Prize for Human Development, receiving $200,000 for its clean-energy innovation.
In his response to PREMIUM TIMES reporter’s question, Prince Abdulaziz bin Talal bin Abdulaziz Al Saud explained that the organisation is seeking to help address unemployment by supporting entrepreneurs rather than relying on governments to absorb an increasing number of graduates into public-sector employment.
“When we talk about unemployment, you know, most of these countries, some of them are our countries as well, whoever graduates is always looking for a government position,” the representative said.
“Government position, they would say it’s much safer, it’s much secure, etc., but we want to stay away from these government positions because government will reach a day where they don’t have any more positions for new employees.”
The representative said AGFUND was exploring ways to help small businesses and entrepreneurs grow, including through financial inclusion banks that provide microloans and share knowledge with beneficiaries.
“So, I think our part of what we’re doing is we’re trying to help SMEs. We’re trying to help entrepreneurs,” the representative said.
The initiative, the representative explained, is intended to help low-income individuals establish businesses, expand their activities and eventually employ other people.
“So, these poor people, whoever they are, wherever they are, tomorrow they will become employers. They will have employees. And this is the effect that we want,” the representative said.
The AGFUND Chair said its approach builds on a mission that began in 2006–2007 and is now being expanded further into Africa.
The organisation’s representative said AGFUND was established to support development initiatives that other funding institutions might not prioritise.
The prince cited the organisation’s work on financial inclusion and microfinance banks, linked to the late Prince Talal, the founder of AGFUND, and Professor Muhammad Yunus of Bangladesh’s Grameen Bank.
He said the organisation was now seeking partnerships with government institutions and NGOs to identify specific needs and develop interventions that could help communities become economically self-reliant.
According to the him, expanding these initiatives would require an understanding of the differences in culture, regulations and development priorities across African countries.
The representative also cautioned against focusing exclusively on large-scale projects, arguing that smaller pilot initiatives could provide a more practical route to sustainable development.
“Sometimes we’re looking for the big projects, the mega-projects, the giga-projects. How many projects we’ve seen in the region have not succeeded? How many projects we’ve seen in Africa, for example, they have not succeeded?” the representative said.
“The aspirations are very big and the dreams are very big, but sometimes you need a pilot project.”
The representative said AGFUND tests initiatives on a smaller scale before expanding successful projects, with adjustments to reflect the circumstances of different regions.
Additionally, Prince Abdulaziz also highlighted the varying economic and social challenges confronting African countries, including instability, economic difficulties and declining global funding for development.
The representative said these challenges made it necessary for African countries to build on existing institutions and development platforms rather than continually creating new ones.
Referring to the African Union’s Agenda 2063, the representative said the continent was entering a new phase of its long-term development vision and needed to align existing efforts to address persistent problems such as unemployment.
“How can we align ourselves with whatever already exists? Why do we need to always create new platforms, find new solutions? No, the solutions are there. The platforms are there,” the representative said.
“All we need to do is just realign to stop having unemployment, if we can.”
AGFUND’s proposed expansion could create opportunities for Nigerian development organisations, government agencies and NGOs to explore partnerships aimed at improving access to finance and supporting entrepreneurship.
However, the organisation did not specify the amount of funding it plans to commit to Nigeria, the number of beneficiaries it expects to reach or a timeline for implementing new initiatives in the country.

title: Shell and Total Post Highest Quarterly Profit Since 2022
body:
Essential news coupled with the finest maritime content sourced from across the globe.
LONDON, Oct 29 (Reuters) – Shell and TotalEnergies reported on Thursday sharply higher third-quarter profits and raised share buybacks, as war-driven energy prices and record refining margins helped both beat expectations.
Shell raised its quarterly buyback to $5 billion from $3 billion, the second-largest buyback on record, while Total reiterated plans to buy back $2.5 billion of shares in the fourth quarter and said it would buy back another $2.5 billion in the first quarter of 2027.
The shareholder distributions offer an insight into how oil majors plan to spend the profits generated by the US-Israeli war with Iran, which is in its ninth month and has disrupted global energy supplies. Energy prices have driven inflation for customers globally and increased input costs for industry.
Reflecting its higher payout, shares in Shell gained 3.2% in early trade on Thursday, while Total’s rose 1.8%, compared with a broader index of European energy companies rising 1.9%.
BP, Chevron and ExxonMobil report results on Friday. Also on Thursday, Austria’s OMV reported its highest quarterly operating profit since 2022.
Refining margins nearly quadrupled for both Shell and Total compared with a year ago. They reached $42 a barrel and $33.2 per barrel, respectively, helping to boost earnings to the highest since 2022, when Shell delivered a record $6 billion buyback program.
Shell posted third-quarter net profit of $10.81 billion, above analysts’ average estimate of $10.33 billion and almost double the $5.43 billion it earned a year earlier.
TotalEnergies reported adjusted net income of $9.1 billion for the July to September quarter, more than double the $4.0 billion a year earlier and above an expected $8.3 billion.
Total’s refining and chemicals division posted record net income of $3.6 billion, more than five times the level of a year ago and double the previous quarter. CEO Patrick Pouyanné said a nearly 10% increase in refining throughput, along with strong oil trading, had captured historically high refining margins in Europe and worldwide.
Total’s income in its LNG unit rose to $1.9 billion on average gas prices that were up 20% compared to the last quarter and strong LNG and gas trading.
The company’s gearing fell to 9.1% at end-September from 13.1% at the end of the prior quarter, below its target of under 10% by the end of 2026.
Jefferies called Total’s results “solid, not standout,” as hydrocarbon production reached 2.5 million barrels of oil equivalent per day, missing Total’s consensus by 4%, the broker said. Total also took a $1.9 billion impairment mainly tied to offshore wind and a South Korean petrochemical stake.
Since December 30, 2022, Shell has delivered a 120% total shareholder return, including reinvested dividends, ahead of BP’s 78%, TotalEnergies’ TTEF.PA 84%, ExxonMobil’s 89% and Chevron’s 51%, according to Shell data.
Shell beat expectations across all its segments.
Its cash flow from operations, excluding working capital, rose to $21.7 billion from $12.24 billion a year earlier and beat expectations of $18.18 billion. RBC analyst Biraj Borkhataria said even with a roughly $5 billion buyback next quarter, Shell will likely miss its 40% to 50% payout ratio guidance for the year, a shortfall he attributed to abnormal macro conditions.
Shell’s oil and gas output fell 17% in the first nine months of 2026 from a year earlier, mainly because war in the Middle East reduced volumes from Qatar. LNG liquefaction volumes rose 12%, driven by the ramp-up at LNG Canada and partly offset by the Qatari disruption.
Shell halted production at its Pearl gas-to-liquids plant in Qatar in March after an attack on Ras Laffan Industrial City damaged one of its two trains. It has has restarted the plant but at reduced output and says repairs could take about a year.
Shell recorded $5.4 billion in non-cash increases to shipping leases, which count toward net debt. Shell booked an impairment of around $2 billion across its European biogas business, which includes assets from its 2023 $2 billion acquisition of Denmark-based Nature Energy, due to lowered expectations of growth in the market.
Shell lowered its capital expenditure guidance for 2026 to $23 billion to $25 billion from $24 billion to $26 billion.
(Reporting by Shadia Nasralla and Stephanie Kelly in London and Dimitri Rhodes in Gdansk. Editing by Jan Harvey, Mark Potter and Barbara Lewis)

title: The Mosquito Bowl and the ‘barbaric madness’ of the Pacific War
body: It feels, at times, as if the viewer can’t escape. Body clenched, stomach tight — eyes perhaps slanted downward — as the oppressive violence folds around you. At face value, that seems absurd. The viewer isn’t one of the 5,000 Marines landing on Tarawa, facing a maelstrom of mortars, machine guns and rifle fire poured by elite troops of the Imperial Navy’s Special Naval Landing Force. Viewers are perfectly safe, perched atop the woven synthetic fibers of a movie theater chair, but that’s how director Peter Berg intended the upcoming film The Mosquito Bowl to feel. The intimate violence thrusts the Marines from the 4th and 29th regiments, 6th Marine Division, as well as moviegoers, into “this barbaric madness,” said Berg. The film, based on Buzz Bissinger’s 2022 book The Mosquito Bowl: A Game of Life and Death in World War II , follows four of America’s top college football stars who traded a pigskin for an M1 Garand and who subsequently faced off on the “gridiron” of Guadalcanal before being shipped off to Okinawa. Yet the actual football game, dubbed the Mosquito Bowl, occupies just a small portion of the movie. That too, according to Berg, was intentional. “This is not a football movie. It’s a war movie that happens to have football players in the middle of the war,” he said in a release. “These young men — who are just sort of blazing in the apex of their youth and their vitality and their joy — you meet them as college football stars. Then you introduce them to a hell, a flavor of which they had no idea even existed.” “I think it would have been a tragedy if you said, ‘Oh God, it’s Hollywood. … Let’s sugarcoat it a little,” Bissinger told Military Times. “People have to know what war is. They have to know. We sanitize too much, and it’s just not the way it is. Maybe they’ll watch, and they’ll say, ‘No more wars.’ I know that’s naive, but at least you know what we’re sending our men and women into, and I think that’s really important.” “So many people were killed in World War II. This is just a story of four of those people, and my feeling was to make it as intense and experiential as I could around those four guys,” Berg said in a release. “Make the audience feel as though they’re actually in it and they can’t escape it and they’re not even sure what’s happening at times, which I think is very true to the experience that so many of these guys went through. … That was our strategy as we approached filming it and editing it and scoring it and sound-designing it,” he continued. “I’ve had many people who watch the film now say afterward that they literally felt like they went through something, and that was kind of what we were trying to achieve.” Berg and Bissinger, who happen to be cousins, collaborated on Bissinger’s bestselling book Friday Night Lights over two decades ago and have once again teamed up to deliver this gut-punch of a film. Peter Berg (left) and Buzz Bissinger attend The Mosquito Bowl Special Screening at the National WWII Museum on Oct.15, 2026, in New Orleans, Louisiana. (Erika Goldring/Getty Images for Netflix) “Pete has this ability to read a 400-page book and crystallize and seize on what he thought the emotional heart was. title: Two killed in Duk cattle raid, 6 injured in ambush
body: At least two people were shot dead, six injured, and 46 head of cattle raided during separate attacks in Jonglei State’s Duk County on Wednesday, authorities said. Peter Chol Galuak, the caretaker county commissioner, told Radio Tamazuj the assailants and cattle rustlers are suspected to have come from the Greater Pibor Administrative Area (GPAA). “In the first incident on Wednesday evening, armed assailants attacked a cattle camp between Poktap and Patuetnoi areas of Ageer Payam, killing two herders. Simultaneously, a truck moving from Pajut to Poktap was attacked by the same group, resulting in six injuries, including a woman,” he said. “Later the same day they raided 46 cows from Duk Padiet Payam. All these incidents occurred while I was in a meeting with the state governor who was on an official visit to the county.” The commissioner condemned the attacks and urged restraint among armed youth while urging intervention from the Greater Pibor Administrative Area (GPAA) authorities to arrest the situation. Several calls to Caretaker GPAA Information Minister Jacob Werchum Jouk have not been answered. Kenya Mach, an activist with Jonglei State Women Association, condemned the attacks and renewed calls for government intervention. The post Two killed in Duk cattle raid, 6 injured in ambush appeared first on Radio Tamazuj .

title: The Mosquito Bowl and the ‘barbaric madness’ of the Pacific War
body: It feels, at times, as if the viewer can’t escape. Body clenched, stomach tight — eyes perhaps slanted downward — as the oppressive violence folds around you. At face value, that seems absurd. The viewer isn’t one of the 5,000 Marines landing on Tarawa, facing a maelstrom of mortars, machine guns and rifle fire poured by elite troops of the Imperial Navy’s Special Naval Landing Force. Viewers are perfectly safe, perched atop the woven synthetic fibers of a movie theater chair, but that’s how director Peter Berg intended the upcoming film The Mosquito Bowl to feel. The intimate violence thrusts the Marines from the 4th and 29th regiments, 6th Marine Division, as well as moviegoers, into “this barbaric madness,” said Berg. The film, based on Buzz Bissinger’s 2022 book The Mosquito Bowl: A Game of Life and Death in World War II , follows four of America’s top college football stars who traded a pigskin for an M1 Garand and who subsequently faced off on the “gridiron” of Guadalcanal before being shipped off to Okinawa. Yet the actual football game, dubbed the Mosquito Bowl, occupies just a small portion of the movie. That too, according to Berg, was intentional. “This is not a football movie. It’s a war movie that happens to have football players in the middle of the war,” he said in a release. “These young men — who are just sort of blazing in the apex of their youth and their vitality and their joy — you meet them as college football stars. Then you introduce them to a hell, a flavor of which they had no idea even existed.” “I think it would have been a tragedy if you said, ‘Oh God, it’s Hollywood. … Let’s sugarcoat it a little,” Bissinger told Military Times. “People have to know what war is. They have to know. We sanitize too much, and it’s just not the way it is. Maybe they’ll watch, and they’ll say, ‘No more wars.’ I know that’s naive, but at least you know what we’re sending our men and women into, and I think that’s really important.” “So many people were killed in World War II. This is just a story of four of those people, and my feeling was to make it as intense and experiential as I could around those four guys,” Berg said in a release. “Make the audience feel as though they’re actually in it and they can’t escape it and they’re not even sure what’s happening at times, which I think is very true to the experience that so many of these guys went through. … That was our strategy as we approached filming it and editing it and scoring it and sound-designing it,” he continued. “I’ve had many people who watch the film now say afterward that they literally felt like they went through something, and that was kind of what we were trying to achieve.” Berg and Bissinger, who happen to be cousins, collaborated on Bissinger’s bestselling book Friday Night Lights over two decades ago and have once again teamed up to deliver this gut-punch of a film. Peter Berg (left) and Buzz Bissinger attend The Mosquito Bowl Special Screening at the National WWII Museum on Oct.15, 2026, in New Orleans, Louisiana. (Erika Goldring/Getty Images for Netflix) “Pete has this ability to read a 400-page book and crystallize and seize on what he thought the emotional heart was. I’ve always admired that,” Bissinger said. “He wrote the script. There were several scripts written, but Pete just hit it. When I read the script, his ability to incorporate everything into a two-hour movie was phenomenal.” For both men, the filming of The Mosquito Bowl was personal, as both their fathers were Marines. Berg’s father served in Korea, and Bissinger’s was a Marine in the Pacific — including Okinawa. “I knew nothing about what he did,” said Bissinger. “He wouldn’t talk about it. He would joke about it sometimes, but it was pretty clear he had put up a wall. As his son, that was his privacy. I didn’t want to violate that. But as I was doing preliminary research for the book. I finally said, ‘Well, might as well figure out what the hell he did.’ “And I’m looking up the records, and there he is. Not only was he a rifleman on the line, but he was also in one of the regiments, the Fourth Regiment that is depicted in the book. It wasn’t like I wanted to write this book as a pay-on to my father, but he was there for every scene, particularly on Okinawa. “I just wish I had said, ‘Dad, I’m really proud of you.’ But he died 20 years ago, and maybe he’s … I don’t know where the hell he is, heaven or hell. But I hope he’s listening, and I hope he’s watching because I did want to honor not just him, but all the men who served back then.” The film is set to hit theaters on Oct. 30 and premiere on Netflix on Nov. 25. It features Nicholas Galitzine ( The Idea of You ) as John McLaughry; Bill Skarsgård ( It ) as Bob Bauman; Ray Nicholson ( Smile 2 ) as Tony Butkovich; and Tom Francis (Broadway’s Sunset Boulevard ) as Dave Schreiner. Berg, who penned the adaptation alongside Mark L. Smith, produced the film with Alex Gayner and Brian Grazer for Imagine Entertainment. Grazer and Imagine Entertainment previously collaborated with Berg on Friday Night Lights . Ezra Emanuel is the executive producer.

title: Elbit Systems to present underwater drones at Euronaval 2026 in Paris
body: Elbit announced on Thursday that it will present its Unmanned Underwater Vehicle (UUV) capabilities for the first time at Euronaval 2026, marking the expansion of the company's autonomous maritime offering into the underwater domain.Euronaval is set to take place in Paris November 3-6.So far, sources have not indicated any expected problems with the French government over Israeli participation, though air force-focused conferences have seen significant drama between Paris and Jerusalem in recent years.These new capabilities were added to Elbit Systems' portfolio following the acquisition last week of International Submarine Engineering Ltd. (ISE), a provider of autonomous underwater systems that has delivered more than 250 underwater vehicles to customers in over 20 countries worldwide.The new UUV solutions will be showcased alongside the company's Seagull family of Unmanned Surface Vessels (USVs) and additional maritime solutions from Elbit Systems' naval portfolio.The existing systems engaged in patrol and reconnaissance missions, located and neutralized sea mines, and supported anti-submarine operations, but were focused on naval missions above the sea surface.For example, Seagull has been carrying out mission since 2017.But underwater vehicles require different technologies and a different conceptual focus.Elbit's new systems enable coordinated surface and underwater missionsThe combined architecture enables integrated operations between underwater and surface autonomous systems, in addition to extended opportunities for integrated manned-unmanned teaming (MUM-T) concepts, meaning vehicles with humans-soldier and drone-style vehicles working in tandem.Elbit's UUV portfolio now includes modular Autonomous Underwater Vehicles (AUVs) designed for missions such as intelligence gathering, mine countermeasure (MCM) operations, anti-submarine warfare (ASW), seabed mapping and protection of critical maritime infrastructure and strategic assets.The systems support long-endurance autonomous operations and integrate a range of payloads, including sonars, ISR systems and mission-specific sensors.Elbit highlights coordinated surface and underwater naval operationsAccording to Elbit, "The company's vertically integrated approach enables coordinated autonomous maritime formations tailored to evolving operational requirements, supporting integrated mission planning, launch and recovery, as well as the execution of coordinated surface and underwater missions.""Navies are increasingly looking for comprehensive autonomous solutions for complex maritime missions," said Oren Sabag, General Manager of Elbit Systems ISTAR & EW. "The addition of UUV capabilities further expands our autonomous maritime portfolio and strengthens our ability to provide customers with a holistic operational solution spanning surface and underwater autonomous systems, payloads and mission management capabilities."

title: Ombudsman's Office denies reports Russian occupation forces have begun evacuating Oleshky residents
body:
The Office of the Verkhovna Rada Commissioner for Human Rights refutes reports that Russian occupiers have begun evacuating residents of the town of Oleshky in Kherson region, without waiting for the announced arrival of representatives of the American media and teams from both the Ukrainian and Russian human rights commissioners.
"We currently have no confirmation of such actions on the part of the Russian side," Director of the Department of Information Policy, Communications, and Protocol Events at the Ombudsman's Office Tetiana Shelest told reporters on Thursday.
Earlier, Russian propaganda media published a series of photos and videos showing civilians from the city sitting on military buggies driving through the streets of Oleshky. It was reported that civilians are currently being gathered and preparations are underway to receive the humanitarian convoy.
As previously reported, according to Fox News, the humanitarian operation in Oleshky was coordinated through the mediation of U.S. First Lady Melania Trump. The agreement was signed on October 23 by Dmytro Lubinets, the Verkhovna Rada's Commissioner for Human Rights, and Russian Ombudswoman Yana Lantratova. A ceasefire in Oleshky area went into effect on Tuesday, and the mission will last about a week. Four American journalists from Newsmax will be stationed directly in the occupied city to document the humanitarian mission, the U.S. First Lady said.
Lubinets himself reported earlier on Thursday that he was already on his way to Oleshky. Commenting on social media posts claiming that he was allegedly in Russia, specifically in Anapa, he wrote: "There are many questions and provocative posts circulating. So I want to clarify: I am going there to be on the ground in person and see what is happening. To keep you informed about the mission's progress. Please trust official sources and do not draw conclusions from unverified reports."
Humanitarian aid for residents of occupied Oleshky was scheduled to be delivered to the city on October 30; demining of the routes for the mission is currently underway. However, Russian propaganda media are reporting that the first batch of humanitarian aid was delivered to the town as early as Thursday.

title: Trial date set for man charged with attacking White House correspondents’ dinner
body:
A federal judge has set a September 2027 trial date for a man charged with attempting to kill President Donald Trump at the White House Correspondents’ Association dinner
WASHINGTON -- A federal judge on Thursday set a September 2027 trial date for a man charged with attempting to kill President Donald Trump at the White House Correspondents’ Association dinner earlier this year.
Cole Tomas Allen's trial is scheduled to start with jury selection on Sept. 7 in Washington, D.C., and is expected to last approximately three to four weeks. Prosecutors had recommended starting the trial in May 2027, but U.S. District Judge Trevor McFadden set the later date after one of Allen's attorneys asked for more time to prepare.
Allen, of Torrance, California, is accused of storming the WHCA dinner while armed with guns and knives and firing a shotgun at a Secret Service officer who tried to stop the April 25, 2026, attack at the Washington Hilton hotel. The officer, who was struck once in a bullet-resistant vest, fired five shots but didn’t hit anybody, authorities said. Allen was injured but not from gunfire.
The attack led to an early end to one of the highest-profile annual events in the nation’s capital. President Donald Trump returned to speak at the rescheduled dinner three months later.
In writings that he sent to relatives before the attack, Allen railed against Trump administration policies and referred to himself as a “Friendly Federal Assassin,” authorities said.
Allen faces an attempted assassination charge that carries a maximum possible sentence of life in prison. He also is charged with assaulting a federal officer with a deadly weapon and two additional firearms counts.

title: Man facing charges related to 3 alleged arsons in Saskatoon: police
body:
A man is facing charges in connection with three suspicious fires in Saskatoon.
The 33-year-old suspect was arrested in the 800 block of Idylwyld Drive North Wednesday morning, the Saskatoon Police Service said in a news release.
He was arrested in relation to a suspicious house fire in the 300 block of Avenue E North that occurred around 4:30 a.m. on Oct. 16.
Additional investigation connected the man to two other alleged arsons that occurred in July on 5th Avenue North, according to police.
The Saskatoon man is facing charges of arson with disregard for human life and two counts of arson with damage to property.

title: U.S. Shipbuilding Delays Push Empire Wind’s First Power Into 2027
body:
Essential news coupled with the finest maritime content sourced from across the globe.
Visualizations of the Empire Wind offshore wind farm. Image courtesy Equinor
Delays involving U.S.-built support vessels have pushed back turbine installation at Equinor’s Empire Wind offshore wind project off New York, with first power now expected in the first half of 2027.
Norwegian energy giant Equinor said Thursday that the 810-megawatt project is approximately 80% complete, but construction delays affecting specialized vessels needed to install its 54 wind turbines have pushed the schedule back several months.
The update came as Equinor reported its third-quarter 2026 financial results.
“Most of the remaining project scope relates to offshore turbine installation, which is expected to start next year,” Equinor Chief Financial Officer Torgrim Reitan told investors. “This is a bit later than planned.”
The delay underscores the challenges of building out the U.S. offshore wind industry, particularly its reliance on specialized vessels and domestic shipbuilding capacity to meet requirements under the Jones Act.
Empire Wind is using a turbine installation system developed by Maersk Offshore Wind, centered on the Singapore-built installation vessel Maersk Viridis .
Because the vessel is foreign-built, it cannot transport turbine components between U.S. points under the Jones Act. Instead, the project relies on specially designed U.S.-built barges and tugs to deliver turbine components from the South Brooklyn Marine Terminal to the installation vessel offshore.
The barges are designed to connect directly to Maersk Viridis , allowing turbine components to be transferred for installation without the installation vessel returning to port.
While Maersk Viridis arrived off Pascagoula, Mississippi, in August for testing and preparations, delays involving the U.S.-built support vessels have pushed back the turbine installation campaign.
Equinor said all 54 turbine foundations have been completed, along with the offshore substation and cable work.
The project is located approximately 14 miles south of Long Island and is expected to generate enough electricity to power roughly 500,000 New York homes once operational.
Despite the schedule setback, Equinor said it does not expect any change to the project’s total capital expenditure, although some spending will shift from 2026 into 2027.
The company has previously estimated the project’s total investment, including redevelopment of the South Brooklyn Marine Terminal, at approximately $7.5 billion.
Equinor also expects approximately $2.5 billion in U.S. investment tax credits, with roughly $2 billion expected to be recognized in 2027 and the remaining $500 million in 2028.
The company said the revised construction schedule is not expected to affect the timing of those tax credits.
The latest delay follows a turbulent period for Empire Wind, which has faced repeated attempts by the Trump administration to halt construction.
The administration first ordered work stopped in April 2025, citing concerns over the project’s federal permitting process. That order was lifted the following month.
A second suspension followed in December 2025, when the Bureau of Ocean Energy Management ordered construction halted on Empire Wind and four other offshore wind projects over national security concerns.
Equinor challenged the suspension in federal court and secured preliminary relief allowing construction to continue.
In its third-quarter financial statements, Equinor said the court dismissed the case on September 30, 2026, after the suspension order expired. The company said the dismissal eliminated the risk that a $2.7 billion project loan could become repayable within 12 months as a result of the order.
Empire Wind remains one of the largest offshore wind projects under construction in the United States, with its latest setback highlighting the growing importance of domestic vessel construction to the industry’s ability to deliver projects on schedule.

title: Imo West Primary: Uzodimma Is Our Authentic Candidate, APC Insists
body: The Imo State chapter of the All Progressives Congress (APC) has maintained that Governor Hope Uzodimma remains its candidate for the Imo West Senatorial District in the 2027 general elections. The party, in a statement by its State Chairman, Austin Onyedebelu, rejected the judgment of the Federal High Court, which declared former governor Rochas Okorocha the winner of the APC primary for the senatorial district. It stated that the judgment delivered by Justice Obiora Egwuatu of the Federal High Court, Abuja, on Thursday, October 29, 2026, against Uzodimma raises grave concerns about constitutional compliance, the application of established judicial precedents, and the evaluation of evidence. The party also described it as “deeply troubling” and believes that the legal questions arising from it warrant rigorous scrutiny. It said that a judgment that appears to depart from established constitutional principles and raises questions about the treatment of material evidence risks undermining public confidence in the administration of justice. “Section 285(9) of the Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, 1999 (as amended), prescribes a 14-day period for instituting pre-election matters within its scope. The APC Imo West Senatorial District primary election was held on May 18, 2026. However, former Governor Rochas Okorocha reportedly instituted his action on August 13, 2026, long after the constitutionally prescribed period had elapsed. “Our concern is straightforward: where an applicant approaches the court seeking to be declared the winner of a party primary, the question of when the cause of action arose and whether the action was instituted within the constitutionally prescribed period becomes fundamental to the court’s jurisdiction,” the APC stated. It stated that it was concerned that the judgment did not sufficiently resolve the implications of the disputed documents and the procedure through which the allegations were presented. These, it said, were substantial issues that deserve further judicial consideration, particularly in a pre- election dispute capable of determining a political party’s candidate for an entire senatorial district. “Perhaps the most troubling aspect of this case is the dispute over the authenticity and origin of the documents relied upon by the applicant. During the proceedings, the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) reportedly maintained that the documents tendered were not in its custody, had not been certified by the commission, and bore a stamp and signature that it did not recognise as authentic. “Similarly, the All Progressives Congress, the political party at the centre of the dispute, reportedly maintained that the documents did not emanate from its recognised organs and were not in its custody. These objections raise questions that cannot be brushed aside lightly,” the party stated. “Where the institution from which a document is purported to have originated disputes its authenticity, and the political party concerned similarly disowns the document, the court must carefully examine the evidence and explain the basis for its conclusions. We are deeply concerned that, notwithstanding the objections reportedly raised by INEC and the APC, the court proceeded in a manner that, in our view, failed to give sufficient weight to these material issues.” The APC also faulted the court’s treatment of INEC’s position, which it said was reportedly characterised as an afterthought. “We believe that the evidence and objections presented by the commission, the APC and the relevant party directorate responsible for its records deserved thorough and transparent consideration. “The fundamental question is this: where both the electoral commission and the political party dispute the authenticity and origin of documents relied upon in a pre-election case, what evidentiary basis justifies the court’s ultimate conclusion? This question goes to the heart of the dispute and deserves a clear answer through the appropriate judicial process,” it added. It further stated that while the court undoubtedly has the authority to evaluate evidence and determine its weight, that authority must be exercised in accordance with the law, the evidence on record and the principles of fair hearing. “Justice must not only be done; it must be seen to be done through a process that commands the confidence of the parties and the public. We will study the judgment and pursue all lawful remedies. “As the judgment has only just been delivered, we will undertake a thorough examination of the court’s reasoning, findings and conclusions before determining the appropriate legal steps,” the party said. “Our position remains unchanged: Hope Uzodimma is our authentic candidate. We reiterate our position that His Excellency, Distinguished Senator Hope Uzodimma, emerged as the authentic winner of the APC Imo West Senatorial District primary election held on May 18, 2026. We remain confident in our position and will pursue all lawful avenues available to defend it.” The post Imo West Primary: Uzodimma Is Our Authentic Candidate, APC Insists appeared first on Channels Television .

title: Ukraine-US-Russia delegation arrives at aid distribution point in Oleshky – Arakhamia
body:
A delegation of representatives from Ukraine, the United States, and Russia has arrived at the point from which humanitarian aid will be delivered to Oleshky on Friday, Head of the Servant of the People parliamentary faction Davyd Arakhamia said.
"A delegation of representatives from Ukraine, the United States, and Russia has arrived at the point from which aid will be delivered to Oleshky tomorrow," Arakhamia said in a Telegram post on Thursday, also noting the presence of media representatives from the three countries on site to ensure maximum transparency during the next phase of the humanitarian mission.
As previously reported, according to Fox News, the humanitarian operation in Oleshky was coordinated through the mediation of Melania Trump. The agreement was signed on October 23 by Dmytro Lubinets, the Verkhovna Rada's Human Rights Commissioner, and Yana Lantratova, the Russian ombudswoman. A ceasefire in Oleshky area went into effect on Tuesday, and the mission is expected to last about a week.
Humanitarian aid for residents of occupied Oleshky is scheduled to be delivered to the town on October 30; demining of the routes for the mission is currently underway.
Four American journalists from Newsmax will be on the ground in occupied Oleshky to document the humanitarian mission, U.S. First Lady Melania Trump announced.

title: Farmers PAC behind election attack ads against GOP
body:
Polls show tight races in more rural states as midterms near
A political group dedicated to supporting farmers is pouring millions of dollars into advertisements targeting Republican candidates over policies that have hurt agricultural communities, including the rising cost of living driven in part by President Donald Trump's tariffs and the war in Iran .
The American Meat Producers Association's political action committee has spent roughly $2.9 million on ads targeting Republicans in Iowa, Colorado, Pennsylvania, and Wisconsin, according to a report from Reuters. It is the latest sign that the economic fallout from the administration's policies has become more and more of a political vulnerability for the GOP, which is now facing the prospect of losing both the House and Senate in next week’s midterm elections.
While according to its website the group behind the ads typically advocates for “policies that promote responsible production” and “protect fair and open meat markets,”which remain a focus of this campaign, some of the ads in the recent blitz target Trump’s foreign policy.
"These ads point out that certain lawmakers have voting records that have hurt farmers," Holly Bice, the group’s president, told Reuters.
“[F]armers and ranchers don't experience policy one bill at a time,” she added.
It is unclear who the donors behind the ad campaign are. The AMPA PAC is not transparent about its donors. Reuters says the group’s president told them it was “supported by farmers, meat companies and ‘people who care about family farming,’” but did not disclose more details. The group has also funded advertisements for two Republican candidates who share their views on congressional legislation related to animal welfare.
The advertisements are part of a broader effort by Democratic candidates and party-aligned groups to home in on the Iran war as a major campaign issue, and tie it to rising living costs ahead of the midterms. A recent Associated Press analysis found that Iran-related television ads had aired more than 43,000 times in competitive congressional races between September 1 and October 14, at an estimated cost of $42 million. The AP found that a majority of the 50 races they analyzed had advertisements focusing on the conflict.
“Of the 65 unique Iran-themed ads identified by the AP, 61 of them stressed household cost-of-living messages such as rising prices for fuel and other items,” according to the report.
American farmers have been particularly hit by the war’s economic fallout, with soaring fuel and fertilizer prices driving up production costs.
Partly as a result, the midterm races in swing states with large agricultural economies are on track to be closer than expected when voters head to the polls next week. Even some deep-red states with large farming constituencies now look more like toss-ups with only a few days left before the election.
Last month, the Iowa Farmers Union endorsed all five Democrats running in federal elections in the state, the first time the group had made any kind of endorsement in a federal race in decades .
After Trump announced his fuel relief program that will only kick in after votes are counted, the union defended its move, saying that instead of “a Band-Aid response now, 2 weeks before the election,” the president needs to “conclude the war without sacrificing our farmers’ bottom lines.” The political arm of the larger and more powerful Iowa Farm Bureau has maintained its record of supporting Republican candidates, though it has notably declined to endorse the GOP nominee for governor for the first time in 16 years.
Regardless, Trump’s popularity among these communities appears to be suffering. Polling from Reuters/Ipsos shows that Trump’s approval rating among rural Americans has slipped from 61% last October to 45% earlier this month.
