title: Hezbollah explosives case continues to roil Lebanese politics as ministers boycott cabinet meeting
body: At least four Lebanese ministers are boycotting a cabinet meeting on Thursday in protest of the state's delay in referring Hezbollah to the Judicial Council over the Iran-backed group's attempts to traffic hundreds of kilograms of explosives into Beirut, according to statements by the officials and media reports.Hezbollah has acknowledged that the explosives were theirs, but said they were intended for use against Israel.The shipment's purpose remains under investigation amid concerns among Lebanese officials that the explosives could threaten domestic security and potentially be used in political assassinations.According to Asharq Al-Awsat, Judge Claude Ghanem, the government commissioner to the Permanent Military Court, was expected to receive on Thursday the findings of investigations conducted by the Directorate of Intelligence of the Lebanese Army, as well as the Information Branch (intelligence, counterterrorism, and criminal investigation unit of the Internal Security Forces), paving the way for charges against suspects whose involvement has been established.Investigators identified seven suspects, including the two men found in the vehicle carrying the explosives who remain in custody.The Lebanese Forces (LF) party ministers, led by its president, Samir Geagea, announced that they would not attend Thursday's cabinet session, protesting what they described as delays in referring the case to the Judicial Council.In a statement on X/Twitter, Geagea criticized the government's handling of the case, arguing that the ministers' absence from the meeting did not mean they would stop challenging the government from within. He also criticized Hezbollah, describing it as an organization operating outside the law.Agenda set to focus on waste management, not explosives caseThe cabinet agenda was set to focus on waste management, despite calls by several ministers, including Foreign Minister Youssef Raggi, Displaced Persons, Technology, and Artificial Intelligence Minister Kamal Shehadeh, Energy Minister Joe Saddi, Industry Minister Joe Issa El Khoury, and Justice Minister Adel Nassar, to refer the explosives case to the Judicial Council.The cabinet had postponed a decision on the referral, pending further investigation, amid disagreements over the timing and handling of the case. Justice Minister Adel Nassar has continued to argue that it should be referred to the Judicial Council, not the military courts, warning that it goes beyond the transportation and storage of explosives and poses a threat to national security and civil peace.Nassar told Asharq al-Aswat that the transportation and storage of the explosives endangered Lebanese lives and that Hezbollah's acknowledgment of ownership, alongside its stated intention to use the shipment on a “new support front,” was an admission that Hezbollah intended to continue placing Lebanese national security at risk.Previous reports said that the postponement of the referral had resulted from discussions among Parliamentary Speaker Nabih Berri, President Joseph Aoun, and Prime Minister Nawaf Salam.

title: Bank of Russia sets official dollar rate at 80.68 rubles for October 30
body:
MOSCOW, October 29. /TASS/. The Bank of Russia set the official dollar rate at 80.6761 rubles for October 30, down 19.03 kopecks against the previous indicator.
The official euro rate was reduced by 34.93 kopecks to 89.8167 rubles. The official yuan rate is fixed at 12.0844 rubles, up 0.28 kopecks.
The Central Bank said earlier it would fix official dollar and euro rates against the ruble on the basis of reports of banks on results of transactions in the over-the-counter currency market.

title: Fresh snow brings hope to Okanagan ski resorts as El Niño looms
body:
Fresh snow brings hope to Okanagan ski resorts as a super El Niño looms.
People across the Okanagan woke up to a welcome sight this week: fresh snow on the surrounding mountains, offering an early taste of winter.
At Big White Ski Resort, skiers are already enjoying the fresh powder, with excitement building ahead of the upcoming season.
But while the early snowfall is encouraging, questions remain about what the weather will bring in the months ahead.
El Niño, a climate pattern caused by warmer waters in the tropical Pacific Ocean, can influence weather around the world, including across British Columbia. It typically occurs every two to seven years as part of a natural cycle of warming and cooling ocean temperatures in the Pacific.
With a potentially strong event developing, warmer-than-normal conditions could pose challenges for ski resorts trying to build a solid snowpack.
“We’ve had a couple of light snow years the last couple of years,” said Trevor Hanna, Big White’s vice-president of hospitality.
The impact of El Niño varies by region, but coastal ski resorts could face particular challenges if warmer temperatures push freezing levels higher. When temperatures rise above zero degrees Celsius, precipitation that might otherwise fall as snow can arrive as rain, slowing the formation of the snowpack needed to sustain ski runs.
In the Okanagan, however, locals are hoping freezing levels stay low enough to keep temperatures below zero, allowing snowfall to build the snowpack needed for a successful ski season.
Weather expert Peter Quinlan says sustained cold temperatures are important for building that base.
“We can’t have above normal temperatures because then that snowpack won’t form and in turn we will have a shorter ski season,” Quinlan said.
For Big White, getting enough snow on the ground is a key step toward opening day. The resort says it needs about 70 to 80 centimetres of snow to safely open some runs, with around 100 centimetres being ideal.
Despite the uncertainty, Hanna says recent conditions have given the resort reason to be optimistic.
Big White is scheduled to open Nov. 26, following a delayed opening last season, when the resort opened about a week later than planned.
“We’re hopefully going to open up on time or early this year and the indications the last few days are positive,” Hanna said.
For now, skiers will be watching the forecast and hoping the recent snowfall is a sign of more winter weather to come. and that temperatures stay cold enough to keep the snow on the mountains.

title: Ethiopia invites Russian universities to cooperate on AI — country’s Prime Minister
body:
MOSCOW, October 29. /TASS/. Ethiopia has invited Russian universities to collaborate on artificial intelligence (AI), including the development of technologies tailored to the national languages of African countries, Ethiopian Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed announced at the plenary session of the third Russia-Africa Summit.
"We have already established a university in Addis Ababa focused on the use of artificial intelligence and information. We invite Russian universities to join us in this endeavor," he said.
According to the Prime Minister, developing homegrown technologies is crucial for ensuring the technological sovereignty of African states.
"We believe it is essential to create tools in the languages of our own peoples," Abiy Ahmed emphasized, noting that African nations should independently define principles for information use and technology deployment.
The Prime Minister also suggested that Russian companies leverage special economic zones in Africa to access the continent's markets.
"Russian companies can participate in the activities within Africa’s special economic zones to bring their products to the continent," he stated, also advocating for simplified cross-border payments and expanded economic ties.
The head of the Ethiopian government underscored the need to transition from agreements to tangible results, adding that Ethiopia highly values Russia’s commitment to the partnership and intends to fulfill its obligations.
The Prime Minister also identified food security as one of Ethiopia’s top development priorities, noting the country's interest in using modern agricultural technologies to boost production efficiency and reduce food losses.

title: West ready to provoke coups anywhere, including Africa — Russian presidential adviser
body:
MOSCOW, October 29. /TASS/. Western countries are prepared to provoke military coups anywhere in the world, including Africa, where they are stoking tensions and posing direct military threats, Russian Presidential Adviser Anton Kobyakov, who also serves as executive secretary of the organizing committee for the summit of heads of state and government of Gas Exporting Countries Forum (GECF) members, said.
"The West uses various means to create tensions, or even a direct military threat, in virtually any part of Africa. It is prepared to provoke coups in any part of the world, not just in Africa. We see this happening everywhere," he told a briefing at the Russia National Center.
He added that military and technical cooperation has been and remains a key element of Russia’s ties with African countries, including efforts to protect joint projects in the modern era.

title: 154 students hospitalised over suspected drug reaction in Katsina
body: One hundred and fifty-four students of Government Science Secondary School, Batagarawa, Katsina State, were hospitalised following a suspected adverse reaction to praziquantel tablets administered to treat bilharzia. The incident occurred on Monday, according to a statement issued on Wednesday by the Katsina State Police Command’s Public Relations Officer, Abubakar Sadiq Aliyu. Aliyu said the students reportedly developed symptoms of an adverse drug reaction after receiving the tablets from the school authorities. Praziquantel is used to treat schistosomiasis, also known as bilharzia, a parasitic disease associated with contact with freshwater contaminated by the parasites. The police spokesman said the affected students were taken to hospital for treatment, with no casualties or deaths recorded. He added that the remaining 25 students, who had been kept in hospital for further medical attention, had also been treated and discharged. According to him, all the affected students were in good health and had been reunited with their families and schoolmates. The Commissioner of Police, Ali Umar Fage, thanked members of the public for their cooperation and calmness during the incident. He urged residents to refrain from spreading unverified reports and rumours, assuring them that the command would continue to protect lives and property across the state. The post 154 students hospitalised over suspected drug reaction in Katsina appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: Revenues of Russian IT companies reach $73.8 bln in H1 2026 — PM
body:
MOSCOW, October 29. /TASS/. The revenue of accredited IT companies for the first six months of 2026 amounted to 6 trillion rubles ($73.8 bln), Russian Prime Minister Mikhail Mishustin said in a video address to the participants of the Kazan Digital Week - 2026 International Forum.
"At the end of last year, the revenue of accredited IT companies approached eight trillion rubles ($98.5 bln), which is almost 1.5 times more than the previous period, and it continues to increase. For the first six months of the current year, this figure has already reached 6 trillion rubles," the prime minister said.
Over the past 6 years, the share of the IT sector in the country's gross domestic product has more than doubled, Mishustin noted. In Russia, the registry of domestic software is expanding, with the number of registered solutions counting in the tens of thousands. Businesses and state corporations are increasingly using them in key sectors of the economy, which helps reduce dependence on foreign suppliers and optimize production processes, he stressed.
In the current situation with external restrictions, it is necessary to more dynamically expand the lineup of domestic software, cloud services, and industrial systems, while simultaneously accelerating the launch of competitive technologies, the prime minister noted. This will help improve people's quality of life, as well as address economic and social challenges both in the regions and across the country as a whole, Mishustin added.

title: Tinubu Departs For Makkah, To Pray For Nation’s Peace, Stability
body: Deji Elumoye in Abuja President Bola Tinubu on Thursday afternoon departed the nation’s capital, Abuja for Makkah, Saudi Arabia, to perform Umrah pilgrimage. During the exercise also known as lesser Hajj, Tinubu will offer prayers for Nigeria’s peace, national unity, stability and sustained development. The president’s plane, Nigeria Air Force 1, took off from the presidential wing of the Nnamdi Azikiwe International Airport, Abuja, at approximately 2:20 p.m, after a brief departure ceremony attended by state governors and some top government officials who were on ground to see him off. Ahead of his departure, the Saudi Arabian Ambassador to Nigeria, Yousef Bin Mohammed Al-Balawi, presented the president with a Bisht, a traditional Arabian ceremonial cloak, on behalf of the Crown Prince of Saudi Arabia. Also on ground at the airport to see the president off were Secretary to the Government of the Federation, Senator George Akume; Kwara State Governor, Abdulrahman Abdulrazaq; his Yobe and Borno States counterparts, Mai Mala Buni; and Babagana Zulum respectively. Others were Governors of Kaduna, Uba Sani; Jigawa, Umar Namadi; Ahmad Aliyu Sokoto; Attorney-General of the Federation (AGF) and Minister of Justice, Prince Lateef Fagbemi; Coordinating Minister of Health and Social Welfare, Professor Muhammad Ali Pate; and the member representing Ikorodu Federal Constituency in the House of Representatives, Hon Babajimi Benson. The Nigerian Ambassador to Mexico, Honduras, Guatemala and Nicaragua, Ambassador Reno Omokri, and Director of Protocol at the Federal Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Ambassador Ibrahim Sule Dan Agundi, also attended the departure ceremony. Presidential spokesperson, Bayo Onanuga, had on Wednesday confirmed the planned journey via a statement issued indicating that President Tinubu was due back in Nigeria next week upon completion of the religious exercise. Tinubu’s visit will provide him an opportunity for spiritual reflection and devotion, while he undertakes the religious rites associated with Umrah and seeking divine guidance and blessings for Nigerians.

title: Lawmakers Vow to Block Use of Training Ship Golden Bear for Deportations
body:
Essential news coupled with the finest maritime content sourced from across the globe.
Two California lawmakers are demanding that the Trump administration abandon reported plans to use ships for mass deportations, including the former Cal Poly Maritime Academy training vessel Golden Bear .
Reps. John Garamendi (D-Calif.) and Salud Carbajal (D-Calif.) sent a letter to Department of Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin opposing the proposal, warning that deportations by sea would present major operational, safety and legal challenges while costing taxpayers millions of dollars.
The letter follows an October 8 report by The New York Times that the administration was considering using ships to transport migrants to Central and South America. The discussions reportedly included the 500-foot Golden Bear , as well as ferries and potentially other vessels.
The proposal remains preliminary, and no decision has been announced to use the Golden Bear or any other ship for deportations.
“Mark my words, Donald Trump, Markwayne Mullin, and ICE will never use the Golden Bear for their mass deportation agenda,” Garamendi said in an October 28 statement.
“Not only is deporting migrants by ship impractical, but it’s also deeply inhumane,” he added.
The Golden Bear recently completed its final training voyage after 30 years of service at the California maritime academy. The vessel, originally built as the U.S. Navy oceanographic survey ship USNS Maury , has been used to provide hands-on training for generations of merchant marine officers.
The ship is now being retired from academy service and returned to the U.S. Maritime Administration (MARAD), making its potential availability for another federal mission a point of contention.
Cal Poly Maritime Academy is awaiting its replacement training vessel, Golden State , part of MARAD’s National Security Multi-Mission Vessel program.
According to the Times, the administration has also explored obtaining other vessels, including ships based in Europe, for possible deportation operations.
The proposed voyages could take several days to reach destinations such as El Salvador, Honduras and Venezuela, compared with hours by air. They would also require substantial security personnel and arrangements for housing, feeding and supervising migrants throughout the passage.
The lawmakers warned that those requirements could drive costs into the millions of dollars per voyage. Questions also remain about the legal authority to conduct such operations and the conditions under which migrants would be held aboard ships.
Carbajal, the ranking Democrat on the House Transportation and Infrastructure Committee’s Coast Guard and Maritime Transportation Subcommittee, warned that using vessels for immigration detention could create additional oversight problems.
“ICE already operates without sufficient transparency or public accountability, and deploying maritime vessels as floating prisons will only open the door to potentially more abuses,” Carbajal said.
The dispute also raises questions about diverting federal maritime assets and resources toward immigration enforcement.
Garamendi argued that the administration’s previous use of military resources for deportation operations has already affected military readiness and warned that using ships could similarly strain U.S. sealift capabilities.
Both lawmakers have previously challenged the administration’s use of military facilities, personnel and aircraft for immigration enforcement, including deportation flights from Travis Air Force Base in California.
For now, there is no indication that the Golden Bear has been formally assigned to a deportation mission or that any maritime deportation operations have been authorized. But Garamendi pledged to use congressional oversight to prevent the ship from being used for that purpose.

title: Russia to Extend Diesel Export Ban, Use Quotas to Fulfill U.S. Deal, Sources Say
body:
Russia will extend its diesel export ban until the end of the year while allowing some companies to ship fuel under a quota system to meet its new export commitment to the U.S., two people familiar with the discussions told Reuters.
Moscow and Washington agreed a diesel supply deal after Presidents Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump spoke by phone earlier this month. The energy ceasefire between Russia and Ukraine announced alongside the agreement has allowed Moscow to increase fuel production. At the same time, fuel shortages earlier this year have prompted the government to maintain tight controls on oil product exports.
Deputy Prime Minister Alexander Novak said on Tuesday that three tankers carrying Russian diesel to export markets were already under way and that a fourth would sail on Oct. 28.
Novak also said Russian refineries were recovering quickly from repairs. The sources said refinery utilization had risen 25% at the end of October from the start of the month after drone attacks on facilities subsided.
Under the current diesel export ban, the government permits limited exports through a quota system. Those quotas will quadruple from October levels to 2 million metric tons, or about 0.5 million barrels per day, in November, the sources said. Shipments under existing intergovernmental agreements will also continue.
The Energy Ministry did not respond to a request for comment.
The current ban on diesel exports is due to expire on Oct. 31.
In October, the government exempted several refiners from the ban and granted them export quotas totaling 0.5 million tons, the sources said. A new government order expected in early November would expand the list of exempt refiners and set new export limits. If the quotas are used up quickly, the government could consider increasing them further, the sources added.
Nominal diesel production in Russia exceeds domestic consumption by about 40%. As refineries return to normal operating rates, they will need export outlets to prevent a domestic glut.

title: Borno Parents Seek Tinubu’s Intervention As 78 Children, Teacher Remain in Captivity
body: Amina Hassan in Abuja Parents of Margi community in Askira/Uba Local Government Area of Borno State have appealed to President Bola Tinubu to intensify efforts to secure the release of 78 schoolchildren and a teacher abducted from Mussa and Lassa communities in separate incidents. Speaking at a press briefing in Abuja on Thursday, the Chairman of the Margi community, Malla Gadzama, said 42 children were abducted from Mussa on May 15, 2026, while 36 children and a teacher were taken from Lassa on June 29, during the period of the National Examinations Council (NECO) examinations. The community said the victims had remained in captivity for months despite repeated appeals to the government and other relevant authorities. Another community member, Frank Kudla, said the abductors had communicated with the government but had not contacted the victims’ families directly. He noted that the community understood that the government was the only party aware of the kidnappers’ demands, leaving the families without direct information about the situation. “We asked the government to resolve quickly so that our children can be released,” he said. Kudla added that the families had received assurances from the Borno State Government that the children would be returned, but they were still awaiting their release months later. Gadzama said the community had previously held press conferences in Maiduguri and at the National Assembly to draw attention to the abductions, but the efforts had yet to secure the victims’ freedom. The community’s secretary, Gambo Kadiri, expressed concern that President Tinubu might not have been fully briefed about the situation, although the community could not establish whether the president had received information about the incidents. Kadiri said the community had also written to the National Security Adviser (NSA) but had yet to receive a response. He called on the relevant authorities to treat the matter with urgency and sustain efforts to secure the victims’ release. Kudla said attempts to secure an audience with the Senate President and other National Assembly authorities had also been unsuccessful, prompting the community to hold another press briefing to draw attention to the matter. The community said it might consider a procession to the National Assembly to press lawmakers to engage the Presidency and security agencies over the continued captivity of the children and their teacher. The community called for coordinated rescue efforts involving federal and state authorities, as well as regular communication with the affected families without compromising the safety of the victims. It also urged the government to establish a designated liaison arrangement through which families could receive verified information and raise concerns about the situation. The community called for psychosocial and welfare support for the affected families, alongside medical care, rehabilitation and educational assistance for the children upon their return. It further urged the authorities to strengthen security around vulnerable schools and communities to prevent future abductions. Appealing to civil society organisations, religious and traditional leaders, professional associations, women’s and youth groups, and the media, the community urged sustained public attention to the victims’ plight. It also cautioned journalists against publishing information that could endanger the children or compromise rescue efforts.

title: Claude users say their accounts were banned after verification showed a Russian passport
body: Users of the Claude chatbot say Anthropic, the service’s developer, has blocked their accounts after they completed identity verification using Russian documents. The complaints appeared on Reddit , on X , and on Telegram . Users said Claude required them to complete verification through a service called Persona. Why they were asked to do this is unclear. Persona requires users to select the region of their document, upload a photo of it, and complete a facial scan. Users say the ban happens immediately after they upload a Russian passport. The ban is issued even to users who do not live in Russia but lack a residency permit elsewhere. One now-blocked Claude user said on Reddit that he is a Russian citizen living in New Zealand on a four-year visa ( unlike Russia, New Zealand appears on Anthropic’s list of countries where Claude is officially available ). He said he used the paid version of the chatbot for both work and personal purposes, as well as Claude Code . Anthropic blocked the user’s account immediately after he uploaded his Russian international passport, without explanation. The company had charged his account for a subscription payment two days before the block. In the comments, other users with Russian documents living in Georgia and Armenia described similar problems. A user in Georgia published a letter from Anthropic’s security team, which said he had been banned for violating the chatbot’s usage policy but did not specify what he had violated: Our automated systems detected a large number of signals associated with your account that violate our Usage Policy. These signals were, in turn, reviewed by our team to confirm the system’s findings. As a result, we have revoked your access to Claude. Another user said that after uploading his Russian passport, he was blocked and could no longer send new queries to the chatbot. He could only export his chat data. He was unable to restore his account through an appeal. Users with Chinese citizenship have faced similar checks. China is also not on the list of countries where Claude is officially available, though some users with Chinese passports have managed to pass verification successfully. In early October, it was also reported that users from regions not supported by Claude, including Russia, who were bypassing the restrictions with a VPN, had faced blocks. What exactly is driving the current blocks remains unclear. Anthropic has not commented on the complaints. Claude itself said it cannot verify the authenticity of users’ posts. The company’s policy does not mention restrictions based on nationality or citizenship. It lists the countries and regions where Anthropic’s products are officially supported. In countries not on the list, the products are “not supported,” meaning people in those countries or regions cannot use the company’s services. title: Kaduna swears in 3 new commissioners, 18 advisers
body: The Deputy Governor of Kaduna State, Dr Hadiza Balarabe, has urged newly appointed political office holders to discharge their duties with integrity, courage and fairness, irrespective of political, ethnic or religious affiliations. Balarabe gave the charge on Thursday while swearing in three commissioners, 18 special advisers, a deputy chief of staff (administration) and a counsellor on infrastructure. She reminded the appointees that the oaths of allegiance and office, as prescribed by the Seventh Schedule of the Constitution, were binding commitments to God and the people of Kaduna State. “The Oath of Allegiance and Oath of Office are not mere words because they bind you before God and the people of Kaduna State to serve faithfully,” she said. The deputy governor described the ceremony as a call to service, stressing that leadership was a responsibility that must be exercised with humility and accountability. She said the appointments reflected Governor Uba Sani’s confidence in the appointees’ abilities, experience and capacity to contribute to the state’s development. Balarabe urged them to see their appointments not merely as recognition of past achievements but as a challenge to deliver better results for the people. On the timing of the appointments during the election season, she said governance must continue irrespective of political activities. “Elections have their calendar, but the needs of our people do not wait for it,” she said. According to her, the administration remains committed to fulfilling its promises and building a peaceful, prosperous and inclusive state where no community is left behind. She said communities previously divided by conflict were reconciling through the Kaduna Peace Model, while farmlands were reopening and markets becoming active. Balarabe added that more than 500 schools previously closed because of insecurity had reopened, while over 300,000 out-of-school children returned to classrooms in 2025 alone. She also said hundreds of classrooms had been constructed or renovated and thousands of teachers trained. In the health sector, the deputy governor said 255 primary healthcare centres had been upgraded to Level Two, while improvements were ongoing in general hospitals. She further disclosed that about 160 road projects, covering approximately 1,335 kilometres, were opening up communities across the state’s 23 local government areas. According to her, the planned light rail and bus rapid transit projects would also contribute to the state’s future development. Balarabe charged the appointees to serve as a bridge between the government and the grassroots, urging them to demonstrate their commitment through measurable results. “Let your performance be the argument that convinces the sceptical and the proof that justifies the trust of the supportive,” she said. The commissioners sworn in were Benjamin Dalhat Solomon Kure for Sports Development, Amina Akilu Dalhat for Special Duties I, and Abdullahi Garba Abbas for Special Duties II. Dr Haliru Musa Soba was sworn in as Deputy Chief of Staff (Administration), while Engr Balarabe Muhammad Bello became Counsellor on Infrastructure. Eighteen special advisers were also sworn in at the ceremony.

title: State Duma Passes Record Defense Spending Budget in First Reading
body:
Lawmakers in the lower house State Duma passed the first reading of a draft three-year federal budget on Thursday, approving record defense spending alongside a new wave of tax hikes designed to fund the rising costs of the war in Ukraine.
The proposed budget allocates 17.1 trillion rubles ($202.6 billion) to national defense, accounting for over a third of total federal expenditures. Combined with a 7. 6% increase in national security and policing, security forces will account for 44% of total government spending, totaling 21. 3 trillion rubles ($262. 1 billion).
“All questions related to security, defense and providing everything necessary for participants of the special military operation and their families have been resolved,” State Duma Speaker Vyacheslav Volodin said during a discussion of the bill.
To offset soaring military expenditures, the draft budget redirects funding away from civilian sectors. Spending on economic support and healthcare will each drop by 3%, while funding for social support falls by 6% and housing and utilities take an 8% cut.
Russia is relying on broad revenue extraction measures to cover its spending priorities. The draft proposal imposes a 22% value-added tax (VAT) on cross-border online retail, alongside a small customs fee on small international packages.
It also introduces a progressive tax scale reaching up to 22% on passive personal income, a 35% levy on dividend transfers to non-resident Type C accounts and a 30% tax on excess corporate profits in the mining and metallurgy sectors.
Finance Minister Anton Siluanov said the budget draft preserves the key priorities of “fulfilling social obligations to our citizens, addressing the tasks of the special military operation, ensuring victory… and achieving the president’s national development goals.”
The draft bill passed with 372 votes in favor, 51 abstentions, and zero opposing votes. It now advances to its second reading before going to the upper-house Federation Council for a vote, after which it will require a final signature from President Vladimir Putin.

title: La General Hospital project expected to be completed by end of 2027 – Health Minister
body: Health Minister Kwabena Mintah Akandoh says the La General Hospital project, valued at €50 million, is expected to be completed by the end of 2027, with about €15 million paid so far. He gave the timeline during a visit to the project site on Thursday, October 29, 2026, to assess construction progress and identify any challenges that could affect the completion deadline. Mr Akandoh said construction was progressing, adding that the contractor could not cite delayed payments as an excuse for slowing down work, as the government had processed the latest interim payment certificate. “This is quite an impressive development, but they can speed up so that we can beat the deadline,” he said. “The whole project is 50 million euros and we’ve paid about 15 million euros. It includes the hospital equipment, and so now they are at the civil end. When they finish, then they will do the installation and that’s where we also pay as and when they install. The completion date we are looking at is by the end of 2027,” he added. The Minister explained that the project cost covers both construction and hospital equipment, with further payments to be made as equipment is installed. He also stressed the need to prioritise the hospital’s emergency unit to help address the persistent problem of patients being turned away from health facilities because of inadequate emergency beds. Mr Akandoh cited Korle Bu Teaching Hospital, which has a capacity of more than 1,000 beds but approximately 65 emergency beds, as an example of the gap between general bed capacity and emergency care needs. He suggested that emergency beds should account for at least 10 per cent of a hospital’s total bed capacity, noting that the country’s growing population required health facilities to plan adequately for emergency cases. “We learn from experience. Going forward, we correct what we have come to meet,” he said, emphasising the need to improve emergency care provision in new and existing health facilities.

title: Denying medical care over language goes against Hippocratic oath — Russia’s envoy to OSCE
body:
VIENNA, October 29. /TASS/. The denial of medical care to Russian-speaking patients because they do not speak Ukrainian is unacceptable and goes against the Hippocratic oath, said Dmitry Polyansky, Russia’s Permanent Representative to the OSCE, commenting on a statement from Yelena Ivanovskaya, the language Ombudsman of Ukraine, that medical workers are allegedly not obliged to treat patients who speak Russian.
"Can anyone sitting here imagine not receiving treatment in Viennese medical institutions just because they will not be able to explain themselves in German? I can assure you that any Ukrainian doctor speaks Russian much better than an Austrian speaks English," he told a regular meeting of the OSCE Permanent Council. The diplomat's speech is available to TASS.
According to the diplomat, telling Ukrainian medical workers this is akin to "bald-faced Nazism that goes against the Hippocratic oath."

title: Former SGF Boss Mustapha Calls for Review of Public Servants’ Salary Structure to Tackle Corruption
body: Linus Aleke in Abuja Former Secretary to the Government of the Federation (SGF), Boss Mustapha, has called for a review of the salary structure of public servants in Nigeria to reflect current economic realities, address the rising cost of living and correct abnormal disparities in the remuneration of Permanent Secretaries, Directors, Ministers, Directors-General and other heads of government agencies. He emphasised the need for a fair and sustainable remuneration system that would improve workers’ welfare, boost morale, help tackle corruption within the service and enhance productivity across the public service. Mustapha made the call while delivering the keynote address at the Colloquium and Unveiling of the Council of Retired Federal Permanent Secretaries and Heads of the Civil Service of the Federation (CORFEPS) Journal on Public Policy and Governance at the Rotunda, Tafawa Balewa House, Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Abuja. The event, which marked the beginning of CORFEPS Week 2026, was themed “Navigating the Headwinds of Governance: Centrality of the Civil Service”. Mustapha said the National Salaries, Incomes and Wages Commission, in collaboration with the Federal Civil Service and the Office of the Head of the Civil Service of the Federation, must address the disparities in public sector remuneration. “The National Salaries, Incomes and Wages Commission has an important role in remuneration options. I sometimes feel a little bit embarrassed when I see budget estimates that come out of successive governments over and over, and they are running into trillions of naira and the people that are supposed to manage those trillions of naira earn peanuts,” he said. He questioned the rationale behind entrusting public servants with enormous responsibilities without adequately remunerating them, describing the situation in which some agency heads earn more than Ministers and Permanent Secretaries combined as abnormal. Citing Singapore’s remuneration structure, he noted that its Prime Minister earned $2.6 million annually, compared with the $400,000 earned by the US President, Donald Trump. He attributed Singapore’s leadership structure to its rigorous recruitment process, which draws many leaders from the civil service. In a goodwill message, the Chairman of the Federal Civil Service Commission, Prof. Tunji Olaopa, supported Mustapha’s position, stressing that policies could only be as effective as the workforce responsible for implementing them. “Professionalising the civil service is therefore not rhetoric. It involves deep talent management reforms and investment in capacity development, training and retraining,” he said. Olaopa noted that retaining talented personnel remained a major challenge despite the service’s ability to attract highly capable individuals. He disclosed that he had discussed the issue with the Salaries and Wages Commission, adding that ongoing deliberations could help advance civil service reforms. Declaring the colloquium open, Vice-President Kashim Shettima, represented by the Special Adviser to the President on Power Infrastructure in the Office of the Vice-President, Sadiq Wanka, described the civil service as central to national development and the state’s ability to fulfil its obligations to citizens. He said the Renewed Hope Agenda reflected the administration’s response to Nigeria’s economic and social challenges, adding that the government had shifted its focus from the number of policies announced and committees inaugurated to whether public interventions solved problems and improved lives. He cited compulsory ministerial deliverables coordinated by the Central Delivery Coordinating Unit (CDCU) and ministerial briefings as mechanisms for assessing government performance. “We are committed to providing positive answers to everyday questions that the average Nigerians want answer to, such as, Are services reaching the people for whom they are intended? Are public funds generating value? Are decisions timely and evidence-informed? Can citizens see and trust the results?” he asked. The Head of the Civil Service of the Federation, Mr Olumuyiwa Enitan Abel, said the colloquium provided a platform for intellectual engagement, professional reflection and the exchange of ideas on strengthening governance and repositioning the civil service for greater effectiveness. He stressed that effective governance depended on the civil service’s ability to provide objective advice, implement policies efficiently and remain accountable to citizens. Earlier, the National Chairman of CORFEPS, Alhaji Yayale Ahmed, said the council was established to enable retired Permanent Secretaries and former Heads of the Civil Service to contribute their experience, professional knowledge and institutional memory to national development. “Our retirement from formal office does not diminish our commitment to Nigeria. Rather, it provides an opportunity to reflect on our collective experience, draw lessons from our service and offer constructive advice on matters of public policy and administration. This commitment is captured in our motto: ‘Continuing Patriotic Service’,” he said. Ahmed added that CORFEPS continued to organise policy dialogues, seminars and conferences, conduct research and provide advice on matters of national importance. “We believe that those who have served the nation at the highest levels of public administration have a responsibility to make their accumulated knowledge available to succeeding generations,” he said.

When it was revealed earlier this month that Withings would require new users to subscribe to a Withings Plus subscription to sync heath data from the company’s devices to third-party apps, Tom Anthony, who was already fed up with the Withings mobile app which they describe as a “bloated mess,” became motivated to “free” their scales. Anthony’s solution was to create an open-source project called YourOwnWeigh that reroutes your data away from Withings’ servers so it can be wirelessly synced to other apps and platforms for free.
You can read more about the project on GitHub , where you’ll also find quick-start guides on how to get YourOwnWeigh set up, but it mostly consists of a web app running on a server of your choice. If you don’t already operate your own, Anthony says YourOwnWeigh can run entirely on a free CloudFlare account given how little data it’s moving around.
The YourOwnWeigh web app handles several tasks, including using Bluetooth to update Withings scales with alternate firmware so they upload data to a non-Withings server you’ve configured. Instead of hosting a copy of Withings’ firmware, it’s downloaded and patched as needed. The web app also imports the scale’s current settings and existing user profiles, and downloads the health data generated by regular weigh-ins.
To get that data into Apple Health, Anthony used Apple Shortcuts to create a scheduled automation that pulls the Withings data off the alternate server and imports it into the app, but they’re hoping the community can come up with ways to expand the compatibility to other apps, including Google Health. YourOwnWeigh is also currently limited to just two older models of Withings’ scales. But assuming the firmware on newer models can be patched in a similar manner, expanding the project’s compatibility should be possible.

title: Rourke, Alexander lead CFL all-star selections
body:
TORONTO – Quarterbacks Nathan Rourke of the B.C. Lions and Davis Alexander of the Montreal Alouettes headline the respective divisional All-CFL teams.
The CFL unveiled the East and West squads Thursday. Voting was conducted by the Football Reporters of Canada, CFL head coaches and fans.
Winnipeg running back Brady Oliveira and Edmonton fullback/tight end Skyler Griffith were also named to the West squad. The receiving corps is made up of Saskatchewan’s KeeSean Johnson, Austin Mack of the Elks, B.C.’s Keon Hatcher Sr., Calgary’s Jalen Philpot and the Riders’ Kian Schaffer-Baker.
Saskatchewan centre Logan Ferland anchors an offensive line that includes guards Christy Nkanu of Calgary and Carter O’Donnell of Edmonton. The tackles are Jarell Broxton of Winnipeg and Jermarcus Hardrick of the Riders.
The defensive line consists of ends Clarence Hicks of Calgary and Malik Carney of Edmonton and tackles Jake Ceresna of Winnipeg and Jaylon Hutchings of the Stampeders.
B.C.’s Darnell Sankey anchors a linebacking corps that includes Saskatchewan’s Jameer Thurman and B.C.’s Deontai Williams.
Edmonton cornerbacks Tyrell Ford and J.J. Ross are in a secondary that also includes Winnipeg’s Evan Holm and Kordell Jackson of the Elks at halfback and B.C.’s Jackson Findlay at safety.
Kicker Vincent Blanchard and punter Jake Julien of the Elks join Winnipeg returner Trey Vaval _ named the CFL’s top special-teams player for a second year Thursday _ and Saskatchewan long-snapper Mike Benson on special teams.
Joining Alexander in the East backfield are teammates Travis Theis at running back and fullback/tight end Jacob Mason.
Montreal’s Tyson Philpot and Tyler Snead anchor a receiving corps that includes Toronto’s Damonte Coxie and David Ungerer III and Ottawa’s Ayden Eberhardt.
Toronto centre Peter Nicastro and guards Pier-Olivier Lestage of Montreal and Brandon Revenberg of Hamilton make up the East offensive line with tackles Nick Callender and Tiger Shanks of the Alouettes.
The defensive line consists of ends Shawn Lemon of Toronto and Phillip Ossai of Hamilton as well as tackles Mustafa Johnson of Montreal and Ralph Holley of the Argos.
Toronto’s Isaac Darkangelo and Adarius Pickett, along with Montreal’s Tyrice Beverette, make up the linebacking corps.
Montreal’s Lorenzo Burns and Toronto’s Benjie Franklin are the cornerbacks with Robert Kennedy III and Wesley Sutton, both of the Alouettes, at halfback and Ottawa’s Alonzo Addae at safety.
Montreal kicker José Maltos Díaz and Toronto punter James Burnip were the specialists. Janarion Grant of the Argos and Montreal long-snapper Louis-Philippe Bourassa rounded out the East special-teams unit.
The ’26 All-CFL Team will be announced Nov. 19.
This report by The Canadian Press was first published Oct. 29, 2026.

title: Iran wins Asian Judo Cup with eight medals
body:
TEHRAN, Oct. 29 (MNA) – Iran's national judo team claimed the Asian Cup championship after collecting eight medals across the men's and women's events in Jordan.
Iran's national judo team won the Asian Cup title in the combined men's and women's competition, collecting eight gold, silver and bronze medals to finish on top of the podium.
The Asian Judo Cup began on Wednesday with athletes from 20 countries competing in Jordan and ended on Thursday evening with Iran's men's and women's teams taking the title.
Iran's national judo teams were coached by Ayoub Rostami, Ehsan Bahramian and Masoumeh Jafari.

title: Fuel reserve volumes for public utilities sector above standard rates — Russian PM
body:
MOSCOW, October 29. /TASS/. Reserve volumes of diesel, fuel oil, and coal for the housing and public utilities sector in Russia have been established above the standard figures, Prime Minister Mikhail Mishustin said during a cabinet meeting.
"We have formed reserve volumes of diesel fuel, fuel oil, and coal exceeding the approved standard values. This is necessary to prepare power generation and public utilities businesses for potential loads, including peak ones," the prime minister said.
"Everything possible should be done to ensure that all facilities operate without interruption. The quality of life for people in both large cities and small settlements depends on this. And most importantly, the sustainable development of all sectors of the economy relies on it," he added.

title: MTN Bright Scholarship supports 500 students and teachers for 2026/2027 academic year
body: MTN Ghana has awarded scholarships to 500 students and teachers for the 2026/2027 academic year under its flagship MTN Bright Scholarship initiative, aimed at supporting brilliant but financially needy individuals to pursue their educational ambitions. The scholarship, spearheaded by the MTN Ghana Foundation, provides financial assistance to beneficiaries through tuition fees, hostel accommodation, stipends and laptops to support their academic work and research. The award ceremony brought together beneficiaries, guardians, academics and MTN officials to celebrate the opportunities created through the initiative. Senior Manager of MTN Scholarship, Robert Kuzoe, said the current cohort forms part of a three-year programme designed to support 500 beneficiaries annually, comprising 300 students and 200 teachers, with a focus on Science, Technology, Engineering and Mathematics (STEM) and related disciplines. “This is the second cohort that we are doing. And with each cohort, we give scholarships to 500 needy but brilliant students. Also, we’ve not left out teachers; we do the same for teachers. So, with the 500, we have 300 students and then 200 teachers who are also in the STEM areas. ”Now, the scholarship comes with tuition, hostel fees, a stipend, and also a laptop just for the students to be comfortable and be able to study hard and do their own research in school,” he asserted. Mr Kuzoe urged beneficiaries to make the most of the opportunity and use their education to contribute meaningfully to society. He said the scholarship is open to eligible applicants from both public and private universities, provided they fall within the designated STEM and STEAM categories. He added that the programme also seeks to encourage women to pursue science-related fields. “Applications are open to all universities, provided you find yourself within the STEM and STEAM categories. Women are also encouraged to find their way into the sciences. So it’s open to all, but it’s very competitive because you have to apply, you’ll be interviewed, you go to a shortlisting process,” he noted. According to Mr Kuzoe, more than 5,000 applications were received nationwide, with the number reduced to 1,200 during shortlisting before the final 500 beneficiaries were selected, highlighting the competitive nature of the programme. He explained that the annual allocation of 500 scholarships is intended to run for three years, after which MTN will consider the next steps for the initiative. For some beneficiaries, the scholarship represents a significant relief from the financial challenges that have threatened their education. A Level 400 student at the University for Development Studies (UDS), Gilbert Abongo, from the Bongo District in the Upper East Region, said he struggled to continue his education after completing senior high school more than a decade ago. Mr Abongo, who had long hoped to use education to change the circumstances of people in his hometown, said financial constraints forced him to combine his university studies with work at a kebab-selling business to support himself. “I was facing financial difficulties, and it wasn’t easy for me. I completed SHS ten years ago, but I never gave up. I had the opportunity to go to school. Things were not easy for me, so I spoke to a man who sells kebab at UDS to work with him, and he agreed. I was combining school with the job. When I was struggling, one of the beneficiaries of the MTN Bright Scholarship,” he said. The initiative forms part of the MTN Ghana Foundation’s broader efforts to expand access to education and develop skills in fields considered important for Ghana’s development, while easing the financial burden on students, teachers and their families. Meanwhile, Esther Quaye, a guardian whose sister benefited from the scholarship, described the award as a major relief for their family, which has been facing financial hardship. “I was very, very excited because our family is going through some hot shifts, and so it was a very huge relief that she won the award, especially with all the things that come with their accommodation, the tuition, and then the stipends and, most importantly, the laptop that they are getting; it’s really refreshing. It has brought some kind of relief to the family. So yes, we are very much happy about it,” she said.

title: NLC faults Tinubu’s fresh external loan request
body: By Olayinka Ajayi The Nigeria Labour Congress (NLC) has criticised President Bola Tinubu’s request to the National Assembly for approval to obtain fresh external loans of $20.5 billion and €1.45 billion, questioning the justification for continued borrowing. NLC President, Comrade Joe Ajaero, said the basis for the proposed loans was unclear, particularly in view of the Federal Government’s claims of increased revenue following the removal of petrol subsidy. Speaking on Channels Television’s The Morning Brief on Thursday, Ajaero challenged the government to explain why it continued to seek loans from international financial institutions despite the reported increase in revenue. “If you come out to tell us that the subsidy is gone, that you are making more money and then you are giving more money to states, what is the justification for continually borrowing from the International Monetary Fund and the World Bank and other agencies when there is enough money?” he asked. The labour leader argued that continued borrowing was worsening the country’s debt burden, adding that international financial institutions lending to Nigeria were not necessarily acting in the country’s best interests. He also cited rising crude oil prices, which he attributed to tensions in the Middle East, as another reason the government should reconsider its borrowing plans. “If the 2026 budget was prepared with crude oil price benchmarked at $70 per barrel and now sells above $100 per barrel due to the US-Iran crisis, should this country still be collecting loans?” Ajaero asked. He maintained that increased oil earnings and revenue accruing to oil-producing states should prompt the government to explain why additional external borrowing remained necessary. Ajaero, however, clarified that the NLC had no authority to approve or reject government loans, noting that such decisions rested with the relevant government institutions. He urged Nigerians and relevant agencies to demand greater accountability from the Federal Government over its borrowing plans. The NLC president also pointed to the role of the National Assembly, saying lawmakers could stop the proposed borrowing by rejecting the request for approval. He called for greater scrutiny of the loans and their justification, given the implications of mounting public debt for the country’s economy. The post NLC faults Tinubu’s fresh external loan request appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: The five issues that determine the Middle East's view of Israel's elections - analysis
body: With the votes mostly counted, Israel is now heading into a holding pattern, as Israeli parties must begin coalition talks. This could take weeks. As Israel waits, so does the Middle East. The view of Israel across the region is complex. Some countries are hostile to Israel, and they will remain hostile. Some openly say they don't care who wins Israel's elections. This kind of talking point is usual among those in the Palestinian Authority. However, the truth is that the region will be impacted by who comes out on top.Does the Middle East care who wins Israel's elections? Across the region, governments are watching the political developments in Israel.However, they are not waiting for a new Israeli government to decide their own policies. The Middle East has changed significantly since the October 7, 2023, Hamas attack on Israel and the conflicts that followed.Countries such as Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates, Egypt, Jordan, Turkey, and Iran have their own policies and concerns. These interests do not change because Israel has an election. Nevertheless, the role of Israel's next government could influence how these countries approach Jerusalem.There are five key issues that illustrate how the region views Israel's elections.The Board of Peace and the future of GazaThe first issue is Gaza. The US-backed Board of Peace has been around for around ten months. It seeks to advance a new peace concept for Gaza's future. However, questions remain about reconstruction, Hamas disarmament, security arrangements and the implementation of the ceasefire. Countries such as Egypt, Qatar and many others want to see Washington move forward. However, the Board appears to be waiting. Washington doesn't want to pressure Israel. On the other hand, the Trump administration could try to get things from a new government based on its endorsement of Israel's prime minister. The region wants to see progress, but the regional countries are also aware that the fundamental challenges will remain regardless of who leads Israel.A new Israeli government might approach the Board of Peace differently. However, it would still need to address Hamas, the future of Gaza's governance and Israel's security requirements.The more important question may be what Washington intends to do next. Regional governments know that the Trump administration remains central to the initiative. They are therefore watching Washington as closely as Jerusalem.The Abraham Accords and normalizationThe second issue is normalization. The Abraham Accords were signed in 2020, during Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's tenure. They reflected an attempt at a regional shift, particularly in the Gulf, where countries increasingly saw opportunities in economic and security cooperation with Israel.The UAE, Bahrain and Morocco have maintained relations with Israel despite the conflicts of recent years. Their interests in trade, technology and regional stability are important. However, it has been hard for Israel to attract new members. Some have suggested the US should pressure countries to join. Countries want to see progress on the Palestinian issues.Saudi Arabia presents a challenge. Riyadh has pursued its own regional diplomacy, including relations with Washington and efforts to reduce tensions with Iran. Normalization with Israel remains linked to broader Saudi interests, particularly the Palestinian issue. Saudi Arabia has also moved close to Turkey and Pakistan.A new Israeli government could make discussions easier, but Saudi Arabia is unlikely to abandon its conditions. The Abraham Accords demonstrated that countries in the region could pursue relations with Israel based on shared interests. The elections are unlikely to reverse that calculation.Is Iran worried about the elections?Iran is watching Israel's elections, but Tehran is likely to tread carefully. It knows about the messaging in Israel and the US about a resumption of strikes. Israel's current Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu shared an image of an Iranian nuclear strike on Israel prior to the election. He was also endorsed twice by US President Donald Trump.For decades, Israeli governments have viewed Iran's nuclear program, ballistic missiles, and regional proxies as major threats. This did not begin recently and will not change. Iran also knows this. The wars involving Iran, Israel and Iranian-backed groups have transformed the regional balance of power. Tehran must now assess its own military capabilities and its choice as to what to do next. Iran may hope that political uncertainty in Israel could constrain future Israeli operations. However, Iran may be surprised to find out that if it takes risks, it will still face Israel's determination. The larger issue for Iran is the relationship between Israel and the United States. Tehran's calculations depend heavily on Washington's policies, including sanctions, military deployments, and the possibility of further confrontation. The US could shift on whether it wants a deal depending on what happens in Jerusalem.Turkey-Israel tensions are not just about NetanyahuTurkey is another country where a change in Israeli leadership might improve the atmosphere without resolving the disputes. There is an increasing view among Israeli policymakers that Ankara represents a threat to Israel and a potential new adversary. One concept is that even if Iran is defeated, Turkey will become the next enemy.Relations between Ankara and Jerusalem have experienced repeated crises over the last two decades. Israel and Turkey both have had the same leader for most of the last two decades. Both leaders, Recep Tayyip Erdogan and Netanyahu, come from a more religious right-wing camp. Political change in either place could reduce tensions, but won't end them.Turkey's growing influence in Syria following the fall of the Assad regime in December 2024 has created another possible area of competition. Ankara wants a central role in shaping Syria's future, while Israel is concerned about threats emerging along its northern frontier.Turkey may welcome a new Israeli government, particularly if it either country adopts less confrontational rhetoric. However, Ankara will continue pursuing its interests in Syria and across the region. This includes Ankara's east Mediterranean policies. The challenge is whether Israel and Turkey can establish mechanisms to manage their competition and avoid a military confrontation.Syria, Jordan and the region's wait-and-see approachSyria illustrates why regional governments are likely to judge Israel by its actions rather than its election results.The new government in Damascus is seeking to consolidate control over the country, rebuild the economy and strengthen ties with neighboring states. It considered warming ties with Israel in 2025. However, Israeli leaders have made clear that they are not interested in a deal. The last real progress toward a deal was in January with US support.  The Iran war has postponed any real focus on Syria. What has replaced strategy are IDF tactics along the border.  Israel has also focused on security threats in southern Syria and the protection of the Druze community. A different Israeli government might pursue a flexible diplomatic approach toward Damascus. However, Israel's security concerns along the Golan Heights will remain.Jordan and Egypt face similar calculations. Both countries have maintained peace treaties with Israel through numerous changes of government. Their priorities include border security, regional stability, and preventing renewed conflict.Jordan is particularly focused on developments in the West Bank and Jerusalem, while Egypt remains central to diplomacy over Gaza. Jordan considers itself tied to the status quo of the Holy Sites in Jerusalem, for instance. It was very critical of Israel at the United Nations General Assembly this year. Egypt's president has sought to downplay tensions with Israel.This reflects a broader reality across the Middle East. Governments may prefer certain changes in Israel, but they have learned to be more cynical and pessimistic about the chance for change.The region is also increasingly focused on its own economic development, infrastructure projects, trade corridors and security partnerships. Israel is an important part of this region, but it does not determine every regional calculation. One concern countries have is that Israel's current government has been lashing out and that it has ambitions to become a kind of regional hegemon. This may be driving Saudi Arabia and other countries to rethink their strategy.In this sense, the Middle East's approach to Israel's elections is best described as “trust, but verify.” The region cares about the outcome, but it is not waiting for Israel to decide its future.

title: Ukraine’s territory is shrinking as Kiev indulges in military illusions — Mendel
body:
MOSCOW, October 29. /TASS/. Ukraine is losing territory amid the ongoing conflict while the authorities indulge in military illusions, Yulia Mendel, former press secretary to Vladimir Zelensky, stated.
"You can talk about any military illusions you want, but the reality is clear: Ukraine is getting smaller on the map, and so is the number of Ukrainians," she wrote on her X page.
According to Mendel, all the country’s authorities can offer under these circumstances is evacuation.
She has repeatedly criticized Zelensky for escalating the military conflict. According to Mendel, Ukrainians hate her former boss because he is sacrificing the lives of thousands of people for his own personal interests and refuses to make peace. As she has emphasized, Ukraine risks losing its independence and the nation itself unless it agrees to realistic negotiations to resolve the conflict.

title: Enugu govt, Humatrix partner to create 100,000 jobs through BPO
body:
The Enugu State Government and Humatrix Limited have signed a partnership agreement to establish a Business Process Outsourcing (BPO) hub in the state. The long-term target is to create over 100,000 jobs for young people and positioning Enugu as a leading destination for digital services in Nigeria and Africa.
The agreement, signed at Government House, Enugu, marks the implementation phase of the initiative, which aligns with Governor Peter Mbah’s economic diversification agenda, human capital development policy and drive to attract private investment.
Speaking at the ceremony, Director of Humatrix Limited, Dr Dakuku Peterside, said the company chose Enugu after assessing its investment climate, policy consistency and the state government’s commitment to economic transformation.
He said, “It was very easy for us to choose Enugu. Enugu is investing, and there is consistency. Most importantly, we have a supportive environment. These are core things any business would request to scale.”
Peterside disclosed that the company would commence operations with a 750-seat BPO centre, expand to over 2,000 seats within the first year and target 100,000 jobs within five years.
He explained that the initiative would go beyond direct employment by equipping young people with industry-relevant digital and technological skills, connecting them to employment opportunities and attracting global companies seeking skilled talent.
According to him, the state government had already provided a building for the take-off of the project, while recruitment and training opportunities would be opened to interested Enugu youths.
Peterside commended the government’s rigorous negotiation process, describing the diligence and thoroughness demonstrated by its multi-agency team as evidence of the seriousness with which Enugu approaches investment partnerships.
Also speaking, the Special Adviser to the Governor on MSME and Digital Economy, Mr Arinze Chilo-Offiah, said the partnership represented a significant step towards actualising the governor’s vision of growing Enugu’s economy from $4.4 billion to $30 billion.
He explained that the Enugu Talent City Initiative was designed to position the state as a leading digital services and outsourcing hub in Nigeria and Africa, attracting global companies, creating employment and enabling young people to work for international clients from Enugu.
The special adviser further disclosed that the state’s long-term ambition was to develop an outsourcing ecosystem with up to 300,000 seats by 2031, building on the initial 750-seat BPO centre and expanding opportunities for digitally skilled youths.
In his remarks, Governor Mbah said the partnership was consistent with his administration’s commitment to ensuring that young people could acquire relevant skills, secure rewarding employment and build their futures in Enugu rather than leave the state in search of opportunities.
The Governor disclosed that over 33 per cent of the state’s expenditure was dedicated to human capital development, reflecting his administration’s emphasis on education, skills acquisition and workforce preparation.
He stressed that developing talent must go hand in hand with attracting companies capable of employing that talent, noting that private capital would be critical to achieving the state’s economic growth ambitions.
Mbah also reiterated his administration’s ambition to scale the digital economy through the proposed Talent City and Digital Industrial Park, expressing confidence that the infrastructure could support growth beyond the 100,000-job target set by Humatrix.
“We want the ‘japa’ where we can stay in Enugu and serve companies across the world, anywhere in the world,” the Governor said, describing the initiative as an opportunity for young people to earn globally competitive incomes while living in their home state.
He also signals the administration’s determination to connect investments in education with industries that can translate knowledge and skills into productive employment.

title: Toronto traffic agent dead after being hit by a dump truck in East York
body:
A City of Toronto traffic agent is dead after being hit by a dump truck in East York Thursday morning.
Mayor Olivia Chow said in a statement the agent was on duty at the time of the collision, which happened near Millwood Road and Overlea Boulevard.
Police said officers were called to the area at 9:02 a.m. on Thursday and that the victim — a 42-year-old man — was pronounced dead on scene.
The dump truck was making a left turn when it hit the traffic agent, police said. The driver of the dump truck — a 33-year-old man — remained at the scene and is cooperating with investigators.
Chow said she was “heartbroken” to learn the news.
“Traffic agents do some of the most demanding work in our city. They work in live traffic, in all weather conditions, to keep people moving and protect pedestrians, cyclists and drivers,” she said.
“Every shift, they help us get where we’re going safely. We are deeply thankful for that service, and this loss is a painful reminder of the risks they take on our behalf.”
Anyone with information is asked to contact police.

title: FG Honours Miden Systems Chair, Usoro, for Corporate Governance
body: Kasim Sumaina in Abuja The federal government has honoured the Executive Chairman of Miden Systems Limited, Dr. Brendan Innocent Usoro, with the Excellence in Corporate Governance and Business Integrity Award for his commitment to ethical leadership, transparency and responsible business practices. Usoro received the award yesterday at the Nigerian Press Council (NPC) National Summit on Curbing Fake News and Misinformation in the Nigerian Media Space, held in Abuja. Speaking at the event, he warned that fake news and misinformation posed serious threats to national security, democratic stability, business confidence and peaceful coexistence, particularly as Nigeria approaches the 2027 general elections. He expressed concern over the growing misuse of artificial intelligence to produce fabricated audio recordings, manipulate videos and spread misleading information. According to him, misinformation has become a tool for damaging reputations, undermining businesses and creating social tension. “People use false information to de-market their political opponents, competitors’ products and services, as well as create tension in the polity,” he said. He urged Nigerians to verify information before sharing it, recommending independent fact-checking organisations such as Dubawa. He also called for improved training for journalists, wider access to verification tools and stronger collaboration among government agencies, media organisations and technology companies. He stressed, however, that efforts to combat misinformation must not undermine press freedom, freedom of expression or legitimate criticism. Speaking on Miden Systems, Usoro said the company was established in 1997 and had grown from providing safety and equipment maintenance services into a diversified business covering marine services, logistics, facility upgrades and management. He attributed the company’s growth to quality service delivery and strong client relationships, reaffirming its commitment to ethical conduct, transparency and integrity. Earlier, the Executive Secretary and Chief Executive Officer of the Nigerian Press Council, Dr. Dili Ezughah, said the summit was organised to strengthen responsible journalism and equip media professionals to tackle misinformation ahead of the 2027 elections. The Minister of Defence, General Christopher Musa, represented by his Special Adviser on Intelligence, Musa Likita, described fake news as a threat to national security and democratic governance, urging collective action to prevent the spread of false information. Similarly, the Minister of Information and National Orientation, Alhaji Mohammed Idris, represented by Dr. Haruna Suleiman, called for stronger editorial oversight, accurate reporting and improved media literacy. Other award recipients included Nasarawa State Governor, Abdullahi Sule; General Christopher Musa; Mohammed Idris; Senator Emmanuel Bwacha; Barrister Obioma Success Akagburuonye; and Dr. Yakubu Barde, Federal Commissioner for Salaries, Income and Wages. The summit ended with a call for stronger cooperation among government institutions, media organisations, businesses and citizens to combat misinformation, protect press freedom and strengthen public trust. The summit brought together media practitioners, government officials, corporate executives and other stakeholders to discuss strategies for combating misinformation and promoting responsible journalism.

title: Images appear to show COMAC's 19-seat electric aircraft
body:
Images circulating on Chinese social media appear to show a full-scale version of the COMAC CE-25A, a 19-seat all-electric aircraft concept unveiled by the Chinese manufacturer in 2023.
The photographs show a red-and-black aircraft parked on an airfield, bearing COMAC markings, the CE-25A designation and the registration B-0EFH. Its most distinctive feature is an array of ten ducted fans, arranged in groups of five on either side of the fuselage.
The authenticity of the images has not been independently established. While they could depict an actual aircraft or a full-scale mock-up, the possibility of digital alterations cannot be ruled out. It is also unclear when and where the photographs were taken.
COMAC has not publicly confirmed whether a full-scale demonstrator has been completed or whether the aircraft shown has flown.
Follow Air Data News: WhatsApp | Instagram | LinkedIn | Twitter | Facebook
COMAC publicly introduced the CE-25A at the China International Import Expo in Shanghai in November 2023, presenting it as a 19-seat electric commuter aircraft intended for short- and medium-distance passenger services and business aviation.
According to specifications released at the time, the aircraft is designed for a range of approximately 250 to 310 miles (400 to 500 km) and a maximum cruising speed of around 249 mph (400 km/h).
Unlike conventional commuter aircraft powered by turboprop engines, the CE-25A uses a distributed electric propulsion concept, with ten electrically driven ducted fans integrated into the wings.
During the 2023 presentation, COMAC indicated that the project had already completed experimental flight verification using a scaled demonstrator. Those tests did not establish that a full-sized aircraft had flown.
The CE-25A is part of COMAC's research into alternative propulsion technologies, separate from its commercial aircraft programs, including the C919 narrowbody airliner and the C909 regional jet.
The Chinese manufacturer has also been involved in battery-powered aviation research alongside battery producer CATL and Shanghai Jiao Tong University. However, no specific connection between that cooperation and the CE-25A's energy storage system has been publicly established.
Battery energy density remains a major obstacle to all-electric passenger aircraft, particularly when combining commercially useful payloads with sufficient range and operational reserves.
Although the CE-25A has been presented as a potential commuter aircraft, there is no confirmed schedule for certification, production or entry into commercial service.

title: ‘If this works, it will be the first real ceasefire across a large stretch of the front’: Russia and Ukraine maintain truce in occupied Oleshky for more than two days
body: Russia and Ukraine have halted hostilities around the occupied city of Oleshky since October 27. The Verkhovna Rada’s human rights commissioner, Dmytro Lubinets, confirmed on the morning of October 29 that the ceasefire had held for more than two days. Russia’s human rights commissioner, Yana Lantratova, said humanitarian aid — “food, fuel, medicine, and hygiene products” — had been sent to Oleshky. Lubinets and Lantratova set out for Oleshky on the afternoon of October 29. Lubinets will be the first Ukrainian official of such rank to visit Russian-occupied territories. Both commissioners said their main task is to deliver humanitarian aid to residents and ensure the safe evacuation of those who want to leave. Sources who spoke to the Ukrainian news outlet Ukrainska Pravda and were involved in organizing the ceasefire said the ceasefire around Oleshky is meant to test whether Ukrainian and Russian military commanders can carry out political agreements to end hostilities. Organizing a halt to the fighting turned out to be “an extremely difficult task,” according to the outlet’s sources. A political order to cease fire does not by itself guarantee automatic compliance on the front line, a source in Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky’s administration told Ukrainska Pravda. Even Ukrainian troops demanded guarantees several times that if they stopped, “nothing bad would happen afterward,” the source said. The source explained: We want to get the military — both our General Staff and the Russian one — used to the idea that if the political leadership has decided that in a given sector of the front we stop, freeze in place, and no one opens fire, the military can make that happen. They can guarantee it. Not a situation where the political leadership has reached an agreement and the military says, “Sorry, we can’t stop, we’ve got something going on.” It is easier for the Russian side than for the Ukrainian side to organize and maintain a ceasefire, according to Ukrainska Pravda’s sources. “They [the Russians] have a rigid military vertical. We have a decentralized army. And someone — some well-known military blogger — could stir up the mood on air so much that everything falls apart afterward,” a source said. If the ceasefire in Oleshky can be maintained, as planned, until the evening of November 1, the Ukrainian side expects to repeat this kind of local ceasefire later along other parts of the front. “That’s precisely so the military can learn how to do this: stop, ensure safe passage, and so on. So that later, if there’s some major agreement, we could implement it right away,” a source who spoke to Ukrainska Pravda said. If this works, this will be the first example of a real ceasefire across a fairly large stretch of the front. It’s come at such a cost — the military, Russia’s Federal Security Service, and everyone else are doing nothing but trying to sabotage it. But we believe it will work out and that this will set a precedent. The war in photographs Russia’s Defense Ministry announced that it had begun clearing mines from roads leading into Oleshky and published photos and video of sappers at work. Russian President Vladimir Putin, speaking at a plenary session of the Russia–Africa summit underway in Moscow, claimed it was Ukraine that had mined the approaches to Oleshky, creating “practically a humanitarian catastrophe.” At Meduza, we are committed to transparency about our use of artificial intelligence in the newsroom.
