title: While Oleshky ceasefire holds for third day, Russian attacks kill 1, injure at least 22 across Ukraine
body:
Editor's note: The count of country-wide casualties over the past day in Ukraine is based on the early morning reports of regional authorities. Today's summary does not include the victims of this morning's deadly attack on Dnipro, which will be included tomorrow.
The local ceasefire around the Russian-occupied city of Oleshky in Kherson Oblast has entered its third day without major violations, as the area is prepared for the provision of humanitarian aid and the evacuation of civilians.
As of the morning of Oct. 29, demining of the area continues, Ukraine's Ombudsman Dmytro Lubinets — who departed with the Ukrainian delegation to the occupied town the same morning — wrote on social media.
Oleshky, which had a pre-war population of around 24,000, has been under Russian occupation since the early days of Russia's full-scale invasion.
Located across the Dnipro River from Kherson , the city has been effectively blockaded by Russian forces, which have prevented humanitarian aid from reaching residents.
The ceasefire — announced by the White House on Oct. 23 as being mediated by Trump and soon confirmed by Ukraine and Russia — is in its third day as of Oct. 29, and is expected to last into early November, as aid is brought in, key roads are demined, and residents are evacuated.
According to Oleksandr Prokudin, governor of Kherson Oblast, no strikes against civilian or critical infrastructure targets, nor any civilian casualties, were recorded in the region.
Elsewhere across Ukraine, Russian attacks both along the front line and in the rear continued without pause.
Overnight, Russian forces launched 112 attack drones, 40 of them jet-powered, at Ukraine, according to the Air Force. 97 of the drones were downed or jammed, including 30 of the jet-powered drones. Strikes were recorded at seven locations, the Air Force added.
One person was killed and eight more injured — including a 13-year-old girl — in attacks on Kharkiv Oblast, regional governor Oleh Syniehubov said . Most casualties came from a drone attack on the capital, Kharkiv.
In Ukraine's northeastern Sumy Oblast, a total of eight civilians were injured as 80 attacks on 35 settlements were recorded in the 24-hour period, authorities said.
Russian forces struck an animal shelter in the city of Chernihiv, injuring three female staff, according to Governor Viacheslav Chaus. Over 100 animals held at the facility were taken into foster care, he added.
Two Ukrainian civilians were injured in front-line Donetsk Oblast, both in and around the city of Kramatorsk, according to governor Vadym Filashkin.
A 35-year-old man was injured in Dnipropetrovsk Oblast, in an attack on a commercial facility in the regional capital, governor Oleksandr Hanzha said.

title: Govt gives entrepreneurs more time to set up shelters or safe spaces – Koretsky
body:
The government is giving business owners more time to set up shelters or safe spaces, and has said that the postponement means the requirements are being waived, Ukrainian Prime Minister Serhiy Koretsky said.
"Today we presented changes to the current regulations to business associations. The priority, as before, is people's safety. At the same time, we are extending the resolution's validity because we cannot allow the country's economy and daily life to grind to a halt. I would like to remind you that the government initiated these changes two months ago. However, we have seen that a significant number of businesses have not even begun to comply with the basic requirements for people's safety," Koretsky said on his Telegram channel.
In light of this, the government is giving business owners more time to set up shelters or safe spaces.
"There are plenty of opportunities to purchase mobile structures. The extension does not mean the requirements have been cancelled. People's safety must be a priority. This could be the simplest safe space, a mobile shelter, or information about the location of and access to the nearest underground shelter," Koretsky said.
According to him, the requirements for shelters will depend on the number of employees and visitors present at the facility at any given time.
He added that the Ministry of Economy and the Ministry of Internal Affairs will provide further details.
"A shelter does not necessarily have to be on the enterprise's own premises. A nearby shelter can be used if it has sufficient capacity. At the same time, people must clearly know where it is located," the prime minister said.
He stated that by March 4, military administrations will collect data on compliance with the requirements, and further decisions will be made based on the results.

title: Russian Deputy PM names key areas of cooperation with Africa
body:
MOSCOW, October 29. /TASS/. Russian Deputy Prime Minister Alexander Novak indicated agriculture, transport, mineral resources mining and electric power as key areas for cooperation with African nations in an interview with Vesti news program.
"First and foremost, this includes agriculture and processing, as this sector has significant potential for growth in Africa. These are transport, industrial plants, and equipment supplies. Many countries possess vast potential capabilities in mineral extraction. Particularly this pertains to oil, gas, gold, and uranium. Our expertise can be valuable here as well," Novak said.
Development of the power sector is important, the deputy prime minister said. "African countries today do not have enough power generation capacity. In this area, our competencies are hydropower, solar panels, and even the general development of energy master plans for these countries, given Russia's leading role in this field," he added.

title: China’s Hainan boosts its international trade in services by 11.7% in nine months
body:
HAIKOU /China/, October 29. /TASS/. China’s southern island province of Hainan increased its international trade in services by 11.7% year-on-year to 56.95 billion yuan ($8.48 billion) in January-September 2026, the region’s Department of Commerce said.
According to the department’s WeChat page, the province’s services exports increased by 14.9% to 40.41 billion yuan (around $6.02 billion) in the reporting period, while imports reached 16.54 billion yuan ($2.46 billion), up 4.7%.
The department said that the cross-border maintenance sector (for vessels and aircraft — TASS), inbound tourism and computer game exports demonstrated particularly impressive results over the nine months. Key transport and logistics companies such as COSCO Shipping played an important role in developing Hainan’s freight sector.
The Department of Commerce forecasted that Hainan’s international transport services sector would grow significantly by the end of 2026. The department highlighted the key role of the visa-free regime and air traffic growth, which have brought far more tourists from Russia, Kazakhstan and South Korea to the island.
In addition, the department noted that the quantitative growth in Hainan’s international services trade came with structural optimization, driven by both traditional and new factors. According to the published data, the Chinese special administrative region of Hong Kong, the United States, Russia, Ireland and Singapore are Hainan’s top five partners in this field. According to estimates, they accounted for more than 57% of total commercial activity in this segment of the island’s economy in the first three quarters of 2026.
The department also stated that the Hainan Free Trade Port would continue to use institutional and other advantages to strengthen the regional transport sector and inbound tourism and to introduce new types of services trade. At the same time, the province’s authorities plan to diversify the entry of local companies into foreign markets and ensure the high quality of their economic interaction with partners from other countries and regions.

title: NIA arrests six staff, dismisses seven over alleged Ghana Card extortion
body: The National Identification Authority (NIA) has announced the arrest of six staff members and the termination of the appointments of seven others over alleged extortion during the free Ghana Card registration exercise at Galaka in the Upper East Region. The disciplinary action follows complaints that some registration officials demanded money from parents before registering their children during the recently concluded exercise for children aged six to 14. In a statement issued on Thursday, October 29, the Authority disclosed that the six staff members, who were identified by affected parents, had been arrested by the Bawku West District Police and were assisting with investigations. The NIA further revealed that an extensive internal review had resulted in the dismissal of seven other members of the registration team who were found to have known about the alleged misconduct but failed to report it. The Authority stressed that the Ghana Card registration exercise must be conducted strictly in accordance with approved procedures, emphasising that no official is permitted to demand unauthorised payments from applicants or their parents. It reaffirmed its commitment to maintaining transparency and accountability in its operations, warning that misconduct would attract appropriate disciplinary sanctions. The NIA also assured the public that it would continue to take the necessary measures to safeguard the integrity of its registration processes and ensure that applicants receive fair and professional services. It consequently encouraged members of the public to report suspected misconduct by registration officials through its official communication channels. The statement was signed by Williams Ampomah Emmanuel Darlas, Head of the Corporate Affairs Directorate of the NIA.

title: Brothers before the ballot - opinion
body: This week's election in Israel is the first since October 7. It comes after three years of pain and grief.During the campaign, each side painted its opponent as a threat to the country's future. While this is not abnormal for an election, it certainly poses a danger for the Jewish people.Disagreement and argumentation are part of our Jewish tradition, but demonizing and fostering hatred certainly is not.In this past week's Torah portion, the shepherds of Abraham and Lot quarrel over grazing land. Abraham does not wait for the disagreement to cross the line.He goes to his nephew and says: “Let there please be no strife between you and me, and between my herdsmen and your herdsmen, for we are brothers” (Genesis 13:8).Notice what Abraham does not say. He does not tell Lot that he must think the same way. He offers to part ways: “If you go left, I will go right.” Achdut, unity, in the Torah's first lesson on the subject, is not uniformity. Brothers can live in different places, make different choices, and still be brothers.Our tradition is built on this. Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel argued for generations over hundreds of topics, some of them touching on marriage itself.Yet the Talmud (Yevamot 14b) records that they did not refrain from marrying into one another's families. They treated each other with affection and respect.Israelis are divided over real questions this week: security, the draft, the place of Torah learning, the courts, and the economy. These are not trivial.People hold their positions out of genuine conviction and love for the country and for our people.But maybe the more important question of this election is not what we disagree on but how we treat each other while disagreeing.The parasha continues after Lot and Abraham separate. Lot settles near Sodom, a choice the Torah clearly disapproves of. Soon after, Lot is taken captive in a regional war.Abraham could have shrugged. Lot had made his bed. Instead, the Torah says, “Avram heard that his brother had been taken captive” (Genesis 14:14). Not his nephew, not the one who chose Sodom, but “his brother.”Abraham arms his household and attacks the army to bring Lot home.Whatever the result of this election, roughly half the country will wake up disappointed, many frightened. The person who voted the other way, whose party you consider a danger, is still the one who sits next to you on the bus, or in the hospital waiting room. When he is in trouble, he is still your brother.In the summer of 2023, Israel was as divided as it had ever been. Then came Simchat Torah.The terrorists who crossed the border did not ask anyone how they voted. They did not distinguish between religious and secular, Left and Right, kibbutznik and yeshiva student.In the weeks that followed, neither did we.Reservists who had marched against the government reported for duty beside those who had marched for it. Haredi (ultra-Orthodox) volunteers cooked for soldiers; secular families prayed for the hostages. For a while, the whole world saw what Jewish unity looks like.We should not need another catastrophe to remember who we are: brothers responsible for each other. That responsibility does not pause for an election.Settling the question of brotherhoodUnity is not a slogan; we need to pursue it actively. Especially in times of high passion, we must guard ourselves from demonization. Those we disagree with are not “traitors” or “enemies of the Jewish people.”The person who votes differently almost always has good intentions and is trying to make Israel and the Jewish people safer, more secure, more successful. They just have a different thought process of how to attain these shared goals.Abraham said “For we are brothers” before the land was divided, not after. He did not wait to see who got the better pasture. He settled the question of brotherhood first, so that nothing that followed could undo it.That is the order we need this week. The Jewish people will not be decided at any polling station. We were brothers before this election, and we will be brothers after it. Let us act like it now.The writer is the CEO of Kesher Yehudi, whose mission is to create unity between religious and secular Israelis.

title: Microsoft’s AI future has fewer jobs
body:
To anyone listening closely to what Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella has been saying over the past couple of years, this week felt like the clearest sign yet that AI is about to fundamentally change the size of Microsoft’s workforce. Microsoft is now offering voluntary buyouts to around 60,000 employees across the US, UK, Canada, and India.
It’s the first time the company has presented such an offer to so many employees, expanding greatly upon the retirement offer that was limited to around 9,000 employees earlier this year. It’s all part of an ongoing effort to avoid reducing investment in AI infrastructure by lowering Microsoft’s operating costs and headcount.
“Our total people costs will go down, our cost per head will go up, and my GPU per researcher will go up,” Nadella said on a podcast almost two years ago, responding to a question about AI’s impact on headcount. That’s a financial way of saying Microsoft will have fewer people, but it will offer higher salaries and more tools and AI power to those who remain.
It also helps explain the continued layoffs we’ve seen at Microsoft over the past couple of years. Microsoft has been performing layoffs regularly over the past decade, but over the past couple of years, the layoffs and executive departures have been significant.
These aren’t the annual layoffs of old; they’re now happening every few months. This week’s voluntary exit offer arrived just months after Microsoft laid off 4,800 employees, cuts that impacted its Xbox and commercial sales teams the most.
For the first time in a decade, Microsoft’s overall headcount has also gone down year over year. Microsoft now employs around 223,000 people as of June 30th, 5,000 fewer than the 228,000 people it employed in 2025. Microsoft laid off 4 percent of its workforce in July last year, and it’s now offering voluntary buyout offers to around a quarter of its employees.
More than 30 percent of the 9,000 eligible employees accepted a retirement offer earlier this year, but that number will likely be far less for the company’s latest Voluntary Exit Offer. That’s largely because, according to sources familiar, the offer is practically the same as regular severance terms at Microsoft — cash based on time at the company, accelerated stock vesting, some additional subsidized health coverage, and several months of career services.
But what makes this unusual is the scale of the amount of employees who have been offered this exit. Even if only 5 percent accept the offer, that’s still 3,000 employees. I understand eligible employees have until December to decide, so we won’t know the impact of this offer for a while yet. With rumors of more layoffs in November and January, the amount of employees who do accept will surely inform Microsoft’s numbers for its next round of cuts.
There are some, both inside and outside the company, who think Microsoft needs these cuts. “Microsoft needs fewer people,” says Merill Fernando, a former Microsoft Entra product manager. “I’ve been on the inside. I’ve seen how things get built. Lots of small orgs. Layers on layers. Silos everywhere.”
Fernando paints a picture of a Microsoft where every organization “had its own priorities and its own decision makers,” so it’s hard to get the company to do anything collectively. It sounds a little like the meme where each organization in Microsoft is pointing guns at each other, competing instead of collaborating.
Nadella even addressed that meme last year in a podcast with Stripe co-founder John Collison, acknowledging that the comic has defined Microsoft’s cultural narrative “more so than reality,” but that it had signaled some very real tensions inside the company. “In some sense, some of these divisional tensions are real issues that need to have tension. Social cohesion is not a goal, winning in the marketplace is a goal,” said Nadella.
The question now is whether Nadella can reshape Microsoft for the AI era without undoing the cultural transformation that helped define his leadership. A company that has shifted to be built around empathy is now asking its employees to reckon with an AI future that could make many of their jobs unnecessary. How Nadella handles that transition will define his legacy as much as the growth and success he’s achieved over the past decade.
Xbox’s architect of Forza Motorsport is leaving after nearly 27 years
A few weeks ago I started hearing from Xbox employees that Dan Greenawalt, the longtime creative force behind Forza Motorsport, is leaving after almost 27 years. Greenawalt is departing as the head of Turn 10 Studios, the Forza Motorsport creator that merged with Forza Horizon developer Playground Games.
Playground Games studio head Trevor Williams revealed the news in a recent internal memo, seen by Notepad. “Dan Greenawalt has decided that this is the right time for him to retire from Microsoft,” says Williams. Greenawalt will stay on as an adviser to Williams and the newly appointed Playground Games chief operating officer, Michel Bastien, “while he transitions to his next phase.” Here’s part of Williams’ memo about Greenawalt:
> It’s hard to overstate Dan’s impact over the past 27 years. From shipping Project Gotham Racing on the original XBOX in 2001 to leading the creation of Forza, founding Turn 10 Studios and appearing so many times on our E3 stage, usually making a dramatic entrance with a supercar in tow – and so much more – we owe tremendous thanks and gratitude to Dan. On behalf of both teams, I would like to thank Dan for his leadership, his support, and his partnership. I wish him well for whatever comes next.
Microsoft revealed last month that it was merging its two Forza developers into a single studio as part of a massive restructuring of Xbox. Both Playground Games and Turn 10 Studios have merged into just Playground Games. The studio now has two locations: Playground Games Leamington Spa and Playground Games Redmond.
With Greenawalt retiring and Turn 10 merged into Playground Games, it’s not clear if we’ll ever see Microsoft return to Forza Motorsport. More than 70 people at Turn 10 Studios were laid off last year, in a move that hit the vast majority of the studio. Over the past year, Turn 10 Studios has essentially been maintaining Forza Motorsport, and now the remaining employees have moved to Playground Games to work on Forza Horizon and Fable.
It’s time to name The Elders Scrolls VI: Sentinel
It’s been more than eight years since Bethesda officially announced the existence of the sixth game in its Elder Scrolls series. While there have been some debates around platform exclusivity for The Elder Scrolls VI, we’ve heard very little detail about the game that Bethesda has been working on all this time.
Sources familiar with Bethesda’s plans tell me that the Xbox-owned publisher is about to announce that the next Elder Scrolls game will officially be called The Elder Scrolls VI: Sentinel. The announcement could come as soon as next month, during a period that will mark 15 years since The Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim was released.
Bethesda has been showing off Sentinel gameplay in recent months, I’m told. Xbox CEO Asha Sharma got a live playthrough of Sentinel in August, and she praised the scale of the game and said “the story is even greater.”
While I’m only expecting a name reveal next month and nothing more, I’ve been hearing some additional details about the game. If you want to totally avoid spoilers about the game, then don’t read the next paragraph.
I understand that Sentinel will be set in Hammerfell, a province in the Elder Scrolls universe that’s appeared in The Elder Scrolls Adventures: Redguard and The Elder Scrolls Online. Sentinel will be the first game about the history of the Elder Scrolls, and help uncover the secrets of these mysterious ancient artifacts.
The pad
* Xbox’s first chief operating officer is out after just a few months. This is a weird one. Helen Chiang is leaving Microsoft after 21 years. She previously served as the head of Minecraft before being promoted to Xbox COO in July. The sudden departure was announced in a surprisingly short memo from Xbox chief Asha Sharma last week. “Helen Chiang is leaving Microsoft today. I’m grateful for her years of service and wish her well,” says Sharma. It doesn’t seem like the Xbox COO position is going away, as Sharma notes that “we’ll share more on COO leadership as plans are finalized.” Eurogamer reported over the weekend that Chiang had been “terminated for policy violations.” I’ve heard similar chatter internally, but Chiang has been described to me by multiple Xbox employees as highly respected, with high integrity, so this turn of events is quite odd. I’m trying to get more details, but if you’ve heard anything, please reach out confidentially at notepad@theverge.com or through the secure Signal messaging app. (I’m tomwarren.01.)
* Microsoft’s new Surface Laptop Ultra update fixes reboot and display bugs. I ran into some weird issues with the Surface Laptop Ultra during my review, and Microsoft is now fixing some of them with a firmware update. The update addresses screen flickering, unexpected restarts, and lengthy reboot times alongside unspecified “additional bug fixes and general performance improvements.” I’m still waiting to see if Nvidia or Microsoft addresses the strange laggy feeling on the Surface Laptop Ultra, and it’s too early to say whether this firmware update addresses that or not yet.
* GitHub’s former CEO launched a competing platform for AI agents. We knew that Thomas Dohmke, former GitHub CEO, was building some kind of competitor to GitHub, but the result has surprised people internally during the week of GitHub’s Universe conference. Developers can use the new Entire platform to host and review code, but it’s also designed to work with AI agents and replaces pull requests with a “Trails” feature that offers “customizable evals that are scored by agents on every code push.” One GitHub employee tells me, “people are shocked, they have ambushed us up and down the stack on our own conference week.”
* Windows will soon let you perform an internet speed test without opening your browser. Microsoft added a speed test option to the Windows 11 taskbar earlier this year, but it was just a link to a speed test in Bing that opened in your browser. Now, Microsoft is actually integrating a full speed test into the taskbar, so you can right-click the network icon and perform an internet speed test right there.
* Windows 11 is getting some neat trackpad features. Microsoft is adding new Windows trackpad features that let you scroll through long documents and webpages faster. You’ll also be able to continuously scroll through a page by swiping the edge of your touchpad, along with support for single-finger scrolling. It’s the small things that count, and I love to see these kinds of features being added to Windows.
* Microsoft says its AI tool is better than doctors at diagnosing conditions. Microsoft claims to have developed an AI-powered tool that it says can diagnose conditions up to four times more accurately than human doctors. The findings were published last week in Science, one of the world’s most prestigious journals. Microsoft has pitted its AI system against human physicians on a series of scenarios drawn from medical case reports and emergency department data. While there’s still a long road ahead before this AI system can be widely deployed, Microsoft thinks its work is significant. “It needs clinical validation,” says Microsoft AI CEO Mustafa Suleyman in an interview with The Verge. “That is a leap, but this is a major milestone along that journey.”
* Microsoft Authenticator flaw lets malicious Android apps steal tokens. Security researchers at Enclave have discovered a vulnerability with Microsoft Authenticator that lets an unprivileged Android app with zero permissions “impersonate any installed Microsoft first-party app and have the Microsoft Authenticator broker hand it that app’s tokens.” The tokens could provide full access to mailboxes, files, and calendars. Microsoft has now fixed the flaw, and if you use Microsoft Authenticator on Android, then it’s time to update it immediately.
* Denmark has abandoned plans to ditch Microsoft Office after technical problems. Last year the government of Denmark announced it was ditching Windows and Office in favor of open-source alternatives to reduce its reliance on US vendors. It seems like the trial of moving away from Microsoft’s software hasn’t gone too well for the Danish government, though. The Danish Ministry of Digitalisation has reportedly ended its trial for an open-source alternative to Microsoft Office. Employees reportedly encountered issues with document formatting, blank pages, and tracking changes.
* Gears of War: E-Day cost $500 million to make. Gears of War E-Day has the highest Metacritic score of any entry in the franchise since the Xbox 360 days, but it faces some tough questions around how much it costs to create a AAA game these days and what success looks like. Kotaku reports that E-Day cost “over $500 million” to make, excluding marketing budgets. This has generated a lot of discussion online over E-Day’s success, especially as it’s a controversial test for any potential return to Xbox exclusivity. One source tells me that more than 400,000 copies of the game have been sold across Xbox and Steam, but the big question is whether Microsoft was happy with its Game Pass numbers for E-Day, and whether that revenue offsets any additional sales on Xbox and potential PS5 sales if a port had been released.
* Arkane Lyon and Blade could be about to be saved. Earlier this year, I reported that Microsoft was weighing up canceling its Blade game and shuttering Arkane. In the months since June, Microsoft has been in ongoing discussions with multiple publishers about a potential sale of Arkane Lyon amid consultations with the union representing the studio’s employees. French newspaper Le Monde now reports that Microsoft has a November 13th cutoff date for a decision on the future of Arkane Lyon, and Microsoft confirmed to PC Gamer that it’s extending this deadline by an additional month. An extension makes it seem like Microsoft is close to a deal, and I’m cautiously optimistic that Blade will be saved. We’ll find out in the coming weeks.
* Microsoft is ending Copilot support on smart TVs. After nearly two years of Copilot support on smart TVs, Microsoft is pulling the plug. I’d love to know how many people actually used Copilot this way, because it can’t be more than a dozen. LG says the Copilot TV feature is “scheduled for discontinuation during 2026” and a specific date is “subject to Microsoft’s timeline.”
* Microsoft reveals strong cloud growth amid financial reporting overhaul. Microsoft overhauled its financial reporting this quarter, placing Windows, Surface, and Xbox in a separate bucket to its more revenue generating AI and cloud efforts. Windows OEM revenue was down 22 percent amid a RAMageddon crisis that has seen the overall PC market drop by 20 percent in the recent quarter. Xbox hardware and content and services were also down, but a whole third of Microsoft’s revenue came from Azure ($33.17 billion of the $92.3 billion). I thought Nadella’s most interesting remarks on the earnings call were about Microsoft’s own AI models. “Our goal is to advance the cost to outcome frontier, which means delivering capabilities comparable to leading models within three to six months of their release at a fraction of the training cost, thereby allowing us to transfer those cost benefits to customers,” said Nadella.
I’m always keen to hear from readers, so please drop a comment here, or you can reach me at notepad@theverge.com if you want to discuss anything else. If you’ve heard about any of Microsoft’s secret projects, you can reach me via email at notepad@theverge.com or speak to me confidentially on the Signal messaging app, where I’m tomwarren.01. I’m also tomwarren on Telegram, if you’d prefer to chat there.
Thanks for subscribing to Notepad.

title: Turning Point rests its reputation on Andy Biggs’ race. It’s not looking good.
body: Turning Point USA has gone all-in to make GOP Rep. Andy Biggs the next governor of Arizona, their top priority of the cycle. It appears they will come up short. Biggs was the last candidate Turning Point founder Charlie Kirk personally endorsed before he was killed one year ago. Kirk himself recruited the longtime ally in their home state to run for governor this cycle — and Turning Point has since spent $18 million, the most they’ve dropped for anyone this cycle, to try to salvage his campaign. “It's a legacy thing for them,” said former Rep. Matt Salmon (R-Ariz.). “This is their swan song. This is kind of all-or-nothing for them.” But Biggs, a former chair of the hardline House Freedom Caucus and close ally of President Donald Trump who previously served as Arizona Senate president, has trailed Democratic Gov. Katie Hobbs in virtually every public poll of the race this year, most of them outside the margin of error. And some Arizona Republicans have been baffled by Turning Point’s strategy. The group faces immense criticism from within the state GOP for delaying its biggest spending until September, just weeks before ballots were sent out, according to conversations with 10 local operatives and officials. Biggs’ race is the most high-stakes political test for Turning Point Action since Kirk’s 2025 death, and the result will have major implications for the group’s reputation and relevancy within the GOP moving forward. Turning Point has already preemptively endorsed Vice President JD Vance , who was particularly close to Kirk, for president. Should Vance decide to run, he could rely on Turning Point’s ground operation in swing states like Arizona and beyond. The group could well overperform this year, and if they are successful in lifting Biggs in their home state, it could send a signal. But a loss could have 2028 repercussions, too. “If JD Vance intends to run for president, I think it would be a good idea to reevaluate any thoughts he might have about utilizing Turning Point Action as his field operation,” said Gina Swoboda, a former chair of the Arizona Republican Party who has openly sparred with the organization. A spokesperson for Vance did not respond to a request for comment. Other Republicans, including the Biggs’ campaign, said they’re grateful that Turning Point didn’t wave the white flag in a tough year for the GOP, as voters reel from the impact of Trump’s policies. “Turning Point Action’s investments both on the ground and over the airwaves in Arizona have been tremendous. We are very grateful they’ve stepped up to support Andy and Republicans up and down the ballot in an extremely difficult environment,” Biggs campaign spokesperson Drew Sexton said in a statement. In a statement, Tyler Bowyer, chief operating officer of Turning Point Action, said he is “very proud of the strides we have made in Arizona and other swing states.” He emphasized TP Action is “a Get-Out-The-Vote (GOTV) centric organization” and not TV-focused, pointing the blame elsewhere. “It is the job of national apparatus groups to go on air early and support Republican nominees,” he said. “We of course are disappointed that more national Republican dollars are not matching the national Democrat dollars being spent on Presidential swing states like Arizona.” While the RGA has stayed out of the race, the Democratic Governors Association has spent at least $10 million . Hobbs, who was elected to the purple state’s governorship in 2022, launched her first general election TV ad in May , while Biggs was still focused on his late July primary. At the time, Turning Point mocked Hobbs for "spending like a drunken sailor" by launching spending so early. But now, Republicans say that Hobbs was able to entrench her lead in the race by spending early while Biggs was dark on the airwaves — and blame Turning Point along with other GOP outside groups like the Republican Governors Association for not spending earlier to keep the race competitive. The RGA declined to comment on their decision not to spend in the race. In a state like Arizona, where an incumbent governor hasn’t lost reelection since 1966 and some 80% of voters cast ballots before Election Day, a late deluge of cash is less likely to sway the race. “If you're spending that much money, a big portion of that would've been really helpful earlier in the race when Andy was completely broke, he didn't have two nickels to rub together, and Hobbs was dominating the airwaves with no response and beating the crap out of Andy,” said Salmon.”A lot of us are scratching our heads.” Biggs’ campaign reported just $1.26 million cash on hand in July, while Hobbs’ campaign reported double that . Many donors to former GOP Gov. Doug Ducey have stayed on the sidelines this year . One Republican operative working on other Arizona races, granted anonymity to speak candidly, said that at this point, “No amount of spending is going to change the fact that Biggs is going to lose.” “In all likelihood, the top statewide seats are going Democrat. And Turning Point owns it,” the strategist added. “They wanted to be the player. They wanted to be the guy. Guess what? They are.” Many local Republicans are frustrated that the RGA never spent a penny on the top race in a state Trump won in 2024. While Biggs was getting hammered early on the airwaves, the RGA was spending nearly $4 million on the Wisconsin Democratic primary to boost a democratic socialist who narrowly lost. For several cycles, Turning Point has muscled statewide candidates through messy Republican primaries, only to see them falter in November. In 2022, it pushed hardliners Blake Masters and Kari Lake as nominees for U.S. Senate and governor, only to see both lose. In 2024, they backed Lake’s bid for Senate; even as Trump won Arizona by five points, Lake lost by two. Biggs, some Republicans thought, would be different. He had high name ID statewide and a track record of public service for Arizona, both in the state Senate and the U.S. House. Kirk himself personally urged Biggs to enter the governor’s race, Biggs told the Arizona Republic , even though Trump had already endorsed Karrin Taylor Robson, a Phoenix attorney and businesswoman, early in the race. After Biggs entered the race in January 2025, Trump split his endorsement between Robson and Biggs — and Turning Point took a victory lap. “Turning Point Action will marshall our organization's full resources, ground game, and support behind the Biggs for Arizona campaign, and we’re honored to be able to do so,” Charlie Kirk said in a May 2025 statement . “He has my full and complete endorsement.” Robson later dropped out , and Turning Point helped Biggs romp to a massive victory in the primary. Next Tuesday will test if their general-election acumen has improved.

title: How debates became high-risk and low-reward in the viral era
body: A short interruption in the Maine Senate debate from Oct. 15 is still relevant a week before Election Day. Democratic nominee Troy Jackson told five-term incumbent Sen. Susan Collins to "shut up," after she said a protester was "obviously one of Troy's supporters." Jackson has since been asked to apologize, which he declined to do, and the clip made its way into GOP attack ads. Maine is among the close races that will determine which party controls the Senate. Jackson's comment, unprompted by a question from the moderator or an answer from Collins, speaks to the high risk of debating. Small moments can cause catastrophes, according to Democratic strategist and CBS News contributor Chuck Rocha."You may not win a race during a debate, but you can certainly lose one," Rocha said. "People are super cautious these days." In  this midterm cycle, 18 of 35 Senate races and 12 of the 36 gubernatorial races did not feature a debate between the major party candidates, and in those that did occur, many were defined by mudslinging and character assaults that wound up viral online. "Debates are defined by big moments," Republican strategist and CBS News contributor Terry Sullivan said. "Ninety-five percent of what happens in debates does not matter. You're banking on not making the 5% mistake and trying to force the other guy to make the 5% mistake."Candidates backing away from debatesOver half of the 2026 Senate races will not feature debates between the major party candidates. That number includes Ohio and Texas, two of the five races rated as toss-ups by CBS News.In an analysis of past toss-up races from Cook Political Report, only one of the four races in 2024 and 2022 did not have debates. The seven toss-ups in 2020, nine in 2018 and seven in 2016 all had debates.Rocha said going on stage "without any control of the messaging" can do more harm than good in these closely contested races. In Texas, which is on track to be the most expensive Senate in history, Democratic candidate James Talarico has repeatedly called on his Republican opponent Ken Paxton to debate and even suggested he would go "into the lion's den" and let Fox News host it. Talarico eventually hosted a solo CNN town hall. Rocha noted that a debate could draw new attention to Paxton's past scandals and controversies. "He don't want to be asked about all the negative [stuff] in his life," Rocha said of Paxton.A third of gubernatorial races will not have  debates, a significant jump from years past. When the same set of 36 gubernatorial seats were up in 2022, candidates in seven opted not to debate. In 2018, all but two races included debates, and in 2014, all but four did. Candidates on both sides of the aisle have also argued there is no benefit to debating. Ohio Democratic candidate Amy Acton said she would not debate GOP nominee for governor Vivek Ramaswamy because it cannot be "a civil dialogue about facts when you're with somebody who's a chronic liar." In Alabama, Sen. Tommy Tuberville, who is running for governor, argued there is nothing to debate with his opponent, former Sen. Doug Jones, because "we know where the Democrats stand, and we know where conservative Republicans stand." Jones held his own "debate" on Oct. 21, where he played clips of Tuberville. Arizona Democratic Gov. Katie Hobbs declined to debate her Republican opponent, Rep. Andy Biggs, because "face-to-face interactions with Arizonans are more effective than a stage that is designed for nothing but political soundbites and theater." Biggs participated in a debate alongside "No Labels" candidate Teri Hourihan and has criticized Hobbs. He wrote on X, "Your record is so disastrous you won't even get on a debate stage to defend it."Pushing the 5% mistakeThe cornering of opponents and the effect of the digital age were on display in the debates that did occur. Debates in Michigan and Alaska, which are among the crucial Senate toss-up races, also had viral moments like in Maine. Nominees appeared closer to enemies than as candidates from opposing parties, with their attacks garnering significant attention online. In Michigan, Democratic Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed said Mike Rogers was a "sock puppet" for the president, and Rogers accused El-Sayed of being an extremist connected to the Muslim Brotherhood. Asked if there should be guardrails for flock cameras, Rogers suggested El-Sayed would want them because of a relative "that might be on the  watch list." El-Sayed challenged his opponent "to go ahead and say it," leading Rogers to allege El-Sayed's mother worked for a company "that was indicted for funneling money to al Qaeda." Alaska's Senate debate also produced viral moments for both candidates. Republican Sen. Dan Sullivan took a few notable swipes at Democratic nominee Mary Peltola. He accused her of "character fraud" over a New York Times' report on Peltola's treatment of staff that led the moderator to call for "some decorum." But in another swipe, he accused Peltola of having pre-written answers, and when moderators assured no one did, Peltola replied, "I'm prepared," leading to a viral moment for Democrats. Debates used to be an opportunity for "people to get out of their echo chambers and their partisan media and listen to the other candidate in a way that is not filtered for them," said Kathryn Cramer Brownell, a history professor at Purdue University who focuses on the relationship between media and politics. The current media climate, however, has "undermined the potential" for debates to actually broaden a candidate's appeal."How do you generate more of that broad viewing experience in the age of social media?" Brownell asks. "Frequently, debates just become boiled down to very short clips that are circulated through social media, and, then, again, filtered through a more partisan lens."

title: Ebola: Africa CDC warns continent ‘not winning’ as cases surpass 10,000
body:
The Director-General of the Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention (Africa CDC), Jean Kaseya, has warned that Africa is not yet winning the fight against the ongoing Ebola outbreak, as confirmed cases have surpassed 10,000 and deaths approach 5,000.
Mr Kaseya made the remarks on Wednesday at an extraordinary meeting of African health ministers convened to discuss the outbreak and strengthen a coordinated continental response.
“I have worked on Ebola outbreaks for more than 30 years. I have never stopped feeling the weight of each life lost,” Mr Kaseya said.
“Yesterday I stood before more than 40 African Ministers and said what the data tells us: we are not winning so far. 10,172 confirmed cases. 4,932 people are gone.”
He said the ministers agreed to prepare every country for possible Ebola cases, coordinate responses across borders and keep borders open while strengthening surveillance.
“Ebola anywhere in Africa demands preparedness everywhere in Africa. We will get there, together,” he said.
The current outbreak is caused by the Bundibugyo virus, a species of Ebola virus, and was first declared in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) in May 2026.
According to the latest figures from the World Health Organisation (WHO), the outbreak has recorded 10,172 confirmed cases and 4,932 deaths across five countries: DRC, Uganda, France, Kenya and Nigeria.
The DRC accounts for the majority of the cases, with 10,141 confirmed cases and 4,928 deaths as of 26 October. It has affected eight provinces.
Kenya has recorded nine confirmed cases and two deaths, while Uganda has recorded 20 confirmed cases and two deaths, alongside one probable case and one probable death.
France and Nigeria recorded one imported case each, with no deaths.
The first Nigerian case was confirmed on 20 October after a traveller with a history of travel to Uganda tested positive for the virus. The patient was subsequently medically evacuated to Switzerland, while contacts continue to be monitored.
According to the Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention (NCDC), 54 contacts linked to the Nigerian case had been traced and were under follow-up as of 26 October.
Mr Kaseya said the scale of the outbreak requires countries across the continent to strengthen preparedness even where no active cases have been detected.
He said the meeting brought together more than 40 African health ministers and that countries agreed to work together on surveillance, preparedness and cross-border coordination.
He also highlighted the economic and social consequences of the 2014-2016 West Africa Ebola outbreak, saying about five million children were kept out of school, about 23,000 children lost their parents and nearly $3 billion in gross domestic product was lost.
“We already know what an uncontrolled Ebola outbreak costs,” he said. “The data is hard to hear, but it is also our best chance to change course.”
WHO has advised against restrictions on travel to or trade with affected countries, while emphasising continued surveillance and preparedness because of the risk of cross-border transmission.
Nigeria’s case has also raised questions about how the virus is moving across the region. Genomic sequencing showed that the virus detected in Nigeria is closely related to the strain identified in Kenya, with the two samples differing by a single mutation, according to the Coordinating Minister of Health and Social Welfare, Muhammad Pate.
However, Mr Pate said the finding does not establish a direct epidemiological link between Nigeria’s case and Kenya’s first confirmed case. Further investigation is needed to determine how the virus reached Nigeria.

title: These Americans remain imprisoned in Russia. Here are their cases.
body: Stephen Hubbard, a 74-year-old American retired English teacher, is finally free after spending more than four years in a Russian prison on charges of fighting as a mercenary for Ukraine. For his family, the long wait is over.But for as many as 10 other Americans, including some with dual Russian nationality, the wait continues as they remain in Russian custody.Russian authorities tightly control all information that comes out of the country, so the detainees' circumstances can be hard to verify, but here's what we know about some of the Americans still locked up in Russian prisons and labor colonies.Travis Michael LeakeTravis Michael Leake, an American rock musician who fronted the Moscow-based band Lovi Noch, was arrested in 2023 on charges of organizing the sale of drugs. He was convicted of drug-related offenses and sentenced in 2024 to 13 years in prison.In a letter to Secretary of State Marco Rubio, Leake's family said he was "left behind" when he was excluded from the August 2024 Ankara prisoner exchange that brought home three other U.S. nationals. A representative for Leake, who had lived in Moscow since 2010, maintains the American is innocent, telling CBS News: "Travis is no drug dealer.""I'm sorry I'm not a journalist. I'm sorry I'm not a basketball player. I'm sorry I'm not somebody that's important," Leake said in a message recorded in prison advocating for his release. Robert Woodland Robert Woodland returned to Russia after living with a U.S. foster family for most of his life, hoping to track down his birth mother. He told a Russian newspaper in 2020 that he decided to move there after connecting with her through a Russian TV show. In 2024, Woodland pleaded partially guilty to Russian drug trafficking charges and was sentenced to 12½ years in prison. His sentence was reduced to 9½ years in 2025. Stanislav Kshevitskii, an attorney for Woodland, told CBS News in October 2026  there have been no updates to his case. David Barnes David Barnes and his Russian ex-wife were embroiled in a bitter custody battle over their two sons in Texas. During the dispute, Boricovna accused Barnes of sexually abusing the two boys, but law enforcement found insufficient evidence to file charges. Texas judges ruled repeatedly between 2014 and 2018 that Barnes should remain a joint custody guardian. After losing her bid for sole custody, his ex-wife took the boys to Russia in 2019.When Barnes went to Russia to pursue visitation rights, his ex-wife again accused him of sexual abuse. He was convicted in a Russian court and sentenced in February 2024 to 21 years in a penal colony.In a letter from prison to his sons, Barnes maintained his innocence, writing: "Thousands of people in America and Russia know I am innocent … You know I am innocent as well. Don't worry, we will be together again … I love you so much. I was devastated when your Mom took you from me."Daniel SchneiderDaniel Schneider is being detained in Russia amid what a website advocating for his release describes as a "complex international child custody dispute."Schneider traveled to Russia to reunite with his 4-year-old son, a Russian citizen. In July 2023, he was arrested while attempting to cross into Poland with the boy and was later sentenced to six years in prison for kidnapping after prosecutors said the child's mother did not consent to him leaving the country.Gordon Black U.S. Army Staff Sergeant Gordon Black was stationed in South Korea in May 2024 when he traveled to Russia to visit his girlfriend. U.S. officials and Russian authorities say he was arrested after she accused him of stealing money from her and was eventually sentenced to 3 years and 9 months in prison.Last year that sentence was reduced by a Russian court to 3 years and 2 months.Charles ZimmermanIn June 2025, retired U.S. Navy veteran and electrician Charles Wayne "Chuck" Zimmerman was pursuing his lifelong dream of sailing the world aboard his private sailboat. When he reached the Black Sea, his family says he was ordered to follow a Russian Navy vessel under threat of military action. Zimmerman followed the vessel to Sochi, where he voluntarily declared a firearm on board. He was arrested, and later convicted of arms smuggling and given a five-year prison sentence in January 2026.Zimmerman's sister, Robin Stultz, alleges that Russian authorities have denied her brother access to U.S. diplomatic representatives since his arrest and says she would not trust any confession they claim he made.Andre Khachatoorian Andre Khachatoorian was traveling from California to Armenia to visit his wife's family for the holidays in December 2021 when he was detained during a layover in Moscow. According to a website advocating for his release, he asked to access his checked bag to retrieve medication, and police noticed a locked firearm case inside.Supporters argue that he had proper paperwork for the weapon and allege that a Russian police officer tricked him into applying for a Russian visa before removing him from the airport. Khachatoorian was charged with arms trafficking in Russia and sentenced to eight and a half years in prison in 2023, Reuters reported.Eugene Spector In December 2024, a Russian court sentenced Eugene Spector to a total of 15 years in prison in an espionage case. The claims against him have not been made public by state media, and his trial took place behind closed doors. Spector, who was born in Russia, had previously pleaded guilty to facilitating bribes to an aide to a former Russian deputy prime minister and was sentenced to three and a half years in prison in 2022.A year later, Spector was charged with new espionage offenses, and in 2024 he was handed an additional 15-year prison sentence.Aleksandr AntonovAleksandr Antonov is a naturalized U.S. citizen who traveled to Ukraine and Russia on business trips. At a passport check in Russia in March 2025, Russian border officers noticed his U.S. passport and claimed he had Telegram messages on his phone containing anti-Russian sentiment. Antonov was detained and eventually sentenced to 6 years for inciting terrorism and extremism. CBS News has learned from current and former U.S. officials that the State Department is debating whether to designate Antonov as wrongfully detained.
